# 2026-08-02 note: the scroll-sequence converter has been REMOVED (block, routes, settings tab, worker pipeline). What was the sequence worker is now the media worker: video optimise only, no rembg/onnxruntime/numpy/Pillow, no baked-in ONNX models. Everything below about matting, see-through gaps, white un-blend and engines is history, kept because it explains why the Fly app is still called `cactus-seqworker`. See the top Last-updated entry.
# FIELD_NOTES.md
Last updated: 2026-08-07 (**Staff see the real stock number on a storefront product page** - `shop` **0.1.194** + `shop-variations` **0.1.112**, both pinned in `modules.json`, core **v0.5.970**. A shopper is told "In stock" and nothing else; the owner had no way to read the shelf without opening the admin. New `modules/shop/lib/admin-stock.ts` exports `canSeeStockLevels()`: `getSessionFromCookie()` -> `hasShopPermission(user, 'shop.products', { allowAccess: true })`. Deliberately the **read** gate (`allowAccess`), unlike `admin-edit.ts` beside it which uses the write key - a stock level is a read, and read-only shop staff already see the same figure in the admin product list. Awaited in the existing `Promise.all` in `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` and carried as the new required `DetailPartContext.showAdminStock`; `ShopDetailBadgesRsc` renders a `.spd-badge-staff` chip (dashed border, `--color-surface`/`--color-text-muted`, tabular numerals) reading `Stock: N` or `Stock: not tracked`, taking the figure off `ctx.product` - nothing extra is fetched. Two decisions worth keeping: (1) the chip is **not** tied to the block's `showStock` field - that switch decides what shoppers are told, and an owner needs the number on a layout that keeps stock quiet; (2) it is suppressed outright when `ctx.slot` is set, because on a claimed product the parent row it reads is not what governs buying, and printing it beside the provider's own figure would put two unrelated numbers on one page. On the variations side the figure belongs to the chosen combination, so `getVariantSelectorPayload` now calls the same `canSeeStockLevels()` and **withholds** rather than merely ignores: `stockCount` is nulled for shoppers (it had been sent to every browser since the payload existed, unused by the storefront), with new `tracksStock` per variant, `showStockCounts` and `baseStock` (the parent's own, for a product claimed for personalisation alone) on the payload - all optional, same JSON-shape reason as `priceSuffix`/`aliasValueIds`. Safe to make the payload per-viewer: it is built per request, `cache()`-scoped to that request only, and its two callers are dynamic route handlers plus the already-dynamic product page. New `AdminStockNote` in `VariantParts.tsx`, rendered under the buy row by **both** purchase paths - `VariantAddToCartPart` (granular block) and `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` (the slot shop's own Add to Cart part hands over to). Deskwell's live `starter-shop-detail-default-live` carries `ShopDetailBadges`, `ShopDetailAddToCart` and `ShopVariantPrice`/`ShopVariantOptions`, so it picks up both halves: the badge chip on plain products, the slot note on products with options. Live-data check that shaped the design, read-only: **every one of the 355 variation parents has `track_inventory = false`** while 21,480 hidden children track theirs, so the two figures can never appear together in practice. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, full `npm test` **1738 pass / 19 skipped / 0 fail**. No schema change, so no backup round-trip gate. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Shop.md` ("The stock figure behind In stock", in the admin-on-the-storefront run), `Shop-variations.md` ("Working through the choices").)

Also 2026-08-07 (**Vercel Speed Insights can be switched off - Settings → General** - new `SiteConfig.speedInsightsEnabled` (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true): init migration edited in place plus idempotent `prisma/core-reconcile/018_speed_insights_enabled.sql`, so an existing install gains the column on its next update and behaves exactly as before, since `app/layout.tsx` rendered `<SpeedInsights />` unconditionally until now. The root layout is now `async` and gates the component on the new `isSpeedInsightsEnabled()` in `lib/config/site.ts` - off means the script never reaches the page rather than loading and being told to keep quiet. That reader is deliberately built like `getAdminPathCached()`/`getSiteStatusCached()` beside it (5s in-memory TTL, best-effort `.catch`, cleared by `invalidateSiteConfigCache()` which the config PATCH already calls): the root layout wraps **every** route including error pages, so a fresh query per request is a cost the whole site pays and a thrown one is a bare 500 for whatever the visitor asked for. A failed read falls back to **on**, the pre-existing behaviour. Wiring: `speedInsightsEnabled: z.boolean().optional()` in the `Patch` schema of `app/api/admin/config/route.ts` (the GET already returns the whole row, and the client PATCHes its whole config object, so the schema entry is the only thing standing between the tick box and persistence), the field on `ConfigPageClient`'s `SiteConfig` type, a `general-speed-insights` anchor + tick box under the noindex one, and a matching `lib/admin/search-index.ts` entry so Cmd-K finds it. **Unrelated fix, forced by the gate**: `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` could not run at all on this machine - `lib/backup/vps-database.ts` shelled out to `sshpass` without `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, and under vitest (no controlling terminal, `DISPLAY` set by XQuartz) ssh preferred a graphical askpass binary that does not exist over the pty sshpass hands it, failing as `exec(/usr/X11R6/bin/ssh-askpass): No such file or directory` and three empty-password retries. Also pinned to `PubkeyAuthentication=no` + `PreferredAuthentications=password`: it is a password login by design, and a dev machine with five agent keys can burn the server's `MaxAuthTries` before ever reaching the password. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, full `npm test` **1726 pass / 14 skipped / 0 fail** (includes `search-index.test.ts`, which statically asserts the new `#general-speed-insights` hash resolves to a real anchor), and - new schema column, so the gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 pass / 0 skip**. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Configuration-reference.md` General-settings table, `Architecture-overview.md` root-layout note.)

Also 2026-08-07 (**Core now mints its own `CRON_SECRET`** - `lib/vercel/cron-secret.ts` (new), wired into setup, core update and module install; `CRON_SECRET` added to `SENSITIVE_KEYS` (`lib/vercel/env.ts`) and to the optional list in `getEnvStatus()` (`lib/config/env.ts`). Trigger: installing Stock Imports on Deskwell failed the required-env gate on `CRON_SECRET`, and the investigation found something worse - **Deskwell has never had a `CRON_SECRET` at all** (41 project vars, none of them it), so every scheduled job on that site, core's four member crons included, has been answering 503 since the day it went live, invisibly. The design point: `CRON_SECRET` is not a third-party credential like `SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, it is an internal shared secret with no meaning outside the site, so making an owner invent one was always the wrong shape. `ensureCronSecret()` never overwrites an existing project value (`pending`) - rotating it would break live crons - and only ever lands in `process.env` via the redeploy the caller already triggers. `app/api/admin/modules/route.ts` provisions when the manifest declares `cronJobs` **or** names `CRON_SECRET`, whichever, then drops it from the required-env gate unless provisioning genuinely failed; a module that merely schedules work no longer installs into a silently dead cron. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint .` clean on every file touched, new `lib/vercel/cron-secret.test.ts` **8 pass**, `lib/vercel` + `lib/config` + `lib/modules` suites **27 pass / 0 fail**. The 7 `tsc` errors outstanding in the tree are another agent's in-flight best-selling/popularity work in `modules/filters-for-shop` and `modules/shop`, untouched here. Wiki: `Configuration-reference.md` (`CRON_SECRET` row rewritten - nothing to fetch, and what breaks without it), `Authoring-a-module.md` (module authors must **not** declare `CRON_SECRET` in `requiredEnvVars`; keep the 503 guard in the route). Note on scope while reading Vercel billing: the plan lives on the **team** that owns the project (`deskwell`, pro), not on `GET /v2/user` (the personal account `chris-9831`, hobby) - so Stock Imports' hourly tick is fine on Deskwell. Env writes against a team-owned project work without a `teamId` query param, as `lib/vercel/env.ts` has always done; the token resolves the project by id across the scopes it can reach. **New module: Stock Imports for Shop 0.1.0** - `stock-import-for-shop`, table prefix `stk_`, repo `cactus-foundation-modules/stock-import-for-shop`, registered in `modules.json` at v0.1.0 (core v0.5.965). Chris asked for stock to be refreshed from a supplier CSV url (`https://edi.dynamicos.co.uk/Uploads/178/STK.csv`) against the SKU, on a frequency adjustable in **Settings → Shop → Stock**, plus a **Fetch Latest Stock** button on the Products page. Full detail in the module's own section below; the four things worth knowing up front: (1) **the frequency cannot be a Vercel Cron schedule** - those are baked in at deploy time - so the manifest registers one hourly tick (`5 * * * *`) and `isRunDue` decides whether the owner's chosen interval has elapsed, with 10 minutes of tolerance because strict arithmetic would drift a daily run an hour forward and start skipping days; **this needs a plan that allows sub-daily crons, which Hobby does not** (Deskwell is Pro, checked - **and check it the right way**: the project is owned by the team `deskwell` / `team_hhDdTpPWm3S23M3N4xXZn1q8`, whose `billing.plan` is `pro`. `GET /v2/user` reports the *personal* account `chris-9831`, which is `hobby` and has nothing to do with this project - reading that and concluding "Deskwell is on Hobby" is a mistake already made once. `GET /v9/projects/{id}` → `accountId` tells you which scope owns a project; `GET /v2/teams` carries the plan). (2) **The 60-second route ceiling is the design constraint**: 21,577 shop SKUs against a 53,497-row 6.4MB file that takes 5.5s just to download, so a run is a resumable job - fetch and diff, park the writes in `stk_import_job.pending`, then apply 1,000 at a time with progress saved per batch and a 45s budget; the button loops `run/step` until done, an unattended run is resumed by the next tick, and a 90s lease (claimed via one `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE`) stops the button and the cron treading on each other while expiring by itself so a dead request cannot wedge it. (3) **Only changed rows are written**, and the pending pairs carry the shop's own SKU spelling read back out of `shp_products`, so `applyStockBatch` compares `p."sku" = v."sku"` and uses the unique index instead of an `upper(btrim(...))` expression that would seq-scan once per 1,000-row batch. (4) **An unreadable stock cell never becomes a zero** - `parseStockValue` returns null and the product is left alone and reported, because guessing there is how a shop refuses orders it could have taken; `missing_behaviour: ZERO` is opt-in for the same reason. Verified against the live catalogue read-only before writing a line: 20,857 of 21,577 Deskwell SKUs match that file directly, no transformation. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, module vitest **65 pass / 0 fail**, and - new tables, so the gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 pass / 0 skip**. No dev server, per standing rule. New `wiki/Stock-Imports.md`, linked from `Home.md` and `Modules.md`; core `README.md` module list updated.)

Also 2026-08-07 (**Best-seller ordering: shop 0.1.193, shop-variations 0.1.110, filters-for-shop 0.1.9** - Chris wanted the shop sortable by best sellers, and asked first whether the supplier's own site could supply sales figures. It cannot: Shopify never exposes units sold, per product or per variant. What `dynamicofficeseating.co.uk` does expose is `?sort_by=best-selling`, an ordinal product ordering, and its theme prints the rendered page's products as a JSON array (`"collection": [...]`) complete with every variant's `sku` and `inventory_quantity`. Crawled all 58 pages: **1,141 products, 27,116 distinct SKUs**, rank 1..1141, `sort_by` verified to survive pagination and the ordering verified different from every other sort. Read-only match against live Deskwell: **20,517 of our 21,577 SKUs and 449 of our 477 parent listings get a rank**. Design (Chris picked both): seed from the supplier and let real sales take over; one `popularity` column on `shp_products` owned by shop and handed to filters-for-shop as a sort key. Shipped as **two** columns, because only one of them is derived - `popularity_seed` is given (importable, hand-editable, never touched by the recompute) and `popularity` is seed + real sales and is what every grid sorts on. `POPULARITY_SALES_WEIGHT = 100_000` makes one genuine sale outrank any seed, so a borrowed ranking retreats on its own without anyone remembering to switch it off; 365-day window; only `payment_status IN (PAID, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED)` and `status NOT IN (CANCELLED, REFUNDED)` count, refunded units subtracted. **Orders reference the hidden variation child, not the listing** (confirmed on live data), so sales roll up through a new extension point **`shop.product-sales-rollup`** -> `modules/shop/lib/popularity.ts`, provider `shopVariationsSalesRollup` in shop-variations (`lib/sales-rollup-provider.ts`, reusing the existing `getVariantParentsByChild`) - shop still knows nothing about variations. Recompute is **nightly only**, folded into the existing `api/cron/low-stock-alerts` route in a try/catch: the money path in `db/orders.ts` is deliberately untouched, and daily is also the only thing that ages sales out of the window. New sorts: `ProductSort 'popular'` (admin, `popularity DESC NULLS LAST`) and `FltSortValue 'best-selling'` (storefront, unranked last, not zero). Seeding tooling lives in `.agents/skills/deskwell-bestseller-seed/` (crawler + importer + the rank CSV); the importer is **dry-run by default**, does the identical work in a transaction and rolls it back so its counts are real, and refuses to run until shop 0.1.193 has actually reached the site. **Nothing has been written to Deskwell** - the columns do not exist there until the owner takes the update, and hand-applying DDL to a live install is not on. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, filters sort suite **10 pass**, `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts` **1 pass**, and - module migration SQL, so the gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 pass / 0 skip**. The seeding SQL itself was proved on a throwaway `cactus_rt_seedcheck` database on the OVH VPS (rollup to the best-ranked variation, refund subtraction, cancelled/unpaid/out-of-window all excluded, unranked left NULL), dropped after. Wiki: new **Best selling** section in `Shop.md`, sort list in `Shop-filters.md`.)

Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Filters for Shop 0.1.8: a "Selected" chip summary at the top of the filter panel** - `filters-for-shop`. Chris asked for the active filters to show at the top, above all the filters. Ticked chips already existed, but only above the GRID - i.e. in the right-hand column on desktop, and behind the closed sheet on phones - so the panel itself never said what was on. `FilterShell` now renders the chips **twice from one list**: `chipRow('panel')` is the first child of `.flt-sheet-body`, above every `fieldset`, and `chipRow('results')` stays above the grid; `.flt-chips-results` is `display:none` on desktop and `display:flex` at `<= tabletBp`, so exactly one copy is on screen per layout - the panel's on desktop and inside the open sheet, the grid's while the sheet is shut. The old `filterById` lookup map is replaced by an `activeChips` memo that walks `groups` in the OWNER'S order rather than `selected` in click order, so removing one chip no longer reshuffles the rest. Panel chips carry a `.flt-chip-group` prefix with the group name because the same label ("Black") appears in more than one group on this catalogue and out of context it says nothing; the prefix and the `.flt-chips-title` use `--color-text-secondary`, not `--color-text-muted`, which is 3.06:1 on `--color-bg-subtle` in dark mode and fails AA at that size (secondary is 5.07:1 light / 6.63:1 dark). The panel copy has no "Clear all" of its own - the panel head carries one on desktop and the sheet footer carries one below the tablet breakpoint - while the grid copy keeps its own, being the only chips visible with the sheet shut. New CSS only in `filter-css.ts`: `.flt-chips-panel`, `.flt-chips-results`, `.flt-chips-title`, `.flt-chip-group`, `.flt-chip-label` (`overflow-wrap:anywhere`, since a long label in a 200px sidebar has nowhere to go), plus a `flex:1 0 100%` row for the `flt-pos-top` layout and bigger touch padding inside the sheet. The existing `.flt-sheet-body .flt-group:first-child{border-top:0}` needed no change: with chips present the first group is no longer first-child, so its rule quietly becomes the separator under them. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, module vitest 30 pass / 0 fail. No dev server, per standing rule. `wiki/Shop-filters.md` "What shoppers get" gained the Selected summary. Both version fields bumped 0.1.7 -> 0.1.8, pushed and released. Root `modules.json` pin jumps 0.1.6 -> 0.1.8 in the same breath, since the 0.1.6 -> 0.1.7 Sort by dropdown from the previous session was never pinned either - this core release is the first time either reaches Deskwell's update button.)

Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Google Sheet Products 0.1.55: stock count and trade price can be kept out of the sheet** - `modules/google-sheet-products-for-shop`, **released as v0.1.55** and pinned in `modules.json` (core v0.5.964). Chris asked for an include/exclude option on **Settings → Shop → Google Sheet** for `stock_count`/`Stock` and `trade_price`/`Trade Price`. **Migration `011_column_toggles.sql`** adds `include_stock` and `include_trade_price` to `gsp_connection`, both `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true` via `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, so an existing sheet is unchanged until the owner switches one off; `mapConnection` reads them as `!== false` so a row read before the migration still reports true. `001_initial.sql` untouched, matching this module's convention (every post-001 column lives only in its numbered file). New pure `lib/columns.ts` is the single contract - `ColumnPrefs`, `DEFAULT_COLUMN_PREFS`, `columnPrefsFrom(conn)`, `excludedProductColumns` (`stock_count`, `trade_price`) and `excludedVariationColumns` (`Stock`, `Trade Price`) - with `lib/columns.test.ts` (11 cases). **The whole mechanism is the Push**: `productColumns(prefs)` filters `CSV_COLUMNS`, `buildProductsGrid(prefs)` follows, and `splitWideGridByProduct(wide, excludedColumns)` drops the named fixed columns from every product tab. Nothing in the Pull needed a special case, because a column absent from the sheet was already inert on the way back: `diffProductRows` only compares header columns it finds, shop's import engine `put()`s a field only when `hasColumn()`, and shop-variations' importer guards every optional column with `col >= 0`. Push's existing narrower-grid clear (`planTabPush`, `ownsColumn` still names both columns) sweeps the switched-off column out of the sheet on the next Push. **The one real trap, fixed:** `mergeVariationTabs` always emitted the full `FIXED_MIDDLE_COLUMNS` header and padded absent ones blank - a `Stock` column of blanks reads to the importer as "clear every variant's stock", the exact opposite of leaving it alone. It now emits a fixed column only when at least one tab actually carries it (which also fixes the same hazard for a column an owner deleted by hand); a column *some* tabs carry is kept and pads as before. `missingProductsColumns(grid, excluded)` filters the switched-off columns out of the Pull's refusal (`stock_count` is not in shop's `OPTIONAL_CSV_COLUMNS`, so an off sheet would otherwise be bounced); `lib/preview.ts` now calls it instead of `missingFormatColumns` so the preview and the Pull agree. `PATCH /settings` takes `includeStock`/`includeTradePrice` booleans (new `saveColumnPreferences` in `lib/db.ts`, per-key writes) and its `ENCRYPTION_KEY` guard moved inside the credentials branch - a checkbox PATCH stores nothing encrypted and must not 503 for want of a key. Settings tab gained a "What goes in the sheet" card with two save-on-click checkboxes that revert on a failed save. Read me tab gained a "COLUMNS YOU CAN LEAVE OUT" section. Both version fields 0.1.54 → 0.1.55. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, module vitest **170 pass / 0 fail**. No dev server, no DDL applied by hand - the migration runner picks 011 up on the install's next deploy. `wiki/Google-Sheet-Products.md` updated with a "What goes in the sheet" section.)

Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Search: an exact product name did not return that product** - `modules/search`, working tree, unreleased, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki. Version fields deliberately NOT bumped and `modules.json` NOT touched - no release asked for, and `modules.json` already carries another session's edit. Chris reported that searching the exact title "Oslo Air Height Adjustable Office Desk" did not bring back the product of that name, on a freshly rebuilt index. **Root cause, proven on the live index before any edit:** `tsQuery` in `lib/query.ts` ORed the trailing-word prefix term over the whole query - `websearch_to_tsquery(q) || to_tsquery('desk:*')` - so the last word stood alone as an alternative to everything before it. The strict half `'oslo' & 'air' & 'height' & 'adjust' & 'offic' & 'desk'` matches that one product and nothing else; the OR turned the search into "anything containing desk", **208 documents**, and the product landed at **position 62**. Second, compounding defect: the rank was `ts_rank_cd` alone, which is cover-density and so rewards repetition - `search_vector` does carry `setweight` A/B/C from the indexer, but a long body that says "desk" thirty times still beats a six-word exact title, which is why the exact match sank rather than merely being diluted. **Fixes, all in the module:** (1) the prefix term is now ANDed - `websearch_to_tsquery(head) && to_tsquery('last:*')`, with the bare `to_tsquery('last:*')` form for a one-word query so `websearch_to_tsquery('')` never fires its NOTICE. Verified on live: the fixed query returns that product **alone, at position 1, rank 1002**. (2) New `titleBoostSql` added to the rank - 1000 title equals query, 100 title starts with it, 10 title contains it - tiers spaced so a title match cannot lose to a body match. (3) Relaxed retry: strict count 0 triggers one `looseTerms` any-word pass (`a:* | b:* | ...`), adopted only if it actually finds something, so a single stray or misspelt word gives near misses rather than a blank page. **The analytics trap that came with it:** the relaxed pass would have quietly emptied the owner's "searches that found nothing" report, which is the single most useful thing on that screen. `SearchQueryResult` gained `relaxed: boolean`, and `app/api/public/search/query/route.ts` now logs `strictTotal` (0 when relaxed) to both `logQuery` and the `syncIndexAlert` gate. The pure query-text half moved out to new `lib/query-terms.ts` (no prisma import, so it is testable) with new `lib/query-terms.test.ts` - 13 tests pinning the AND split, the one-word and short-token cases, and the deliberate bail-outs on quoted phrases, `-negation` and `or`/`OR`, which the split would otherwise corrupt into their opposite. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, full vitest **1641 pass / 0 fail / 7 skipped**. No dev server run, per standing rule; verification was read-only SQL against the live Deskwell index. `wiki/Search.md` updated - visitor-facing behaviour, the owner's analytics caveat, and the developer notes.)

Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Filters for Shop 0.1.7: a Sort by dropdown on the category pages** - `filters-for-shop`, working tree, unreleased, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki. Chris asked for the usual sort settings on pages like `/shop/categories/bench-desks-workstations`; those pages are drawn by this module's `ShopFilterGrid`, not shop's own fallback category page, so the control belongs beside the filters. New `lib/sort.ts` holds the pure half - `FLT_SORT_OPTIONS` (Recommended / Price low-high / Price high-low / Name A-Z / Name Z-A / Newest / Oldest), `isFltSortValue`, `sortProductIds` - and `lib/sort.test.ts` pins it (9 tests): stable over the server's own id order so ties never shuffle, `Intl.Collator` with `numeric:true` so "800mm Bench" precedes "1200mm Bench", null prices last in BOTH directions, and the input array never mutated. The RSC builds `sortKeys` per product from `Number(ctx.fromPrice ?? ctx.prices.now)` - the same figure the PRICE bands and the cards themselves use, so a sorted grid can never disagree with the numbers on screen - plus `name` and `createdAt`. `FilterShell` gained `sortKeys`/`showSort`, a `.flt-toolbar` row above the grid ("Showing X of Y" left, the select right; full-width row <= mobile bp) and a re-order effect that does **real DOM moves** via one `DocumentFragment` re-append, not CSS `order`: the cards carry a stretched link and carousel buttons, and a visual order disagreeing with the tab order would fail WCAG 2.4.3 focus order. Safe under React because `children` is a stable server-passed node it never re-reconciles; the server order is captured in a ref on first sort, and the effect no-ops entirely while nothing has moved. The choice rides the same single query-string writer as the ticks (`?sort=`, or `?order-by=` if an admin group already owns the `sort` slug), read back post-mount and whitelist-validated. Also 2026-08-06 (**Space Planner: the simplifier was tearing models apart at the seams** - `space-planner-for-shop`, since released as 0.1.11, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki, no schema change, **live data write - see below**. Reported as the Oslo oval boardroom table drawing correctly on the product page and wrong in the planner. Not scale, not the fabric: `decimate()` in `lib/three/planner-model.ts`. **A glTF loader splits one mesh into one geometry per material, so parts finished differently arrive as separate geometries SHARING A RIM** - `oslo-oval-boardroom-table-2400.glb` is a `Table top finish` slab and a 26 mm `Table Edge` band. `decimate()` simplifies each geometry independently, so each end of that shared rim moved by a different amount and the two stopped meeting. Measured offline against the real file (17,528 tris, Draco, `spl_settings` `decimationEnabled: true` / `decimationTarget: 0.45`, no `spl_model_meta` row so no exemption): the band held at 2400 x 26 x 1000 mm (err 0.0001) while the slab pulled to 2382 x 33 x 992 from 2394 x 33 x 994 (err 0.0092) - a 12 mm crack at the rim, the oval's ends reduced to chords, and a hole through one end. **The error term hides it rather than catching it: meshoptimizer reads `target_error` as a fraction of the MESH EXTENT, so `0.01` on a 2.4 m table permits ~24 mm of wander - most of the edge band's entire height.** No threshold could have saved it. Two changes, both in `decimate()`/`build()`: **(1)** `simplify(..., 0.01, ['LockBorder'])` - open boundary vertices are pinned, which is exactly the shared rim. Verified: the slab comes back untouched (2396 tris, bbox identical, err 0.0000) and the band still gets its 55% (3014 tris). **(2)** new `DECIMATION_FLOOR_TRIANGLES = 30_000`, checked with the existing `countTriangles(object)` before the pass runs - at 17.5k tris the Oslo table was giving up its silhouette to save ~8k triangles against a 14-model budget, which is no trade at all. The per-file `no_decimation` tick remains the escape hatch. Also corrected a comment in the same function claiming nothing in this catalogue is Draco compressed; `extensionsUsed` on that file is `EXT_texture_webp`, `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `KHR_texture_transform`. **LIVE DATA WRITE, at the owner's explicit request, on `db.dwoffice.furniture:5432/neondb`:** `spl_model_meta` was empty (0 rows); one `'file'`-scope row now exists per `p3d_models` row - **11,600 rows, all `no_decimation = true`**, notes `Decimation off - simplifier damaged shared rims (2026-08-06)`. No other table touched, no DDL. This makes the fix visible on Deskwell without a release, and is scoped-deletable by that notes string; rollback SQL and the (empty) pre-write CSV were written to the session scratchpad, and the notes string is the whole of what identifies the rows. **Note the two now overlap:** the tick wins over the floor and the `LockBorder` flag alike, so nothing decimates on Deskwell at all until those rows are cleared. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` - 9 errors, all pre-existing and in other modules (`crezco-*` not checked out, `truelayer` `signing.ts`), none in this one; `eslint` clean. **Not verified in a browser** - the planner is `adminOnly` and no dev server was run; the before/after evidence is an offline Draco decode + meshopt run + software rasterise of the real file. `wiki/Space-planner.md` updated.)

Also 2026-08-05 (**View in your room stopped guessing a model's size from a rough outline and started reading its real shape** - `product-3d-views-for-shop` **v0.1.84**, released and pinned (core **v0.5.952**), module dir only, no schema change. `measureModelHeight`/`measureModelWidth` (`lib/three/load-model.ts`) and the three AR sizing points in `lib/three/ar.ts` (`bakeUsdzUrl`'s scale factor and floor lift, `startWebXrAr`'s equivalent) all called `Box3.setFromObject(model)` with no second argument - three's CONSERVATIVE form, which transforms the eight CORNERS of each mesh's own local box rather than its vertices, exact only while every node's rotation is a multiple of 90 degrees. All five calls now pass `true` (precise, per-vertex; `InstancedMesh` ignores the flag and is unaffected either way, so the 16 GPU-instanced models on the live catalogue cost nothing extra). Found 5 files inflated over 1% (three Air height-adjustable desks, 28%/28%/22%, 22 products between them; Penza 3.8%; Florence Sled 1.8%) - fixed same day by baking the offending node's rotation into its own vertices and re-uploading over the same object keys (script `bake-offaxis.mjs`, texel density verified unchanged to <0.06%, no DB row touched) - and 7 more under 0.5% (Eclipse Plus, Impulse B2B extension kit, Chiro Plus, Chesterfield, Galaxy, Eclipse XL Plus, Evolve Plus boardroom) now caught automatically by this release with no file needing to change. Separately, unrelated code path: **Storm High Back chair's stated real height was `10.5cm` for a 105cm chair**, a data-entry slip rather than this defect - corrected directly in `p3d_fabric_configs`, no release involved. 11 FBX/OBJ-modelled products remain unverified either way; the audit toolchain (`~/.cactus-3d-tools/`) is glTF-only.)

Plus `GTAOPass` on an `EffectComposer` with `OutputPass`, dynamically imported so the shopper's 3D view never downloads it, and wrapped in try/catch - a composer that will not build still yields a room lit and shadowed, which beats failing over a Fly machine already paid for. Nothing new from npm: `RoomEnvironment`, `GTAOPass`, `EffectComposer` and `OutputPass` all ship inside three 0.180, so **no core release**. **(2) The site header, footer and cookie bar were in every photograph.** Module public pages hang off the core public catch-all, so `/space-planner/render/[id]` renders inside `app/(public)/layout.tsx` - the page's own comment claimed "no chrome" and was simply wrong - and the worker's browser is brand new, so the consent banner always fires. No full-screen opt-out exists, so the page now ships a **server-rendered** `body > *:not(main)` blanking rule; server-rendered because the worker shoots as soon as `__splRenderReady` goes true and a header that vanishes a frame later is a header in the shot. **(3) The camera was always the canned standpoint.** `eyeLevel()` stands 0.6 m in from the end of the longest wall and ignores the shopper entirely; `SceneDescription` had no camera field at all. Also new: **saved views** (`spl_room_views`, room-scoped so Option A and Option B photograph from the identical spot - the comparison the plan doc wanted; 12 per room, no ownership column because the room is the authority) and an **eye-height slider** with Sitting/Standing presets, Alt+wheel and PageUp/PageDown. Also 2026-08-05 (**3D finishes render at true size again: texel density is now measured per FILE, not per product** - `product-3d-views-for-shop`, module dir only, no core diffs, no schema change (the config is jsonb). `slot.texelDensity` was measured from ONE chosen model - the face model - and applied to every model on the product, which is only right while every file in a range is unwrapped identically. Audit of all 641 attached models on the live Deskwell shop (Draco/meshopt/GPU-instancing decoded locally, cross-checked against the browser's own stored numbers: 570/574 heights and 574/602 densities agreeing to within 1%) found **133 painted slots across 15 products tiling more than 25% out**. Two shapes: the FILES changed and the config did not - the Impulse desk ranges had been re-unwrapped to the 45cm grain target (2.2222 UV/m) while the saved density stayed pre-unwrap at ~1.41, so wood grain drew at 70cm instead of 45cm on every width - and the files DISAGREE with each other, worst on `eclipse-plus-medium-back` (0.97 vs 97.3, a hundredfold) and the `air-back-to-back` benches (0.999 vs 33.4). New `FabricConfig.modelDensities` (url → material name → UV/model-unit) and `measuredDensityFor` in `lib/fabric/resolve.ts`, read in preference to the slot value and falling back to it, so a config saved before this behaves exactly as it did. `measureConfigured` in `FabricConfigPanel.tsx` now measures density for EVERY configured model rather than only the face model - the file is already open for its bounding box, so it costs one walk of the geometry - and takes the material-name list as the UNION across all readable models, which had been hiding parts that only some widths of a range carry. New slot tag "no texture map on some of this product's models" for the mixed case, which previews perfectly on whichever variation the admin is looking at and wrongly on the rest. Densities for 137 products / 581 model files written to the live DB on 2026-08-05, measured off the served GLBs; backed up first with a per-row rollback. Simulated post-change: slots >25% out **133 → 0**, correct 662 → 801. Two faults found and NOT fixed by this: **125 models carry no TEXCOORD_0 at all** on a painted part, so no finish can map at any size (the Air Lite desk range among them - box projection at 1 UV/unit prepared and verified for 124 of them, not yet uploaded), and **117 slots name a material the file does not contain**, the supplier exporting the same part as `New Material`, `New Material (1)` and `*A1` across widths of one range. Also 5 products whose stated overall height disagrees with the model by 6-15%, which is a product-data question rather than a rendering one.)

Also 2026-08-05 (**Space Planner: models stop being squashed, and they arrive in the right colour** - `space-planner-for-shop` **v0.1.6**, released and pinned (core **0.5.947**), module dir only, no core diffs beyond the pin, no schema change. Four faults, one visible symptom - a customer-facing planner drawing a stretched, pancaked, white office chair. **(1) The size parser lost the unit off a range.** `parseDimensionValue` split `"66.5-131.5cm"` on the hyphen and parsed `"66.5"` alone, so `assume` fell back to millimetres: every height-adjustable desk on the live site was cached **67 mm tall**, the Galaxy chair's `111-127cm` read as **111 mm**, `43.5-50cm` as 44 mm. New `withUnitFrom()` lends the lower bound the unit written on the upper one (and the first of a list the unit on the last) - not a guess, it is written down, on the same expression, about the same measurement. 537 products carry a ranged overall dimension; 60 of the 212 modelled listings. **(2) Variations inherited nothing from their listing.** `getSpecValues` reads per product, and in this catalogue a listing states its dimensions once while its twelve colours state only their colour - so every placed variant fell past a perfectly good spec sheet to the `marker` fallback, literally `800 x 600 x 750`. New `getVariationParents()` in `lib/spec-attributes.ts` (raw SQL behind a `to_regclass` probe, no shop-variations import); `resolveDimensions` now reads child values then listing values, child first, and falls back to the listing's category too. Freshness gained `parentMovedSince()` - checked against the row's `resolved_at`, deliberately NOT banked into `product_updated_at`, because that column is compared against `shp_products.updated_at` by the sweep's own SQL and a parent's stamp in a child's row would make it look permanently stale for ever. **(3) Scaling was three independent divisions.** Right until one of the six numbers is wrong, and then the worst possible answer: a bad axis does not draw a small chair, it draws a squashed one. New pure `lib/three/model-scale.ts` + tests - an axis ratio outside 0.4-2.5 is a data fault and is dropped, an **approximate** size never deforms a real mesh, axis ratios disagreeing by >1.5x fall back to uniform; below that per-axis stretch stays, because a supplier widening a desk by sliding its ends apart is a real size. **(4) The planner never applied p3d's fabric paint at all.** This catalogue is one file per SHAPE with the colour painted at view time, so 138 of the 212 modelled listings rendered in the bare file's white. `lib/model-resolver.ts` now asks p3d for the same `FabricBundle` its own viewer uses (`resolveFabricForChild`), prefers **the bundle's model** where there is one (material names are the contract; painting them onto a different file of the same product silently does nothing), and ships `slots` + a `fabricKey` to the client. `ResolvedModel` gained `fabricKey` and `instanceGroups` are keyed on **file plus paints** via new `instanceKey()` - keyed on the file alone a room holding a blue chair and a black one drew whichever resolved first, twice. New `paintedModel()` in `lib/three/planner-model.ts` **clones the materials** named in the slots before painting them, because prepared models are shared by every placement and three.js clones share materials by reference. A **listing** placed from the browse panel borrows its first enabled variation's colours (`getFirstVariationChildren`), the same one the product page opens on. `autoScale` is carried through, not dropped - a weave left at repeat 1 comes out ~17x too big. Bundles are cached per server instance for 60s and resolved 6 at a time: each is ~8 queries, one of which reads the shop's whole swatch vocabulary, and 20 fired off together is 160 queries arriving at PgBouncer at once (measured 38.5s cold / 1.5s warm for 20 products from a laptop with 700ms RTT). **Rung 1 of the size ladder finally exists.** The README has always said `scripts/calibrate.mjs` writes the measured rows; there is no such script and there never was, so in three releases **not one `glb`-sourced row was ever written** - 0 of 100 on the live site, and so 0 conflicts ever flagged. It cannot run in a route (60s, ~4 MB a file), so it runs in the ADMIN'S BROWSER: new `GET/POST /api/m/space-planner-for-shop/admin/dimensions/measure` + a **Measure** card on the Sizes screen that loads every distinct model file with the same code that draws them, grouped by file rather than by product, clearing the prepared-model cache every 8 files and posting extents back in batches of 25. New `applyMeasurements()` in `lib/resolve-dimensions.ts` writes `source: 'glb'` with the conflict note computed against the spec sheet, **never over a hand-typed size**, and refuses an implausible measurement outright. New `listModelledProductIds()` in `lib/db/model-meta.ts`. Verified against the live Deskwell database: all four Galaxy products now resolve 675 x 640 x 1110 with distinct fabric keys per colour, and the Air height-adjustable desks 665 mm rather than 67 mm. **Existing cached rows are still wrong until somebody presses the buttons** - Sizes -> Measure, then "Work the sizes out again". ~27 rows were rewritten with correct values during that verification. `wiki/Space-planner.md` and the module README updated.) Also 2026-08-04 (**One variation can now answer to two values of the same option** - shop-variations **0.1.109**, working tree, unreleased. Deliberately not a second `svr_variant_values` row: that table's sorted value-set is the variation's identity for `upsertVariantForCombination`, the CSV importer, the Google-Sheet `pull-diff` and the deletion planner, and the sheet carries one value cell per option - a second row there reads as a different combination, and the next Pull's `setVariantValues` "corrects" it away. Also 2026-08-04 (**Quotes: VAT restored, the site's fonts applied, and five new document controls** - quote-for-shop **0.1.9**, working tree, unreleased. Module dir only, no core diffs, no schema change (`QuoteLine.delivery` is a new optional key inside the existing `lines` jsonb). **The VAT one was a real fault, not a gap**: `buildQuoteSnapshot` called shop's `resolveOrderTotals` with `zoneId: null` on the reasoning that neither tax nor delivery can be known without a delivery address - but no zone means no rate means `taxAmount: 0`, and the Totals block drops a zero row, so a VAT-registered shop's quote read "there isn't any" rather than "not known yet". Module v0.1.4 in the working tree, unreleased, plus a NEW repo `space-planner-render-worker`.** Photoreal pictures were the one thing in the module that needed somebody to go and build a machine; now the owner presses a button on **Space Planner → Pictures**. New idempotent module migration `002_render_worker.sql`: table `spl_render_worker` (singleton; `fly_token`, `app_name`, `region`, `worker_token`, `image`, `self_provisioned`) and `spl_render_jobs.machine_id` + a partial index on it. The Fly token lives in its own table rather than the `spl_settings` blob **because the settings API hands that blob out whole** - a secret in it would escape the first time somebody added a field. New `lib/fly/api.ts` (Machines REST + GraphQL, deliberately a private copy - reaching into `google-reviews-for-shop` for it would make this module refuse to install without that one), `lib/fly/render-worker.ts` (provision / per-job machine / teardown / orphan sweep), `lib/db/render-worker.ts`, `lib/render-dispatch.ts` (job payload + a SESSION_SECRET-derived render-page token), admin route `app/api/admin/space-planner-for-shop/render-worker/` (GET view / POST provision / DELETE teardown; read on `space-planner.access`, write on `space-planner.manage`), and public page `app/public/space-planner/render/[id]` + `components/public/RenderFrame.tsx`. **The Fly key is borrowed, not asked for twice**: `resolveFlyToken()` tries the module's own, then core's `getMediaWorkerConfig().fly.token` (Media → Video), then `MEDIA_WORKER_FLY_TOKEN`/`SEQUENCE_FLY_TOKEN` - so on a site with the video converter set up the screen is one button and no box. An app-scoped deploy token cannot create an app, so `getOrganisations()` doubles as the capability probe and the failure says so in English rather than 403-ing. **The worker does not draw the room**: it opens `/space-planner/render/[id]?token=...` (signed, 30-minute, job-bound; the page 404s once the job is finished so a live token is not a free render), waits for `window.__splRenderReady`, and screenshots it - so the renderer is `lib/three/planner-scene.ts`, the same code the shopper was looking at, and there is no second scene assembly to drift. **Machine lifecycle is the whole design**: one `performance-8x`/16384MB machine per render (matching core's `cactus-seqworker`, because with no GPU on Fly the render is SwiftShader and cores *are* the frame rate), `auto_destroy` + `restart:'no'`, destroyed by the callback the moment the picture is filed, by the worker's own `IDLE_MS` exit if that callback is lost, and by the nightly sweep (new step 5, after the stale-job step so an aged-out job stops claiming its machine) if it managed neither. New config key `maxRenderMachines` (default 6) is a **spend ceiling, not a queue depth** - past it a shopper is told to try again, because a queue behind a 60-second route is a timeout wearing a hat. The worker uploads straight to the media Worker with a `signUploadToken` key **the site chose before the machine existed** and reports only `sizeBytes`; the callback writes the `Media` row from the key kept on the job, never from the request, and no route anywhere accepts image bytes. `renderWorkerConfigured()` is now **async** (env first, then the provisioned app) - `renderEnvConfigured()` is the sync half. `SPACE_PLANNER_RENDER_URL`/`_SECRET` still work and still win, and suppress the button entirely. `requiresCoreVersion` raised to 0.5.942 for the media-worker Fly config. No core diffs. Also 2026-08-03 (**A customer's own order page now prints the bank transfer details, instead of only the thank-you page doing it** - `modules/shop/app/public/shop/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx`, no schema change, no new config key, no API change. `bankTransferInstructions` / `cashInstructions` have always been read by three places - the checkout page (gated on `bankTransferInstructionsOnCheckout` / `cashInstructionsOnCheckout`, via each provider's `createIntent`) and `GET /api/m/shop/public/orders/status` for the confirmation page - and the comment in `lib/payments/bank-transfer.ts` claimed "the thank-you page and the shopper's own order page read the same setting's words", which was half true: the account order page had never read them. That is the gap an owner falls into who switches the checkout copy off (the live Deskwell install has `bankTransferInstructionsOnCheckout: false`), because then the account-out-of-inbox route was the one place the account number could not be found again. New file-local `MANUAL_INSTRUCTION_KEYS` (`BANK_TRANSFER` -> `bankTransferInstructions`, `CASH` -> `cashInstructions`) and `PaymentInstructions`, rendered as the **first** child of the detail grid, above the open-request alert, on the same reasoning the confirmation page uses for its own ordering - anything the shopper still has to do about money comes before anything else the page says. One tone only, after the same-day revision below: `alert alert-warning` headed "How to pay - {total} still to reach us" plus the confirmation page's own "awaiting payment confirmation" sentence, rendered **only** while the money is outstanding. (It shipped with a second tone - a plain `card` headed "How you paid" once the payment was in, on the reasoning that the wording often carries a reference worth looking up. Wrong call: on a paid order a panel of bank details reads as a bill arriving twice.) Outstanding means `paymentStatus` `PENDING` or `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION` **and** order status not `CANCELLED`/`REFUNDED` - a cancelled bank transfer sits at `PENDING` forever precisely because nobody ever paid it, so the status test is what stops the page invoicing for an order that is off. Methods are named one by one rather than taken from the payment registry's `confirmMode === 'manual'`: a manual method contributed by a module keeps its instructions in its own settings, so matching on "manual" alone would have printed the shop's cash wording under somebody else's method. The printable receipt at `[id]/receipt` deliberately unchanged. Module version NOT bumped and nothing committed - other agents have `lib/config.ts`, `ShopSettingsTab.tsx` and `BuyAgainButton.tsx` open in the same working tree.)

The `paymentOutstanding` test itself is unchanged (`paymentStatus` `PENDING`/`AWAITING_CONFIRMATION` **and** order status not `CANCELLED`/`REFUNDED`), so cancelled and refunded orders go on showing nothing, as before. The `awaiting && isManual` warning band above it is untouched, and since `POST public/checkout/confirm` parks every `confirmMode: 'manual'` order at `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`, that band is the only one a shopper with money still to send ever sees - the removed one only ever fired on `PAID`/`PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`/`REFUNDED`/`FAILED`. `.soc-instructions` in `order-confirmation-css.ts` is still used by the warning band, so the CSS stays. Also 2026-08-03 (**The burger drawer measures the header instead of guessing at it** - `lib/puck/components/MenuBlockClient.tsx`, finishing what the entry below started. `top: '100%'` resolves against the drawer's offset parent, which is the header's *content box* - and that box is centred in the header, so 100% is the bottom of the ROW, not of the header. Identical only when the header has no spare height, which was exactly the case at the one height every header used to be (96px header, 32px row). Deskwell's mobile header at 48px has 17px spare, so the drawer opened 9px high and painted its own background over the header's bottom rule. New `measureDrawerTop()` takes `header.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - offsetParent.getBoundingClientRect().top` off the toggle button (whose offset parent IS that content box) **on click, before the drawer renders**, so there is no first-frame jump; `drawerTop` state, `top: drawerTop ?? '100%'` keeps the old behaviour when there is no `<header>` ancestor at all (the block is not header-only). Re-measured on resize and capture-phase scroll while open, the same treatment `SearchBoxClient`'s bar already had - which is precisely why the bar measured flush at 0 and the drawer did not. Deskwell's header is now `height: {desktop:'96px', mobile:'48px'}`, applied after the 0.5.927 deploy for the reason the entry below gives; 42px was tried first and the row (31px, the burger button being the tallest thing in it) sat too tight in it.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The composable header's height is a per-screen-size setting, and the burger drawer stops assuming 96px** - `lib/puck/config.tsx` + `lib/puck/components/MenuBlockClient.tsx`. `headerPuckConfig.root.fields.height` was a `select` of six fixed values (`auto`/48/64/72/80/96) applying at every width, so a phone header holding one row of 20px icons could not be shortened without shortening the desktop one, and no preset matched what was wanted anyway. Now a `ResponsiveUnitValueField` in px/rem/vh, mirroring the `paddingX` field added the same day: desktop stays inline on the element, tablet/mobile come out of `responsiveMediaCssFor('header[data-header-root]', …)`, blank resolves to `64px` (the old default) and `'auto'` still means content height floored at 48 at whichever breakpoint asks for it. Old data was a plain string and normalises, so every saved header renders byte-identically. `splitUnitValue` already shows an unparseable keyword as-is rather than blanking it, which is what lets `auto` survive the field-type change. Specificity checked: the new rule is `header[data-header-root]` (0,1,1) against the shrink-on-scroll override's `header[data-shrink-root][data-shrunk]` (0,2,1), so a shrunk header still wins on scroll despite both carrying `!important`. The legacy all-in-one `SiteHeaderBlock` render keeps its own plain-string height - different block, not the composable header. Second half: `MenuBlockClient`'s hamburger drawer was positioned `top: 64`, absolute inside the header's centred content box. That box's bottom edge IS 64 when the header is 96px tall and the row is 32 - which it always was - so the constant was a coincidence that broke the moment a header wasn't 96. Now `top: '100%'`, which is the same pixel today (63.5, a half-pixel from the hardcoded value) and follows any height. **Deskwell's own header data is deliberately NOT updated yet**: a responsive object in `root.props.height` reaching the currently-deployed render would land as `height: [object Object]` and collapse the live header to content height at every width, so the 42px mobile value goes in only once the install has taken this release.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The search field stops iOS zooming the page in on itself** - `modules/search` **0.1.12**, one CSS rule. Reported as "the search box is too wide, its left edge is cut off" on an iPhone 13 mini, and invisible to every measurement here: Playwright WebKit at 375x812 put the bar at 0-375 and its field at 12-363 with nothing clipped, in both schemes. The cause is not layout at all - **iOS Safari zooms the whole page whenever a focused input computes under 16px**, and the bar autofocuses, so the zoom fires the instant it opens and takes the field's left edge off-screen with it. The block's size vars are 13px (small), 15px (medium) and 17px (large), so two of the three tripped it. New `@media (pointer:coarse){.srch-input{font-size:max(16px,var(--srch-font))}}` floors the live input on touch pointers only - a mouse or trackpad keeps the chosen size exactly and no desktop layout moves. Deskwell's own block also moved from Medium to **Large** as the immediate fix, since that clears 16px on the deployed 0.1.11 without waiting for a release; the trigger is unaffected either way because `fieldStyle: minimal` zeroes its padding and `iconSize: 20` pins the glyph, verified after the change - search glyph still 20x20 at x=50, midY 47.5, every gap still 16. The site's viewport meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1` with no `maximum-scale`, which is correct and stays that way: suppressing zoom to dodge this would take pinch-zoom off every visitor who needs it.)

Toggle icons go to `strokeWidth="2"`, and the bars move into a shared `HAMBURGER_BAR` style object at `20 * 2 / 24` - the arithmetic left in place so the next person can see where it comes from rather than meeting 1.667 cold. `AdminNav.tsx`'s 14px star icons keep their 1.6: admin chrome at a different size, nothing lines up beside them. The bar change takes the toggle button 1px shorter (3 x 1.667 + 2 x 5 gap + 16 padding = 31, was 32), which the centre-aligned header row absorbs. Deskwell's own colour outlier was data, not code: the mobile `Phone` block had inherited `color: var(--color-1)` from the desktop block, where the number is a teal call to action, so it was the one icon in six not painted `var(--color-text)` - fixed in the layout row, along with its `--color-2` hover.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**A header icon row that lines up to the pixel** - three separate 2-3px defects, found by measuring every glyph's rect on the live Deskwell header at 375px. (1) `modules/search` **0.1.11**: the icon button is `inline-flex` inside a plain block wrapper, so it sat on the text baseline and the line box's descender space rode the glyph **2.5px above** the centre line of the icons beside it - new `.srch-box-icon{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;line-height:0}` on the wrapper (added in both the client island and the editor render) takes the baseline out of it. `minimal` also swapped `border-color:transparent` for `border:none`, since a transparent 1px edge still measures and made an 18px box out of a 16px glyph. The editor render also stops applying `boxStyle`'s `width:100%` to an icon button, which the live render never did. (2) Core `Phone` block: with the number hidden by "icon only on mobile" the lone glyph still sat on the link's baseline and measured **2.3px low**; the same media rule that hides the text now flexes `a[data-phone-link]` (`display:flex;align-items:center;line-height:0`) with `justify-content` restating the block's own alignment, which a flex container would otherwise ignore. Deliberately NOT at `createPendingOrder`: an abandoned checkout would otherwise file an address nobody committed to. Guest orders (`memberId` null) are a no-op, and the whole thing is try/caught - a shop that cannot write an address book has still taken a real order. **Dedupe**: new exported `addressDoorKey()` in `lib/db/addresses.ts` - `line1|line2|postcode`, whitespace stripped, lower-cased - plus `rememberAddressForMember()`, a single `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS` that rebuilds the identical key in SQL (`lower(regexp_replace(coalesce(address->>'line1','')||'|'||..., '[[:space:]]', '', 'g'))`; POSIX class, not `\s`, which a tagged template would eat). Name and phone are deliberately outside the key: same door, different recipient, one entry. `is_default` is set only when it is the member's first row, via a second `NOT EXISTS` in the same statement. **JS and SQL keys must be changed together** - verified equal against the live Postgres at build time; the JS half is pinned by new `lib/db/address-door-key.test.ts` (6 cases). **Reading**: `CheckoutShippingClient` fetches `/api/m/shop/member/addresses` on mount (skipped in the Puck preview), draws a **Deliver to** radio fieldset above the fields listing each saved address plus **Use a different address**, and prefills from the default (or first) address only when `shippingAddress.line1` is empty, so a part-typed or stepped-back-to checkout is never clobbered. Picking one calls `chooseSaved` (fills the form, clears `touched`); editing any field or picking an address-lookup suggestion drops the radio back to "a different address", since the fields no longer describe the stored entry. A 401 (signed out) leaves the list empty and the form exactly as it was. `AddressesClient` gained `addressTitle()` so label-less automatic rows show the recipient's name rather than three identical "Address" headings, and the page's standfirst now describes what actually happens. `wiki/Shop.md` Customer accounts section updated.
