Six module repos moved onto the seam: **shop** (its 10 order emails, `shp_email_templates` table and its own settings sub-tab retired - migration `014` carries across only wording an owner had actually edited), **quote-for-shop** (4), **reviews-for-shop** (2), **boards** (2, and the digest's thread titles are escaped now), **twilio** (2), **contact-form** (2 owner notifications; the auto-reply and an owner's own typed reply are deliberately left alone).) Also **the frontend member sign-in form is identifier-first**: email address + Continue, then only the methods that address actually has, from the new public `POST /api/members/auth/methods` (rate limit `member_auth_methods`, 30/15min/IP). Passkey button only for a member with a `MemberPasskey`, password button only for one with a `MemberPassword`, sign-in link whenever the site allows it - so a member with neither is offered the link and nothing else. Unknown addresses, unparseable bodies and rate-limited callers all get that same link-only answer; a failed lookup client-side falls back to every method the site allows. New `.field input[readonly]` styling in `app/globals.css` for the settled email field.

Also 2026-08-03 (**A collapsed menu button can fill its slot, and stops overflowing it** - `MenuBlock` gains the per-breakpoint `navButtonWidth` field (`auto`, the default and old behaviour, or `full`), which sizes the "Dropdown (current page)" trigger to the slot it was dropped into and pushes its bars to the far edge like a select; at `auto` the button is exactly its content's width, so there is no free space and both values render identically - every existing menu is untouched. `fitOneLine` ("Keep on one line") now reaches that trigger too: it caps the button at `max-width:100%` and shrinks the label through `HeadingFitText` instead of letting a long page name wrap or spill past its column. The trigger carries `data-menu-dd-id="<block id>"` so the width rules scope to one block. Threaded through `lib/puck/config.tsx`, `MenuBlockClient.tsx`, `MenuBlockEditorPreview.tsx` and both editors. Alongside it, the **search module** (0.1.8) makes the Search Box's `size` per-breakpoint: `searchSizeStyles()` returns the desktop `srch-size-*` class plus, only where a breakpoint differs, a media rule re-declaring `--srch-pad`/`--srch-font`/`--srch-icon` scoped to `[data-srch-id="<block id>"]` - so a header box reads smaller on phones with desktop untouched. `SRCH_SIZE_VARS` in `search-css.ts` is now the single source for the three sizes, and the client config carries `sizeClass`/`sizeCss`/`blockId` in place of the old flat `size`.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The member account is a real account area now, and a shop customer can manage their own orders in it** - core gains two seams so a module can live *inside* the account rather than beside it: **`members.account-nav`** (`lib/members/account-nav.ts`, collected by `getMemberAccountNavExtras()` from installed manifests; a provider that throws is dropped rather than locking a member out of their own security settings) contributes `{key,label,href,badge?}` tabs to the account tab bar, and **`components/members/account/MemberAccountShell.tsx`** is the chrome (container, `AccountFlash`, deletion banner, `notice` slot, `AccountNav`) lifted out of `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` so a module's own member pages - which are outside that route group and never saw the layout - wear the identical thing. `AccountNav` now matches Overview exactly and every other tab by prefix, so a module's detail page still lights its tab. The overview stopped being two lines of signposting and became a dashboard: avatar, email, member-since, an unverified-email nag with a working resend button (`VerifyEmailNudge.tsx`), and four cards (security posture, profile gaps, notifications, last three activity events) in one `Promise.all`. **shop 0.1.181** takes both seams: Orders and Addresses are tabs with a pending-request count pill, and every `/shop/account/*` page wraps `MemberAccountShell` instead of rendering bare - which was the actual defect, a shopper clicking "Order history" landed on a page with no tabs and no way back. Order history gained dates, thumbnails, status/fulfilment pills and JS-free `?show=` filters; order detail gained the totals breakdown, both addresses, per-parcel carrier + tracking, itemised refunds, pre-order and dispatched/refunded per-line badges, Buy again, and a printable receipt at `/shop/account/orders/[id]/receipt`. **Customer cancel and return requests** are new end to end: migration `015_order_requests.sql` (mirrored in 001) adds `shp_order_requests` + `shp_order_request_items`, with a partial unique index on `(order_id) WHERE status='PENDING'` as the real race guard; `lib/order-requests.ts` holds the eligibility rules ONE place so the button and the endpoint cannot disagree (cancel only before anything is dispatched, return only after and only inside `returnWindowDays` counted from the LAST parcel out, never from the order date); `lib/db/order-requests.ts` records under the same advisory lock refunds and dispatch already share (now exported from `lib/db/shipments.ts` rather than copied a fourth time); `lib/order-request-actions.ts` decides what approving MEANS - record the decision first so two admins cannot both run the refund behind it, then the optional refund, then the status change, with a failed refund reported in `refundError` rather than silently swallowed or rolled back. Member APIs `POST /api/m/shop/member/orders/[id]/requests` and `DELETE /api/m/shop/member/requests/[id]`; admin queue at **Shop → Cancellations & returns** (`/m/shop/requests`, `RequestsScreen.tsx`, `GET|POST /api/m/shop/admin/requests[/id]`) where the refund tickbox is a deliberate second step because money leaving should never be one stray click. Four new email templates (`shop.request-received`/`-approved`/`-declined`/`shop.admin-new-request`) and three config keys (`cancelRequestsEnabled`, `returnRequestsEnabled` both default true, `returnWindowDays` default 30). Auto-approval was deliberately left out: money leaving on a timer is not a default anyone should inherit.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Registration survives a broken mail server, and the username/display-name fields are optional** - `POST /api/members/register` no longer throws when `sendVerificationEmail` fails: the `Member` row already exists by then, so the failure is caught, `console.error`ed and reported as `verificationEmailSent: false` in the 200 body. Throwing produced a bare 500 whose non-JSON body made the browser's own `Response.json()` parse failure the error the member saw - in Safari, "The string did not match the expected pattern." - while the account sat unusable on `PENDING_VERIFICATION` with no link ever sent. `RegisterForm` now parses error bodies with `.catch(() => ({}))`, and on `verificationEmailSent === false` stays put with a warning rather than sending them to `/verify-email` to wait for a link that was never sent. The existing-email branch sends for real too (magic link if ACTIVE, verification link again if PENDING_VERIFICATION and past the resend throttle) so the new flag means the same thing on both branches and stays enumeration-safe. `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend` likewise catches and logs - a 500 there answered "is this address registered?" out loud. Two new `MembersConfigSchema` keys, both default true: `registrationCollectUsername` and `registrationCollectDisplayName`. Off hides the field AND makes the API ignore anything sent for it; with the username off, `generateUsernameFromEmail()` (new, `lib/members/registration.ts`, `lib/members/registration.test.ts`) builds one from the local part plus 4 random digits, widening to 8 after 15 collisions and falling back to `member` when the address leaves nothing usable. Admin toggles live in the Members → Registration tab. Separately, `RegisterForm`'s username `pattern` was `[a-z0-9_-]{2,32}`, which browsers compile with the regex `v` flag where a bare trailing `-` in a class is a syntax error: the attribute was skipped, so it had been validating nothing in every browser. Now `[a-z0-9_\-]{2,32}` - previously: **A payment method can be named by the site owner** - `ShpPaymentProvider` gained an optional `getLabel(): Promise<string>`, resolved per request by the new `resolveProviderLabel()` in `modules/shop/lib/payments/registry.ts`; `getPaymentMethodLabels()` is async as a result, and its three consumers now await it (`GET public/config`, `GET public/orders/status`, `GET admin/settings`'s `listPaymentMethodsForAdmin`). The static `label` is the fallback whenever `getLabel` is absent, returns blank, or throws - a checkout radio with no wording beside it being worse than a stale one. First user: `square-payment-for-shop` v0.1.3, whose **Payment description** setting now names the method everywhere instead of only reaching Square's own hosted page - previously: **Shop Payments settings rebuilt around one method per tab** - `modules/shop/components/admin/PaymentsSettings.tsx` (new) replaces the flat block that was `ShopSettingsTab`'s Payments sub-tab. A chip strip runs across the top: **Payment methods** (the list) then one chip per method that has settings of its own. The list shows EVERY registered method - shop's own four plus whatever modules contributed - each with an on/off `role="switch"`, a live status badge (Showing at checkout / Not finished / Off), a one-line reason, a Set up link into its own chip, and drag-handle + ▲▼ reordering that sets the order the checkout offers them in. Two new `ShpConfig` keys back it: `disabledPaymentMethods` (the shop-wide veto, and the ONLY off switch a module-contributed method ever had - being named there beats a provider reporting itself ready) and `paymentMethodOrder` (the arrangement; empty falls back to `enabledPaymentMethods` order, so an existing shop's checkout does not reshuffle itself). `getAvailablePaymentMethods()` was rewritten around one per-provider rule (`paymentMethodAvailability`) plus `sortPaymentMethods`. The ordering and switched-on rules live in the new client-safe `modules/shop/lib/payments/admin-methods.ts` (unit-tested in `admin-methods.test.ts`) because the settings screen cannot import shop config without dragging Prisma into the browser bundle. `GET admin/settings` now also returns `paymentMethods[]` ({id,label,builtIn,ready,panelId}), and `registry.ts` gained `getModuleProviderEntryIds()` so a method row can find its module's own panel. The `shop.payments` hosted slot is now consumed as the **labelled** shape (`hostedSettingsPanels`), one chip per panel, not merged - previously: **The member area gated its own sign-in page** - `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` is the session gate for the whole member area, and in Next.js a layout wraps *every* page beneath it, so `login`, `register` and `verify-email` were gated too. Signed out, `/{memberAreaPath}/login` redirected to `/{memberAreaPath}/login?redirect=<itself>`, and each hop `encodeURIComponent`-ed the entire previous URL into the next one, doubling the encoding every round until the address outgrew what a browser will load. The shop's post-purchase "Create an account" link into `/{memberAreaPath}/register?email=…` walked straight into it and dead-ended on Safari's "can't open the page". The gate now excepts those three sub-paths through a new pure `isPublicMemberPath(fullPath, basePath)` in `lib/members/paths.ts` (with `MEMBER_PUBLIC_SUBPATHS`, unit-tested in `lib/members/paths.test.ts`) and renders them bare - no `AccountNav`, no deletion banner, since neither belongs to a visitor without a session. The login page separately drops a sanitised `?redirect=` that points back at a signed-out member page, so a stale link cannot restart the loop. This mirrors what `proxy.ts` has always done for the admin area, where the `/login` sub-path is explicitly skipped before the session check - previously: **Square holds sandbox and production credentials separately** - `square-payment-for-shop` v0.1.2 (`requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.875): `SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT` now picks between the unprefixed production vars and a new `SQUARE_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`SQUARE_SANDBOX_LOCATION_ID`/`SQUARE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY` set, so both can be held at once and the settings tab's "(set)" tick means set FOR THAT ENVIRONMENT - one shared set of variables meant a saved production token read as a saved sandbox one, and switching environment silently pointed production credentials at the sandbox API. `isSquareConfigured()` no longer requires the webhook signature key: Square only issues one once the subscription exists, so demanding it up front made the method impossible to switch on. Token + location gate the method; the key is reported separately as `webhookConfigured` on `admin/status` and drives a warning band explaining that without it only the redirect-return path confirms payments. New `POST app/api/admin/locations` route lists `GET /v2/locations` for a token supplied in the request BODY - env vars are not readable by the running server until the next deployment, so a just-typed token could not otherwise be looked up - behind a **Look up locations** button, because Square's Credentials page hands out an Application ID and an access token and keeps the location id on another page entirely (the Application ID is for the Web Payments SDK and OAuth, and is not used by this module at all). Two core fixes fell out of it, both generic: `PATCH /api/admin/modules/[id]` `update` now refreshes the row's stored `manifest` to the tag being installed (it was frozen at install time, so no module could ever add a new `requiredEnvVars` entry in a later version), and `POST /api/admin/env` now returns `skipped: string[]` for filled-in keys it does not manage - 400 if that is all of them - instead of dropping them and answering `ok`. Square's settings tab surfaces `skipped` as a save error telling the admin to update the module first. The module's `requiresCoreVersion` is raised to **0.5.874** accordingly - previously: **A variation now takes its tax class from the listing, not from itself** - a variation is a hidden child `shp_products` row and the basket rates a line from the CHILD's tax class, but the class was only ever copied off the parent at the instant the child was created, so any shop that set up its VAT class (or moved a range onto a different one) after generating its matrices quoted the same chair WITH tax on the product page - which prices from the PARENT, see `getVariantSelectorPayload` - and WITHOUT it in the basket; on the Tester database 14,034 of 17,484 variations were adrift. New generic shop seam `shop.product-saved` (`modules/shop/lib/product-saved.ts`) fires from `updateProduct` itself rather than from the admin route, so the product editor, the CSV upload and the Google-Sheet Pull are all covered by the same three lines, and hands listeners the list of fields the write actually carried; shop-variations' `lib/tax-class-sync.ts` listener puts every child of that parent back onto the parent's class in one statement, and migration `009_variant_tax_class.sql` is the one-off catch-up for the children already written. The owner is never asked to pick a tax class per variation - the editor does not offer one - so the parent is the only answer there is - previously: **Checkout now prints the order-payment-state note** - `shop` v0.1.170 renders whatever sentence a module offered about the chosen payment method (`data.notes` from `POST /checkout/payment-intent`) as an info band above the method's own fields in `CheckoutPaymentClient`, cleared on every method change, completing the seam v0.1.169 added - previously: **Pay-later orders no longer promise a delivery date they cannot keep** - new generic shop seam `shop.order-payment-state` (+ an opaque `LineMeta.data` bag) lets a module restate an order line's own snapshot at the two moments an order's payment state moves - creation and payment - and add a sentence under the chosen method at the checkout; `advanced-shipping-for-shop` v0.1.32 uses it to show a lead time in working days on BANK_TRANSFER/CASH orders until the money lands (keyed on the payment provider's `confirmMode === 'manual'`, never a method id) and to re-date every line from `order.paidAt` once it does - previously: **Shop checkout agreements, business name, and a post-purchase account prompt that finally exists** - `shp_orders.agreements` JSONB (migration `013_checkout_agreements.sql`) snapshots the wording of every tickbox the shopper was shown, so editing a statement later cannot rewrite what a past order agreed to; new shop config for the business-name box (enable / require / label, rendered above address line 1) and for the terms tickbox plus owner-defined ones, both re-enforced in `/checkout/payment-intent` because a browser-side `required` is only a suggestion; `postPurchaseAccountPrompt` had been saved by the settings screen and read by nothing since it was added, so the prompt it promised had never once appeared - `/orders/status` now resolves it (setting AND members enabled AND not invite-only AND guest order) and `listOrdersForMember` claims guest orders by verified email, without which the prompt leads to an account with an empty order history; order confirmation screen rebuilt around `ORDER_CONFIRMATION_CSS` with thumbnails, a real totals breakdown and address/method/payment cards, and `/orders/status` narrowed from `SELECT *` (it was handing the internal row id and `payment_reference` to anyone with an order number and an email) - previously: **New module: Square Payments for Shop** - `sqp_`-prefixed card-payment provider on Square's hosted checkout (Payment Links API) via `shop.payment-providers`; webhook HMAC-verified (signature covers notification URL + body) and status still re-fetched server-side before settling, refunds via Square's Refunds API with over-refund/currency re-validation; released v0.1.0 and pinned in modules.json - previously: **New module: Crezco Direct Bank Payments for Shop** - `czp_`-prefixed pay-by-bank provider on Crezco's Collect API via `shop.payment-providers`; unsigned Crezco webhooks are never trusted (status re-fetched server-side before settling), refunds are manual by design, webhook registration is API-driven from the settings panel; released v0.1.0 and pinned in modules.json - previously: **The confirmation page polls a settling payment to PAID** - `OrderConfirmationClient` re-reads `GET /orders/status` while `isSettling` (AWAITING_CONFIRMATION on a non-manual method): 5s for the first minute, then 15s, giving up at 5 minutes, skipping the request entirely on a hidden tab and taking one catch-up read on `visibilitychange`. Announcing the flip needs three new flags - `watched` (only the shopper who sat through the wait is told it cleared), `pollGaveUp`, and `basketCleared`, the last because a payment that fails AFTER settling began has already had its basket emptied, so the retry copy must point at the shop rather than an empty checkout - previously: **A failed open-banking payment now actually lands, and "awaiting confirmation" stops meaning two opposite things** - `markOrderPaymentFailed`'s default branch guarded on `payment_status = 'PENDING'`, but the GoCardless return route had already moved the order to `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`, so the failure webhook that followed matched no rows and the order sat in that queue for good; the guard is now `IN ('PENDING','AWAITING_CONFIRMATION')` (PAID still excluded, so a late failure can't undo a paid order). `GET /orders/status` returns `manualPayment` from the provider's own `confirmMode`, and the confirmation page splits the one AWAITING_CONFIRMATION message in two - manual keeps "we'll be in touch once it clears", automated gets "your payment has gone through, clearing usually takes a few minutes" - plus a FAILED branch that retitles the page, says nothing was charged and links back to checkout - previously: **Off-site payment methods redirect on Place order, not on selection** - `CheckoutPaymentClient` split `prepareIntent` (creates the pending order + provider intent, mounts Stripe Elements or shows manual instructions, NEVER navigates) from the `cactus-shop-place-order` handler, which is now the sole place that follows `approvalUrl`; a method restored from sessionStorage into a fresh mount re-prepares rather than confirming the abandoned order id (which parked it at AWAITING_CONFIRMATION and sent the shopper to the confirmation page unpaid), and the GoCardless provider's `confirmPayment` now rejects a billing request still at `pending` instead of reporting `success: true, pending: true` - previously: **Scroll sequences removed; video optimise gains multi-select** - the converter is gone in full (`ScrollSequence` block, `MediaSequenceDialog`, the Media › Scroll sequences tab, `convert-sequence`/`sequence-status`/`sequence-jobs`/`sequence-presets`/`webhooks/sequence`, `SEQUENCE_MIME`, the worker's whole `pipeline.py` matting stack); `services/sequence-worker` is now `services/video-worker`, `SiteConfig.sequenceConfig` is `mediaWorkerConfig` (Fly settings carried over by `prisma/core-reconcile/014_media_worker_config.sql`), and `SEQUENCE_WORKER_*`/`SEQUENCE_FLY_TOKEN` are read as fallbacks for the new `MEDIA_WORKER_*` names so no live install has to change its environment. The media library's selection bar gained **Optimise videos…**: one job per video, four started at a time, each on its own Fly machine, with a per-video progress list - previously: **Video optimise in the media library** - any video can be re-encoded in place to the one format every device plays (MP4/H.264 High/yuv420p/AAC/faststart) on the same worker the scroll sequences use; measured CRF ladder (23 = half the file at VMAF 96.4), only ever downscales, drops a silent audio track, writes an .mp4 back over its own key so every reference survives, and uploads nothing at all when it cannot beat the source by 5% - previously: **New FeatureVideo block** - a self-hosted video plays in normal flow beside a title and copy, rounded to the shop product-image radius (16px) and framed like it, lazily preloaded at 400px and played only while on screen; the media picker gained a video mode; Deskwell product descriptions move off scroll sequences onto it - previously: **Scroll sequences: unlimited parallel conversions** - the five-machine cap in `lib/media/fly-machines.ts` is gone, and with it the "fallback" that caused the bug: past the cap a job posted to the shared app URL with NO `fly-force-instance-id`, and Fly load-balances unrouted traffic across every machine carrying the app's service config - the job machines included - so the enqueue landed on one machine and the status polls on another, which 404'd and reported "The conversion service restarted and lost this job." `createJobMachine` now always returns a machine id (or throws); the optional `SEQUENCE_MAX_JOB_MACHINES` env var puts a lid back on for spend, refusing rather than misrouting. Boot wait cut 45s -> 35s and enqueue retries raised 6x2.5s -> 8x2s to keep the whole enqueue inside the route's 60s ceiling when several machines boot at once (a route that times out strands a live machine). `sequence-status` no longer fails a job on a bare 404: with a machine id it asks Fly whether that machine is still up first, and reports 'running' if it is. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequences: rembg premultiplies its cut-out** - the defect under the mesh-on-black complaint. `rembg.remove` composites onto transparent BLACK, so it multiplies the COLOUR channels by the mask as well as alpha, and the worker has been writing premultiplied colour into a straight-alpha WebP since day one (measured RGB/source = 0.217/0.484/0.995 at alpha 0.22/0.50/1.00) - every soft pixel darkened twice, and the un-blend fed `a*C` instead of `C`, which is what blotched the defocused Chiro backrest. `_matte_to_webp` is now one ordered pass: straighten -> colour-implied alpha floor -> coverage -> un-blend by THAT coverage -> optional alpha cut, replacing the two passes that each had their own idea of alpha. Un-blend no longer divides by matte alpha, which structurally fixes the flashing (swing 8.66 -> 3.24 -> **1.04**). Key re-gated on the neighbourhood MEAN, since brightness cannot separate cream fabric (L~185) from mesh holes (L~215). birefnet measured as the WRONG engine for mesh (97.6% opaque vs isnet 78.6%); admin copy and wiki corrected. Both of the user's clips verified end to end over black and white. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequences: see-through gaps moved to the convert dialog** - it is now a PER-VIDEO checkbox in `MediaSequenceDialog` (`useState(false)`, never carries over) sent on the convert-sequence POST body and read as `body?.seeThrough === true`, not a stored setting: whether keying the white sweep out of holes helps depends on the product in the clip, not on the site. Dropped from `SettingsSchema`, the `sequence-presets` PUT and the Scroll sequences tab; a stored key from v0.5.861 is stripped by the zod parse, no migration. Engine/fps/maxWidth stay server-side only. Worker unchanged - it already took `seeThrough` per job. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequences: see-through gaps; mesh flashing root-caused** - rembg returns a silhouette, so mesh backs come back ~0.95 alpha when they are half holes and the white sweep stays baked into every hole; `_unblend_white` is the identity there and could never fix it. The flashing was the un-blend faithfully amplifying that wrong alpha: composited over a page of luminance `bg` an un-blended pixel is `C - (1-a)*(255-bg)`, a flat offset on every pixel, so a per-frame alpha wobble shifts a whole region together instead of cancelling (measured 8.66 levels of swing vs 4.33 with no un-blend; a gain cap does not help since mesh alpha is high). New `_key_white_gaps` derives coverage from the frame's own colour (`(255-L)/(255-L_localmin)`, two ramps guarding flat pale surfaces and dark textured fabric), run before the un-blend: swing drops to 3.26 and the holes show the page colour. DEFAULT OFF - a specular on dark gloss keys away too - exposed as a **See-through gaps** checkbox under Media > Scroll sequences and plumbed `SettingsSchema.seeThrough` -> enqueue -> worker `JobSpec.see_through`. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequence block: text beside the animation** - new `textSide` (above/left/right) lays in-screen copy alongside the canvas inside the shared faded stage, so copy and animation fade together on every viewport (a sibling Grid column could not); collapses to stacked on mobile; both cells pinned to grid row 1 so a right-side copy does not bump the canvas to a second row; default scroll length now 1 screen. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequence block: in-screen title/text** - ScrollSequence gains optional `title`/`body` rendered inside the pinned full-screen stage (copy top, canvas sized to the leftover height so both always share the screen) plus `topOffset` clearance for sticky headers that shifts and, where needed, shrinks the whole pinned stage (canvas included); renders without text or clearance are unchanged. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequences: mesh-friendly cut-outs + engine choice** - two fixes for mesh-backed products. (1) The worker's `_matte_to_webp` now runs `_unblend_white` (new `WHITE_UNBLEND` env, default on): rembg keeps the original white-contaminated colour in semi-transparent pixels, which composited as a milky grey haze over any non-white page; since the studio sweep is always white the true foreground colour is exactly recoverable, so the pass is identity over white and strictly better elsewhere. (2) The `birefnet` engine is re-enabled worker-side (`ENGINE_MODELS`) and core-side (`SEQUENCE_ENGINES = ['isnet','birefnet']`): the old ban existed because it OOM-killed a 3.8 GB OVH box shared with Postgres, but per-job Fly machines clone a 16 GB performance template. Both models are now pre-baked into the worker Docker image (fresh rootfs per job machine would otherwise re-download ~930 MB per conversion). Admin: Media > Scroll sequences gains a "Cut-out quality" select (Standard = isnet / Detailed = birefnet), saved via `sequence-presets` PUT (`engine` optional in the schema, absent = keep stored); the convert dialog's summary line now names the quality. `enqueueSequenceJob`'s `engine` type widened. Worker changes live in services/sequence-worker (own repo, needs deploy + image rebuild before they bite). tsc + eslint clean, sequence tests 17/17 - previously: **Scroll sequence conversions: optional start/end trim** - the convert dialog gains optional Start/End time fields (`90` / `1:30` / `0:01:30`), route re-validates and forwards `trimStart`/`trimEnd` seconds, and the sequence worker applies output-side `-ss`/`-to` so only that window is sequenced; worker change lives in its own repo and needs deploying before the fields bite. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Scroll sequence notifications: real progress, right button** - `upsertSequenceNotification` was rounding the worker's 0-1 fraction as if it were a percentage, so every conversion sat at 0% and finished at "1%"; it now renders `round(progress*100)%`. The notification also carried `link:'/media'` with no `actionLabel`, so it inherited the `message` type's **"View Messages"** button - nonsense on a conversion, and a no-op when you were already on Media. In-flight jobs now have `link:null` (no button) and draw a live bar via the new `components/admin/SequenceProgress.tsx`, which polls `sequence-status` every 5s and so keeps the stored progress moving even with the convert dialog closed; on completion the webhook passes the tile's `folderId` and the button becomes **Open media folder** → `/media?folder=<id>`. Supporting changes: `upsertAlert` gains three-state `link`/`actionLabel` (omitted = keep) and `resurfaceOnTitleChangeOnly` so progress ticks don't re-light the bell; pure parsers extracted to `lib/media/sequence-notification.ts` (client-safe) and shared by the bell, the notifications page and `sequence-jobs.ts`; the notifications page now selects and honours `actionLabel` at all (it never did). tsc + eslint clean, alerts tests 12/12 - previously: **Specification groups: WebKit column-break gap fixed (product-attributes-for-shop 0.1.43)** - the 16px rhythm moved off `.pat-spec-group`'s margin onto a new `.pat-spec-item` wrapper's padding: a margin at a column break is dangling and WebKit carries it to the top of the next column, so column three's first group sat 16px low in Safari while Chromium showed nothing wrong. Measured in `playwright.webkit` against the live page, six desktop widths, before and after. tsc + eslint clean - previously: **Specification groups: multi-column fill + auto-sort + proper Your choice pill** - product-attributes-for-shop's `SpecificationPanel` swaps its grid for CSS multi-columns so no whitespace sits under short groups; a new **Auto-sort specification groups** field on shop's Product: Sections block orders groups tallest-first via a new optional `autoSort` hint on `ShopDetailSpecPanelProps`; the chosen-variation markers (subtle pill + sentence banner, per-row left border) are replaced by the same solid Your choice pill the gallery stage wears. tsc + eslint clean; needs shop + product-attributes releases - previously: **Scroll sequences: presets replaced by one high-quality setting; conversions get per-job Fly.io machines** - the Fast/High-quality choice is gone: every conversion runs the single settings object (30 fps / 1920px defaults) tuned under Media → Scroll sequences. New pure `shop-variations/lib/rename-repoint.ts` (`repointOnRename`, 11 unit tests) decides the move: adopt the source value the new label names (taking its swatch only where the stored one was the old link's or absent, so a hand-set colour survives), or cut the link entirely when the new label matches nothing in the source, matches two things, or belongs to a sibling copy already. `updateOptionValue` grows a `sourceRef` field; `csv.ts`'s rename pass now carries each value's swatch/ref and applies the decision in the same write as the rename. `009_repoint_renamed_option_values.sql` repairs the copies already written (20 rows on deskwell: 8 leg finishes, 2 Beech, 1 Iris fabric, 9 Width links), skipping anything ambiguous; guarded on `to_regclass` + `EXECUTE` so it is a no-op without shop-variations, and verified idempotent on a throwaway VPS database. Previous entry follows.) (**"High quality" scroll-sequence preset was OOM-killing the worker every job; birefnet removed, worker cap raised (core + sequence-worker repo)**: every conversion failed with "The conversion service restarted and lost this job." Root cause on the OVH box (shared with live Postgres): the `quality` preset ran the **birefnet** engine, which needs **3 GB+ of RAM even on a 640px frame** (it does not downscale internally the way isnet does), so the kernel OOM-killed the `MemoryMax=2G` unit mid-matte; systemd restarted it, the in-memory job vanished, `GET /jobs/{id}` 404'd, and the status route flipped the job to Failed. (A separate earlier fix had already defaulted `ALPHA_MATTING_MODE` off - matting is a second, smaller memory hog - but birefnet alone still blew the cap.) Fix, core: `lib/media/sequence-presets.ts` drops `birefnet` from `SEQUENCE_ENGINES` (now `['isnet']`) and the `quality` default engine becomes `isnet` (still fps 30 / maxWidth 1920); removing the enum value **self-heals any stored `sequenceConfig` that still names birefnet** - `parseSequenceConfig`'s `safeParse` rejects it and falls back to the isnet defaults, so no DB edit is needed. The engine picker is gone from `SequenceSettingsPanel.tsx` (only one engine now; `type Engine = 'isnet'`), `MediaSequenceDialog.tsx`'s preset summary drops the engine phrase (`describePreset` = fps + width), and the quality blurb now reads "more frames + wider image" (its real difference) rather than "sharper edges" (birefnet's). `MediaTabs.tsx` + `lib/media/sequence.ts` `Engine` unions narrowed to `'isnet'`. Fix, worker (`services/sequence-worker`, own repo, deployed to the box): `app.py` `ENGINE_MODELS` drops birefnet so a birefnet request returns a clean **400** instead of taking the box down; `sequence-worker.service` `MemoryMax` **2G -> 2.5G** (isnet peaks ~1.85 GB in the long-running process as onnxruntime holds its arena; the cap still leaves ~1.3 GB for DB+OS and keeps this service the kernel's OOM victim if anything ever exceeds it). **Verified on the box:** two full 1920px isnet jobs ran start-to-finish (0->100%, frames+manifest uploaded to B2), RSS flat at ~1.85 GB, no OOM; a birefnet POST returns 400. isnet is model-bound (~constant RAM 1280-1920px, resizes internally to 1024²), so lowering width would not have bought headroom - the cap bump was the lever. tsc + eslint clean. Core needs a patch bump + release; worker already committed/pushed (`cactus-sequence-worker`) and live on the box. Previous entry follows.) (**Scroll-sequence Recent jobs: manual Refresh + live worker poll + orphaned-job auto-fail (core, working tree)**: `app/cactus-admin/media/SequenceSettingsPanel.tsx` gains a **Refresh** button in the Recent jobs header. Root fix: a job's notification only advances via the convert dialog (while open) or the worker's final done/error callback, so a job whose dialog was closed froze at its last-seen % and both the button and the 8s poller (which only re-read `/api/admin/media/sequence-jobs`) showed nothing new. `loadJobs` now, for every job still `queued`/`running` (tracked via a `jobsRef`), first pokes `/api/admin/media/sequence-status?jobId=…` (best-effort, `cache:'no-store'`) - which proxies the worker's live progress and rewrites the notification - then re-reads the list; the button and the poller share it. Second fix: the worker keeps jobs in memory only, so a restart makes it answer **404 `job not found`** for an in-flight job forever, stranding it at "Building 0%". `lib/media/sequence.ts` `SequenceWorkerError` now carries the response `status` (constructor 2nd arg; `getSequenceJob` passes `res.status`), and `app/api/admin/media/sequence-status/route.ts` on a 404 marks the notification `error` ("The conversion service restarted and lost this job. Convert the video again.") and returns `{status:'error'}` instead of a bare 502 - so the next Refresh auto-flips a stranded job to Failed rather than leaving it stuck. (**Scroll sequence Puck block (core, working tree)**: new core Puck block "Scroll sequence" (Media category) that plays a converted sequence as a scroll-scrubbed animation. `lib/puck/components/ScrollSequence.tsx` ('use client'): fetches the manifest, preloads frames (deferred via an IntersectionObserver near-viewport gate), draws to a `<canvas>` sized to the frame aspect (transparent, so it sits on any light/dark page background); scroll-scrubs the frame index across a sticky spacer (height = `(1 + scrubScreens) * 100vh`), loops at the end via rAF at the manifest fps, and fades opacity on enter/exit via an IntersectionObserver ratio; the editor path shows a static poster (never scrolljacks the builder), and a failed manifest degrades to the poster/message. `lib/puck/config.tsx`: `ScrollSequence` registered in `puckConfig.components` + the `media` category; fields sequenceUrl/scrubScreens/loop/fade/maxWidth/ariaLabel; the render only hands props to the client component (editor-safe, and the RSC/published path reuses it via `getModuleLayoutSharedParts`, so no config.rsc.tsx change — it therefore appears in the shop product-description editor, which is core shared-categories only). `lib/puck/MediaPickerField.tsx`: `MediaPickerModal` gains `kind: 'image' | 'sequence'` (sequence mode filters by `isSequenceType`, fetches `type=other` then narrows, hides the upload control, shows poster thumbnails); new `SequenceUrlPickerField` + `SEQUENCE_PICKER_FIELDS`, both wired through the existing `withImagePickerFields` (now swaps image AND sequence fields), so the block's `sequenceUrl` field becomes a sequence picker that stores the picked item's manifest url. No schema change (no backup gate). tsc + eslint clean, 1273 tests pass. **The verify-email page no longer looks like you can change your address there** - it always drew an editable email box, seeded from `?email=`, which reads as "fix your typo here"; it never was that. The box only ever fed `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend`, which re-sends to an address that is already `PENDING_VERIFICATION` and answers `{ok:true}` to everything else, so a corrected address got the same 60s countdown and no email. `page.tsx` is now a server component reading `membersConfig`, and the client half moved to `components/members/VerifyEmailPanel.tsx`: with a valid-looking `?email=` it prints the address as text with a "Send it again" button, and only the paramless case (bookmarked/stale link) still asks for one. Sending now says so - the wording promises nothing about whether that address is registered, keeping the page as enumeration-safe as the endpoint. A mistyped address is unrecoverable by design, so the panel offers a "sign up again" link to `/{memberAreaPath}/register`, passed in only when `enabled && registrationMode !== 'INVITE_ONLY'` - an invite-only site would be offering a door needing a key the visitor hasn't got. `?email=` is checked against a basic address shape before being rendered, so a crafted link can't put arbitrary wording on the page under the site's name. No schema change (no backup gate). **A verified email now lands in the member area, not on the verify page** - `VerifyEmailPanel` takes a new required `accountHref` prop (`/{memberAreaPath}`, from the page) and on success stores the wording via `setMemberFlash()` then `router.replace(accountHref)` instead of rendering it as an inline `alert-success`; the account layout's gate hands a signed-out visitor straight on to `login?redirect=…`, which is where the message is wanted anyway. New `lib/members/flash.ts` (+ `flash.test.ts`, jsdom) is a one-shot sessionStorage hand-off - `setMemberFlash()` / `takeMemberFlash()`, read once then cleared, validated and capped at 300 chars on the way out, every storage access wrapped in try/catch for private-browsing setups. New client `components/members/account/AccountFlash.tsx` renders it as a fixed pill at the top of the viewport (`.member-flash*` in `globals.css`, `z-index: 9990` - above a sticky menu at 100/101, below the consent banner at 9998/9999), auto-dismissed after 9s with a manual close. It is mounted on **both** sides of the account layout's gate and its take effect is keyed on `usePathname()`, not mount: verify-email and login both render the layout's signed-out branch, so the component keeps its slot across that navigation and a mount-only effect would never look again. `VerifyEmailPanel` also gained a `submitted` ref so the one-shot token is POSTed once even though the effect now depends on `router`/`accountHref`.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The shop's post-purchase prompt now carries the registration form, not a link to it** - `RegisterForm` gains two optional props: `showHeading` (default `true`; embedded uses already sit under a heading of their own, so its `<h1>Create an account</h1>` would be the second one on screen) and `verifyEmailUrl` (default keeps the old `window.location.pathname.replace(/\/register$/, '/verify-email')` derivation, which only ever worked on the register page - an embedded form reloaded its own URL with `?email=` on it instead). Shop's `GET /api/m/shop/public/orders/status` widens `accountPrompt` from `{registerUrl}` to also carry `verifyEmailUrl`, `registrationMode`, `collectUsername`, `collectDisplayName` and `privacyPolicyUrl` - read from `getMembersConfig()` plus a `SiteConfig.privacyPolicyPageId` → `InfoPage.slug` lookup, the same sources the register page reads, so an owner who drops the username picker doesn't find it back again on the confirmation. `OrderConfirmationClient` renders `<RegisterForm>` inside `.soc-account` in place of the `soc-btn` anchor, falling back to that anchor when `registrationMode` is absent (an older cached bundle answers with `registerUrl` alone). Two CSS rules added to `ORDER_CONFIRMATION_CSS`: `.soc-account form{margin:0}` and `.soc-account form p.field-hint{color:var(--color-text-muted)}`, the latter undoing the box's own `p` colour rule. The form styles itself with core's global `.field` / `.btn` / `.alert` classes. Shop 0.1.179 raises `requiresCoreVersion` from `0.5.571` to `0.5.885`, the core release carrying the two `RegisterForm` props - without them an older core ignores both and the box gets a second "Create an account" heading plus a redirect back onto itself. No schema change (no backup gate).)

Also 2026-08-03 (**New `MembersSignIn` Puck block, label "Members: Sign In"** - one click-to-sign-in control for headers and pages, modelled deliberately on the shop's `ShopCartSummary` cart widget so the pair look like siblings. Icon (person / person-in-circle / padlock / key / door-arrow / none) + optional label, bordered/filled/plain box with colour and radius knobs; `clickAction` either links to `<memberArea>/login?redirect=…` or opens `components/members/SignInModal.tsx` over the page, hosting the real `LoginForm` (lazily imported, `ssr:false`). Signed-in state is an account link, an account link plus sign-out, or nothing, optionally showing the member's own avatar. `audience: 'admin'` is the shop cart's try-it-live gate, reproduced: withheld from the public, rendered only for a signed-in site admin. **The field is `audience`, never `visibility`** - core injects a same-named responsive-visibility field into every block and strips it from render props. Editor half + block def in `lib/puck/config.tsx` (`MembersSignInBlock`, always the signed-out preview, modal inert), server half `MembersSignInRsc` in `lib/puck/components/MembersBlocksRsc.tsx`, RSC overrides in `config.rsc.tsx` for the page/layout/header configs. `LoginForm` gained optional `showHeading` and `basePath` so the modal can drop the form's own `<h1>` and keep its `verify-email` / SMS-enrolment detours absolute; the sign-in page passes neither and is unchanged.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Notifications can be cleared in one go, from either place they appear** - the collection route `/api/admin/notifications` gains `PATCH {read: boolean}` (bulk `updateMany`: true stamps `readAt` on every unread row, false clears every read one) and `DELETE` (bulk `deleteMany({})`), both still behind `config.manage`. They deliberately act on the whole table rather than the slice the caller is holding - the page renders 100 rows and the bell 20, so a "mark all as read" scoped to what was on screen would leave the badge stubbornly non-zero. New `app/cactus-admin/notifications/NotificationBulkActions.tsx` puts "Mark all as read" (disabled at zero unread) and "Delete all" beside the total in the page header; the bell dropdown carries the same pair as quiet text buttons in its header (`.admin-bell-dropdown-headaction`), sharing the existing per-item loading/error maps under a `__bulk__` sentinel key. **`DELETE` deliberately spares open deployment notifications** (`{type: 'deployment', deployInitiatedAt: null}`, excluded via `NOT`): everything else is re-derivable - a video-optimise job still encoding rewrites its notification on the next progress tick and the update alerts are re-raised by the next check, all keyed by `dedupeKey` - but nothing re-creates the open deployment record, so deleting it would leave the site serving saved-but-unshipped config with no reminder and no Redeploy now button. It returns `{deleted, kept}`; both UIs disable Delete all when only the spared row is left, and both confirms say the pending changes are kept. The page's confirm names `total - pendingDeploy` (a fourth `count()` in its existing `Promise.all`), which can still be larger than the hundred rows rendered; the bell re-reads via `fetchNotifications()` after a delete rather than assuming an empty list, since the survivor may sit outside its twenty rows and still counts towards the badge.)

Flat factual inventory of the platform's routes, models, permissions, modules, env vars, components, scripts, and config - the current state, not a changelog. Per-release history lives in git and the GitHub releases. Update the affected sections plus this date after any substantive change.

---

## Core Application

### Routes

Pages (public):

- `/` - `app/(public)/page.tsx` - redirects to `/setup` until setup completes; renders the InfoPage set as `homepageId` (draft only for admins, with draft banner), else a welcome card with siteName/tagline/description. `force-dynamic`.
- `/[slug]` - `app/(public)/[slug]/page.tsx` - renders an InfoPage by slug; drafts 404 for non-admins; `generateMetadata` (title, metaDescription, OG image), `generateStaticParams` for published slugs, `revalidate = false`. On an InfoPage miss, falls back to a module's public index via `resolveModulePublicPage(slug, [])` (InfoPage always wins a collision) - calls `getSessionFromCookie()` first so that fallback path always renders dynamically rather than being cached under `revalidate = false`.
- `/[slug]/[...path]` - `app/(public)/[slug]/[...path]/page.tsx` - generic catch-all for a module's public sub-pages, via `resolveModulePublicPage`. `force-dynamic`.
- `/[slug]/feed.xml` - `app/(public)/[slug]/feed.xml/route.ts` - delegates to a module's `feed.xml` route via `dispatchModulePublicRoute`; a dedicated literal segment because `route.ts` can't share a folder with the `[...path]` page catch-all. `force-dynamic`.
- `/[slug]/[a]/feed.xml`, `/[slug]/[a]/[b]/feed.xml` - `app/(public)/[slug]/[a]/feed.xml/route.ts`, `app/(public)/[slug]/[a]/[b]/feed.xml/route.ts` - generic nested-feed delegates (Boards' per-board and per-sub-board RSS), same passthrough pattern one and two segments deeper. `force-dynamic`.
- `/logged-out` - `app/(public)/logged-out/page.tsx` - client page, 3-second countdown then redirect to `/`.
- `/page-preview/[id]` - `app/(public)/page-preview/[id]/page.tsx` - draft preview of an InfoPage; requires session + `pages.read`; always renders `builderData` with a fixed preview bar; noindex.
- `/layout-preview/[id]` - `app/layout-preview/[id]/page.tsx` - preview of a Layout; requires `layouts.manage` (was `isAdmin`, i.e. the protected role only - so the Preview button 404'd for every non-Admin role that had been granted layouts.manage); renders with the type-matched Puck RSC config plus placeholder content blocks; noindex. Outside the `(public)` group so header/footer are not applied.
- `app/(public)/layout.tsx` - public shell: resolves header/footer Layouts via `resolveThemeLayout`, injects design-token CSS + Google Fonts link, `AosInit`, `ConsentBanner` when enabled, favicon override from `faviconMediaId` (plus a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` icon from `faviconDarkMediaId` when set), and threads `logoDarkUrl` into the header/footer template context for the dark-mode logo swap.
- `app/layout.tsx` - root layout: Instrument Sans + JetBrains Mono fonts, theme flash-prevention inline script (`localStorage cactus-theme` → `data-theme` attribute), consent-init inline script (`cactus-consent` cookie → `window.__cactusConsent`, deny-by-default). Now uses `generateMetadata`/`generateViewport` (not a static `metadata` export) reading `resolveBranding()` (`lib/config/branding.ts`, React-`cache()`d) so the site's icons + app name + theme colour apply on EVERY route (fixing the default-cactus-favicon fallback); a custom favicon fully replaces the cactus svg/png/ico set (+ optional dark variant via `prefers-color-scheme`). The web-app manifest is generated dynamically by `app/manifest.ts` (`force-dynamic`, reads `resolveBranding`, served at `/manifest.webmanifest`); the old static `public/site.webmanifest` was removed.
- `app/not-found.tsx` - 404 page; renders the resolved `notFound` Layout via Puck if published, else a plain 404 card. `force-dynamic`.
- `app/robots.ts` - dynamic robots.txt; disallow-all when no site URL, `hideFromCrawlers`, or status ≠ live; else allow with disallows for `/cactus-admin/`, `/setup/`, `/cactus-status/`, `/api/`.
- `app/sitemap.ts` - site URL root plus all published InfoPage slugs.

Pages (status screens, reached only by proxy rewrite):

- `/cactus-status/coming-soon` - `statusPage` Layout (ctx `siteStatus: 'coming_soon'`) or fallback card. `force-dynamic`, noindex.
- `/cactus-status/maintenance` - same with `maintenance`; fallback "Down for maintenance" card.

Pages (setup):

- `/setup` - `app/setup/page.tsx` - client wizard, three steps: `connect` (Vercel token + project selection via `/api/setup/vercel-connect`), `database` (sub-states for Vercel bootstrap, Neon auto-provision, existing-project reuse, manual DATABASE_URL, local mode), `configure` (admin account + passkey or TOTP, admin path, site essentials, optional env vars, complete). Polls `/api/health` and `/api/setup/env-check` across the redeploys it triggers.
- `app/setup/layout.tsx` - `setup-shell` wrapper, noindex, absolute title.

Pages (member area, live under internal `/cactus-account/*`, reached only via the rewritten `/<memberAreaPath>/*` - Phases 1-3 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md):

- `/{memberAreaPath}/register` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/register/page.tsx` - server component: 404-styled message when `membersConfig.enabled` is false; in `INVITE_ONLY` mode, validates `?invite=` server-side and shows an "invite-only" message instead of the form when missing/invalid; otherwise renders `RegisterForm` with the resolved privacy-policy page link, the `collectUsername`/`collectDisplayName` flags and `passwordPolicy` (`authMethodPolicy(config,'PASSWORD')`) from `membersConfig` (the Puck `MembersRegister` block passes the same three; its editor preview keeps the defaults, as it already does for `registrationMode`). `RegisterForm` shows a password field whenever that policy is not `OFF`, marked required at `REQUIRED` - left the prop undefined it fetches `/api/members/auth/config` itself and treats a failed lookup as `OFF`, so the editor preview and any embedded copy show what the live page shows without being told. Also reads `?email=` and passes it as `initialEmail` (a starting value for the field only - still editable, still verified; shop's post-purchase account prompt links here with it so the customer signs up under the address their guest order was placed with).
- `/{memberAreaPath}/setup-signin` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/setup-signin/page.tsx` + `components/members/account/RequiredSignInSetup.tsx` - where the account layout's required-setup gate sends a member, and the only member-area page that gate lets through. Session-gated like the rest; redirects back to `/{memberAreaPath}` for anyone who bookmarks it with nothing outstanding. The client component works its own outstanding list out from live status (`GET /api/members/passkeys` + `GET /api/members/password`) rather than a server snapshot, so finishing one step updates the page without a reload: "add a passkey" (same WebAuthn calls as `SecuritySection`), "set a password", and - only once a password exists - a second step via `2fa/setup-options`+`setup-verify`, offering email codes when `isEmailConfigured()` and always the authenticator app (TOTP needs no delivery, so a site with no mail can still satisfy a required password). First-time recovery codes are shown before a manual "Continue to your account" button rather than an automatic bounce, since they are shown once. A "Sign out" escape hatch is offered throughout, for the member whose device cannot do what the site asks.
- `/{memberAreaPath}/verify-email` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/verify-email/page.tsx` - server component: reads `membersConfig` and passes `registerHref` (`/{memberAreaPath}/register`) to `VerifyEmailPanel` only when `enabled && registrationMode !== 'INVITE_ONLY'`, plus the always-present `accountHref` (`/{memberAreaPath}`); all behaviour lives in the panel.
- `components/members/VerifyEmailPanel.tsx` - client half of the above (wrapped in `Suspense` for `useSearchParams`); with a `?token=`, POSTs it (once - a `submitted` ref, since the effect depends on `router`/`accountHref` and a spent token answers "invalid or has expired"). On success it puts the wording (branching on the response: "Your email is verified and you are signed in. Welcome." when `signedIn`, the awaiting-approval variant on `PENDING_APPROVAL`, "You can now sign in." otherwise) into the session-storage flash and `router.replace(accountHref)`s, so the news arrives as a pill on the member area (or the sign-in page its gate hands them to) rather than as an inline alert on a page whose only remaining purpose is to be left; the panel keeps a muted "Taking you to your account…" line with a plain link, for a browser that doesn't move. Failures still render here, with the resend form. The resend half branches on `?email=`: a value matching a basic address shape is shown as text with a "Send it again" button (no input - the box implied a typo could be corrected here, which the resend endpoint cannot do), anything else (missing, or not address-shaped, so a crafted link can't print arbitrary wording under the site's name) falls back to the labelled email field. 60s client-side countdown mirrors the server throttle, and **starts at 60 on arrival whenever `?email=` is present**: a link was just sent, `canResendVerification()` refuses another within 60s of the last token, and it refuses in silence (it must - "too soon" is only knowable for an address genuinely awaiting verification), so a button offered immediately reported success and sent nothing. That was the whole of "I clicked resend and still got no email" on the live Deskwell site: seven POSTs to the resend route, one verification token, all clicks inside the throttle window. The post-send confirmation is worded to promise nothing about whether the address is registered, keeping the page as enumeration-safe as `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend`. When `registerHref` is set, a "typed your address wrong? sign up again" link - the only actual fix for a mistyped sign-up.
- `/{memberAreaPath}/login` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/login/page.tsx` - server component reading `redirect`/`magic_token` straight from `searchParams` (no client `useSearchParams`, so no Suspense boundary needed); sanitises `redirect` via the shared `sanitizeRedirect` in `lib/auth/redirect.ts` (an earlier inline copy omitted the `/\` backslash guard, so `/\evil.com` normalised to `//evil.com` post-login) **with `/{memberAreaPath}` as the fallback, not `/`** - a magic-link email carries only `?magic_token=`, so the default fallback landed every link sign-in on the homepage. A sanitised target that is itself a signed-out member page (`isPublicMemberPath()`) is dropped for `/{memberAreaPath}` - signing in to land back on the sign-in page is a loop. Renders `LoginForm`.
- `components/members/RegisterForm.tsx` - client form: email/username/display name (email seeded from the optional `initialEmail` prop), privacy-policy consent checkbox, optional `TurnstileWidget`, submits to `POST /api/members/register`; redirects to `verify-email?email=…` when verification is required, else shows the final status inline (PENDING_APPROVAL vs ACTIVE copy). Optional `showHeading` (default true) drops its own `<h1>` for embedded uses, and optional `verifyEmailUrl` names the verify-email destination outright instead of deriving it from the current path - both used by shop's post-purchase prompt, which renders this form inside the order confirmation.
- `components/members/LoginForm.tsx` - client form, identifier-first: step one is the email field and a "Continue" button and nothing else; Continue POSTs `/api/members/auth/methods` and step two offers only what that address can use - passkey if they have one, "sign in with a password" if they have one, "email me a sign-in link" whenever the site allows it, with the first of those as the primary button and a "use a different email address" link back. A member with neither a password nor a passkey has nothing to choose between, so step two is skipped altogether: Continue sends the sign-in link itself (`handleMagicLink(address)`, address passed explicitly since `setEmail` has not landed) and goes straight to the "check your inbox" screen, which carries its own "use a different email address" link back. A failed lookup (network blip, non-200) falls back to every method `GET /api/members/auth/config` says the site allows, so a passkey holder is never left without the button. The email is trimmed once on Continue and shown read-only from then on (with `autoComplete="username"`, so password managers still match the saved credential). Auto-consumes a `?magic_token=` on mount; either path redirects to `verify-email` on a `redirectToVerify` rejection, else to the sanitised `redirectTo`. Optional `showHeading` (default true) drops its own `<h1>` for embedded uses, and optional `basePath` ("/account") makes its two internal detours - the `verify-email` redirect and the SMS-enrolment landing - absolute instead of relative to the current URL; both used by `SignInModal`, which floats this form over an arbitrary page where a relative `verify-email` would resolve against that page. The sign-in page passes neither, so its behaviour is byte-identical to before.
- `components/members/SignInWidgetClient.tsx` - client island behind the `MembersSignIn` Puck block. Owns the look (icon set, label, bordered/filled/plain box, colours, radius), the click behaviour (anchor to `<memberArea>/login?redirect=…`, or a button that lazily imports `SignInModal`), and the signed-in variant (account link, optional sign-out `<form method="POST">` to `/api/members/auth/logout`, optional `MemberAvatar` in place of the icon). Hides itself on the sign-in page via `usePathname`, and resolves a blank `redirectTo` to the current path. Exports `SignInWidgetOptions`, `SignInWidgetState`, `SIGN_IN_WIDGET_DEFAULTS`. Session state and the `audience` gate are decided server-side (`MembersSignInRsc`), never here - this island is trivially inspectable, so it can't be a security boundary. Icon-only renders (blank `label`, or blank `signedInLabel` on the signed-in face - the shape a header uses) also emit the shared hover/focus tooltip: `className="member-signin-trigger"` on the anchor/button plus an `aria-hidden` `.member-signin-tip` span naming it ("Sign in" / "My account"), styled in `app/globals.css` to match `.theme-toggle-tip` but hanging below the icon. Skipped entirely when a text label is set, and the sign-out button never gets one.
- `components/members/SignInModal.tsx` - the sign-in panel `SignInWidgetClient` opens in modal mode. `createPortal` to `document.body` (a header is very often a positioned/overflow-clipped stacking context), `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, escape to close, tab trap, body scroll lock, focus to the close button on open, backdrop click closes. Hosts the real `LoginForm` (with `showHeading={false}` and `basePath`), plus an optional sign-up link. Reached only through `next/dynamic` `ssr:false` from the widget, so `LoginForm` and `@simplewebauthn/browser` stay out of the bundle of every page that merely shows a sign-in button.
- `components/members/TurnstileWidget.tsx` - loads the Cloudflare Turnstile script on demand and renders/tears down a widget instance; reads/writes `window.turnstile` via a local type cast rather than a global `Window` augmentation, because `modules/gazette`'s comment form already augments `Window.turnstile` with a narrower shape and TypeScript requires merged global augmentations to match exactly - core must not depend on or collide with an optional module's globals.
- `components/members/account/AccountFlash.tsx` + `lib/members/flash.ts` (`flash.test.ts`, jsdom) - one-shot message handed from one member-area page to the next and shown as a fixed pill at the top of the viewport (`.member-flash*`, `globals.css`, `z-index: 9990`, auto-dismissed after 9s, manual close, `role="status"`). Session storage rather than a query string because the account gate folds the URL it was given into `?redirect=`, so a flag on the URL arrives buried inside another parameter; taken (read then cleared) so a refresh doesn't replay it, validated and capped at 300 chars, every storage access in a try/catch for private-browsing setups. The take effect is keyed on `usePathname()`, not mount: the layout is shared by every member-area page, so verify-email → login leaves the component in the same slot and a mount-only effect would never look again. Only used by email verification so far.
- `/{memberAreaPath}` + 5 sections (`app/(public)/cactus-account/{layout.tsx,page.tsx,profile,security,notifications,activity,danger-zone}`) - session-gated (redirects to `login?redirect=…` otherwise); `layout.tsx` wraps **every** member-area page including `login`/`register`/`verify-email`, so its gate excepts those three via `isPublicMemberPath()` from `lib/members/paths.ts` and renders them bare (no nav, no banner) - without the exception the gate sent `/login` to `/login` and folded the whole previous URL into the next one's `?redirect=` on every hop, growing it exponentially until the browser refused to load it (the shop's post-purchase "Create an account" link into `/{memberAreaPath}/register?email=…` hit this). A missing `x-cactus-member-full-path` header falls through to the gate, which is one safe hop. A second gate sits below the session one: `memberOutstandingAuthSetup()` redirects to `/{memberAreaPath}/setup-signin` while any sign-in method the site marks `REQUIRED` is still unset, so "required" is enforced rather than suggested; it skips the redirect entirely when that header is absent, since a redirect on an unidentifiable path would point the setup page at itself (proxy.ts 404s direct `/cactus-account` hits, so the header is always there in practice), and the check short-circuits with no query at all when nothing is required. `layout.tsx` mounts `AccountFlash.tsx` on **both** sides of that gate - the pill it shows is usually the news that got the visitor bounced through it. `layout.tsx` also shows a cancellable deletion-grace banner and the `AccountNav.tsx` tab bar (reuses `components/admin/TabStrip.tsx`), filtered by `membersConfig.accountSectionsEnabled`. Overview (`page.tsx`) is a dashboard, not a signpost: avatar + display name + email + "member since", an unverified-email nag with a resend button (`VerifyEmailNudge.tsx` -> `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend`), and four summary cards (Sign-in & security: passkey count / password set / 2FA on / active session count; Profile: which fields are still blank; Notifications; Recent activity: last 3 `MemberActivityEvent` rows) gathered in one `Promise.all`, each card filtered by the same `accountSectionsEnabled` flags as the tab bar. It also renders any `members.account-section` extension-point contributions (content-injection only, not a new nav tab). Two seams let a module live inside the account rather than beside it: **`members.account-nav`** (`lib/members/account-nav.ts`, `getMemberAccountNavExtras()`) collects `{key,label,href,badge?}` tabs from installed modules' manifests - a provider that throws is dropped rather than locking a member out of their own security settings - and **`components/members/account/MemberAccountShell.tsx`** is the chrome (container, flash, deletion banner, `notice` slot, tab bar) extracted out of `layout.tsx` so a module's own member pages, which are outside this route group and never see this layout, can wear the identical thing. `AccountNav.tsx` matches Overview exactly and every other tab by prefix, so a module's detail page (`/shop/account/orders/<id>`) still lights its tab. `ProfileSection.tsx` (avatar, displayName/bio/website, per-field visibility toggles - its page is the one section that also **enforces** its `accountSectionsEnabled` flag, `notFound()`ing when off rather than merely losing its tab, with the same gate on all four routes it saves through), `SecuritySection.tsx` (passkeys, password, 2FA incl. QR setup, sessions, trusted browsers, recovery codes - the single biggest client component), `NotificationsSection.tsx`, `ActivitySection.tsx`, `DangerZoneSection.tsx` (data export request/download/expiry via a blob-download helper - same pattern as `app/cactus-admin/account/page.tsx`'s `handleExport`, not a raw `<a href>`, deletion request/cancel).

Pages (public member profile, Phase 4 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md - fixed paths, no proxy rewrite involved):

- `/members/[username]` - `app/(public)/members/[username]/page.tsx` - see the Middleware/Authentication sections for the full visibility matrix; old-username redirect; `members.profile-section` extension point.
- `/members` - `app/(public)/members/page.tsx` - paginated directory (24/page), gated on `directoryEnabled`.
- `components/members/MemberAvatar.tsx`, `GeneratedAvatar.tsx` - see Media Layer section.

Pages (admin, live under internal `/cactus-admin/*`, reached only via the rewritten `/<adminPath>/*`):

- `/cactus-admin` - dashboard: page/user/media counts, site-status badge, optional-feature checklist (media, email, Turnstile, Edge Config, GitHub, Sentry) with links into Settings tabs. Below that, a generic grid renders any module's contributions to the `core.admin-dashboard-widgets` extension point (permission-filtered live from `Module.manifest.extensionPoints`, same pattern as the Settings → Users → Roles subtab's `core.roles-page` section) - currently Boards' `boardsDashboardWidget` (thread/post/open-queue counts, link into the module admin).
- `/cactus-admin/login` - server `page.tsx` wrapper (calls `resolveBranding()` and a `SiteConfig.designTokens` read, **both `.catch()`-guarded** - this is the page a locked-out or expired session lands on, so a passing DB failure must cost the site's colours, not the sign-in form; it was an unguarded `Promise.all` and produced a bare 500), passes `siteName`/`faviconUrl`/`faviconDarkUrl` down) + `LoginForm.tsx` ('use client', the whole former page): passkey (default, WebAuthn prompt fires automatically on page load unless a recovery token is in the URL; fallback options hidden behind "Use another way to sign in" until the auto attempt fails/is cancelled - a cancelled auto attempt (`NotAllowedError`) shows no error banner), password → email OTP (trust-device checkbox), authenticator (TOTP), recovery-token completion, no-passkey fallbacks (register new passkey or recovery email), lost-access instructions including Neon console link. Logo above "Sign in" shows the site's uploaded favicon (light/dark variant swap via `data-logo-variant`, same mechanism as the admin sidebar logo) falling back to the Cactus mark when the admin hasn't set one.
- `/cactus-admin/account` - profile (displayName), change email, passkeys add/remove, TOTP set-up/remove, password add/change (with sign-out-other-sessions), active sessions list/revoke, GDPR JSON export, self-delete account. Split into a server `page.tsx` wrapper + `AccountPageClient.tsx` ('use client', the whole former page): the wrapper resolves `admins.account-section` extension-point contributions (permission-filtered live from `Module.manifest`, same pattern as the dashboard's `core.admin-dashboard-widgets`) and passes them via an `extensionSections` prop, rendered between the "Your data" row and the Delete account card. First consumer: Twilio's `TwilioAdminSmsSection` (self-service SMS login-code enrolment).
- `/cactus-admin/pages` - InfoPage list with pagination, bulk select + delete (`PagesTable.tsx`); gated per `pages.write`/`pages.delete`.
- `/cactus-admin/pages/new` - title/slug form (+ optional menu assignment when `menus.manage`), creates a builder-format draft then opens the editor.
- `/cactus-admin/pages/[id]` - full-screen Puck editor (`PuckEditor.tsx`): content only saves on an explicit Update/Publish click (no background autosave - **changed 2026-07-08**, was 1.5s debounced), gated on `pages.publish`, preview link, delete. Unsaved edits trigger a `beforeunload` warning and a confirm on the in-app back link. Sidebar gained Settings/SEO/History/Saved Blocks tabs (see Puck Integration) - History tab lists live + up to 10 archived versions with restore into editor. Markdown pages are silently migrated to builder format on open.
- `/cactus-admin/menus` - menu list: create, rename, delete (with main-menu warning), item counts, a Created column + "empty" badge, a name filter (shown when >1 menu), **Set as main** (promote to header menu without leaving the page), and **Duplicate** (deep-clone the whole menu + items). Create/rename inputs take Escape-to-cancel; create is blocked client-side on a duplicate (case-insensitive) name.
- `/cactus-admin/menus/[id]` - menu item editor: add page/module-content/external items, edit label/url/new-tab, delete. Reordering: drag a row via its handle, or use ↑/↓ (siblings-only swap, keyboard/click-friendly, no native drag required). Per-row actions are Edit/Delete plus a "⋯" kebab: a **Who can see this** section (Everyone / Signed-in only / Signed-out only / Admins only → `PATCH item {visibility}`), add child item (pre-sets the parent; disabled past the 3-level depth cap), promote one level if nested, and a depth-aware "nest under" select. Non-PUBLIC items show an inline audience badge (Members/Guests/Admins only). A header summary line counts items · limited-visibility · needs-attention; **attention badges** flag a deleted page/entity (error) or a draft page / unpublished entity that's hidden from the live site (warning). Destination cell links out (PAGE → page editor, external/module → live URL, new tab). An item filter (matches label/destination, keeps whole matching branches; disables drag/reorder while active) and Collapse all / Expand all (per-parent chevrons) tame large menus. Add-item lightbox has a "Who can see this?" picker and Escape-to-close. Header shows a "Main menu" badge when this menu is the one assigned in Settings → General.
- `/cactus-admin/media` - media library with folders + tags (redesigned 2026-07-13: full restructure). Server `page.tsx` loads the flat folder list (+ per-folder + root media counts), the tag list (+ counts), the root's first page (`queryMediaLibrary`), AND a whole-library overview (`computeLibraryStats`, `lib/media/library-stats.ts` - one pass over every row + the usage index: `totalFiles/totalSize/imageFiles/optimisedFiles/optimisableFiles/unusedFiles/unusedSize`), then hands off to `MediaLibrary.tsx` (client orchestrator). **Folder is in the URL (2026-07-28): `?folder=<folderId>`.** `page.tsx` reads it, verifies the id with a `prisma.folder.findUnique` (`root`/`all`/unknown → root) and renders that folder's first page instead of the root's; `MediaLibrary` seeds `currentFolderId` from the new `initialFolderId` prop (initial state, not a post-mount effect, so server and client open on the same folder and there's no root-then-refetch flash), and an effect mirrors every folder change back into the address with `window.history.replaceState` - replace, not push, so folder clicks don't stack up in the back button and no router navigation re-runs the server page. Refresh/bookmark/paste-a-link therefore lands in the folder you were in. **Perf (2026-07-26): `computeLibraryStats` is no longer awaited in the page's `Promise.all` - it was the one thing forcing a full-library scan + usage-index build before first paint, so an empty root still felt slow. The un-awaited promise is now passed to `MediaLibrary` as `statsPromise` and resolved client-side via React `use()` inside a `<Suspense fallback={<StatsBarSkeleton/>}>` (a four-tile placeholder in `MediaLibrary.tsx`), so the grid + folder tree paint at once and the tiles stream in. Paired with `queryMediaLibrary` now short-circuiting the usage-index build when a page has zero rows (`lib/media/library-query.ts`), the empty-root first paint no longer touches the page/layout builder JSON at all.** Layout top-to-bottom: page header (title + `MediaUpload`); `MediaStatsBar.tsx` (4 tiles - Files[+folder count], Storage used, Unused→click filters to unused, Optimisable→click filters to images; the two action tiles take a warning/info accent while there's work and drill into the WHOLE library via a `browseAll` flag); then a **resizable** split of `FolderTree.tsx` sidebar + content: a three-column grid `${folderPaneWidth}px 8px 1fr` whose middle column is `FolderPaneResizer.tsx` (new 2026-07-28) - a `role="separator"` drag handle (pointer events + pointer capture, so trackpad/pen/touch all work and the drag survives leaving the strip), arrow-key resize (±16px, ±48px with Shift), Home/End to the limits, Enter/Space or double-click to reset. Width is clamped 160-520px (default 220) and persisted to `localStorage['cactus.media.folderPaneWidth']`, hydrated in a post-mount effect like the view/sort prefs so the server render can't mismatch. `FolderTree` is unchanged behaviourally (recursive/expandable, path-to-current force-open, each row a nav button + `(count)` + drop target, folder rows draggable to move via `PATCH /api/admin/media/folders/[id]` `{parentId}` [self/descendant drops rejected by `isDescendant`], rows accept OS files dropped onto them when `media.upload`, hover rename/delete icons, "+ New folder") plus a new `browsingAll` prop that drops the active-row highlight while a search/tag/stat drill-down spans all folders. Content: breadcrumb (Media / … drop targets; shows "All folders" when spanning the tree), `MediaToolbar.tsx` (search-all box, sort/type/usage/tag selects, a grid|list **view toggle** persisted to `localStorage['cactus.media.view']`, and a removable **active-filter chip** strip + "Clear all"), a sticky selection/clipboard bar (Cut/Copy/Move to…/Optimise/Mark as optimised[flips to "Mark as not optimised" when every eligible selected item is already flagged]/Change ratio…/Resize…/Delete/Paste-here/Clear), then either a **grid** of `MediaCard.tsx` or a dense **list** `MediaList.tsx` (table: select-all header, thumb, sortable Name/Size/Uploaded headers wired to the sort state, Type, Folder, Usage pill; rows draggable + right-click + row-click-to-open). Nav/sort/filter/search/tag changes refetch `GET /api/admin/media` (first render reuses server items via a `firstRun` ref; `folderScope='all'` when search/tag/`browseAll`); further pages via an `IntersectionObserver` sentinel. Content pane + folder rows are OS-file drop targets (when `media.upload`) → `POST /api/admin/media`. Cards/rows are draggable (dragging a selected one drags the whole selection) onto any tree node/breadcrumb → `POST /api/admin/media/move`. Right-click opens `ContextMenu` (Open details / Optimise[raster unoptimised] / Mark as optimised|not optimised[raster+GLB, either state; acts on the whole selection when right-clicking inside one, but only on the items sharing the clicked item's flag] / Replace file…[library-accepted types] / Edit image…[raster] / Change ratio…[raster] / Resize…[raster] / Cut / Copy / Paste here / Rename… / Move to… / Tags…[opens the detail panel] / Delete); Cut/Copy fill a clipboard (cut items dimmed), Paste calls `/move` (cut) or `/duplicate` (copy). Opening a thumbnail/row opens **`MediaDetailPanel.tsx`** - a right-hand **slide-over** that replaced the old full-screen `MediaLightbox`: large preview (**3D models draw live from 2026-07-28** - `ModelPreview.tsx`, `next/dynamic` + `ssr:false` so three only loads once a model is opened: own `WebGLRenderer` + `OrbitControls` (damped, autoRotate until first pointer, no pan) + `RoomEnvironment` PMREM, model normalised to a 2-unit box and re-centred (scale MULTIPLIED, never assigned - FBX roots carry a unit conversion), loader chosen via `extensionForModelType` (GLB/glTF via `GLTFLoader` + `MeshoptDecoder` + `DRACOLoader` at `/draco/`, OBJ/FBX/3DS via their own loaders), bytes fetched by plain `fetch` in parallel with the loader chunks, everything disposed on unmount/step-to-next), In use/Optimised badges, metadata (type/size/folder/alt/uploaded), an **inline tag editor** (type-to-create + autocomplete, Save/Reset, `PUT /api/admin/media/[id]/tags`), Prev/Next with ArrowLeft/Right (ignored while typing), and an action footer (Open original / Optimise[raster unopt, `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/optimise`] / Mark as optimised|not optimised[raster+GLB, label follows `item.optimised`, `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-mark-optimised` with one id] / Replace file…[library-accepted types] / Edit image… / Change ratio… / Resize… / Rename… / Move… / Cut / Copy / Delete). Rename (`NameDialog`) / move (`MoveDialog`) / folder rename+delete (`NameDialog`/`DeleteFolderDialog`) / name-clash (`CollisionDialog` Keep both=suffix/Replace/Skip[move]/Cancel) dialogs are unchanged. Delete (single or bulk) always runs the in-use warning flow (`POST /bulk-delete` without force → still-referenced items return in `skipped`, dialog switches to "Delete anyway"). Edit image… opens `MediaImageEditor.tsx` (unchanged: crop box w/ 8 handles + rule-of-thirds + aspect presets Free/1:1/3:2/4:3/16:9/2:3/3:4/9:16 + custom W:H, "Save (replaces original)" [confirm] / "Save as new…" [filename], posts the source-pixel crop rect to `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/edit`). **Change ratio…** opens `MediaAspectDialog.tsx` (new 2026-07-16) - reshapes one image (detail panel / context menu) or the whole selection (selection bar) to a target ratio by **padding**, never cropping or stretching: ratio presets 1:1/3:2/4:3/16:9/2:3/3:4/9:16 + custom W:H, fill picker (Blurred image [default] / Colour [`<input type=color>` + White/Black shortcuts] / Transparent), a live CSS preview mirroring the server output (contain + pad; chequerboard for transparent), and Save-as-new [default] vs Replace-original [confirm step].
