Runs `resizeMediaImage` over each id sequentially, one failure never aborts the rest; sends no `newName` (one name across many would collide, so the server suffixes each with its own new size). Returns `{ ok, changed: string[], skipped: {id, reason}[], failed: {id, error}[], bytesSaved }`. Backs the media library's multi-select "Resize…" bar, called once per id through `runBulkImageJob`'s 6-worker pool since 2026-07-20 (route unchanged, still accepts any length).
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/optimise-video` - `media.upload`, `maxDuration 60`. Re-encode ONE video into the platform's single delivery format (MP4 / H.264 High / yuv420p / AAC / faststart) on the media worker. Body `{ quality?: 'high'|'balanced'|'small', maxWidth?: 1920|1280|1080|720 }` - both validated against `lib/media/video-quality.ts` and defaulted server-side, so the browser cannot ask for an encode the worker would clamp. Refuses anything that isn't `isVideoDirectType`, and anything not on the `B2` provider (the worker writes into that bucket with its own credentials). Destination key is `optimisedVideoKey(media.key)`: an `.mp4` is written back **over its own key** so every reference to it survives untouched; a `.webm` becomes `.mp4` and the route 409s if that key is already taken. Creates a per-job Fly machine exactly as `convert-sequence` does, signs a `{mediaId, machineId, name}` context token, enqueues `POST /video-jobs` on the worker, writes the `video-job:{jobRef}` notification and returns `{ jobId, destKey }`.
- `GET /api/admin/media/video-jobs` - `media.upload`. The video-optimise jobs, read back off their notifications (`lib/media/video-jobs.ts`); the Media › Video panel's list. Clearing a job is the ordinary notification delete.
- `GET/PUT /api/admin/media/video-worker-config` - GET `media.upload`, PUT `config.manage`. The media worker's Fly settings on `SiteConfig.mediaWorkerConfig` (`{fly:{token,appName}}`). `fly.token` is three-state (absent = keep, `''` = clear, string = save) and is NEVER echoed - responses report only `fly.source` ('saved'|'env'|null). Replaces `sequence-presets`, minus the conversion knobs (quality and largest-size are per video now).
- `GET /api/admin/media/video-status?jobId=` - `media.upload`. Twin of `sequence-status` for video jobs: settled state comes off the notification first (the job's machine is destroyed the moment the webhook lands, so a later poll cannot reach it), otherwise proxies the worker's `GET /jobs/{id}` through the machine-routed header and rewrites the notification. A bare 404 only fails the job once Fly agrees the machine is gone.
- `POST /api/webhooks/video-optimise` - no session; HMAC-gated on `X-Cactus-Signature` (raw body, keyed with `SEQUENCE_WORKER_SECRET`) with the enqueue-time context token as the bearer. On `optimised: true` calls `applyOptimisedVideo` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) → `repointMediaToBlob`, so the row keeps its id (and every reference) and simply weighs less; on `optimised: false` (the worker could not beat the source by `VIDEO_MIN_SAVING`, so it uploaded nothing) calls `markVideoAlreadyOptimised`, which stops the library offering a re-encode that has already been tried. Destroys the job's Fly machine either way, and settles the notification with a plain-words saving ("45.0 MB → 21.9 MB, 51% smaller").
- **Media usage index (`lib/media/references.ts`)** - `loadMediaUsageIndex()` (React `cache`, once per request) returns `{ referencedIds, haystack, degraded }`; `isMediaInUse(row, index)` decides the library's in-use dot, the Unused tile and the folder-delete warning. `referencedIds` is core's own FK columns (site logo/favicon/app icons, page OG images, member avatars, data exports); `haystack` is every InfoPage `builderData`/`publishedData` + Layout `builderData` blob **plus every string returned by the new `core.media-usage-providers` extension point** (contract `lib/media/usage-providers.ts`: `() => Promise<string[]>`, raw urls/keys/`Media` ids in any mixture, JSON columns returnable whole as text). Without it core could only see its own tables, so every shop product image, option/attribute swatch, 3D model, product download, board icon, directory photo and gazette hero counted as **unused** and was offered up for bulk deletion. Providers run in parallel; one throwing sets `degraded`, which makes `isMediaInUse` return `true` for everything (unused count 0) rather than trusting a half-built index - an over-cautious "nothing to reclaim" is a wasted click, an under-cautious "unused" is a delete button aimed at live product photography. Registered providers: `shop` (`shp_product_media.url`, `shp_digital_files.url`, `shp_products.og_image_id`, `shp_collections.image_id`/`og_image_id`, `shp_categories.og_image_id`/`image_url`), `shop-variations` (`svr_option_values.swatch`, `svr_uploads.media_ref`/`media_key`), `product-attributes-for-shop` (`pat_attribute_values.swatch`), `product-3d-views-for-shop` (`p3d_models.url`/`media_key`/`media_id` + `p3d_fabric_configs.config` as text), `product-downloads-for-shop` (`pdl_files.url`/`media_key`/`media_id`), `boards` (`brd_boards.icon_media_id`, `brd_user_profiles.avatar_id`), `directory` (`dir_entries.images` as text, `dir_categories.icon`), `gazette` (`gz_posts.featured_image_id`, `gz_author_profiles.avatar_id`).
- Media migration (`config.manage`): `GET /api/admin/media/provider-breakdown`, `POST migration-start`, `POST migration-batch` (one 15-item batch per call, driven by the open admin tab), `GET migration-status`, `POST migration-cancel`, `POST migration-retry`.
- `GET /api/admin/media/storage-check` - `config.manage`, `maxDuration = 60`. Reconciles `Media` rows against the objects storage actually holds (`reconcileMediaStorage`, `lib/media/reconcile.ts`). Rows are grouped by their own `provider` (a library that has been through a provider switch holds rows on several), each configured+listable provider is enumerated via `listStoredMediaKeys`, and the pure comparison lives in `diffStorageAgainstRows` (unit-tested in `lib/media/reconcile.test.ts`). Returns `{ providers: ProviderScan[], orphaned, missing, mismatched, orphanedBytes, partial }` - `orphaned` = object with no row (keys ending `/` skipped as folder placeholders), `missing` = row whose object is gone, `mismatched` = row whose `sizeBytes` disagrees with the object. `partial: true` (with a per-provider `skippedReason`) whenever a provider could not be listed: unconfigured, list threw, over the 50,000-object `KEYS_PER_PROVIDER_LIMIT`, or CLOUDINARY/IMAGEKIT (provider-minted ids, `listStoredMediaKeys` returns `null` = "cannot tell", never an empty list).
- `POST /api/admin/media/storage-check` - `config.manage`. `{ action: 'correct-sizes' }` rewrites every mismatched row's `sizeBytes` to the stored size (`correctRecordedSizes`, re-derives the list itself). `{ action: 'delete-orphans', keys: string[] }` additionally needs `media.delete` and re-runs the scan server-side, deleting only keys a fresh scan still calls orphaned; returns `{ deleted, skipped, reclaimedBytes }`. `{ action: 'purge-missing', keys: string[], force?: boolean }` also needs `media.delete` and deletes the `Media` rows whose object is gone (`purgeMissingRows`) - no blob call at all, since the object it names no longer exists; same re-scan-server-side guard, and without `force` a row `getMediaReferences` still finds in use is skipped and returned in `skipped: { key, originalName, references }[]` rather than deleted. Returns `{ purged, skipped, stale }` (`stale` = requested keys a fresh scan no longer calls missing).
- Menus (`menus.manage`): `GET/POST /api/admin/menus`; `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/menus/[id]` (GET also resolves each MODULE_ENTITY item's live label/href/publish-state via its provider, and returns `isMainMenu` (computed against `SiteConfig.mainMenuId`) for the admin editor's badge; PATCH accepts `name` and/or `isMainMenu` - `isMainMenu:true` sets `SiteConfig.mainMenuId` to this menu, `false` clears it only if this menu is the one assigned; delete clears `mainMenuId`, returns `wasMainMenu`); `POST [id]/duplicate` (deep-clones the menu + entire item tree into a new "<name> (copy)" menu, parents-first inside a transaction so child `parentId`s resolve; safe against the (menuId,pageId) unique since the copy is a fresh menu); `GET [id]/resolve` (public-shape resolved tree, anonymous viewer); `POST [id]/items` (PAGE unique per menu / EXTERNAL label+url / MODULE_ENTITY moduleId+entityKind+entityId, validated against the provider; optional `visibility` default PUBLIC; order auto-assigned per parent scope); `PATCH/DELETE [id]/items/[itemId]` (PATCH accepts label/url/openInNewTab and `visibility`); `POST [id]/items/reorder` (bulk parentId+order in a transaction); `GET /api/admin/menus/module-entities` (no moduleId/kind: lists registered modules+kinds; with both: searches that kind via its provider).
- Roles (`roles.manage`): `GET/POST /api/admin/roles` (unique name); `DELETE /api/admin/roles/[id]` (protected roles and roles with assigned users blocked); `POST/DELETE /api/admin/roles/[id]/permissions` (RolePermission upsert/remove; protected roles immutable).
- Users (`users.manage`): `GET /api/admin/users` (paginated); `PATCH /api/admin/users/[id]` (roleId / suspend; self-modification blocked; only protected-role actors may act on protected-role targets; last-admin guard on demotion); `DELETE /api/admin/users/[id]` (content ownership nulled; last-admin guard).
- `GET /api/admin/people` (`users.manage`, additionally unions in Member rows when `members.list` is also held) - unified staff+member directory backing `/cactus-admin/users`'s single Users tab: raw `UNION ALL` of `User`/`Role` and `Member`/`Role` (Prisma has no cross-model union), search across username/email/displayName, `type=staff|member` filter, sort by `username`/`createdAt`, real SQL pagination.
- Notifications (`config.manage`): `GET /api/admin/notifications`; `PATCH /api/admin/notifications` `{read: boolean}` (bulk - `updateMany` over the whole table, not the returned slice; true stamps every unread, false clears every read); `DELETE /api/admin/notifications` (bulk `deleteMany({ NOT: {type: 'deployment', deployInitiatedAt: null} })` - spares the open deployment notification, the one row nothing re-creates; returns `{deleted, kept}`); `PATCH /api/admin/notifications/[id]` (read/unread); `DELETE [id]`; `POST [id]/redeploy` (409 if already initiated; flips `pending_deploy` modules to `deploying`; `startDeferredRedeploy`; 503 in local mode).
- Pages: `GET /api/admin/pages` (`pages.read`); `POST` (`pages.write`, publish status additionally `pages.publish`, optional menu assignment with `menus.manage`, unique slug); `DELETE` bulk `{ids[]}` (`pages.delete`; blocked for pages referenced as privacy/terms). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/pages/[id]` (PATCH cannot flip draft→published - Publish endpoint only). `POST [id]/autosave` (`pages.write`; writes only `builderData` + menu links; draft pages reconcile title/slug/meta/ogImage columns, published pages freeze them). `POST [id]/publish` (`pages.publish`; the only writer of `publishedData`/`status: published`; archives the previous live version into `history`, capped at 10; `revalidatePath`). `GET [id]/history` (`pages.read`; `?index=live|N` for full blobs, no param for the version list). `GET /api/admin/pages/perms` (session; returns canRead/canWrite/canPublish/canDelete/canManageMenus).
- Modules (`modules.manage`, `maxDuration 60`): `GET /api/admin/modules` (list); `POST` (install: GitHub required, DeployLock, fetch + zod-parse `cactus.module.json`, tablePrefix uniqueness, `requiresModules` dependency check with minVersion, latest GitHub release required by channel, `requiredEnvVars` presence check, permission registration, then `deploying` + `startDeferredRedeploy`). `PATCH /api/admin/modules` `{action: 'update-all'}` - bulk-updates every module with `status: 'update_available'` in one DeployLock + one `startDeferredRedeploy` (avoids the per-module 409 that calling `PATCH [id]` `update` repeatedly would hit); per-module release fetch failures are skipped and reported back in a `failed: string[]` array rather than aborting the batch; each module now also runs the same compat gate the single-module path uses, via `checkModuleUpdateCompat()` (`lib/modules/compat.ts`, reads the manifest at the target tag and checks `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules` against core + the current installed set) - an incompatible module is dropped from the batch into `failed[]` with its reason and is never pinned into `modules.json`, closing the hole where one incompatible latest tag bricked every future deploy; drives the Modules admin page's "Update all" button. `PATCH /api/admin/modules/[id]` - `updateChannel` | `enable` | `disable` | `check-status` (lazy Vercel deploy reconcile for Hobby plan) | `update` (new tag held in `pendingVersion` until the deploy succeeds; the row's stored `manifest` is **also refreshed** to the one already fetched at that tag - it was previously frozen at whatever was recorded on INSTALL, so a module adding a `requiredEnvVars` entry in a later version could never have that variable managed by `/api/admin/env`, which derives its allowed keys from these stored manifests. Written at update time rather than on deploy success on purpose: the new credentials have to be settable while the new code is going out, not after). `DELETE [id]` `{mode: code_only|code_and_data}` - dependent-module guard; `code_and_data` drops the manifest's `teardown` tables with verification and deletes the module's `ModuleMigration` rows (otherwise a later reinstall skips its migrations and the tables never come back); deletes module permissions and row; redeploy. `GET [id]` - per-module update check against the latest release for its channel; raises/clears the `module-update:{id}` notification. `GET /api/admin/modules/directory` - lists public repos of the GitHub org `cactus-foundation-modules` (5-minute in-memory cache, `?refresh=true` busts), merged with installed state; `directoryUnavailable` flag when GitHub is unreachable; each uninstalled repo probed for a stable GitHub release (`hasPublicRelease`) so the admin UI can hide the Public channel option and force Beta for modules with pre-releases only. Both routes also pre-check the manifest's `requiresModules` against the installed `Module` rows via the shared `findUnmetModuleDependencies(requiresModules, installed)` (`lib/modules/dependencies.ts`, the one place `minVersion` is compared): install rejects with the existing plain `errorResponse` message, while `update` reuses its single `requiresCoreVersion` manifest fetch and returns a structured `409 { error, code: 'module_version_required', moduleName, dependencyName, requiredVersion, currentVersion }` naming the module to update first (`currentVersion` null when the dependency is absent or inactive rather than merely out of date) - updating a module whose new release raised a dependency pin (shop-variations and product-attributes-for-shop both pin `shop >= 0.1.38`) would otherwise break the site's next build on a missing module import, exactly as the core check prevents for core imports. Both manifest pre-checks in `update` are skipped silently when the manifest can't be fetched, so a transient GitHub hiccup never blocks an otherwise-fine update. `fetchManifestFromRepo(repoUrl, filename, ref='HEAD')` now takes a ref: install and both update paths pass the exact `release.tag` they are about to ship, so `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules`/permissions are validated against that tag's manifest, not default-branch HEAD. The `requiresCoreVersion` rejection on install/update no longer plain-texts the manifest's kebab-case `name` slug - both routes now return a structured `409 { error, code: 'core_version_required', moduleName, requiredVersion, currentVersion }`, `moduleName` from the new `formatModuleDisplayName(repoUrl)` (`lib/modules/manifest.ts`, same "cactus-module-foo-bar" → "Foo Bar" transform the Modules page already used for its cards). The Modules admin page catches `code === 'core_version_required'` in both its install and update handlers and opens a dedicated lightbox (title "Cactus needs updating first", message, a link to `../config?tab=general` - the Settings → General tab holding `UpdatesPanel`) instead of the page-top `alert-danger` banner used for every other install/update failure.

Members admin API (Phase 5 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md; every route below is `getSessionFromCookie` + a specific `members.*` permission):

- `GET /api/admin/members` (`members.list`) - search (`q`, case-insensitive across username/email/displayName) + status/trusted filters + sortable columns (`createdAt`/`username`/`status`) + pagination.
- `GET /api/admin/members/dashboard-summary` (`members.list`) - counts by status + `pendingDeletion` + 5 most recent suspensions.
- `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/members/[id]` (`members.view`/`edit`/`delete`) - PATCH is displayName/bio/websiteUrl; DELETE is the admin hard-delete, bypassing the member's own grace period entirely (no `MemberAdminActionLog` row for this one - see the top-of-file summary for why).
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/suspend` (`members.suspend`, optional `reason`/`until`) - also revokes every live `MemberSession` for the member immediately; `POST .../unsuspend` restores `ACTIVE` (there's no stored pre-suspension status to restore to - suspension is only ever expected on an already-ACTIVE member in practice).
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/approve` (`members.approve`, only from `PENDING_APPROVAL`) - sends a plain "you're approved" email when configured; `POST .../reject` deletes the member outright (never became a real active member, so nothing to keep - like admin-delete, no action-log row survives this one).
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/trust` (`members.trust`, `{trusted}`).
- `GET/POST /api/admin/members/[id]/notes` (`members.notes`) - append-only, mirrors `MemberAdminNote`'s own no-PATCH/DELETE design.
- `GET/DELETE /api/admin/members/[id]/sessions`, `DELETE .../sessions/[sessionId]` (`members.view`/`edit`) - admin-side session list/revoke-all/revoke-one.
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/reset-password` (`members.edit`) - deletes `MemberPassword` + `MemberTwoFactor`; there's no admin-settable member password, so "reset" means forcing the member back onto passkey/magic link until they set new ones themselves.
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/export-trigger` (`members.edit`, `maxDuration 60`) - runs the same `createDataExportRequest` flow as the member's own Danger Zone button, e.g. to fulfil a support request; the member downloads it themselves once ready.
- `GET /api/admin/members/[id]/action-log` (`members.view`) - last 100 `MemberAdminActionLog` rows.
- `POST /api/admin/members/bulk` (`{ids[], action}`, permission checked per action type against `ACTION_PERMISSIONS`) - suspend/unsuspend/approve/reject/trust/untrust/delete, `{done, skipped}` response (same shape as Boards' bulk endpoints).
- `GET/POST /api/admin/members/invites`, `DELETE /api/admin/members/invites/[id]` (`members.invite`) - create returns the full shareable `inviteUrl` (`/{memberAreaPath}/register?invite=<token>`) once; delete only revokes an unused invite (`usedAt: null` guard).
- `GET/PATCH /api/admin/members/settings` (`members.settings`) - GET also returns the read-only `memberAreaPath`; PATCH is a partial merge-then-validate against `MembersConfigSchema` (same pattern as `designTokens`/`consentBannerConfig`), then refuses the save when `hasAnyAuthMethod()` is false (every sign-in method off locks the members system shut with no screen left to undo it from - refused here rather than in the schema so the message can say what to do about it), invalidates the config cache.
- `GET /api/admin/emails/templates` (`emails.templates`) - every registered email (core + installed modules only), grouped by source, defaults merged with any DB override, plus the `emailWrapper` layouts available and which is the site default. `PATCH /api/admin/emails/templates/[key]` - save any of `subject`/`bodyHtml`/`wrapperLayoutId`/`isActive`; rejects an edit whose combined subject+body has dropped a `requiredTags` merge tag, rejects switching off a transactional template, rejects an unknown wrapper id. `DELETE` on the same path resets the **copy only** to the code default (nulls `subject`/`bodyHtml`), keeping the wrapper choice and on/off state. `POST /api/admin/emails/templates/preview` - renders unsaved editor content through the real send path with stand-in merge values, returns `{subject, html}` for the sandboxed preview iframe. `POST /api/admin/emails/templates/test-send` - same render, emailed to the requesting admin's own address only, subject prefixed `[Test]`. (Replaces `/api/admin/members/email-templates*`.)
- `GET /api/admin/members/gdpr` (`members.gdpr`) - one combined read: pending deletion requests, last 50 data-export requests, last 50 consent records, last 50 `MemberAdminActionLog` rows filtered to GDPR-relevant actions (export/reset-password/suspend/unsuspend).

Setup API (each returns 403/404 once setup is complete with users, except deployment-logs):

- `GET /api/setup/env-check` - required/optional env status, `missingRequired`, `databaseState` (`set` | `provisioned-redeploying` [checked via Vercel API] | `missing`), `neonAvailable`, `vercelConfigured`, `localMode`.
- `POST /api/setup/vercel-connect` - `list-projects` (token validation, projects + domains) | `list-account-domains` (every domain on the account/team owning the project, so already-bought domains can be attached) | `add-domain` (attaches a domain to the project; returns its full `DomainState`; a 409 from a re-add of an already-attached domain is reported as that domain's current state, not an error) | `domain-status` (re-reads a domain's `DomainState`, first POSTing Vercel's `/domains/{d}/verify` so a freshly-added ownership TXT is actually re-checked) | `configure` (writes VERCEL_API_TOKEN, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, generated SESSION_SECRET + ENCRYPTION_KEY, SITE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, optional NEON_API_KEY, GITHUB_REPO from the project's git link; deliberately does not redeploy yet). `DomainState` = `{ name, verified, verification[], misconfigured, recommended }` - `misconfigured` (from `GET /v6/domains/{d}/config`) means DNS isn't pointing at Vercel, `!verified` (from `GET /v9/projects/{p}/domains/{d}`) means Vercel hasn't accepted the ownership TXT challenge; the two are independent and both gate the wizard's Configure button. `.vercel.app` aliases short-circuit to ready.
- `POST /api/setup/configure-env` - writes optional allowlisted env vars during the wizard.
- `POST /api/setup/provision-db` - actions: `list` (Neon projects incl. org-scoped) | `check-existing` (counts user tables) | `save-url` (user-supplied DATABASE_URL → Vercel + redeploy) | `use-existing` (pooled URI via Neon API, optional `destroyData` = DROP SCHEMA public on the direct endpoint) | `create` (default: Neon project `cactus-<vercelProjectId>`, Postgres 18, chosen region, idempotent by name search; writes DATABASE_URL + NEON_PROJECT_ID; redeploys) | `ensure-redeploy` (self-heal for the "provisioned, awaiting redeploy" state: returns the in-flight deployment if one is running, otherwise triggers a fresh one; `status: 'missing'` if DATABASE_URL isn't in the Vercel env after all). Credentials may come from the body pre-redeploy. Env writes go through `upsertVercelEnvVars` (overwrites stale values; sensitive vars skip the `development` target Vercel rejects). Provisioning responses carry `deploymentId` on success or `redeployError` when the trigger failed - the wizard shows the error with a retry instead of a phantom "Redeploying…". No short-circuit on a stale DATABASE_URL already sitting in Vercel env vars.
- `POST /api/setup/read-state` - wizard resume state; 404 once complete.
- `POST /api/setup/create-admin` - seeds core permissions, ensures the protected Admin role, creates the admin user (email verification exempt); exact-match retry path preserves the WebAuthn user handle and clears stale passkeys.
- `POST /api/setup/set-admin-path` - 3–64 chars `[a-z0-9-]`, blocklisted values rejected; upserts SiteConfig.
- `GET /api/setup/suggest-path` - random `word-suffix` admin path suggestion.
- `POST /api/setup/essentials` - siteName + timezone.
- `POST /api/setup/complete` - seeds Home page (slug `home`, published), Main Menu, the default layouts (`seedDefaultLayouts`, not "all starters" - see `lib/setup/`), the Styles draft page; sets `setupCompleted`, status `comingSoon`, `hideFromCrawlers`, default design tokens; Edge Config sync; generates missing SESSION_SECRET/ENCRYPTION_KEY (Vercel write + redeploy, returns `needsRedeploy`, plus `redeployError` if the trigger failed so the wizard can point at a manual redeploy) or auto-logs the admin in; stamps `SiteConfig.starterTemplatesVersion`. Re-POST after setup is refused 403.
- `POST /api/setup/reset` - sets `setupCompleted = false`, only when zero users exist.
- `GET /api/setup/deployment-logs` - Vercel deployment state + log lines with a `since` cursor; post-setup requires session + `config.manage` and the server's own token; pre-setup accepts the wizard's token in the **`x-vercel-token` header** (never `?token=` - a live API credential in a URL lands in access logs and browser history) plus `?projectId=` for team-scope resolution. The setup-complete check tolerates a missing database (pre-setup there is none - previously this 500'd and the wizard never showed deploy state). Passes `teamId` to the Vercel API for team-owned projects.

GitHub App connect flow (under `app/cactus-admin/integrations/github/`, reached via the admin path rewrite):

- `GET start` (`config.manage`) - builds the GitHub App manifest (name "Cactus Foundation - {siteName}", permissions `contents: write` + `metadata: read`); state cookie `cactus_github_app_state` (10 min).
- `GET callback` (session) - state check; converts the manifest code via `POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions`; encrypts pem/webhook secret/client id/client secret with `ENCRYPTION_KEY`; replaces the GithubAppConnection row; uploads `cactus.svg` as the app logo (non-fatal); redirects with `github=connected|error&reason=…`.
- `GET install` (`config.manage`) - returns `github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new` URL + state cookie.
- `GET installed` (session) - stores `installation_id` and the installation account login.
- `POST disconnect` (`config.manage`) - deletes the GithubAppConnection rows (the App itself remains on GitHub).

Loading/error boundaries: one exists - `app/cactus-admin/error.tsx` ('use client'), covering every page under the admin prefix including `/cactus-admin/login` (which sits in this segment but renders outside `AdminLayout`'s shell). Shows a card with "That didn't load", the `error.digest` reference when present, and a "Try again" button wired to `reset()`, which re-runs the server render - the right cure for the transient failures this catches. Note React's nesting rule: a throw from `AdminLayout` itself goes to the *parent* boundary (root), not this one, so the layout guards its own reads inline: `getSessionWithMeta()` is `try`-wrapped and a failure is treated as no-session → `redirect` to login (safe - proxy.ts is the primary gate, no session ever fabricated), while `getSiteConfig`/`getInstalledModules`/`getUnreadCount`/`hasPermissions` each `.catch()` to an empty fallback the shell already tolerates (`null`/`[]`/`0`/`{}` - the permission catch can only ever hide nav, never reveal it; `isProtected` admins take hasPermissions' no-DB all-true branch so the catch bites only non-admins). No `loading.tsx` and no `global-error.tsx` anywhere.

### Middleware

There is no `middleware.ts`. `proxy.ts` at the repo root is the Next.js 16 replacement, running on the Node runtime (so it uses Prisma directly).

- Matcher: everything except `_next/static`, `_next/image`, and static file extensions (ico/png/jpg/jpeg/svg/webp/gif/woff/woff2/ttf/eot/css/js).
- Security headers (production only; skipped in development): CSP (`default-src 'self'`; scripts `'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'`; styles allow Google Fonts; img allows self/data/blob/picsum/the Worker host; `frame-ancestors 'none'`; `form-action 'self' https://github.com`), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, Permissions-Policy (camera/mic/geolocation off, WebAuthn self), HSTS 2 years preload.
- Always-pass paths: `/api/health`, `/api/webhooks/`, `/_next/`, `/favicon.ico`.
- `resolveAdminPath()`/`resolveSiteStatus()` fall back to `getAdminPathCached()`/`getSiteStatusCached()` in `lib/config/site.ts` when Edge Config isn't writable. Both cached readers **serve the last known value when their query throws** rather than propagating: a throw in `proxy.ts` isn't an error page, it's a bare 500 on whatever the visitor asked for, and the 5-second TTL guarantees a cold instance always misses. `undefined` from the guarded query means "the read failed" and is kept distinct from `null`, which legitimately means "no SiteConfig row".
- Direct requests to `/cactus-admin*` return 404.
- Direct requests to `/cactus-account*` return 404 (Members system internal prefix, `MEMBER_INTERNAL` from `lib/members/paths.ts`).
- First-run gate: until `setupCompleted && userCount > 0`, everything redirects to `/setup` except `/setup`, `/api/setup`, `/api/auth/passkey/`, `/api/auth/totp/`, `/api/health`, `/_next/`, `/favicon.ico`. After setup, `/setup*` returns 404.
- Admin path enforcement: resolves the admin path from Edge Config (when write creds present) else a 5-second-TTL Prisma cache; rewrites `/<adminPath>/*` → `/cactus-admin/*`. The `/login` sub-path is rewritten without an auth check (header `x-cactus-is-login: 1`). All other sub-paths validate the `cactus_session` cookie; on success sets `x-cactus-admin-path`, `x-cactus-user-id`, `x-cactus-role-protected`; unauthenticated requests redirect to `/<adminPath>/login?next=…`. (The former full-page redeploy trap is gone - in-flight redeploys are surfaced by the admin shell's `DeployStatusBar` and the notification bell instead.)
- Member-area path rewrite: unconditionally rewrites `/<memberAreaPath>/*` → `/cactus-account/*` (sets `x-cactus-member-path` and `x-cactus-member-full-path` - the latter is the original public pathname+search, used by `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` to build an accurate post-login `?redirect=` since the internal pathname alone can't reconstruct it), checked after admin enforcement so admin wins any prefix collision. Still no session validation in proxy itself - the account layout does its own gate. Unlike the admin rewrite, this currently runs before the site-status gate below, so member pages stay reachable during comingSoon/maintenance; revisit when Phase 8 wires `siteWideMembersOnly`.
- API requests pass through, with a CSRF origin check on non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS: a present-but-mismatched `Origin` header returns 403.
- `/page-preview/` and `/layout-preview/` always pass (so editors can preview while the site is gated).
- Site status gate: when status ≠ `live`, public routes are rewritten to `/cactus-status/coming-soon` or `/cactus-status/maintenance` unless the session's role `isProtected`. That protected-role bypass now returns `withSecurity(NextResponse.next())` (2026-07-23) rather than a bare `NextResponse.next()` - it was the one path out of the proxy that shipped no CSP, no HSTS and no `X-Frame-Options`, so an admin previewing a gated site browsed it entirely unprotected.
- Members-only site access (Phase 8 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md, runs after the status gate, only for ordinary public content - admin/api/preview/member-area paths have already returned by this point): gated when `membersConfig.siteWideMembersOnly` is on OR the path resolves to a non-`PUBLIC` module route tier (`lib/members/access.ts`'s `resolveRouteTier`, cached module read). `siteWideMembersOnlyExceptions` prefix-exempts a path outright; admins bypass; else the `cactus_member_session` cookie is validated (`TRUSTED_MEMBER` tiers additionally require `member.trusted`). Unsatisfied + `guestPreviewEnabled` → passes through with `x-cactus-guest-preview: 1` (consumed by the Puck `MemberGate`/`TrustedMemberGate` blocks' teaser rendering only, for now). Unsatisfied + no preview: no session → redirect to `/{memberAreaPath}/login?redirect=…`; signed in but insufficient tier → 404 (no sensible redirect target, no dedicated status page for this case).

### Environment Variables

Core:

- `DATABASE_URL` - PostgreSQL pooled connection string. Required. Consumed by Prisma (`lib/db/prisma.ts`), build scripts, setup routes.
- `DIRECT_URL` - optional non-pooled connection for migrations; `scripts/build-migrate.mjs` (falls back to stripping `-pooler` from DATABASE_URL).
- `SESSION_SECRET` - HMAC ingredient for session/trusted-device token hashing, min 32 chars. Required (auto-generated on Vercel during setup). `lib/config/env.ts:getSessionSecret`, `lib/auth/session.ts`.
- `SITE_URL` - canonical public URL; also the WebAuthn rpId/origin source. Required. `lib/config/env.ts` (`getSiteUrl`, `getWebAuthnRpId`, `getWebAuthnOrigin`), robots/sitemap, recovery links.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` - browser-visible copy of SITE_URL shown in the setup wizard. Optional in code, written by setup.
- `VERCEL` - platform-injected. Its absence defines local-development mode (`isLocalMode()` in `lib/config/env.ts`), which disables env editing, redeploys, and core/module updates.
- `VERCEL_URL` - platform-injected fallback for site URL in robots/sitemap.
- `NODE_ENV` - dev/prod switches (security headers, cookie `secure`, WebAuthn localhost overrides, Prisma logging).
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` - injected by `next.config.ts` from `package.json` version.
- `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` - set to `1` by `next.config.ts`.
- `PORT` - `scripts/dev-warm.sh` only (default 3000).

Vercel control plane:

- `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` - required on Vercel; env-var writes, redeploys, deployment logs/status, Edge Config writes. `lib/vercel/env.ts`, `lib/vercel/deploy.ts`, `lib/deploy/redeploy.ts`, setup + admin env routes.
- `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` - required on Vercel; identifies the project for all of the above.
- `EDGE_CONFIG` - optional; Edge Config read connection string (`lib/config/edge-config.ts`, `@vercel/edge-config`).
- `VERCEL_EDGE_CONFIG_ID` - optional; Edge Config item writes via the Vercel REST API.
- `VERCEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` - optional; verifies `/api/webhooks/vercel` (Pro/Enterprise; Hobby falls back to lazy polling).

Auth:

- `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` / `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` - optional; Cloudflare Turnstile on login/register/recovery and module forms. `lib/auth/turnstile.ts` fails open when unset, fails closed on network errors when set.
- `MEMBER_AREA_PATH` - optional; public URL prefix for the member account area (default `account`). Deploy-time only, changing it requires a redeploy. Read via `getMemberAreaPath()` in `lib/members/paths.ts` (sanitised, blocklist-checked, falls back to the default). Member-area pages live internally at `/cactus-account/*`, rewritten in `proxy.ts` (see Middleware section).

GitHub:

- `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` - optional; PAT fallback for all GitHub operations (`lib/github/client.ts`), `scripts/sync-wiki.mjs`.
- `GITHUB_REPO` - `owner/repo` of the site's own repository; module registry commits and core-update pushes (`lib/modules/github.ts`, `lib/updates/core.ts`).
- `CACTUS_CORE_REPO` - optional upstream override for core updates; defaults to `usersaynoso/cactus-foundation` (`lib/updates/core.ts`).
- `WIKI_SOURCE_REPO` - optional; `scripts/sync-wiki.mjs` (defaults to GITHUB_REPO).

Encryption:

- `ENCRYPTION_KEY` - 64-char hex (32 bytes) AES-256-GCM key. Required for the GitHub App flow, TOTP secret storage, and the reply-catcher module's mailbox credentials. `lib/crypto/secrets.ts`.

Neon:

- `NEON_API_KEY` - optional; automatic database provisioning during setup (`/api/setup/provision-db`).
- `NEON_PROJECT_ID` - written by provisioning. **No longer surfaced by `/api/auth/config` (2026-07-23)**: it used to feed the lost-passkey Neon console deep link on the login screen, which is a pre-auth payload, so the link is now the plain console URL and the value stays server-side.

Media (one provider active at a time; per-provider keys defined in `lib/media/providers.ts`):

- `B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID`, `B2_APPLICATION_KEY`, `B2_BUCKET_NAME`, `B2_ENDPOINT` - Backblaze B2.
- `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `R2_BUCKET_NAME` - Cloudflare R2.
- `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME`, `S3_REGION` - AWS S3.
- `SPACES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `SPACES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `SPACES_BUCKET_NAME`, `SPACES_REGION` - DigitalOcean Spaces.
- `WASABI_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `WASABI_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `WASABI_BUCKET_NAME`, `WASABI_REGION` - Wasabi.
- `MINIO_ENDPOINT`, `MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MINIO_BUCKET_NAME`, `MINIO_USE_SSL` - MinIO.
- `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` - Vercel Blob.
- `SUPABASE_STORAGE_PROJECT_URL`, `SUPABASE_STORAGE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME` - Supabase Storage.
- `CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME`, `CLOUDINARY_API_KEY`, `CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET` - Cloudinary (direct).
- `IMAGEKIT_PUBLIC_KEY`, `IMAGEKIT_PRIVATE_KEY`, `IMAGEKIT_URL_ENDPOINT` - ImageKit (direct).
- `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` - shared Worker URL for all proxied providers; required by every proxied provider (`envKeysForProvider` appends it).
- `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_HOSTNAME` - Worker hostname for `next.config.ts` remotePatterns and the proxy CSP img-src. Optional: when unset, both derive it from `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` (`workerImageHost()` in `proxy.ts` and `next.config.ts`), so the admin auto-deploy needs no extra env var.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` - client-side Worker URL fallback used by the custom image loader (`lib/media/loader.ts`).

Email:

- `BREVO_API_KEY` - Brevo transactional API; takes priority over SMTP. `lib/email/index.ts`.
- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` (default 587), `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS` - nodemailer SMTP fallback.

Other:

- `SENTRY_DSN` - optional. Read only for configured-status display (dashboard, env editor); no Sentry SDK is installed or initialised anywhere.
- `CRON_SECRET` - **core-owned and self-minting; never asked of the owner.** Vercel attaches it as `Authorization: Bearer` on every scheduled invocation (core's four `/api/cron/members/*` jobs and every module `cronJobs` entry), and each cron route 503s without it. `ensureCronSecret()` (`lib/vercel/cron-secret.ts`) generates `randomBytes(32).toString('hex')` and upserts it as a **sensitive** project var; called from setup (`vercel-connect` mints it inline with SESSION_SECRET/ENCRYPTION_KEY, `setup/complete` covers the pre-set-token path), from core update (`app/api/admin/updates/route.ts`, before the lock - heals sites predating this), and from module install when the manifest has `cronJobs` or names `CRON_SECRET` (`app/api/admin/modules/route.ts`, which then drops it from the required-env gate unless the outcome is `unavailable`). Outcomes: `present` | `provisioned` | `pending` (already on the project, this deployment predates it - **never overwritten**, rotating it would break live crons) | `skipped` (local mode) | `unavailable` (no Vercel creds or API refused). Only ever reaches `process.env` via the redeploy the caller triggers, never within the request that mints it. Shown as an optional entry in `getEnvStatus()`.
- `GOCARDLESS_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `GOCARDLESS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GOCARDLESS_ENVIRONMENT` (`sandbox`|`live`) - gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop module; the API access token, the webhook endpoint secret, and the environment. Presence of the token + secret gates the Instant Bank Pay checkout method (`modules/gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop/lib/env.ts`).
- `CREZCO_API_KEY`, `CREZCO_USER_ID`, `CREZCO_ENVIRONMENT` (`sandbox`|`production`) - crezco-direct-bank-payments-for-shop module; the Collect API key (header `X-Crezco-Key`), the merchant user id every pay demand is created under, and the environment. Presence of key + user id gates the Direct bank payment checkout method (`modules/crezco-direct-bank-payments-for-shop/lib/env.ts`).
- `SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT` (`sandbox`|`production`), `SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SQUARE_LOCATION_ID`, `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY`, `SQUARE_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SQUARE_SANDBOX_LOCATION_ID`, `SQUARE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY` - square-payment-for-shop module. `SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT` picks the API host (connect.squareup.com vs connect.squareupsandbox.com) **and** which credential set is read: the `SQUARE_SANDBOX_*` trio for sandbox, the unprefixed trio for production (`squareEnvVarNames()`/`getSquareCredentials()` in `modules/square-payment-for-shop/lib/env.ts`). Both sets can be set at once. Access token + location ID for the live environment gate the Card payment (Square) checkout method; the signature key is optional and only gates the webhook route (`isSquareWebhookConfigured()`).
- `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK` - set to `1` by `scripts/build-migrate.mjs` at build time only.

Cloudflare Worker (separate deployment, `workers/media-worker`): `ALLOWED_ORIGIN`, `BLOB_BASE_URL`, `UPLOAD_SIGNING_SECRET`, `ASSET_SIGNING_SECRET`, plus the same provider secret sets as above, configured via `wrangler secret put` (the two signing secrets are pushed automatically on Deploy Worker).

**3D models on the direct path (v0.5.468).** The Worker's write path accepts model extensions as well as raster images, and `MAX_DIRECT_UPLOAD_BYTES`/`UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES` rose 25 → 50 MB in step. Why it had to: a module posting a 50 MB model through a serverless route was never going to work - Vercel 413s any body over ~4.5 MB *before* the handler runs, and that 413's body is not JSON, so `res.json()` threw and the 3D editor's `?? 'Upload failed'` fallback was all anyone ever saw. The direct path is the only route in for a file that size.

- `MODEL_EXTENSION_TYPES` (`lib/media/limits.ts`) is the ext→type map: `glb`→`model/gltf-binary`, `gltf`→`model/gltf+json`, `obj`→`model/obj`, `fbx`→`model/x-fbx`, `3ds`→`model/x-3ds`. **Mirrored verbatim in `workers/media-worker/index.ts`'s `EXTENSION_TYPES` - keep the two in step.** Keyed by extension because a 3D file's declared type is worthless (browsers send `application/octet-stream` for .glb, an empty string for .fbx) and because on this path the extension is the only claim a client cannot forge: it is baked into the key the token signs.
- `extensionForMimeType` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) consults `extensionForModelType` **first**. Model types are not derivable from their subtype - `model/gltf-binary` must land as `.glb`, not `.gltf-binary` - and a key whose extension names no type is one the Worker refuses. The old `application/octet-stream` produced exactly that: `.octet-stream`.
- Models are **not** in `SERVABLE_IMAGE_TYPES`, deliberately. GET serves every non-image as `application/octet-stream` + `Content-Disposition: attachment`, which is fine: a model is fetched by XHR inside a WebGL canvas, which reads the bytes and ignores both headers. GET already sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the cross-origin fetch works.
- `isAcceptedUploadType`/`isRasterDirectType`/`preflightUploadError` are untouched - the media library UI still offers images only.
- **Every existing install must redeploy its Worker** (Settings → Media → Deploy Worker) before 3D uploads work; an old one 415s every model key. `product-3d-views-for-shop`'s client turns that 415 into a "redeploy your Worker" message rather than a bare refusal.
- Not fixed here, same latent bug: **shop's `admin/digital-files`** advertises a 200 MB cap through the serverless multipart path, so anything over ~4.5 MB dies the same way. It needs the same treatment (or an honest limit) whenever someone gets to it.

Media worker (video optimise, standalone service at `services/video-worker`, deployed on Fly.io app `cactus-seqworker` - the app keeps its old name because renaming it would change the hostname every install holds):
- `MEDIA_WORKER_URL` - the worker's base URL (`lib/config/env.ts:getMediaWorkerUrl`). Unset hides the Optimise video action.
- `MEDIA_WORKER_SECRET` - shared bearer secret for the worker API and the HMAC key its completion callback is signed with (`getMediaWorkerSecret`, header `X-Cactus-Signature`).
- `MEDIA_WORKER_FLY_TOKEN` - optional Fly.io API token fallback (`getMediaWorkerFlyTokenEnv`). A token saved under Media → Video (`SiteConfig.mediaWorkerConfig` `fly.token`) wins; either enables per-job Fly machines (see Media Layer).
- `MEDIA_WORKER_MAX_JOB_MACHINES` - optional ceiling on simultaneous per-job Fly machines (`getMediaWorkerMaxJobMachines`). Unset or 0 = no ceiling, which is the default: every video gets its own machine. A positive value refuses further jobs in plain English rather than queueing them.
- **The `SEQUENCE_WORKER_URL` / `SEQUENCE_WORKER_SECRET` / `SEQUENCE_FLY_TOKEN` / `SEQUENCE_MAX_JOB_MACHINES` names are still read**, as a per-variable fallback in `readEnv`, so an install that predates the rename needs no environment change.

### Database Schema

Single Prisma schema at `prisma/schema.prisma` (PostgreSQL). One init migration: `prisma/migrations/20260626000000_init/migration.sql`. All timestamps UTC.

- `User` - `id` (cuid PK), `email` (unique), `username` (unique), `displayName?`, `passwordHash?`, `roleId` → Role, `emailVerifiedAt?`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `suspendedAt?`, `acceptedPrivacyPolicyAt?`, `totpSecretEncrypted?`, `totpVerifiedAt?`, `totpLastStep? BigInt`, `smsOtpPhoneEncrypted?` (AES-256-GCM phone; when set and an SMS provider module is active, password-login OTPs go by text). Relations: passkeys, sessions, trustedDevices, emailChallenges, recoveryRequests, infoPages, mediaItems, consentRecords. Indexes: email, username.
- `Passkey` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `credentialId` (unique), `publicKey Bytes`, `counter BigInt default 0`, `transports String[]`, `label?`, `createdAt`. Index: userId.
- `Session` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `tokenHash` (unique; sha256(token + SESSION_SECRET)), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`. Indexes: userId, expiresAt.
- `TrustedDevice` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `tokenHash` (unique), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`. Indexes: userId, expiresAt.
- `EmailChallenge` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `codeHash`, `purpose` (`login_otp` | `verify_email` | `recovery`), `expiresAt`, `attempts Int default 0`, `createdAt`. Indexes: (userId, purpose), expiresAt.
- `RecoveryRequest` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `tokenHash` (unique), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`, `used Boolean default false`. Indexes: userId, expiresAt.
- `Role` - `id`, `name` (unique), `isProtected Boolean default false`, `createdAt`. Relations: users, members, permissions. A protected `"Members"` row is lazily created (name-unique-race-safe) the first time anyone registers via `/api/members/register` (`lib/members/default-role.ts`), and assigned as every new Member's `roleId`.
- `Permission` - `key` (PK), `description?`, `module?` (null = core, else the registering module name). Relation: rolePermissions.
- `RolePermission` - composite PK (roleId, permissionKey); both FKs cascade.
- `SiteConfig` - singleton (`id = "singleton"`): `siteName` (default "My Cactus Site"), `tagline?`, `description?`, `timezone` ("UTC"), `locale` ("en-GB"), `dateFormat` ("DD/MM/YYYY"), `timeFormat` ("HH:mm"), `adminPath` (unique), `setupCompleted` (false), `status SiteStatus` (comingSoon), `hideFromCrawlers` (true), `speedInsightsEnabled` (true; Settings → General - gates `<SpeedInsights />` in `app/layout.tsx` via `isSpeedInsightsEnabled()` in `lib/config/site.ts`, a 5s-TTL best-effort reader that falls back to on, matching the pre-switch behaviour), `trustDeviceDays` (28), `starterTemplatesVersion?` (core version whose starter templates were last seeded; mismatch with `package.json` version triggers `ensureStarterLayoutsCurrent`'s auto-refresh), `emailFromName?`, `emailFromAddress?`, `emailProvider?` ('brevo' | 'smtp'), `mediaProvider MediaProviderType?`, `lazyLoadImages` (true; Settings → Media - sets `loading="lazy"` vs `"eager"` on every core content image [Image block, Quote photo, Card cover, Panel image, logo strip] via Puck `metadata`, see `lib/puck/renderMetadata.ts` + `lib/puck/imgLoading.ts`; the Image block's original exemption [it can be the LCP element] was removed on the owner's call - the trade is real and is surfaced in the setting's help text rather than decided in code; module blocks don't consult it), `privacyPolicyPageId?`, `termsPageId?`, `logoMediaId?`, `logoDarkMediaId?` (optional dark-mode logo; frontend swaps to it via CSS keyed on `data-theme="dark"`), `faviconMediaId?`, `faviconDarkMediaId?` (optional dark-mode favicon; served via a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query, so it follows the browser/OS scheme not the in-site toggle), `appIconMediaId?` (square source image the admin uploads; favicon/apple/PWA icons auto-generated from it), `appleTouchIconMediaId?`, `webManifest192MediaId?`, `webManifest512MediaId?` (each independently overridable), `appName?`, `appShortName?`, `themeColor?`, `backgroundColor?` (web-app manifest identity; fall back to `siteName`/white via `lib/config/branding.ts`), `sessionPurgeAfterDays` (30), `recoveryPurgeAfterDays` (7), `mainMenuId?`, `homepageId?`, `pendingRedeployId?`, `pendingRedeployAt?`, `designTokens Json?`, `consentBannerConfig Json?`, `coreUpdateChannel` ("public"), `membersConfig Json?` (Members settings, Zod-parsed with defaults by `lib/members/config.ts`), `adminMenuConfig Json?` (admin-sidebar customisation - per-item order/rename/visibility set in Settings → Navigation; null = built-in defaults; parsed by `parseAdminMenuConfig`/`AdminMenuConfigSchema` in `lib/nav/admin-menu.ts`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
- `UserColourPreset` - user-created Styles > Colours presets: `id`, `name` (unique), `tokens Json` (`{primary:{light,dark}, linkColour, linkHoverColour, linkColourDark, linkHoverColourDark}` - same shape as the hardcoded `ColourPreset` in `lib/design/tokens.ts`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. The 10 default presets (`COLOUR_PRESETS`) are still hardcoded in app code with no DB row and can't be overwritten/deleted through this model; the Styles preset bar shows these user rows first, then the defaults.
- `InfoPage` - `id`, `slug` (unique), `title`, `body Text`, `bodyFormat BodyFormat` (markdown), `builderData Json?` (working draft; autosave target), `publishedData Json?` (live content, written only by Publish), `publishedAt?`, `publishedById?` (no relation), `history Json?` (array of `{data, title, at, byId}`, max 10, newest first), `status PageStatus` (draft), `metaDescription?`, `ogImageId?` (Media id, no relation), `createdById?` → User (SetNull), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Relation: menuItems. Indexes: slug, status.
- `Media` - `id`, `key` (unique), `provider MediaProviderType`, `url`, `uploadedById?` → User (SetNull), `altText?`, `isDecorative` (false), `originalName?` (the filename the user uploaded, kept verbatim for display since `key` is deliberately mangled with a nanoid prefix; null for legacy rows + generated files - icons/avatars/exports - which fall back to the key basename; the media library card/lightbox/grid and the Puck media picker all show `originalName || key.split('/').pop()`, and both the `/api/admin/media` GET and the media library page search it alongside key/altText), `mimeType`, `sizeBytes Int`, `optimised` (Boolean, false - set true once the media library's in-place optimise has re-encoded the item to WebP, drives the "Optimised" badge and stops it being offered again), `folderId?` → Folder (SetNull; null = library root; the folder's path is baked into the item's `key`/`url`), `tags MediaTag[]`, `createdAt`. Indexes: uploadedById, createdAt, provider, folderId.
- `Folder` - media library folder. `id`, `name`, `parentId?` → Folder self-relation "FolderTree" (`onDelete:Cascade`; null = root), `children Folder[]`, `media Media[]`, `createdAt`. `@@unique([parentId, name])` (root uniqueness also enforced in app since Postgres treats null parentId rows as distinct), index parentId. Folders are physical: the sanitised slash-joined ancestor path lives in each contained item's storage key/url, so rename/move/delete relocate or remove blobs (see `lib/media/organise.ts`).
- `Tag` - `id`, `name` (unique), `createdAt`, `media MediaTag[]`. Freeform, created on the fly.
- `MediaTag` - join: `mediaId` + `tagId` (composite PK), both FKs `onDelete:Cascade`, index tagId.
- `MediaMigrationJob` - `id`, `toProvider MediaProviderType`, `status` (pending | running | completed | failed | cancelled), `totalItems Int`, `migratedItems Int default 0`, `failedItemIds Json default []`, `cursor?`, `startedAt`, `completedAt?`, `lastError?`. Indexes: status, startedAt.
- `Layout` - `id`, `name`, `type` (header | footer | infoPage | notFound | statusPage | module type; default infoPage), `description?`, `builderData Json?` (working draft; autosave target), `publishedData Json?` (live content, written only on publish), `publishedAt?`, `publishedById?` (no relation), `history Json?` (array of `{data, title, at, byId}`, max 10, newest first - mirrors InfoPage), `displayConditions Json?` (`{include: Rule[], exclude: Rule[]}`), `priority Int default 0`, `status PageStatus` (draft), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. (`isStarter Boolean` is **gone** - starter templates are in-code data now. `prisma/core-reconcile/005_retire_starter_layouts.sql` deletes the legacy starter rows and then drops the column and its index; the init migration no longer creates either, and `004_perf_indexes.sql` no longer indexes it - leaving that `CREATE INDEX` in place would have failed every build after the column was dropped.)
- `SavedBlock` - reusable Puck block snapshots, shared by the page and layout builders: `id`, `name`, `componentType` (the Puck component type, e.g. "Hero"), `data Json` (full ComponentData blob, reinserted verbatim on use), `createdAt`. Single-tenant, no categories/folders.
- `Module` - `id`, `name` (unique), `repoUrl`, `version` (confirmed live tag), `pendingVersion?` (in-flight target, promoted only on deploy success), `tablePrefix` (unique), `status ModuleStatus` (pending_install), `installedAt`, `lastError?`, `lastCheckedAt?`, `updateAvailable?`, `updateNotes? Text`, `updateChannel` ("public"), `manifest Json?` (parsed cactus.module.json), `layoutsSeededAt?` (set the one time this module's `publishByDefault` layouts were stamped, by `markModulesDeploySucceeded()`; never cleared, because a module *update* redeploys down the same path and a create-only upsert would resurrect layouts the owner deleted).
- `Notification` - `id`, `type NotificationType` (deployment), `title`, `reasons Json?` (deployment type: `{label, detail?, at}[]`), `link?` (admin-relative), `dedupeKey?` (core-update, module-update:{id}, contact-form:messages), `readAt?` (null = unread, drives nav badge), `deployInitiatedAt?` (null = open deployment notification), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Indexes: (type, deployInitiatedAt), readAt, dedupeKey.
- `ModuleMigration` - `id`, `moduleName`, `migrationName`, `appliedAt`, `checksum` (sha256 of the SQL). Unique (moduleName, migrationName); index moduleName. Tracked separately from Prisma's own history.
- `DeployLock` - singleton: `id = "singleton"`, `lockedAt`, `lockedBy` (module or update identifier). Prevents concurrent installs/updates. Every acquire/check site now goes through `getActiveDeployLock()` (`lib/deploy/lock.ts`): a lock whose `lockedAt` is older than `STALE_LOCK_MS` (15 min) is treated as orphaned (from a hard-killed function that never ran its release), deleted-if-still-stale, and reported as absent - so a stranded lock self-heals instead of returning a permanent 409 on every future install/update/core-update.
- `GithubAppConnection` - `id`, `appId`, `appSlug`, `installationId?`, `installationAccount?`, `privateKeyEncrypted Text`, `webhookSecretEncrypted? Text`, `clientIdEncrypted? Text`, `clientSecretEncrypted? Text`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted with ENCRYPTION_KEY.
- `Menu` - `id`, `name`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Relation: items.
- `MenuItem` - `id`, `menuId` → Menu (cascade), `parentId?` self-relation (cascade), `type MenuItemType`, `pageId?` → InfoPage (cascade), `label?`, `url?`, `moduleId?`, `entityKind?`, `entityId?` (MODULE_ENTITY target - no FK, module tables live outside Prisma, resolved via `core.menu-entity-provider`), `openInNewTab` (false), `visibility MenuItemVisibility` (default PUBLIC - per-item front-end audience gate, filtered in `lib/menu/resolve.ts` against the current viewer; hiding an item hides its subtree), `order Int`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Unique (menuId, pageId); indexes menuId, pageId.
- `RateLimit` - `id`, `key` (`ip:<addr>` | `account:<id>` | `account_email:<email>` | `consent:<id>`), `action`, `attempts Int default 1`, `windowStart`. Unique (key, action); index windowStart. In-database rate limiting with atomic INSERT … ON CONFLICT.
- `ConsentRecord` - append-only: `id`, `consentId`, `userId?` → User (SetNull), `categoriesVersion Int`, `decision Json`, `action` (accept_all | reject_all | custom | withdraw | acknowledge), `ipTruncated?`, `uaHash?`, `createdAt`. Indexes (consentId, createdAt), userId.
- `WebAuthnChallenge` - transient: `id`, `userId?`, `memberId?` (member passkey flows), `challenge` (unique), `purpose` (registration | authentication | member_registration | member_authentication), `expiresAt` (5 min), `createdAt`. Indexes userId, memberId, expiresAt.

Members system (all cuid PKs, all token/code columns store hashes only, every child table FKs `Member` with cascade delete; see MEMBERS_SPEC.md):

- `Member` - `id`, `email` (unique), `username` (unique, stored lowercase), `displayName?`, `avatarMediaId?` (Media id, no relation), `avatarChoice AvatarChoice` (GENERATED), `bio?`, `websiteUrl?`, `trusted` (false), `status MemberStatus` (PENDING_VERIFICATION), `roleId?` → Role (SetNull; assigned to the seeded "Members" role at registration, nullable for rows predating the field), `emailVerified` (false), `emailVerifiedAt?`, `backupEmail?`, `suspendedUntil?`, `suspensionReason?`, `suspensionNotified` (false), `deletionRequestedAt?`, `deletionScheduledAt?`, `deletionExportReady` (false), `usernameChangedAt?`, `previousUsername?`, `previousUsernameExpiresAt?`, `userId?` (unique → User, SetNull - set when the row is the member half of a staff account; see the admin-link entry at the top), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Indexes: status, previousUsername, deletionScheduledAt, createdAt.
- `MemberPasskey` - `credentialId` (unique), `publicKey Bytes`, `counter BigInt default 0`, `transports String[]`, `deviceName?`, `lastUsedAt?`. Index memberId.
- `MemberPassword` - one per member (`memberId` unique), bcrypt `hash`.
- `MemberTwoFactor` - `method TwoFactorMethod`, `secretEncrypted?` (AES-256-GCM TOTP secret; null for EMAIL/SMS), `phoneEncrypted?` (AES-256-GCM phone; SMS method only), `verified` (false), `lastStep? BigInt` (TOTP replay guard). Unique (memberId, method).
- `MemberTrustedBrowser` - `tokenHash` (unique), `deviceInfo?`, `expiresAt`. Indexes memberId, expiresAt.
- `MemberSession` - `tokenHash` (unique), `ipAddress?`, `userAgent?`, `location?`, `lastActiveAt`, `expiresAt`. Indexes memberId, expiresAt.
- `MemberMagicLink` / `MemberVerificationToken` - `tokenHash` (unique), `usedAt?`, `expiresAt`. Indexes memberId, expiresAt.
- `MemberEmailChallenge` - `codeHash`, `purpose` (login_2fa | setup_2fa | email_change), `pendingEmail` (nullable; set only for `email_change` - the address being moved TO, so `Member.email` is untouched until a code sent there comes back), `expiresAt`, `attempts` (0). Indexes (memberId, purpose), expiresAt.
- `MemberRecoveryCode` - `codeHash` (unique), `usedAt?`. Index memberId.
- `MemberNotificationPreference` - `channel NotificationChannel` (EMAIL), `category` (core or module key), `digestMode DigestMode` (INSTANT), `enabled` (true). Unique (memberId, channel, category).
- `MemberConsentRecord` - `consentType`, `granted`, `ipAddress?`, `userAgent?`. Indexes memberId, createdAt.
- `MemberDataExportRequest` - `status DataExportStatus` (PENDING), `mediaId?` (Media id, no relation), `expiresAt?` (48h download cut-off), `completedAt?`. Indexes memberId, status.
- `MemberActivityEvent` - `type` (core or module key), `source?` (null = core, else module name), `metadata Json?`. Index (memberId, createdAt desc).
- `MemberProfileVisibility` - `memberId` unique; `showBio`/`showJoinDate`/`showWebsite` (all true).
- `MemberInvite` - `tokenHash` (unique), `createdById?`/`createdByName?` (admin snapshot, no relation), `usedAt?`, `usedByMemberId?`, `revokedAt?`, `expiresAt`. Index expiresAt. Single-use registration invites for INVITE_ONLY mode.
- `MemberAdminNote` - append-only: `authorId?`/`authorName?` (admin snapshot), `body Text`. Index (memberId, createdAt desc).
- `MemberAdminActionLog` - `actorId?`/`actorName?`, `action`, `detail Json?`. Index (memberId, createdAt desc).
- `EmailTemplate` - `key` (unique, e.g. `member.verify-email`, `shop.order-confirmed`), `subject?`, `bodyHtml? Text`, `wrapperLayoutId?`, `isActive` (default true), `updatedById?`. Admin overrides for the code-registry defaults in `lib/email/registry.ts`, covering core AND module emails. Absent row, or a null copy column, = use the default; reset-to-default nulls `subject`/`bodyHtml` rather than deleting the row, so the wrapper choice and on/off switch survive it. `wrapperLayoutId` is deliberately NOT a relation - a deleted wrapper falls back to the site default instead of cascading away someone's rewritten copy.

Enums: `SiteStatus` (live, comingSoon, maintenance); `PageStatus` (draft, published); `BodyFormat` (markdown, builder); `MediaProviderType` (B2, R2, S3, SPACES, WASABI, MINIO, VERCEL_BLOB, SUPABASE_STORAGE, CLOUDINARY, IMAGEKIT); `ModuleStatus` (pending_install, deploying, pending_deploy, active, inactive, failed, update_available); `NotificationType` (deployment, core_update, module_update, message); `MenuItemType` (PAGE, EXTERNAL, MODULE_ENTITY); `MenuItemVisibility` (PUBLIC, AUTHENTICATED, GUEST, ADMIN); `MemberStatus` (PENDING_VERIFICATION, PENDING_APPROVAL, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, DELETED); `AvatarChoice` (UPLOAD, GRAVATAR, GENERATED); `TwoFactorMethod` (EMAIL, AUTHENTICATOR_APP, SMS); `NotificationChannel` (EMAIL); `DigestMode` (INSTANT, DAILY, WEEKLY, DISABLED); `DataExportStatus` (PENDING, PROCESSING, READY, EXPIRED).

### Authentication

WebAuthn (passkeys):

- `@simplewebauthn/server` v13 in `lib/auth/passkey.ts`; browser side `@simplewebauthn/browser` loaded on demand.
- rpName "Cactus Foundation"; rpId = hostname of SITE_URL (hard-coded `localhost` in development); origin = SITE_URL. rpId cannot change once passkeys exist.
- Challenges persisted in `WebAuthnChallenge` with a 5-minute TTL, deleted on use or expiry; verify calls extract the challenge from the assertion's `clientDataJSON`.
- Registration uses a stable user handle (userId bytes) so Safari/iCloud Keychain retries do not conflict; `excludeCredentials` from existing passkeys; `residentKey: preferred`, `userVerification: required`, `requireUserVerification: true` (both registration and authentication). Member passkeys (`lib/members/passkey.ts`) now match this exactly.
- Passkeys store credentialId, COSE public key bytes, signature counter (updated on every authentication), transports, and a label derived from the user agent ("Chrome on macOS").
- Zero-passkey accounts have **no** register-and-login path (`register-login` was deleted): a fresh attestation proves someone holds *an* authenticator, not that they hold *the account*. They sign in by password + OTP, authenticator app, or recovery link, then enrol a passkey from Account → Security.
- `authenticate-options` (admin `/api/auth/passkey/authenticate-options` + member equivalent) always returns an unscoped challenge with empty `allowCredentials` (discoverable-credential flow), byte-identical regardless of whether the email maps to an account or has a passkey - so it can't be used to enumerate registered emails or harvest stored credential IDs.
- **Step-up on enrolment:** adding a new authenticator (passkey `register-options`+`register-verify`, TOTP/2FA `setup-options`, admin + member) requires the current session to have authenticated within `STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_MS` (10 min; `isCurrentSessionFresh` / `isCurrentMemberSessionFresh`, keyed on the session row's `createdAt`). A stale session gets a 403 with `reauthRequired: true`; the first-run setup window is exempt. Prevents a borrowed unlocked browser from planting a durable sign-in method.

Sessions:

- Cookie `cactus_session`: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, 24-hour lifetime (`SESSION_DURATION_MS` in `lib/auth/session.ts`).
- Server stores only `sha256(token + SESSION_SECRET)` in `Session.tokenHash`. Validation (`validateSessionWithMeta`): row lookup by hash, expiry check (expired rows deleted on touch), suspended-user check; returns `{ user, expiresAt }`. `validateSession` is a thin wrapper returning just the user.
- Server-side validation happens twice per admin request: in `proxy.ts` and again in the admin layout/route handlers via `getSessionFromCookie()`.
- `getSessionWithMeta()` is the React-`cache()`d cookie→session lookup; `getSessionFromCookie()` derives from it, so a render wanting both the user and the expiry still costs one query. `msUntilExpiry(expiresAt)` converts the expiry to a duration (kept out of component bodies - reading the clock mid-render trips `react-hooks/purity`).
- **Stale-tab sign-out:** an admin tab left open past the 24-hour limit used to keep showing the last-rendered screen until the next request bounced. `components/admin/SessionExpiryWatcher.tsx` (mounted by `AdminShell`, fed `sessionExpiresInMs` from the admin layout) now shows a corner warning banner 2 minutes out and then sends the tab to `/<adminPath>/login?next=<path>&expired=1`. `LoginForm` renders an `alert-info` notice on `?expired=1`. No polling and no extra requests - it is arithmetic against the browser's own clock, anchored at mount from a *duration* (not an absolute timestamp) so a badly-set client clock can't sign anyone out early. Timers re-arm in 15-minute chunks and recheck on `visibilitychange`/`focus`, because long timeouts are throttled in background tabs and stop entirely while a laptop sleeps. Deliberately a non-blocking banner, not a modal, so anyone mid-edit can still reach their save button.
- Trusted devices: cookie `cactus_trusted`, same hashing scheme, N days from `SiteConfig.trustDeviceDays` (default 28), expiry refreshed on valid use; lets password logins skip the email OTP.

Other mechanisms:

- Password login: bcrypt (12 rounds), minimum 8 chars, Pwned Passwords k-anonymity breach check (fails open); always second-factored by a 6-digit OTP (`EmailChallenge`, 10-minute TTL, 5 attempts, sha256-hashed, timing-safe compare) unless the device is trusted. Unavailable when email is not configured. The OTP goes by SMS instead of email when `User.smsOtpPhoneEncrypted` is set and an active module contributes a configured SMS provider (`lib/auth/sms.ts` `getActiveSmsProvider()` over the generated `lib/modules/sms-providers.ts`); any SMS failure falls back silently to email, verification unchanged (`/api/auth/email-code`). Login response gained `channel`/`destination` (masked phone) for the OTP-step copy.
- TOTP: otpauth SHA1/6-digit/30s, issuer "Cactus Foundation", secret AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest, ±1 window, replay-protected via monotonically increasing `totpLastStep`.
- Recovery: 32-byte token, sha256-hashed, 30-minute TTL, single-use; completion revokes all sessions and trusted devices. The emailed link's GET hands the token to the login page via a short-lived HttpOnly `cactus_recovery_token` cookie + `?recovery=1` flag (never `?recovery_token=` in the URL, which would leak into history/logs/Referer); the POST reads it from that cookie (body token still accepted for older links) and clears it on success.
- Password change (`/api/account/password`, `/api/members/password`): on any successful change, unconditionally revokes every other session and every trusted device/browser, keeping only the caller's session. The old opt-in `signOutOtherSessions` flag is ignored (still parsed for client compatibility). Stops a pre-existing trusted device from surviving the change and bypassing OTP/2FA.
- Rate limiting: in-database (`RateLimit` table), atomic check-and-record. Admin OTP verify (`/api/auth/email-code`) keys on both `ip:` and `account:${userId}` (was IP-only). Limits: login 10/15min, register 5/60min, recovery_request 3/60min, email_code 5/15min, passkey_authenticate 20/15min, consent 30/15min, totp_verify 5/15min, member_register 5/60min, member_magic_link 5/15min, member_login 10/15min, member_2fa 5/15min (Members system).
- Turnstile: applied to login, register, and recovery-request; fail-open when unconfigured, fail-closed on network error when configured.
- CSRF: SameSite=Lax cookie plus an explicit Origin-mismatch 403 for unsafe methods in `proxy.ts`.

Admin path obfuscation:

- The real admin URL prefix is a per-site secret string (`SiteConfig.adminPath`, unique, suggested as e.g. `lemon-x7k2p9`), resolved at the proxy from Edge Config or DB and rewritten to the internal `/cactus-admin/*` tree. Direct `/cactus-admin` access 404s; wrong prefixes fall through to a plain Next.js 404 indistinguishable from any missing route.
- What it hides: the location of the login page and admin UI from casual scanning.
- What it does not protect: it is not an authentication factor. All admin API routes under `/api/admin/*` sit at fixed, guessable URLs and rely entirely on session + permission checks; the admin path leaks to anyone with a valid session.

Members authentication (Phase 2 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md, protected/isolated-diff-per-sub-feature; fully separate from everything above - no shared tables, cookies, or code):

- Cookie `cactus_member_session`: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, sliding expiry off `membersConfig.sessionDays` (default 30d, refreshed on every valid check). Server stores `sha256(token + SESSION_SECRET)` in `MemberSession.tokenHash` (`lib/members/session.ts`), same hashing scheme as admin sessions.
- `validateMemberSession` only returns a member whose `status` is `ACTIVE` - PENDING_VERIFICATION/PENDING_APPROVAL/SUSPENDED/DELETED are all rejected even with an unexpired session row.
- Trusted browser: cookie `cactus_member_trusted`, same scheme, `membersConfig.trustedBrowserDays` (default 30d).
- Passkeys (`lib/members/passkey.ts`, `@simplewebauthn`, same rpId/origin as admin): login with an existing passkey (`/api/members/auth/passkey/authenticate-options`+`authenticate-verify`) and adding a passkey from an authenticated session (`register-options`+`register-verify`). No bootstrap-without-a-session path - see the Routes section note on why that would be unsafe for members specifically (no narrow one-time setup window the way admin has).
- Magic link (`lib/members/magic-link.ts`): 15-minute single-use emailed link, `/api/members/auth/magic-link/request`+`consume`. This is how a brand-new member gets their *first* session (they have no passkey yet and passwords are off by default) - hence it, not passkey, is what makes `/{memberAreaPath}/login` actually usable end-to-end.
- `loginRejectionForStatus` (`lib/members/registration.ts`) is the shared status gate every login method calls before creating a session: only ACTIVE passes; PENDING_VERIFICATION returns a `redirectToVerify` hint back to the Phase 1 holding page.
- Password + mandatory 2FA (`/api/members/auth/password/login` + `2fa/verify`): only reachable when `authMethodPolicies.PASSWORD` ≠ `OFF`; a password without a `MemberTwoFactor` row is treated as unusable (403) rather than allowing a password-only session, since 2FA is mandatory whenever passwords are on - actually setting up that first 2FA method is a Phase 3 Security-page action. Trusted browser (`isMemberBrowserTrusted`) skips the 2FA step entirely. A verified `SMS` method (phone in `MemberTwoFactor.phoneEncrypted`) takes priority over other methods when an active SMS provider module can deliver; SMS codes share the member email-challenge store (`login_2fa`), so `2fa/verify` treats EMAIL and SMS identically, and delivery falls back silently to email when the provider is unavailable. Factor selection (both `password/login` and `2fa/verify`) only ever picks a `verified` factor - an unverified row (secret generated but never confirmed) never gates login, and there is no unverified fallback. Recovery codes (`lib/members/recovery-codes.ts`) are an alternate second factor for a member who's lost their email/authenticator access.
- `/{memberAreaPath}/login` (`app/(public)/cactus-account/login/page.tsx` + `components/members/LoginForm.tsx`): identifier-first - email + "Continue", then only the methods that address has (`POST /api/members/auth/methods`): passkey, a password step branching into 2FA/recovery-code, and/or "email me a sign-in link" (link-only addresses skip the choice and have the link sent on Continue); auto-consumes a `?magic_token=` on load; `?redirect=` is sanitised to same-origin relative paths only (open-redirect guard) - set by the account layout's session gate and by the shop's gated `/shop/account/*` pages, and additionally dropped when it points back at a signed-out member page (loop guard, see the Pages section).
- Logout: `POST /api/members/auth/logout` (single, redirects `/logged-out`) and `POST /api/members/auth/logout-all` (every session, forces full re-auth - unlike admin's "revoke all" which preserves the caller's own).
- **Phase 2 (Authentication) is now fully built.** Phase 3 (member account area) is also complete - see the Member account API and member-area Pages entries above. Next up: Phase 4 (public profile).

### Permissions System

Core keys (registered by `seedCorePermissions()` in `lib/permissions/check.ts` at setup):

- `pages.read` - view info pages including drafts (admin page list, page GET/history APIs, page-preview route).
- `pages.write` - create/edit pages (POST/PATCH/autosave).
- `pages.publish` - publish pages (publish endpoint; also required to create a page already published).
- `pages.delete` - delete pages (single + bulk).
- `users.manage` - view and manage users (users page + API).
- `media.upload` - upload media.
- `media.delete` - delete media.
- `roles.manage` - Settings → Users → Roles subtab + role/permission APIs.
- `modules.manage` - module list/install/update/uninstall/directory; also grants GitHub App status read.
- `config.manage` - settings GET/PATCH, notifications, updates, media migration, redeploy dismiss, deployment logs, GitHub App flow.
- `menus.manage` - all menu APIs; also gates menu assignment from the page editor.
- `appearance.manage` - design-token PATCH.
- `layouts.manage` - layout read/create/update/delete/publish, and `/layout-preview/[id]`. Every layout route gates on it, reads included.
- `members.manage` / `members.list` / `members.view` / `members.edit` / `members.suspend` / `members.delete` / `members.invite` / `members.approve` / `members.trust` / `members.notes` / `members.settings` / `members.gdpr` - Members system admin permissions (registered in Phase 0; enforcing routes/UI land in later Members phases - see MEMBERS_SPEC.md).

Module-registered keys (declared in each module's `cactus.module.json`, registered on install): `contact.view`, `contact.reply`, `contact.delete`, `contact.export` (contact-form); `replycatcher.manage` (contact-form-reply-catcher); `boards.access`, `boards.manage`, `boards.moderate` (boards); `directory.access`, `directory.manage` (directory); `gazette.access`, `gazette.contributor`, `gazette.author`, `gazette.editor` (gazette); `shop.access`, `shop.manage`, `shop.products`, `shop.orders`, `shop.customers`, `shop.discounts`, `shop.reports` (shop); `twilio.manage` (twilio); `googlesheets.manage` (google-sheet-products-for-shop, built but not yet registered). Stored in `Permission` with `module` set; deleted on module uninstall.

Where checks occur:

- Protected roles (`Role.isProtected`, only "Admin" is seeded) bypass every check (`hasPermission` short-circuits; `isAdmin()` = `role.isProtected`).
- `proxy.ts`: session validity only (plus `isProtected` for the site-status bypass and the redeploy trap); no per-permission checks.
- API routes: `getSessionFromCookie()` + `hasPermission(user, key)` per handler (see the Routes section for each route's key).
- UI: server components branch on `hasPermission`/`isAdmin` (page buttons, nav module entries via manifest `permission`); client editors fetch `/api/admin/pages/perms` for capability flags.
- Cross-cutting guards: `assertProtectedUserWouldRemain` (transactional last-admin invariant on delete/demote/self-delete), `canActOnUser` (only admins act on protected-role users).

### Admin UI

Navigation (defined in `components/admin/AdminNav.tsx`): Dashboard; then any ungrouped module nav entries (no `navGroupLabel` - currently just contact-form's Inbox); Content → Pages, Menus, Media; System → Users, Styles, Layouts, Modules, Settings; then labelled module nav groups (own named section, e.g. Gazette, Boards); footer: My Account, Sign out, version. Sidebar collapses to a rail (auto-collapses inside Puck editors), mobile drawer with backdrop; toolbar has collapse toggle, ThemeToggle, NotificationBell. When collapsed, each icon link shows a custom hover/focus tooltip to its right (label text) instead of the native `title`: a `createPortal`-to-`<body>` fixed-positioned `.admin-nav-tip` (visuals match `.theme-toggle-tip`), because the nav scroll container's `overflow-x: hidden` would clip a pure-CSS tooltip; collapsed links also carry `aria-label` for the accessible name. Each labelled section is independently collapsible (click the label, chevron flips) - state persisted per-label in `localStorage` (`cactus-sidebar-sections-collapsed`), defaults to all sections maximised; only visible when the rail itself isn't collapsed. There is no standalone Members section, People section, or Roles link any more (all removed in an admin-UI reorganisation - see below and the top-of-file changelog); Users lives in System now.

**Sidebar is now server-resolved (2026-07-15).** The hardcoded `NAV_SECTIONS` array is gone; `AdminNav` renders a `sections` prop the server layout builds via `resolveAdminMenu` (`lib/nav/admin-menu.ts`) from core items + module groups + the saved `SiteConfig.adminMenuConfig` + this user's permissions. Core items each declare a stable id and any-of default permission keys (`pages.read`, `users.manage`, …) so a role that can't use a screen no longer sees its menu item; `isProtected` admins bypass all visibility (seeing hidden/restricted items with a small lock/eye-off badge) so they can't hide the editor from themselves. Client UX added in `AdminNav`: a filter box, a Favourites pinned group + Recently-visited group (both `localStorage`), a per-item route-change loading spinner, roving Up/Down keyboard nav, auto-expand of the active section + scroll-into-view, a Quick "New…" create menu (deep-links collected from visible items), expand/collapse-all, and empty-section hiding. `AdminShell` mounts `CommandPalette` (Cmd/Ctrl+K fuzzy jump over all destinations; `?` opens a shortcuts overlay; also openable from a new sidebar-toolbar search button). The menu builder itself is the Settings → Navigation tab (see Settings tabs + `NavBuilder.tsx`).
