Whether a module is *installed* is a database fact and is not decided here - `GET /api/admin/emails/templates` filters the list by `getInstalledModuleNames()` before showing anything. Six modules use it: shop (10), quote-for-shop (4), reviews-for-shop (2), boards (2), twilio (2), contact-form (2).
- `scripts/generate-module-extension-points.mjs` - collects `extensionPoints` from every module manifest (`{point, id, permission, import, component}`); writes the gitignored `lib/modules/extension-points.ts` (`moduleExtensionPointComponents: Record<point, Record<id, Component>>`), grouped by the arbitrary `point` string. Core has no knowledge of any specific point name - a *publishing* module (e.g. `contact-form`) defines its own point names in its own page code and permission-filters live from `Module.manifest` (same pattern as `navEntries`/`settingsTabs`); a *contributing* module (e.g. `contact-form-reply-catcher`) declares entries against that point name in its manifest. See the "Module extension points" section in wiki/Authoring-a-module.md. First core (not module) publisher: `app/cactus-admin/config/page.tsx` (the Settings → Users → Roles subtab) reads `core.roles-page` the same way. **Import dedupe (2026-07-23, shared by this generator, `generate-module-puck.mjs`, `generate-module-settings-tabs.mjs` and `generate-module-sms-providers.mjs`):** each keeps an `ident → importPath` map and emits an import line once. A module legitimately contributes the same component to two extension points (or two settings tabs, or two Puck block types), and the emitted identifier is derived from module name + component name, so the same import line was written twice and the generated file did not compile. Re-emitting is silently collapsed; the same identifier mapping to a DIFFERENT path is a real name clash and throws, failing the build rather than emitting a duplicate declaration. `generate-module-puck.mjs` keeps two separate maps, one per generated file, since the client and RSC imports live in different modules.
- `scripts/generate-module-layout-types.mjs` - collects `layoutTypes` from every module manifest; writes the gitignored `lib/layout/module-layout-types.ts` (pure data: groups + flat type→group lookup, each type optionally carrying `editorPreview: {className?, maxWidth?}`) and `lib/setup/module-starter-layouts.ts` (starter-template loader functions, imported per module). See "Module-declared layout types" under Puck Integration above.
- `scripts/generate-media-worker.mjs` - build-step: transpiles the Cloudflare media Worker (`workers/media-worker/index.ts`) to a plain ES module via `typescript` and embeds it as a string constant the app reads at runtime, so the admin > Settings > Media "Deploy Worker automatically" flow (`POST /api/admin/media/deploy-worker`) can upload runnable JavaScript to the user's Cloudflare account without a runtime transpile (`typescript` is a devDependency, pruned from the production runtime).
- `scripts/run-module-migrations.mjs` - build-step-only runner: for modules with status active/deploying/update_available, applies unapplied `modules/<name>/migrations/*.sql` files in lexicographic order, each in a transaction, recording name+checksum in `ModuleMigration`. The applied-migration ledger is read **once** into a Set up front, not one SELECT per (module, migration file) pair - with seven modules and several migrations each that was dozens of Neon round trips on every deploy purely to establish that there was nothing to do, which is the outcome on every build except the one that introduces a migration. The skip decision itself is unchanged. **Stale-ledger self-heal (2026-07-15):** before the per-module skip loop, if a module has recorded migrations in the ledger yet **no** table with its `tablePrefix` exists, the ledger is treated as stale (a restored/branched DB that carried the `ModuleMigration` rows but not the module's actual tables - which are not in a backup's schema section), its ledger rows are purged and its migrations re-applied from scratch. Restricted to the zero-prefixed-tables case so a healthy install is untouched and a non-idempotent `CREATE TABLE` can't collide. This is what recovered the live dwoffice.furniture contact-form/twilio tables after a restore left the ledger lying.
- `scripts/flush-pooled-plans.mjs` - build-step-only, runs last in `build-migrate.mjs` after every DDL step. Ends idle backends on the database so Postgres rebuilds their cached query plans against the new schema. Postgres plans a prepared statement against the table shape it saw at prepare time, and `SELECT *` makes that shape every column of the table; change the table and the next execution on a connection still holding that plan fails with `cached plan must not change result type` (SQLSTATE 0A000). A deploy normally replaces its own connections, but Neon's pooled endpoint is pgBouncer and its **server** connections outlive the deployment, while our DDL deliberately runs on the direct endpoint and never touches them - so a schema change strands stale plans on the pool for as long as pgBouncer keeps those connections. The symptom is a half-working site: requests landing on a fresh pooled connection succeed, requests landing on an old one 500, varying request to request. This is what broke every product page on dwoffice.furniture after v0.5.578 (shop `005_price_types` dropped `compare_at_price` and added sale/retail/trade, leaving `SELECT * FROM "shp_products"` planned against the old column list; shop-variations' `getVariantSelectorPayload` and a Google Sheet push both threw P2010/0A000 until the connections aged out on their own). Terminates via the direct endpoint (asking pgBouncer to end pgBouncer's connections just routes back through the pool), **idle backends only** so nothing in flight on the still-serving old deployment is interrupted, in two passes 3s apart to catch backends that were mid-query on the first. Skips only without DATABASE_URL. Best-effort: it never exits non-zero, so it cannot fail a deploy. **It had never once run on a pooled install before 2026-07-19.** `build-migrate.mjs` gives its children a DATABASE_URL already rewritten to the direct endpoint, so this script's `-pooler` test was reading a hostname with `-pooler` stripped out, concluding "not a pooled connection" and exiting having cleared nothing - on exactly the installs it was written for. Fixed on both sides: `build-migrate.mjs` now passes the site's real `DATABASE_URL` to this step alone (`runWithRetry`'s `childEnv` option), and the pooled/direct test no longer gates the sweep - it only picks the log line, because a wrong answer there is silent and surfaces as a broken site one migration later. The runtime retry in `lib/db/stale-plan.ts` is the actual guarantee; this script keeps that retry rare rather than routine, and cannot cover connections opened after the build.
- `scripts/sync-module-manifests.mjs` - build-step-only: rewrites `Module.manifest` from each deployed module's `cactus.module.json` so nav entries/teardown stay in step with shipped code. Skips without DATABASE_URL.
- `scripts/sync-wiki.mjs` - `npm run sync-wiki`: pulls all `.md` files from the GitHub wiki repo (`WIKI_SOURCE_REPO` or GITHUB_REPO + `.wiki`) into `/wiki` via the API.
- `scripts/fetch-google-fonts.mjs` - standalone maintenance script (own npm script, not in the build): fetches the Google Fonts metadata catalogue and writes `lib/design/google-fonts.json`, the source for the admin font pickers. Run manually to refresh the available-fonts list.
- `scripts/dev-warm.sh` - `npm run dev:warm`: kills anything on the port, clears `.next`, starts `next dev --webpack` (webpack chosen over Turbopack to avoid an HMR chunk-hash reload cascade), and pre-warms `/`, `/home`, `/logged-out`, `/setup`, `/style-guide`, `/privacy-policy` in the background.

Build-time order (from `package.json` `build`, which is now just `prebuild.mjs && next build`): checkout-modules, then three concurrent branches - (a) prisma generate, (b) build-migrate (migrate deploy → reconcile-core-schema → run-module-migrations) → sync-module-manifests, (c) generate-all (generate-module-router → generate-module-puck → generate-module-cron → generate-module-settings-tabs → generate-module-sms-providers → generate-module-extension-points → generate-module-layout-types → generate-media-worker → generate-module-email-templates) - then `next build`. Dev (`npm run dev`) runs the generators then `next dev --webpack`.

### Build and Deploy

- Build steps in order: see Scripts above. `npm run build` is the single entry; Vercel runs it on every push. It is `node scripts/prebuild.mjs && next build`, where the prebuild is `checkout-modules` (barrier) followed by `prisma generate`, the `build-migrate` → `sync-module-manifests` database chain, and `generate-all` running concurrently.
- **Turbopack's build filesystem cache is on** (`next.config.ts` → `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: true`). It persists the compilation cache in `.next/cache`, which Vercel already restores from the previous deployment (the "Restored build cache from previous deployment" line in the build log). Without it the full Turbopack compile - 41s of a measured 103s deploy - was paid on every push regardless of how small the diff was. It is still flagged experimental in Next 16, so if a deploy ever produces stale or impossible output, this is the first thing to switch off.
- **`next build` does NOT type-check.** `next.config.ts` sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true`. Measured on a real Vercel build, the `tsc` pass inside `next build` was 26s of a 123s deploy, and it duplicated the `tsc --noEmit` gate that CLAUDE.md's work loop already requires on every change. The check moved, it was not dropped: **`npm run typecheck` is now the only thing standing between a type error and production**, so it is not optional before a commit. There is deliberately no CI workflow enforcing it - `lib/updates/core-plan.ts` excludes only `modules/`, `modules.json` and `.gitmodules` from the core-update push, so a `.github/workflows/*` file would propagate into every customer's repo and run CI on their GitHub account. Adding one means excluding `.github/` from the core sync first.
- Prisma migrations run only inside the Vercel build step (`build-migrate.mjs` → `prisma migrate deploy`), never at runtime; the advisory lock is disabled because Vercel serialises builds and Neon cold starts exceed the lock timeout. One migration file exists, edited in place for schema changes (fresh-install platform). Because migrate deploy never re-applies an edited-in-place migration, additive core changes reach already-provisioned installs via idempotent `prisma/core-reconcile/*.sql` run by `reconcile-core-schema.mjs` immediately after migrate deploy.
- `prisma db push` is blocked (`npm run db:push` exits 1 with a message).
- Vercel-specific: `vercel.json` is generated (cron entries only) and gitignored; deployments are auto-triggered by pushes to `main`; env-var-only changes use the redeploy API (`POST /v13/deployments?forceNew=1` based on the latest production deployment); module/core changes deploy via Git Data API commits (registry sync / core sync) whose push triggers the build; the redeploy gate (`pendingRedeployId` sentinel → real id → cleared on READY / webhook / dismiss / 4-minute server timeout) drives the admin shell's deploy status bar and the notification bell's live section meanwhile. Deployment status arrives via webhook (Pro) or lazy polling (`getLatestDeploymentStatus`, Hobby).
- jsdom is pinned to `^26` (jsdom 29 breaks the Vercel serverless update check with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM).
- Tester repo relationship: `usersaynoso/Cactus-Foundation-Tester` is a downstream install of this platform used for live testing; local `.env.local` points at the same Neon database as the live Tester site. Pushes to the Tester repo use the identity `Chris Taylor-Guest <airings.snug-0m@icloud.com>` and version-prefixed commit titles; core code reaches it via the in-app core-update sync (blob-level tree diff of core files vs the matching upstream tag, skipping `modules/`, `.gitmodules`, `modules.json`).
- Release flow (per CLAUDE.md): patch-only version bumps, tag format `vX.Y.Z`, GitHub release created immediately after every push.

### Slash Commands

None. `.claude/commands/` does not exist. `.claude/` contains only `settings.json` (permission allowlist + `caveman@caveman` plugin enablement) and runtime state files. Available slash commands come from installed plugins, not this repo.

### Utilities and Lib

`lib/` root:

- `admin/search-index.ts` - `ADMIN_SEARCH_ENTRIES`: static, framework-agnostic registry the command palette adds on top of the nav (Settings tabs, their sections, and individual settings). Each entry: `{ id, label, section (breadcrumb), path (admin-relative, incl. `?tab=`/`?sub=`/`#hash`), keywords?, requires? (nav base path gate) }`. `search-index.test.ts` statically asserts unique ids, admin-relative paths, known `requires` values, and that **every `#hash` resolves to a real `id="…"` anchor** in `ConfigPageClient.tsx` (the one invariant tsc/eslint can't see). Adding a searchable setting = one entry here + a matching `id`/`admin-anchor` on the page.
- `deploy-log-translator.ts` - `translateLogLine(raw)`: maps Vercel build-log lines to friendly British-humour status messages (null = drop the line). Final line marker: "Bish bash bosh. You're live."
- `deploy-log-translator.test.ts` - vitest unit tests for the translator (run via `npm test`; no vitest config file exists).
- `markdown-client.ts` - browser-only markdown → sanitised HTML (marked + DOMPurify on `window`); identical allow-list to the server renderer.
- `sanitize.ts` - server/browser markdown → sanitised HTML; lazy-requires jsdom on the server; strips raw angle brackets pre-parse; also `markdownToPlainText`, `sanitizeRichText` (Puck RichText allow-list) and `sanitizeAndObfuscateRichText` (published RichText: sanitise first, obfuscate after - DOMPurify's re-serialisation decodes the obfuscator's entities, so the reverse order leaks the plain address; test: `lib/sanitize-obfuscate.test.ts`).
- `sanitize-config.ts` - shared `ALLOWED_TAGS`/`ALLOWED_ATTR` constants for both renderers.
- `email-obfuscate.tsx` - email spam-protection server half. `encodeEmail` = base64 of reversed address (the `data-eml` payload). For text: `linkifyEmails(text)` → React nodes (`<ObfuscatedEmail>` per match, entity-encoded visible text + `data-eml`); `obfuscateEmailsInHtml(html)` → same anchor markup spliced into text runs, entity-masking (not wrapping) inside `<a>`, rewriting a hand-written `href="mailto:…"` to `data-eml`, leaving `<code>/<pre>` verbatim. For owner-typed links: `emailSafeHref(href, obfuscate)` → `{href}` for ordinary links, `{'data-eml'}` and **no href** for a `mailto:` (query string preserved); `maskEmailText(label, obfuscate)` → entity-encoded `<span>` for label text inside an anchor, which can't be linkified without nesting an `<a>`. Consumed by every block in `config.tsx` (free text via the local `protectText` gate, hrefs via `emailSafeHref`) when `!puck.isEditing`, plus `MenuBlockClient.tsx`; client half is `components/EmailDeobfuscator.tsx`. Tests: `lib/email-obfuscate.test.ts`.
- `utils.ts` - `generateSlug`, `generateId` (nanoid), `parsePaginationParams` (page/perPage/skip, perPage ≤ 100), `errorResponse`, `successResponse`, `truncate`, `formatInTimezone`, `isHttpUrl` (2026-07-23). `isHttpUrl(value)` is the scheme allow-list for any owner- or member-supplied address that will end up in an `href` or an iframe `src`: it parses the trimmed value as a URL and accepts only `http:`/`https:`, so `javascript:` and `data:` (stored XSS) are rejected along with `mailto:`/`tel:`/relative values a website field is never meant to hold. Zod's `.url()` is not a substitute - it accepts `javascript:…` quite happily, which is exactly how a member `websiteUrl` reached the public profile page. Applied at every write path that stores such a URL (`app/api/members/profile/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/members/[id]/route.ts`) AND at the render path (`app/(public)/members/[username]/page.tsx`), since rows written before the guard existed are still in the database; also gates the Puck Embed block's `src` and, via a protocol test inside `toEmbedUrl`, the Video block's.

`lib/members/`:

- `config.ts` - `MembersConfigSchema` (Zod, all Members settings with defaults: enabled false, registrationMode OPEN, emailVerificationRequired true, registrationCollectUsername/registrationCollectDisplayName/registrationCollectPassword true (off hides the field on the register form and makes the API ignore anything sent for it), authMethodPolicies { PASSKEY: OPTIONAL, MAGIC_LINK: OPTIONAL, PASSWORD: OFF }, trustedBrowserDays 30, sessionDays 30, avatar/gravatar toggles true, siteWideMembersOnly false + exceptions [], guestPreviewEnabled false, username changes off with 90/30-day cooldown/redirect, deletionGracePeriodDays 14, domain allow/blocklists [], profileVisibility PUBLIC, accountSectionsEnabled all true, directoryEnabled false, smsTwoFactorPolicy OPTIONAL - OPTIONAL|REQUIRED, whether members with a password must enrol a mobile number for SMS sign-in codes; REQUIRED only bites while an SMS provider module is active, see `sms-policy.ts` below), `parseMembersConfig` (corrupt column falls back to defaults), `getMembersConfig`, `getMembersConfigCached` (5s TTL for proxy reads), `invalidateMembersConfigCache`. Also `AccountSectionKey` + `isAccountSectionEnabled(config, key)` - the one accessor for the account-tab switches, used by the tab bar, the Overview cards, the Profile page's own `notFound()` gate and the routes that page saves through. Also `AUTH_METHODS`/`AUTH_METHOD_LABELS` and the accessors `authMethodPolicy`/`registrationPasswordPolicy`/`isAuthMethodEnabled`/`isAuthMethodRequired`/`enabledAuthMethods` - every caller goes through these rather than reading the map directly, because `MAGIC_LINK`'s own type is only `OFF|OPTIONAL` (nothing to enrol: the credential is a verified mailbox, so REQUIRED would mean exactly what OPTIONAL already means) and a direct `=== 'REQUIRED'` on it is a type error. Each field carries a `.catch` so one unrecognised stored value falls back per method instead of dropping the whole members config - and with it `enabled` - back to defaults. `normaliseLegacyAuthMethods` reads rows written under the previous `allowedAuthMethods` array + `passwordsEnabled` boolean pair (both had to agree before passwords were offered, so only that combination maps to `PASSWORD: OPTIONAL`); nothing is written back, the first admin save persists the new shape and Zod drops the old keys. Covered by `lib/members/auth-policy.test.ts`.
- `account-sections.ts` - `PROFILE_SECTION_OFF_MESSAGE` + `profileSectionOffResponse()`, the shared 403 returned by every route the member Profile page saves through (`/api/members/{profile,profile-visibility,avatar,username}`) when `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` is off. One message rather than four, so a member who left the page open before an admin switched it off gets a consistent answer. 403 not 404: the route exists, the site has stopped offering it, matching the `avatarUploadsEnabled` refusal alongside it.
- `auth-policy.ts` - what "required" actually means. `ENROLABLE_AUTH_METHODS = ['PASSKEY','PASSWORD']` (the two a member holds something for); `outstandingAuthSetup(config, held)` pure rules + `memberOutstandingAuthSetup(config, memberId)` I/O wrapper, returning the required methods a member has yet to set up - a password only counts as done once a verified `MemberTwoFactor` exists alongside it, since password login refuses outright without one and calling it satisfied would strand the member at the sign-in screen; `newMembersCanSignIn(config, emailConfigured)` (false without the email sign-in link: passkeys and passwords are both enrolled from inside an account a brand-new member cannot yet reach - drives the admin warning); `hasAnyAuthMethod(config)` (guards the settings save). Unit-tested in `lib/members/auth-policy.test.ts`.
- `paths.ts` - `MEMBER_INTERNAL = '/cactus-account'`, `DEFAULT_MEMBER_AREA_PATH = 'account'`, `getMemberAreaPath()` (sanitised MEMBER_AREA_PATH env var; invalid or blocklisted values fall back to the default, `account` itself exempt from the blocklist check), `MEMBER_PUBLIC_SUBPATHS = ['/login','/register','/verify-email']` and `isPublicMemberPath(fullPath, basePath)` (pure, unit-tested in `lib/members/paths.test.ts`; query-string tolerant, trailing-slash tolerant, prefix-exact so `/account/logins` does not match, and false for anything outside the member area so a site's own `/login` page is left alone). Used by the account layout's session gate and by the login page's redirect loop guard. Also `MEMBER_SETUP_SIGNIN_SUBPATH = '/setup-signin'` + `isSetupSignInPath(fullPath, basePath)` - the one page the required-setup gate must let through, or it would redirect to itself for ever; unlike the public subpaths it needs a session.
- `sms-policy.ts` - `memberNeedsSmsEnrolment(config, twoFactorConfigs)`: true only when `smsTwoFactorPolicy` is REQUIRED, the member has no verified SMS `MemberTwoFactor` row, AND an SMS provider module is active/configured (`getActiveSmsProvider`) - no provider means the policy silently behaves as OPTIONAL. Consumed by the password login + 2fa verify routes (`smsEnrolmentRequired` response flag → `LoginForm.tsx` `finishLogin` redirects to the account overview instead of `redirectTo`) and by the member account layout (warning banner, shown only to members who actually have a password).
- `tokens.ts` - hashed single-use tokens for member verification links (mirrors `lib/auth/recovery.ts`): `generateMemberToken`/`hashMemberToken`, `createVerificationToken`/`consumeVerificationToken` (`MemberVerificationToken`, 24h TTL), `canResendVerification` (60s per-member throttle, keyed off the latest token row regardless of used/unused).
- `registration.ts` - `isUsernameFormatValid`/`isUsernameAvailable` (format regex + blocklist + `Member.username` uniqueness), `generateUsernameFromEmail` (for sites with `registrationCollectUsername` off: email local part sanitised to `[a-z0-9_-]`, trimmed to 20 chars, `member` when nothing usable survives, plus 4 crypto-random digits - 8 after 15 collisions - re-checked through `isUsernameAvailable` each try and throwing after 25; covered by `lib/members/registration.test.ts`), `isEmailDomainAllowed` (allow/blocklist against `membersConfig`), `deriveInitialStatus`/`deriveActivatedStatus` (status a `Member` is created with vs. the status it moves to once verified, per `registrationMode`; verification is only "required" when both `emailVerificationRequired` is true AND email is actually configured, otherwise there'd be no way to ever satisfy it), `validateInviteToken`/`consumeInviteToken` (`MemberInvite`, single-use), `sendVerificationEmail` (shared by the register route and the resend route), `loginRejectionForStatus` (single source of truth for every login method: null when a status may sign in (ACTIVE only), else `{error, redirectToVerify?}`).
- `session.ts` - member session/cookie layer, fully separate from `lib/auth/session.ts`: `createMemberSession`/`validateMemberSession` (ACTIVE-only, sliding expiry) /`deleteMemberSession`/`deleteAllMemberSessions`/`listMemberSessions`/`revokeMemberSessionById`, cookie helpers (`cactus_member_session`), `getMemberFromCookie`; trusted-browser twin `createMemberTrustedBrowser`/`isMemberBrowserTrusted`/`revokeAllMemberTrustedBrowsers` (cookie `cactus_member_trusted`). Durations read from `membersConfig.sessionDays`/`trustedBrowserDays` via `getMembersConfigCached`.
- `passkey.ts` - WebAuthn registration/authentication for members, mirrors `lib/auth/passkey.ts` against `Member`/`MemberPasskey`; reuses `WebAuthnChallenge` with `memberId` set and `member_registration`/`member_authentication` purposes instead of a second challenge table.
- `magic-link.ts` - `sendMagicLink`/`consumeMagicLink`, hashed single-use `MemberMagicLink` tokens (15-min TTL, plain sha256 like `tokens.ts` - status gating happens at the route, not here).
- `email-challenge.ts` - mirrors `lib/auth/email-challenge.ts` against `MemberEmailChallenge`; `createMemberEmailChallenge(memberId, purpose, pendingEmail?)`/`verifyMemberEmailChallenge` (its success branch returns `pendingEmail`, the row's only survivor since verifying deletes it)/`pendingMemberEmailChange(memberId)`, purposes `login_2fa`/`setup_2fa`/`email_change`, 10-min TTL, 5 attempts, hash compare.
- `recovery-codes.ts` - `generateMemberRecoveryCodes` (10 codes, shown once, replaces any unused set), `consumeMemberRecoveryCode`, `countRemainingRecoveryCodes`.
- `activity.ts` - `recordMemberActivity` (`source: null` = core, else the contributing module name), `listMemberActivity`.

- `export.ts` - `assembleMemberExport` (core tables + each active module's `memberExtensions.dataExportPath`, called over self-origin HTTP with an internal bearer derived from `SESSION_SECRET` - `verifyInternalExportBearer` is exported for a module's own handler to check it), `createDataExportRequest` (assemble→upload→ready, synchronously within the request; refuses a second request while one is in flight; deletes the stuck row on failure rather than leaving it stuck, since the schema has no FAILED status), `expireDataExports` (cron target, 48h).
- `admin-log.ts` - `logMemberAdminAction(actor, memberId, action, detail?)`, writes a `MemberAdminActionLog` row (actor snapshot, not a live relation - survives the admin user being deleted later).
- `admin-notify.ts` - `notifyAdminMemberPendingApproval`/`notifyAdminMemberDeletionRequested`: in-app alert (reuses the generic `message` `NotificationType` + `upsertAlert` dedupe - members have no dedicated notification type of their own) + an email to every protected-role admin when email is configured (both render through the registry now - `member.deletion-admin-notify` and the new `member.pending-approval-admin-notify`, which was the last inline send in here). Gating on `notifyAdminOnPendingApproval`/`adminNotifyOnDeletion` happens at the call site, not in here.
- `digest.ts` - `runDigest('DAILY'|'WEEKLY')`, see the Email section.
- `access.ts` - pure matching logic for `proxy.ts`'s Phase 8 site-access gate: `isPathExcepted`, `resolveRouteTier` (no I/O, unit-testable in isolation from the session/DB lookups that surround them in proxy.ts).
- `avatar.ts` - `resolveEffectiveAvatarChoice`, see Media Layer section.

`lib/db/prisma.ts` - global-singleton PrismaClient (query logging in development), extended with `stalePlanRetryExtension`: a `$allOperations` wrapper that replays a query once when Postgres rejects it with `cached plan must not change result type` (SQLSTATE 0A000). Migrations run in the build step against a database whose pooled connections outlive the deploy, so a migration adding a column leaves live backends holding prepared plans that no longer match the table and every query using one throws until replayed - this took the live shop's product pages, product editor and CSV export down after shop `006_supplier.sql` on 2026-07-19, and needed a Neon compute restart to clear. The extension covers raw queries as well as model calls, and every module imports this client, so the guard is platform-wide. `stalePlanRetryExtension` and the `ExtendedPrismaClient` type are exported: an extended client is structurally not a `PrismaClient` (no `$on`), so anything taking the shared client as a parameter is typed `ExtendedPrismaClient` (`lib/backup/restore.ts`, `lib/setup/stylesInfoPage.ts`), and clients built elsewhere (the backup round-trip test's throwaway database) apply the same extension so they behave like the one the site runs on.

`lib/db/stale-plan.ts` - `isStalePlanError` (matches on the message, deliberately not on SQLSTATE 0A000, which is Postgres's generic "feature not supported" and covers errors that must not be retried) and `retryOnStalePlan` (one replay only; the first failure is what evicts the stale plan). Unit-tested in `lib/db/stale-plan.test.ts` against the error shape captured from the live 2026-07-19 deployment log.

`lib/deploy/`: `lock.ts` (2026-07-23 - `STALE_LOCK_MS` (15 minutes) and `getActiveDeployLock()`, the single reader every acquire/check site uses for the `DeployLock` singleton: install, update, core update and uninstall. A lock is normally released by the handler that took it, by the Vercel deploy webhook or by the redeploy-status handler, but a function hard-killed by a Vercel timeout or OOM runs none of those, and the stranded row then made every later install/update return a permanent 409 "install in progress" with no way out from the UI. A lock older than the threshold is treated as orphaned, deleted, and reported as absent; the delete is scoped to the exact `id` + `lockedAt` pair so a fresh lock taken in the window between read and delete is never removed by mistake. 15 minutes comfortably exceeds the longest legitimate hold - a 60s route plus the Vercel build it triggers), `reconcile.ts` (`markModulesDeploySucceeded` - promotes pendingVersion, clears alerts; `markModulesDeployFailed` - reverts to update_available or failed), `redeploy.ts` (`startDeferredRedeploy` - arms the redeploy gate synchronously, then in `after()` syncs modules.json or falls back to an env-var redeploy, and polls Vercel for the new deployment id). Both git-push paths (a modules.json commit, and `committedSince` mode where the caller already pushed) go through `captureOrTrigger`: poll first so the push's own build is adopted rather than double-deployed, then, only if no build ever appears, start one via `ensureVercelRedeploy`. Without that fallback a push that produces no build (missed webhook) is never retried by anything - the commit sits unbuilt while module rows are promoted to versions whose code never deployed.

`lib/design/tokens.ts` - `DesignTokens` v2 type, `DEFAULT_DESIGN_TOKENS`, `COLOUR_PRESETS`, `buildTokenStyles` (tokens → CSS custom properties for the public site), `buildAdminThemeStyles` (primary-colour family + `--font-sans` only, for admin white-labelling), `buildFontHref` (Google Fonts URL for non-system fonts). Every `themeStyle` colour has an optional `*Dark` sibling (`colourDark`, `hoverColourDark`, `textColourDark`, `bgColourDark`, `borderColourDark`, `labelColourDark`); `buildTokenStyles` emits each as a CSS var (`--color-link`, `--body-color`, `--btn-bg`, `--field-text`, `--h1-color`, …), redefines only the overridden ones in the `[data-theme="dark"]` + `@media(prefers-color-scheme:dark)` blocks, and its scoped `main …` rules reference those vars so a dark override cascades on the frontend (unset → inherits the light value). `ColourPreset` carries `linkColourDark`/`linkHoverColourDark` alongside the light pair, so applying a preset seeds dark-mode link colours too. `buttons.secondary`/`.outline` (`ButtonVariantStyle`) and `themeStyle.badges` (`Partial<Record<BadgeColourKey, BadgeStyle>>`, `BADGE_COLOUR_KEYS` export) follow the same optional-field/`*Dark`-sibling pattern; `themeStyle.pillRadius` is a plain string (no dark variant - a radius, not a colour), emitted as `--radius-pill` alongside the fixed `--radius-sm`/`-md`/`-lg` in the same `fixed` CSS-var string.

`lib/email/index.ts` - transport + the typed helpers, see Email section. `lib/email/registry.ts` - the single template registry (core defaults + the module seam). `lib/email/render.ts` - override lookup, `{{tag}}`/`{{#if}}` interpolation, wrapper resolution. `lib/email/blocks.ts` - the email block set as pure `toHtml()` functions (no React, no client imports; shared by the Puck editor config and the renderer). `lib/email/wrapper.ts` - walks an `emailWrapper` layout's Puck data into the final HTML document. `lib/email/palette.ts` - design tokens flattened to colour/font lookups (client-safe, so the layout editor can use it too). `lib/email/templates.ts` - the members-only sending rule (notification-preference gate) that survived the move.

`lib/github/client.ts` - see GitHub API Integration. `lib/github/retry.ts` - shared Git Data API resilience: `isTransientGitError` (BadObjectState / 5xx / "not a fast forward" / "Reference does not exist" / secondary rate limit), `retryTransient` (8-attempt equal-jitter backoff, cap 60s), `createReplicatedBlob` (createBlob + read-back confirm before referencing in a tree). Used by `lib/updates/core.ts` (`syncCoreFromUpstream`) and `lib/modules/github.ts` (`commitModulesJson`) - both now wrap the whole createTree→createCommit→updateRef write in `retryTransient`, re-reading HEAD each attempt so replication lag and HEAD races self-heal.

`lib/layout/`: `displayConditions.ts` (rule types, match + specificity scoring), `resolveThemeLayout.ts` (best published layout for a type/context), `starter-templates.ts` (**the single source of truth for starter templates** - `CORE_STARTER_TEMPLATES: Record<layoutType, StarterTemplate[]>` = header ×14 / footer ×5 / infoPage ×4 / notFound ×4 / statusPage ×4 / emailWrapper ×4 (Default Email `publishByDefault`, Plain, Branded, Blank), plus block-prop helpers; `getStarterTemplates(type)` merges core with the module-declared ones from the generated `lib/setup/module-starter-layouts.ts`, `allStarterTemplates()` flattens the lot for the seeder. **Must stay free of server-only imports** - the new-layout picker imports it straight into the browser. A `StarterTemplate` is `{id, name, description, data, publishByDefault?, defaultConditions?}`. Replaces both the old DB-seeded starter rows *and* the separate hardcoded `STARTERS_BY_TYPE` map that used to live inside `layouts/new/page.tsx` - the two had already drifted, 13 header variants vs 9), `layout-type-tabs.ts` (`CORE_LAYOUT_TYPES`, `TYPE_LABELS`, `CORE_TYPE_TABS`, `MODULE_GROUP_TABS` - shared by the Layouts list and the picker so their tab sets cannot disagree, which they previously did).

`lib/media/`: `providers.ts`, `loader.ts`, `upload.ts` (also `downloadMedia`, `deleteMedia`, `saveMediaRecord`, `getMediaReferences`), `migration.ts` - see Media Layer.

`lib/menu/resolve.ts` - `resolveMenu` (published-page filtering, nested tree build), `resolveMainMenu`.

`lib/modules/`: `manifest.ts` (zod schemas for `cactus.module.json` and `cactus.theme.json`, `parseGitHubRepo` strict URL validation, `fetchManifestFromRepo`, `validateTablePrefixUnique`; **`fetchManifestFromRepo(repoUrl, filename, ref = 'HEAD')` gained the `ref` argument (2026-07-23)** - install and update now pass the `release.tag` they are actually shipping, so `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules`/permissions are validated against the released manifest rather than whatever is on the default branch; `HEAD` remains the default only for callers that genuinely want the latest; gained an optional `memberExtensions` field - `activityTypes[]`, `notificationCategories[]`, `dataExportPath?`, `routeTiers[]` - for modules to declare Members-system contributions, see MEMBERS_SPEC.md amendment 5), `member-extensions.ts` (live reads of every active module's `memberExtensions`: `getModuleActivityTypes`, `getModuleNotificationCategories`, `getModuleDataExportPaths`, `getModuleRouteTiers` (+ `getModuleRouteTiersCached`, 5s TTL, for `proxy.ts`); pure data, no codegen step needed since none of it is a component import, unlike `extensionPoints`/`settingsTabs`), `github.ts` (`getLatestRelease` by channel, `syncModulesJson`, `getLatestDeploymentStatus`), `updates.ts` (`findModuleUpdates` - pure detection), `compat.ts` (2026-07-23 - `checkModuleUpdateCompat({ repoUrl, coreVersion, installed, ref })`: reads the manifest at the tag about to be installed and returns a short human-readable reason when the running core or the installed module set does not satisfy `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules`, or null when it is fine. This is the pre-check the single-module install/update paths always ran, lifted out so the BULK "Update all modules" path applies it per module too - it previously pinned every latest tag blindly, so one incompatible module could break every future build on a missing import. Incompatible modules now land in `failed[]` instead of in `modules.json`. A manifest that cannot be fetched returns null (compatible), matching the single-module path, so a transient GitHub hiccup never blocks an otherwise-fine update), `router.ts` (AUTO-GENERATED, gitignored - API dispatch + page loaders for installed modules).

`lib/notifications/`: `alerts.ts` (`upsertAlert` keyed by dedupeKey - re-surfaces on title change; `clearAlert`; `recordCoreUpdate`; `recordModuleUpdate`), `deployment.ts` (`recordDeploymentNeeded` rolling reasons list, `getUnreadCount`, `labelForEnvKeys`).

`lib/permissions/check.ts` - see Permissions System.

`lib/privacy/template.ts` - privacy-policy generator: `WizardAnswers` type, `DATA_COLLECTED_OPTIONS`, `PURPOSE_OPTIONS`, `DISCLAIMER_TEXT`, `assemblePolicyMarkdown` (jurisdiction-aware GDPR/CCPA sections).

`lib/puck/`: `config.tsx` (all block definitions + per-context configs; TipTap HTML conversion for RSC richtext), `siteLogoAlign.ts` (`LOGO_ALIGN_OPTIONS` + `siteLogoAlign()`, shared by SiteLogo's two render halves so the editor and live markup cannot drift), `module-components.ts` (AUTO-GENERATED, gitignored), `editor-routes.ts` (`isPuckEditorRoute(pathname)` - the single definition of "this route is a full-viewport Puck editor", consumed only by `AdminShell`; matches `/pages/<id>`, `/layouts/<id>` and the legacy `/appearance/header|footer`, and deliberately NOT `/pages/new` or `/layouts/new`, which are an ordinary form and the starter-template picker. Unit-tested in `editor-routes.test.ts` because getting it wrong strips a normal admin page's padding and scrollbar, which typechecks fine), `resolveTemplateData.ts`, `renderInfoPage.tsx` (`resolveContentData`, `renderInfoPageContent`), `renderLayoutWithContent.tsx` (injects page content into a layout's ContentSlot), `MediaPickerField.tsx` (`OgImagePickerField`, `ImageUrlPickerField`, `withImagePickerFields` - media-library modal fields + the helper that swaps a config's image URL text fields for the picker in both editors; the shared `MediaPickerModal` now has a "+ Upload" button in its header that POSTs the chosen file to `/api/admin/media` and auto-selects the returned item, so the Image / Image+Floating Chips / Card / OG-image pickers can add a brand-new image without leaving the block, not just pick an existing one; the modal also browses the media folder tree - breadcrumb + subfolder tiles from `/api/admin/media/folders`, media scoped per-folder, search spans all folders), `MenuCheckboxField.tsx`, `MenuSelectField.tsx`, `MinMaxPairField.tsx` (two plain text inputs side-by-side in one custom field slot - min/max pair, used by MenuBlock's fluid spacing/letter-spacing/font-size fields), `UnitValueField.tsx` (`UnitValueField` + `ResponsiveUnitValueField` - number box + unit dropdown for CSS lengths, per-field `units:` list, stores the plain CSS string so saved data/render paths are untouched; responsive variant rides `ResponsiveFieldShell`; used by every length field that was previously free text - grid column widths, sticky offsets, image max-width, embed height, header shrunk height, underline thickness/offset, Section/Spacer custom sizes), `MenuBlockEditorPreview.tsx` (editor-side MenuBlock preview with live menu fetch), `SiteColourField.tsx` (palette swatch picker, dual light/dark preview per swatch, + custom native-picker swatch; optional `allowManual` prop adds a free-text CSS-colour box under the swatches - used by the border/icon/text-colour fields that were previously bare text inputs), `SiteFontField.tsx` (font-family picker for block fields - site fonts first, then Google Fonts catalogue search, free text allowed) + `useSiteFonts.ts` (cached `/api/admin/appearance` fonts fetch, mirrors `useSiteColours`), `BorderField.tsx` (show/hide + colour-swatch field, one box - colour swatches hide entirely when `show: 'hide'`), `useSiteColours.ts` (shared cached `/api/admin/appearance` fetch behind both of the above, avoids remount flicker), `SiteLogoEditorPreview.tsx` + `useSiteBranding.ts` (cached `/api/admin/config` fetch, injects real branding logo into the `SiteLogo` block's editor preview), `BgColorField.tsx` (`SectionBgColorField`/`HeroBgColorField`/`HeaderBgColorField`/`PageBgColorField` - background mode select + a mode-aware second input, one box: colour swatches only for the solid-colour modes (`color`, `transparent-scroll` - the SWATCH_MODES set), a CSS-gradient text box for `gradient`, and nothing at all for none/transparent/image/decorative modes, whose `color` value never paints. Shared body takes `allowOpacity` + `allowDark` flags (both on for Section + Hero only). `allowOpacity` adds a "Colour opacity" 0-100 slider for `mode: color`; a translucent colour is stored as `color-mix(in srgb, <base> N%, transparent)` - via `splitBgColour`/`composeBgColour` round-trip - so it still rides a `var(--color-N)` (rgba() can't). `allowDark` adds a "Dark mode colour" swatch row; when set, the whole value is encoded as CSS `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)` (round-tripped by `splitLightDark`/`composeLightDark`, paren-aware split since each arm may be a color-mix). The site sets `color-scheme: light|dark` with its theme (globals.css), so the browser resolves the right arm with NO render-side change - Section/Hero already paint `backgroundColor: color`. Lets a section/hero background colour be made see-through (translucent card over a hero photo) AND carry a separate colour per light/dark mode. One opacity applies to both arms), `ColourSwatchButton.tsx` (shared swatch button w/ hover tooltip, used by `SiteColourField`/`BorderField`/`BgColorField`; also exports `CustomColourSwatch` - a rainbow swatch wrapping a hidden native colour picker, appended to all three swatch rows so any colour can be set, not just the palette, storing a raw hex - and `isCustomColour` helper), `components/AosInit.tsx` (AOS init client component), `components/MenuBlockClient.tsx` (public interactive menu: dropdowns, mobile hamburger, and a per-breakpoint "Nav behaviour" of show/collapse-to-hamburger/dropdown-current-page - the `navToggle` responsive field; dropdown mode shows a current-page trigger via `NavDropdown`, revealed by `cactus-nav-dd-*` breakpoint classes from `buildTokenStyles`; the trigger carries `data-menu-dd-id="<block id>"` and takes two newer controls - the per-breakpoint **`navButtonWidth`** field (`auto` = fits its text, the old and default behaviour / `full` = spans its slot, which also sends the bars to the far edge like a select; at `auto` there is no free space so both render identically), and **`fitOneLine`**, which used to reach only the inline list: the trigger now also caps at `max-width:100%` and shrinks its label via `HeadingFitText` rather than wrapping to a second line or overflowing its column), `menuNavButton.ts` (`navButtonWidthCss()` - the dropdown trigger's per-breakpoint width rule, kept out of the client component so it is one shared emitter and unit-testable; `menuNavButton.test.ts`), `components/SiteLogoClient.tsx` (logo/site-name link with hover state), `components/ScaleToFit.tsx` (client wrapper that shrinks any content to fit its grid column via `transform:scale`, opt-in per column via Grid `col*Scale`; also see `getGridTemplateColumns` now using `minmax(0, W)` not `minmax(min-content, W)` so a set column width is honoured instead of propped open by content), `components/MembersBlocksRsc.tsx` (Members system Puck blocks' live async RSC render functions - see Puck Integration section).
- `lib/puck/tabs/`: `createPanelPlugin.tsx` (shared sidebar-tab factory + hand-rolled lucide-style tab icons), `rootFieldsOverride.tsx` (`hideRootFieldsOverride`), `headerBackLinkOverride.tsx` (`createBackLinkOverride(href, label)` - `overrides.header` factory that overlays a back-arrow link into Puck's own header, in the blank gutter it already reserves left of its title on desktop; see Puck Integration), `sidebarOverrides.css` (global CSS matched by class-name-prefix substring since `@puckeditor/core` hashes its CSS Modules class names - see Puck Integration), `LayoutSettingsTab.tsx`, `PageSettingsTab.tsx`, `SeoTab.tsx`, `PageHistoryTab.tsx`, `SavedBlocksTab.tsx`.
- `lib/puck/outline/`: `OutlineTree.tsx` (default export, wired as `overrides.outline` in both editors - draggable replacement for Puck's select-only Outline tab; pointer-event drag, drop indicator, auto-expand on hover, panel autoscroll, Alt+arrow keyboard moves), `tree.ts` (pure tree logic, no React: `buildOutline` walks root content + slot props + legacy `data.zones`, `indexOutline`/`ancestorIds`/`zoneIsInsideItem` for parent lookup and the drop-into-own-subtree guard, `flattenOutline` for visible rows, `computeMove` for Puck's remove-then-insert index shift), `tree.test.ts` (unit tests - the index shift and the subtree guard are the two things that silently corrupt a page if wrong).
- `lib/layout/layout-type-labels.ts` - `getLayoutTypeLabel(type)`: human label for a layout type (`Header`/`Footer`/`Page Layout`/`404`/`Status Page`, or the generated module-type label via `moduleLayoutTypeToGroup`). Used for Puck's `headerTitle` prop in `LayoutPuckEditor.tsx`.

`lib/setup/`: `starterLayouts.ts` - **no longer seeds starter rows**; starter templates are in-code data (`lib/layout/starter-templates.ts`). Jobs, deliberately kept apart:
  - `seedDefaultLayouts(db)` (**install only** - `/api/setup/complete`, `reset-database`): for each template flagged `publishByDefault` (core's default header/footer/full-width page/404 hero/coming-soon/maintenance, plus module templates whose pages have no hardcoded fallback, i.e. Shop's), seeds **one ordinary published Layout** at id `<template-id>-live` with the template's `defaultConditions`. Create-only upsert. The `-live` suffix is load-bearing: existing installs' live layouts already sit there, and renaming it would seed them a second header.
  - `seedPendingModuleLayouts(db)` (**request time**, from `ensureLayoutsCurrent()`): seeds any `active`/`inactive`/`update_available` module still carrying a **NULL** `layoutsSeededAt` whose code is in this build, then stamps it. Covers both the reconcile that ran on a build without the module's code (skipped unstamped) and the stamps `core-reconcile/009` cleared. It lives on a request path because reconcile only runs when a *module* deploy finishes - a site whose Shop was already mis-stamped would otherwise stay 404ing until the owner happened to install or update another module. **NULL-only**, so it can never re-mint a layout an owner deleted: a seeded module keeps its stamp regardless of what happens to the rows afterwards. Runs *after* the prune, so a module's fresh layouts are never binned by the same pass that made them, and outside the version gate (recovery must not wait for the next core update). `planPendingModuleSeeds(pending, inBuild)` is the **pure, unit-tested** half (5 cases in `starterLayouts.test.ts`).
  - `ensureLayoutsCurrent()` (**request time** - `app/(public)/layout.tsx`, `GET /api/admin/layouts`): runs `pruneLegacyStarterCopies` once per core version, gated on `SiteConfig.starterTemplatesVersion` vs `package.json` (module-level flag = one `SiteConfig` query per warm instance; a failed run leaves the stamp unwritten so a later request retries), then `seedPendingModuleLayouts` on every warm instance. **Never re-creates a layout a seeded module once had** - an existing site has its layouts already, and seeding a second `entire_site` header into it would silently change its design (Tester's live header is `starter-header-tall-live`, not `starter-header-live`, so a naive re-seed would have done exactly that).
  - `pruneLegacyStarterCopies(db)`: deletes the `<id>-live`/`<id>-edited` copies the old scheme spawned - its migration branch keyed off `status === 'published'`, which every starter row also was, so it minted a `<id>-live` copy of **every** starter on **every** core update (Tester had accumulated 54 published-but-condition-less rows + 21 `-edited` "(Copy)" drafts on top of 68 starters = 158 Layout rows). Deciding these is a **content** comparison against the in-code templates, which SQL cannot do, so it stays at runtime. **The starter rows themselves are NOT deleted here** - `prisma/core-reconcile/005_retire_starter_layouts.sql` does that at build time. That split is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the reconcile drops the `isStarter` column during the build, so a runtime `where: { isStarter: true }` would run *after* the column was gone, throw, get swallowed by `ensureLayoutsCurrent`'s catch, leave the stamp unwritten, and strand the rows forever. Delete-then-drop, in one SQL file, in that order. Everything this function keys on (row id, display conditions, `builderData`) survives the drop.
  - `planStarterCleanup(rows, templates)` - **pure, unit-tested** (`starterLayouts.test.ts`). Deletes a row only when all three hold: id is `<known-template-id>-live` or `-edited`; `displayConditions.include` is empty (renders nowhere); and `builderData` still `stableStringify`-equals the canonical template (nobody edited it). Anything the owner touched, published, or built fails one of the three and survives. `stableStringify` sorts object keys at every depth so a jsonb round-trip (Postgres does not preserve key order) still compares equal.

  `stylesInfoPage.ts` (`upsertStylesInfoPage` - seeds the draft `style-guide` page; `STYLES_PAGE_SLUG`/`TITLE`).

`lib/updates/core.ts` - `compareVersions`, `getCoreUpdateStatus` (channel-aware, cached 10 min / errors 30 s, aggregates release notes for all newer releases), `syncCoreFromUpstream` (reconcile-toward-target push, see GitHub API Integration), `invalidateCoreUpdateCache`; re-exports `planCoreSync`/`isSkippedCorePath`. `lib/updates/core-plan.ts` - pure dependency-free reconciliation planner `planCoreSync` (writes = target blob sha ≠ base blob sha; deletes = core-managed + removed upstream + present in base; none if base tree truncated) + `isSkippedCorePath`; unit-tested by `lib/updates/core.plan.test.ts`.

`lib/vercel/`: `deploy.ts` (`triggerVercelRedeploy` - redeploy latest production deployment; `ensureVercelRedeploy` - same but adopts an already-in-flight production deploy instead of stacking another. Both build via `createRedeploy`, which passes `withLatestCommit: true` alongside `deploymentId`: without it Vercel inherits the source deployment's gitSource *including its commit sha*, so a "redeploy" replays the last-deployed commit rather than the branch's current HEAD - correct-looking whenever the two coincide, and a silent rollback when they don't), `env.ts` (list/upsert/delete project env vars; sensitive-key typing - sensitive vars skip the `development` target; `SENSITIVE_KEYS` set, which now includes `CRON_SECRET`), `cron-secret.ts` (`ensureCronSecret()` / `cronSecretSatisfied()` - see the `CRON_SECRET` entry under Environment variables; `cron-secret.test.ts` pins the never-overwrite and mint-fresh-each-time behaviour).

### Components

Admin (`components/admin/`):

- `AdminShell.tsx` - sidebar shell: mobile drawer, collapsible rail (persisted in localStorage, auto-collapse inside Puck editors - "inside a Puck editor" is `isPuckEditorRoute` from `lib/puck/editor-routes.ts`, which also decides the `admin-content--puck` chrome class), toolbar (collapse toggle, command-palette search button, ThemeToggle, NotificationBell), wraps children in `AdminPathProvider`; renders `DeployStatusBar` as a full-width strip above the whole shell (sidebar included) on every admin page; mounts `CommandPalette` once for the whole admin. Props: adminPath, siteName, version, sections (server-resolved `ResolvedNavSection[]`), moduleSettingsTabs (permission-filtered `{id,label}[]` of module Settings tabs, forwarded to `CommandPalette` for search), unreadCount, faviconUrl, faviconDarkUrl, sessionExpiresInMs (mounts `SessionExpiryWatcher` when present), children. Sidebar logo swaps `/cactus.svg` for the admin's uploaded favicon (via `resolveBranding()` in `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx`, `faviconUrl`/`faviconDarkUrl` - light/dark pair shown/hidden by the existing `data-logo-variant` + `data-theme` CSS toggle) once one's set, falling back to the Cactus mark otherwise; `.admin-sidebar-logo-text` wraps the site name onto up to 2 lines (`-webkit-line-clamp: 2`) before ellipsis-truncating, instead of clipping to one line.
- `SessionExpiryWatcher.tsx` - client component mounted once by `AdminShell`. Anchors a deadline at mount from the `expiresInMs` prop (client clock, so server/client skew can't sign anyone out early), shows a fixed bottom-right warning banner for the last 2 minutes with a live countdown and a "Sign in again" button, then navigates to `/<adminPath>/login?next=<path>&expired=1`. Timers re-arm in ≤15-minute chunks and recheck on `visibilitychange`/`focus` (background tabs throttle timers, sleeping laptops stop them). No polling, no network calls. Banner is non-blocking on purpose so unsaved work can still be saved; countdown is `aria-hidden` with a static `sr-only` sentence beside it so screen readers aren't re-announced to every second. Props: expiresInMs, adminPath.
- `DeployStatusBar.tsx` - always-mounted, self-hiding slim strip pinned (sticky) to the very top of the admin shell, above sidebar and content. Reads the shared client deploy-status store (`lib/deploy-status-client.ts`); shows spinner + state badge + latest translated log line, or a Dismiss button on failure. The store does the polling: `/api/admin/redeploy-status` until the `'pending'` sentinel resolves to a real deployment id (2s), then `/api/setup/deployment-logs` (4s); on READY tail-done it clears the gate (`DELETE /api/admin/redeploy-status`), drops the update-check sessionStorage cache and `window.location.reload()`s. `announceRedeployStarted()` (same store) is called by every redeploy-triggering client action - it flips the store active immediately and fires the `cactus:redeploy-started` window event, which pops the notification bell open.
- `AdminNav.tsx` - renders the server-resolved `sections` prop (`ResolvedNavSection[]` from `resolveAdminMenu`); no hardcoded nav array any more. Each item row is a link + hover pin (favourite) star + optional restricted badge (lock/eye-off, admins only) + route-change loading spinner; module icons are still manifest-supplied SVG innerHTML (sanitised server-side) or a fallback icon. Above the sections: a filter box (live-filters items to a flat result list), a Quick "New…" menu (deep-links collected from visible items' `createAction`), and an expand/collapse-all button. Optional Favourites and Recently-visited groups (both `localStorage`: `cactus-sidebar-favourites`, `cactus-sidebar-recents`) render above the real sections. That tools row and the Favourites group sit together in a `.admin-nav-pinned` wrapper that is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside `.admin-sidebar-nav-scroll` (needs `z-index` because the rows below are positioned; `background: var(--admin-sidebar-bg)` so scrolled rows don't show through), so both stay put while the rest of the tree scrolls; Favourites itself (`.admin-nav-pinned-favs`) is capped at `40vh` with its own scrollbar so a long pinned list can't swallow the rail, and a `ResizeObserver` keeps the scroll container's `scroll-padding-top` matched to the pinned block's height so scroll-into-view never parks the active item underneath it. Neither renders on the collapsed rail. Up/Down arrow keys rove focus between items; navigating auto-expands the active item's section and scrolls it into view. Section labels still toggle+persist per-label (`cactus-sidebar-sections-collapsed`); collapsed-rail tooltips (portal `.admin-nav-tip`) + account/sign-out/version(→`AboutModal`) footer unchanged. Props: adminPath, version, sections, collapsed, onNavClick.
- `CommandPalette.tsx` - Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette. Subsequence match (`scoreCommand`) over: every sidebar destination + `createAction` shortcut, **plus the static deep-settings index** `lib/admin/search-index.ts` (every Settings tab, the sections inside them, and individual settings - backup, SMTP, roles, cookie banner, colours, etc.). Each index entry matches on label **and** keyword synonyms (label hits rank above keyword hits above breadcrumb hits) and carries a breadcrumb hint + a deep-link `path` (query `?tab=`/`?sub=` and/or a `#section` hash). Deep entries are gated by `requires` (a nav base path): only offered when that page is visible in the user's resolved sidebar, so search never links to a screen the role hides. Also indexes **module-provided Settings tabs** (Shop, Gazette, …) as `${label} settings` → `/config?tab=<id>`, from the `moduleSettingsTabs` prop the admin layout resolves (permission-filtered server-side from each active module's `manifest.settingsTabs`, gated by the tab's own permission in the layout's existing batch query). Up/Down + Enter to jump (`router.push`); when the target `href` has a `#`, also fires a `cactus:scroll-hash` window event so a same-tab hash-only jump still scrolls. Esc to close; `?` (when not typing) opens the shortcuts overlay. Portals to `document.body`; also opened by `AdminShell`'s toolbar search button via `cactus:open-command-palette`. Props: adminPath, sections, moduleSettingsTabs?.
- `useScrollToHash.ts` - hook: scrolls the element named by the current URL hash into view (retries ~2s so it lands after tab-gated content mounts), then flashes it (`.admin-search-target-flash`). Listens to `hashchange` + the palette's `cactus:scroll-hash` event; re-attempts when caller-passed `deps` change (e.g. active tab). Powers the command-palette "jump straight to this setting" deep links. Used by `ConfigPageClient` (Settings). Anchors are plain `id="…"` + `className="admin-anchor"` (`scroll-margin-top` in globals.css) on the page's section wrappers.
- `AboutModal.tsx` - About Cactus Foundation dialog opened from the sidebar version number. Cactus mark (`/cactus.svg`) + name + slogan + blurb + grouped credits roll (from `lib/about/credits.ts` `ABOUT`/`CREDITS`, includes a Claude Code credit), footer with a "Release notes" button. That button opens a second stacked overlay `ReleaseNotesModal` (same file) which infinite-scrolls the full release history from `GET /api/admin/release-notes?page=N` (15/page), newest-first, rendering each release's sanitized notes HTML. **Portals to `document.body`** via `createPortal` (gated on a `useSyncExternalStore` mounted check) - required because `AdminNav` mounts it inside `.admin-sidebar` (`position: sticky`, which always creates its own stacking context), so a non-portaled `position: fixed` overlay nested there paints within that context and gets covered by `<main>` regardless of z-index. `ReleaseNotesModal` doesn't need its own portal call, it renders inside the already-portaled tree. Both layers are token-styled overlays (backdrop-click + Escape close; release notes on top; each `Overlay` sets `isolation: isolate`). Colours/radii via CSS vars only; header/body/footer rows each set their own `background: var(--color-bg)` and the card clips with `overflow: hidden`.
- `AdminPathContext.tsx` - React context (default `cactus-admin`); `useAdminPath()`.
- `LayoutPreview.tsx` - a small structural drawing of a layout, **derived from that layout's own Puck `data`** (`{type, data, height?}`). Containers (`Grid` cols/`columnSizes`, `Split` `ratio` + `zones`, `Section` `maxWidth`, `Group` `direction`/`justify`) give the shape; leaf blocks become boxes and bars (`SiteLogo`, `MenuBlock`, `LoginButton`, `ThemeToggle`, `SocialLinks`, `Copyright`, `Heading`, `TextBlock`, `Callout`, `Hero` (height from `minHeight`), `ContentSlot` (the dashed primary well - the one thing a page layout must show)). Header/footer render as a band with a ghost page body behind it, sized from `root.props.height` and inset from `maxWidth`, with the bottom/top border reflecting `border.show`. **Unknown block types - i.e. every block a module ships - fall back to a plain box**, with shape hints keyed on ordinary English words in the type name (`/Header$/`, `/List|Grid|Browser/`, `/Body|Comments|Detail/`); no module is named anywhere, so a module gets previews for free and core stays clean. Used by both the Layouts list cards and the starter picker; replaces the old `LayoutThumbnail` that guessed a layout's shape from substrings of its **name** (`n.includes('sidebar')`). Colour tokens only, no hex.
- `NotificationBell.tsx` - bell + unread badge, portal dropdown listing notifications with view/redeploy/read-toggle/delete actions (same handlers as the notifications page). The dropdown header carries "Mark all read" / "Delete all" text buttons (`.admin-bell-dropdown-headaction`) hitting the collection route, so they cover the whole table rather than the twenty rows the bell holds; both share the per-item loading/error maps under the `__bulk__` sentinel key. Delete all is disabled when nothing held passes the local `isDeletable()` (the mirror of the endpoint's open-deployment guard) and re-fetches afterwards rather than blanking the list. While a redeploy is in flight the dropdown shows a compact live status section at the top (spinner, state badge, ~3-line scrollable translated log fed by `lib/deploy-status-client.ts`); the dropdown auto-opens on the `cactus:redeploy-started` window event. Also renders the **live media-upload batch** (`UploadSection`) as its own section below the deploy status, fed by the shared `lib/upload-status-client.ts` store (subscribed via `useSyncExternalStore`) - per-file progress bars, a Clear for finished files, per-file dismiss; these entries have **no read/unread state** and don't touch `unreadCount`. The bell shows the spinner (not the count badge) while uploads are active, and auto-opens on the `cactus:upload-started` window event. Props: adminPath, unreadCount, collapsed.
- `SequenceProgress.tsx` - live progress bar for one scroll-sequence conversion, rendered on that job's notification in **both** the bell dropdown and the notifications page. Self-polls `GET /api/admin/media/sequence-status?jobId=` every 5s while the job is queued/running (that route proxies the worker's live figure AND rewrites the notification, so the bar is also what keeps the stored progress moving once the convert dialog is closed); its own polled value supersedes the server-rendered one until the job's `state` prop changes. On done/error it stops, calls `onSettled?.()` and `router.refresh()` **once** (`settledRef`), so the finished notification's button appears without a manual reload. Renders `.admin-seq-progress*` classes (globals.css); no hex. Props: jobId, state, progress (0-100|null), detail, onSettled?.
- `DeployLogViewer.tsx` - renders translated deploy-log messages (via `translateLogLine`), deduped, last 8 visible, `onComplete` on the final line. Props: rawLines, onComplete, onError.
- `UnsavedChangesModal.tsx` - cancel/discard/save-and-leave dialog. Props: pendingHref, saving, message, onCancel, onDiscard, onSave?.
- `useUnsavedChanges.ts` - hook: `dirtyRef` + beforeunload warning + in-app link interception → `pendingHref`.
- `TabStrip.tsx` - shared underline-style horizontal tab bar (flush edges, no side gaps); scrolls with edge fade + click arrow overlay when tabs overflow. Items render as `<Link>` (if `href`) or `<button>` (if `onClick`). Props: items (key, label, href?, onClick?, active), trailing?, style?. Used by Settings, Appearance→Styles, Layouts, and by Gazette/Boards/Contact-form module nav and list tabs.

Public/shared:

- `components/ThemeToggle.tsx` - light/auto/dark toggle; persists `cactus-theme`, applies `data-theme`, follows system in auto. `style` prop selects one of 6 presentations (`segmented` icon pill (default), `text` label pill, `expand` icon+hover menu, `dropdown` icon+click menu, `switch` two-state sun/moon slider light↔dark no-auto, `cycle` single icon click-to-step); admin `collapsed` prop still forces `cycle` regardless of `style`. Shared `useThemeMode` hook + `ThemeMenu` popover; CSS for all variants in `app/globals.css` (`.theme-toggle--text`, `.theme-switch*`, `.theme-menu-wrap`/`.tt-menu*`). 2026-08-03: optional `appearance` prop (`ThemeToggleAppearance`) + exported pure helper `themeToggleVars()` (unit-tested in `components/ThemeToggle.vars.test.ts`) turn `variant`/`iconSize`/`iconColour`/`bgColour`/`borderColour`/`borderRadius` into `--tt-*` custom properties set inline on the cycle button (and on `.theme-menu-wrap` for expand/dropdown, which inherits to the trigger). `.theme-toggle-cycle` in globals.css now reads `--tt-box`/`--tt-pad`/`--tt-radius`/`--tt-bg`/`--tt-border`/`--tt-shadow`/`--tt-fg` (+ `--tt-bg-hover`/`--tt-fg-hover`, and `--tt-icon` on a new `> svg` rule that beats the SVG's own width/height attributes), each falling back to the value it always had - so the admin rail, and any block that sets nothing, render byte-identically. Box vars are only emitted for `variant` bordered/filled/plain; the `default` variant keeps the round grey icon button, which is why filling defaults into a pre-existing block changes nothing.
- `components/consent/ConsentBanner.tsx` - GDPR banner (bottom-bar or modal): accept-all / reject-all / manage-per-category / notice-only dismiss; writes the `cactus-consent` cookie (versioned payload) + `cactus-consent-id`; POSTs `/api/consent`; re-prompts on categoriesVersion bump or reConsentDays expiry; registers `window.cactusConsent`. Props: config, privacyPolicyUrl.
- `components/EmailDeobfuscator.tsx` - client component mounted once in `app/(public)/layout.tsx`; after hydration walks every `a.cactus-eml[data-eml]` on the page, decodes the address (base64 of reversed string) and sets `href="mailto:…"`. ## Modules

Modules live in `/modules` (gitignored), cloned at build time by `scripts/checkout-modules.mjs` from the tags pinned in `modules.json`. Wiring into core is exclusively via the generated files (router, puck components, cron, settings tabs, extension points). Twenty-five modules are registered and present on disk (address-lookup-for-shop, advanced-shipping-for-shop, boards, contact-form, contact-form-reply-catcher, directory, filters-for-shop, gazette, gemini-watermark-remover, gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop, google-reviews-for-shop, google-sheet-products-for-shop, product-3d-views-for-shop, product-attributes-for-shop, product-downloads-for-shop, quote-for-shop, reviews-for-shop, search, shop, shop-variations, space-planner-for-shop, square-payment-for-shop, stock-import-for-shop, twilio, ultimate-seo). **filters-for-shop** was written on 2026-08-03 and registered with pin v0.1.0, but its **GitHub repo/tag does not exist yet** - creating `cactus-foundation-modules/filters-for-shop`, pushing, and releasing v0.1.0 is a deferred release step (same situation google-sheet-products-for-shop sat in; a Vercel build before that release would fail the checkout). product-3d-views-for-shop joined the registry in v0.5.465. **quote-for-shop** was released and registered in v0.5.795 (pin v0.1.3, alongside shop's pin moving to v0.1.147 - the release publishing the two points it needs). **google-sheet-products-for-shop** is still built and on disk but **not registered in `modules.json` or released** - its GitHub repo/tag does not exist yet, so registration remains a deferred release step (see its own subsection below). **reviews-for-shop** was written, released and registered on 2026-07-30 (pin v0.1.0, core v0.5.799; 18 modules registered as of that release). Until an entry exists, `scripts/lib/module-names.mjs` filters a directory out of every generator, so nothing of it is wired into a build.

**The pin is the build (v0.5.459).** The clone is `--branch <version>` at the pinned tag - "the build always gets exactly the module code the registry says it should, never silently ahead of it" - and default-branch HEAD is only the fallback for an entry with no `version` or a tag that has gone. So **releasing a module ships nothing on its own**; its `modules.json` pin has to move too. Every pin had drifted behind its module's latest release (shop v0.1.28 vs 0.1.39, shop-variations v0.1.0 vs 0.1.7, twilio v0.1.1 vs 0.1.12, …) and all eleven were reconciled to their latest release in v0.5.459. **A pin bump is not a free-standing act:** shop-variations 0.1.7 and product-attributes-for-shop 0.1.2 both declare `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.38`, so bumping either while shop sat at v0.1.28 would have cloned a shop with no `product-editor/context` and failed the build on a missing module import. Pins joined by a `requiresModules` edge move together; check the whole graph against the pinned set and the core version (`requiresCoreVersion`) before writing.

**"Installed here" vs "in this build" (working tree, core, unreleased).** `lib/modules/live-status.ts` owns the module status filter for every feature a module contributes. `status` conflates two questions - is the module installed on this site (database fact) and is its code in this build (build fact) - and the `status: { in: ['active', 'update_available'] }` filter that had been hand-copied to 21 call sites answered the wrong one. A module being **updated** moves to `deploying`, then `pending_deploy` if the deploy is deferred, while its code stays live in the running build; the old filter read that as uninstalled, so everything the module contributed silently vanished from the public site for the length of the deploy, or open-endedly for `pending_deploy`. Reported as "3D models stop working when we redeploy": `resolveShopGalleryExtras` dropped the product-3d-views provider, taking the swatches and the viewer with it, with no error anywhere. `INSTALLED_MODULE_WHERE` now answers only the database question (`active`, `update_available`, `deploying`, `pending_deploy`); the build question is already answered better at each call site, which looks the module up in a generated registry (`moduleExtensionPointComponents`, `moduleSmsProviders`, `moduleLayoutTypeGroups`, …) and skips anything absent - so a **first** install, which is `deploying` with no code in the build, still renders nothing. Only use it where such a registry does that second half. `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx` is the exception: nav entries come straight off the stored manifest, so it intersects with `MODULES_IN_BUILD`, a new `ReadonlySet<string>` emitted into the generated `lib/modules/router.ts` by `scripts/generate-module-router.mjs`. `app/api/admin/env/route.ts` stays deliberately wider (adds `inactive`, so a switched-off module's env vars survive). `lib/modules/updates.ts` is the one deliberate holdout - a `deploying` row holds the old tag in `version` and the new one in `pendingVersion`, so including it would re-offer the update already in flight. `lib/modules/live-status.test.ts` is the backstop: it walks the tree and fails on any reintroduced hand-rolled filter, because tsc and eslint have nothing to say about any of them and the failure mode is a silently missing feature rather than an error.

**`npm run check:module-pins` enforces the above.** `lib/modules/pin-check.ts` is a pure planner (IO-free, mirroring `lib/updates/core-plan.ts`): given the registry, each module's latest release tag, the manifests at those tags and core's `package.json` version, it reports pins behind their release, entries with no `version` at all (the build silently takes HEAD), and - the part per-module staleness can't catch - whether the **current** and **proposed** sets actually resolve. It reuses `findUnmetModuleDependencies` (`lib/modules/dependencies.ts`, v0.5.458) and `compareVersions` rather than second-guessing them, and judges each module against the manifest **at the tag being proposed**, since 0.1.7 requiring `shop >= 0.1.38` says nothing about what 0.1.9 will require. An unread manifest is reported, never assumed dependency-free.

`lib/modules/pin-check.live.test.ts` is the network half (gh: `release list`, then the manifest via `contents/cactus.module.json?ref=<tag>`), gated on `CHECK_MODULE_PINS=1`. **It is deliberately not in the commit gate.** It needs network + gh auth, so in CI it would skip, and a check that skips where it matters is a false pass; and pin lag isn't a property of the working tree - it appears when someone *else* publishes a release, so gating commits on it would fail unrelated work. It is a manual/cron command that exits non-zero on lag, and skips cleanly (exit 0, loud warning) where gh is missing or unauthenticated. The resolution logic itself is covered offline with **no skip** in `lib/modules/pin-check.test.ts`, which encodes the v0.5.459 trap as a regression. gh calls retry 3× on transient failures (a 404 is definitive and isn't retried) - a first run failed on a blip reading a manifest that was plainly there a second later.

### Filters for Shop

- Slug: `filters-for-shop` (table prefix `flt_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/filters-for-shop` (v0.1.0 released 2026-08-03, v0.1.1/v0.1.2/v0.1.3 released 2026-08-04; registry pin v0.1.3). 0.1.1: price-band groups, attribute-sourced rules, sticky panel. 0.1.2: card-carousel handshake fix (see `shop.card-media` fourth-contribution entry) - requires `shop >= 0.1.189`. 0.1.3: the grid finally resolves `resolveShopCardExtras` into `buildCardContext` (it never had - so no contributed variation photos and the 0.1.2 constraint had nothing to match on the live site), mirrors shop's current div + stretched `.shop-card-link` card wrapper, and passes `partTypes` into `injectShopProductCardEmbed`; `shop-variations >= 0.1.107`; `product-attributes-for-shop` optional (probed, never imported). 0.1.4: automatic Category group on category pages - see the Puck block entry below (released 2026-08-04, registry pin moved to v0.1.4 in core v0.5.935/936). 0.1.6 (working tree): single-option groups dropped - the RSC now offers a group only when >= 2 filters survive the page's hide-empty pass (`.filter((g) => g.filters.length >= 2)`), and the synthetic Category group needs >= 2 offered children; a heading with one tick (e.g. "Height adjustable: Yes" on the sit-stand page) filters nothing. 0.1.5 (released 2026-08-04, pin bumped in core v0.5.937): storefront UX pass - overlay filter sheet at <= tablet breakpoint (bottom sheet on phones, right slide-over on tablets; floating "Filter" pill entry point, scrim, body scroll lock via position:fixed pin with instant-scroll restore, Escape/scrim close, focus trap + dialog semantics, sticky "Show N products" apply footer that scrolls back to the results), per-group selected-count badges, tick lists >10 fold behind "Show all" (ticked entries never fold away), bigger touch targets in the sheet, focus-visible outlines, `role="status"` on the "Showing X of Y" line; `FilterShell` gained a `tabletBp` prop (matchMedia drives the sheet-only behaviours). 0.1.7 (working tree): **Sort by dropdown** on every filter-grid surface - see the Puck block entry below; new `lib/sort.ts` + `lib/sort.test.ts`, new block prop `showSort`, new `FilterShell` props `sortKeys`/`showSort`, new `.flt-toolbar`/`.flt-sort`/`.flt-sort-select` CSS.
- Grouped storefront filters built for variation-heavy catalogues: an owner-defined filter (Colour > Blue) stands for any number of real `svr_option_values` matched by **(option name, value label)** pairs, so one Blue covers Blue/Stevia Blue/Sky Blue across every product with no per-product wiring. Matching is variant-driven: a product matches a filter when any **enabled** variant carries a matched value; the first such variant (owner's variant order) is the representative whose child-product photo the card swaps to and whose child slug the card links to (shop-variations' existing deep-link resolver turns that into the parent page with the options pre-selected - no shop/shop-variations changes were needed).

**Database** (`flt_`): `flt_groups` (`name`, unique `slug` = query param, `control_type` CHECK CHECKBOX|SWATCH|IMAGE|DROPDOWN, `kind` CHECK VALUES|PRICE from 002, `position`), `flt_filters` (`group_id` FK cascade, `label`, `slug` unique per group, `swatch` hex-or-URL, `price_min`/`price_max` NUMERIC from 002 - band bounds, min inclusive / max exclusive, NULL = open end, `position`), `flt_filter_rules` (`filter_id` FK cascade, `source` CHECK OPTION|ATTRIBUTE from 002, `option_name`, `value_label`, unique on the quadruple - 002 drops the old triple constraint), `flt_settings` singleton (`hide_empty_filters`, `swap_card_images`, `preselect_on_click`, all default true). Migration `002_price_and_attribute_rules.sql` is idempotent and ships in 0.1.1.

**Matching sources** (0.1.1): OPTION rules = original variant-driven svr matching (swap photo/deep link kept). ATTRIBUTE rules match `pat_attributes`/`pat_attribute_values`/`pat_product_values` by (attribute name, value label), read at product level AND via `svr_variants.child_product_id` (specs are stamped per-variant), behind a separate `lib/attributes-probe.ts` (`to_regclass`, module isolation - product-attributes code never imported); matrix only, no card swap. PRICE groups are matched in the RSC, not SQL, against `Number(ctx.fromPrice ?? ctx.prices.now)` - the same figure the card prints - via `priceInBand()` in `lib/types.ts`, so they also work for variation-less products. Admin catalogue (`admin/option-values`) now returns `source` per section and includes attributes only when their distinct label count is <= 60 (free-text specs like weights would flood the picker).

**Permissions**: none of its own - shop's `shop.products` (manage screen/APIs) and `shop.manage` (settings).

**API routes** (`/api/m/filters-for-shop/…`): `admin/groups` GET+POST, `admin/groups/[id]` PATCH+DELETE, `admin/groups/reorder` POST, `admin/filters` POST (accepts inline rules), `admin/filters/[id]` PATCH+DELETE, `admin/filters/[id]/rules` PUT (whole-set replace), `admin/filters/reorder` POST, `admin/option-values` GET (distinct (option, value) catalogue with product counts + representative swatch, sourced from `svr_*` behind a `to_regclass` probe), `admin/settings` GET+PUT. No public routes - the storefront is fully server-rendered.

**Admin**: nav entry Shop > Filters → `/cactus-admin/m/filters-for-shop/filters` (`FiltersScreen`: groups, filters, searchable value picker keyed `source␀optionName␀valueLabel` with attribute sections labelled "Spec: ...", auto-borrowed swatches; group creation offers Product values vs Price bands - a PRICE group is forced CHECKBOX and its filter rows swap the value picker for from/up-to band inputs via `PriceBandEditor`); settings sub-tab hosted at `shop.settings-sub-tabs`.

**Puck block** `ShopFilterGrid` ("Shop: Filters & Product Grid", layoutTypes shopIndex/shopCategory/shopCollection, editor/RSC split via `rscImport`). RSC half mirrors product-attributes-for-shop's grid: shop's own `listProducts` (perPage cap 100 is the honest ceiling) + card template render, cards stamped `data-flt-product`; client `FilterShell` shows/hides/re-dresses cards in place (never re-renders), with facet-style live counts (`facetCount` - a tick never counts against its own siblings), active-filter chips, collapsible groups with selected-count badges, URL sync via `replaceState` after mount (hydration-safe), and the image/href swap.
