(2) Ownership of the order was proved by `sessionStorage['cactus_shop_order_number']` alone, while the basket lives in `localStorage` - a browser handing the tab back with a fresh session after the provider's page left a full basket under a thank-you. `checkout-state.ts` gained `rememberPlacedOrder(orderId, orderNumber)` / `isPlacedOrder(orderNumber)` / `forgetPlacedOrder()`, writing the sessionStorage keys as before **plus** a timestamped `cactus_shop_placed_order` localStorage mirror trusted for `PLACED_ORDER_TTL_MS` 6h; `isPlacedOrder` accepts either. The TTL plus exact order-number match plus `forgetPlacedOrder()` on use is what still keeps a confirmation link opened weeks later from emptying a basket somebody has since refilled. `CheckoutPaymentClient` calls `rememberPlacedOrder` where it used to set the two keys by hand.
- **Product search is word-AND, not substring (v0.1.153):** `lib/db/products.ts` exports `searchTerms(raw)` (trim → split on whitespace → drop empties → cap 8) and `listProducts` now requires EVERY term to match `p."name"` or `p."sku"` (`ILIKE '%term%'`, joined with AND), instead of one `ILIKE` over the whole raw string. "evolve screen" now finds "Evolve / Impulse Plus Bench Screen"; word order and what sits between words no longer matter. Same filter serves the admin products list (`GET /api/m/shop/admin/products?search=`) and the public grid, so both change together. Not applied to `lib/menu-entity-provider.ts`, `lib/db/orders.ts`, the customers route or `shop-variations/lib/variations-list.ts` - those are still single-substring.
- **Cart totals: Subtotal / charges / VAT / Total (v0.1.136, working tree):** the cart footer was one Subtotal row that quietly included whatever a resolver had priced into the lines. Now `lib/line-meta.ts` carries `CartLineCharge { label, amount }` (per unit) on `CartLineResolution.charges` - an ATTRIBUTION of money already inside `priceAdjust`, never an addition. `resolveLineMeta` folds them across resolvers, dropping non-positive ones; `resolveCartLines` multiplies by quantity through the new `attributeCharges(charges, unitPrice, quantity)`, which scales the set down proportionally if it would ever outrun the line price (so the goods figure cannot go negative) and hands back LINE totals, not per-unit. `POST …/cart/validate` echoes `charges` plus a per-line `taxRate`, resolved against `getDefaultTaxZoneId()` (new in `lib/db/tax-shipping.ts` - the catch-all zone, else the first alphabetically, else null) with ONE rate lookup per distinct tax class, not per line. `CartFullClient` does the arithmetic client-side (so it moves the instant a quantity or service changes): goods `subtotal = Σ lineSubtotal − Σ charges`, one row per charge label merged across lines, then tax per line at its own rate - `taxMode` comes from the config call it already makes, and INCLUSIVE labels the row "VAT (included)" and leaves it OUT of the Total, EXCLUSIVE adds it. Rendered as a `<dl class="scl-tot">` (label/figure pairs, tabular-nums, Total ruled off). The sticky bar now shows the Total, not the subtotal. New Puck fields `taxLabel` ('VAT') / `totalLabel` ('Total'); `showSubtotal`'s label became "Show totals". Live consumer: `advanced-shipping-for-shop` v0.1.20's `Delivery` charge.
- **The checkout review shows the same split (v0.1.136, working tree):** `OrderTotals` gained display-only `charges: CartLineCharge[]` (merged by label across the order) and `goodsSubtotal` - `subtotal` and `total` are deliberately UNTOUCHED, since those are the figures the order is written and the card is charged with, and this only says what the money already there was for. `POST …/checkout/session` passes both through; `CheckoutReviewClient` renders Subtotal (goods) → a row per charge → Discount → Shipping (the postcode-priced carriage, a different thing from a per-item service, now only shown when it is actually charged) → VAT → Total, with the VAT row labelled "VAT (included)" on INCLUSIVE pricing from the `taxMode` the route already returned. Both new fields are optional client-side, so a stale cached bundle falls back to the old single undivided Subtotal row.
- **"Only option" removed from the summary picker (v0.1.136, working tree):** a single-service line no longer gets the muted "Only option" tag beside its price (`.scl-s-only` gone from `cart-line-css.ts` too). The bar without a control already reads as a statement rather than a question.
- **New extension point `shop.cart-summary` (v0.1.135):** whole-basket notes, the thing no per-line resolver can answer. `lib/cart-summary.ts` (`CartSummaryLine { product, quantity, meta }`, `CartSummaryNote { id, text }`, `CartSummaryProvider`, `getCartSummaryNotes`); providers gathered via `gatherCartExtensionPoint`, newly exported from `lib/line-meta.ts` so both seams share its memoised installed-module read. Called from `POST /api/m/shop/public/cart/validate` AFTER `resolveCartLines` (caches warm) with the raw request meta matched back by line key - `ResolvedCartLine` deliberately normalises it away. Response gained `notes`; `postCartValidate` now returns `ValidateResponse<T> = { lines, notes? }` (the sessionStorage bootstrap cache still stores lines only, so notes appear when the validate lands). Each provider is try/caught - a thrown note must never 500 the cart. Both cart clients join them onto the sticky bar meta after the item count with " · ". Live consumer: `advanced-shipping-for-shop` v0.1.19 `summariseCartDelivery`.
- **New extension points `shop.commerce-mode` + `shop.cart-header-actions` (v0.1.147, released):** the seam a quote add-on needs, and the only shop-side change `quote-for-shop` required. `lib/commerce-mode.ts` (server) resolves `shop.commerce-mode` through the memoised `gatherCartExtensionPoint`; the pure half - types, `SHOP_DEFAULT_COMMERCE_MODE`, `normaliseShopCommerceMode`, `commerceModeMoney`, `commerceModeButtonLabel` - lives in **`lib/commerce-mode-shared.ts`** so the client cart surfaces use the identical defaults and helpers (same reason `tax-display-shared.ts` exists; the resolver imports prisma and must not reach a client bundle). ONE point rather than four, because the buy-button label, the cart CTA + destination, price visibility and the checkout gate are one decision - a shop half-switched reads as broken. First provider with an answer wins; a throwing provider is ignored (an add-on with a broken settings read must not take the storefront down). 5s cache, `invalidateShopCommerceModeCache()` for a settings save. Consumers: `GET /api/m/shop/public/config` gained a `commerce` slice, `CartFullClient`/`CartDrawerClient`/`CartPageClient`/`CartSummaryClient` read it (money via `commerceModeMoney`, CTA via `commerceModeButtonLabel` + `cartCtaHref`; `CartStickyBar` gained an optional `checkoutHref`), `parts/detail-parts.tsx` uses it for the add-to-cart label and drops the price row for `hidePrices`, `parts/card-parts.tsx` + `MinimalCard` do the same on cards (threaded as `pricing.commerce` through `buildCardContext`, resolved once per grid beside `taxDisplay` - optional, so an un-rebuilt card surface in another module still compiles), `DetailPartContext`/`CardPartContext` carry `commerce`, and `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` also strips `offers.price`/`priceCurrency` out of the JSON-LD when prices are withheld. Gates: `/shop/checkout` redirects to `commerce.cartCtaHref` and both `POST /checkout/session` + `POST /checkout/payment-intent` 503 with `blockedMessage` (`/checkout/confirm` deliberately untouched - it only finishes an order that already exists). `hidePrices` renders `hiddenPriceLabel` (default `POA`) ONCE per price row, not per figure.
- **`shop.cart-header-actions` (v0.1.147, released):** `lib/cart-header-actions.ts` `getShopCartHeaderActions()` returns `{id, Component}[]` from installed manifests; `app/public/shop/cart/page.tsx` renders them in a flex row to the right of the `<h1>Your cart</h1>` (heading alone, wrapping, on a shop with no add-ons). Exists because a control a shopper must be able to FIND without being told - "Retrieve quote" - cannot depend on the owner having placed a block.
- **Cart page: summary picker, sticky bar, undo (v0.1.135):** `CartLineControl.renderAs` gained `'summary'` and each option an optional `summary: { headline, secondary?, switchLabel?, priceLabel? }` (`lib/line-meta.ts`, type `CartLineControlSummary`). `CartFullClient.renderSummary` draws the chosen option as a ticked bar (headline / secondary / price, `priceAdjust <= 0` → `.scl-free`) with the rest as radio-backed chips under "Switch to:"; it is used ONLY when every option carries `summary.headline`, else it falls back to the radio group - shop never parses a label. A line whose control is a summary gets `.scl-deliv-sum` (flex-grow, no width probe) and the product column drops to `flex:0 1 260px` whenever any line has a control, which is the "narrower product column". New shared client file `components/public/CartChrome.tsx` (`TickIcon`, `RemoveCross`, `QuantityStepper`, `CartStickyBar`, `CartUndoToast`) and `components/public/use-cart-undo.ts` (`useCartUndo` - snapshots the `CartLine` + its index before `removeFromCart`, toast holds 5s then fades 300ms; `useOutOfView` - IntersectionObserver, `rootMargin 0 0 -90px 0`, gated on the way out so no setState-in-effect). `cart.ts` gained `restoreCartLine(line, index)` (no-op if the key is back already). Both cart renderers use them - `CartFullClient` (Puck block) and `CartPageClient` (the unpublished-layout fallback). Puck block gained `stickyBar` / `undoRemove` (both `'yes'`), and its defaults moved to `quantityControl: 'stepper'` + `removeStyle: 'icon'` (label now "Cross") - **already-published cart layouts keep the values saved with them, so an existing layout needs those two dropdowns flipping by hand**. All new chrome is in `cart-line-css.ts`, token-coloured, light/dark clean.
- **Cart-line control options can carry a `description` (v0.1.134):** `CartLineControl.options[]` (`lib/line-meta.ts`) gained optional `description` - supporting copy the resolver wants shown with an option. `CartFullClient` renders it muted under the option label (radios) or under the picker for the chosen option (select). Generic seam growth with `advanced-shipping-for-shop` v0.1.18 as the live consumer (its per-service shopper-facing description); a resolver that omits it renders exactly as before, and an older shop ignores the field.
- **Designed description:** a product's full description is opt-in Puck content, not just a paragraph. Column `shp_products.description_puck JSONB NULL` (init `001` + idempotent `011_description_puck.sql`). `mapProduct` exposes `descriptionPuck: PuckData | null`; `updateProduct` sets it with a dedicated `"description_puck" = ${…}::jsonb` fragment (`COLUMN_MAP` typed `Exclude<…, 'descriptionPuck'>` and the generic loop skips the key); the products `PUT` accepts `descriptionPuck` (z.any, stored verbatim like `Layout.builderData`). `panels/details.tsx` is presence-based: `state.descriptionPuck === null` shows the "Full description" textarea + "Design with the page builder"; a non-null doc shows the "Remove design, use plain text" button plus a hint pointing at the full-screen builder (a confirm clears it back to null). `descriptionPuck` sits on `EditorState` (not `ProductForm`), owned by the `details` tab via `TAB_EXTRAS`. Storefront: `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` builds the body once with `getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig('shopProductDescription')` (only when `content.length > 0`) onto `DetailPartContext.descriptionBody` (attached by reference by the injector, so the React node survives); `buildDetailSections` picks `descriptionBody ?? <p>{description}</p>` for the Description tab. Editor/RSC markup match because both paths use the same core shared parts; JSON-LD still quotes plain `shortDescription ?? description`.
- **Full-screen description pop-out is now the only editing surface (0.1.114):** the inline `<Puck>` canvas on the Details tab is gone (`DescriptionBuilder.tsx` deleted) - it duplicated the pop-out and let the two surfaces drift. Designing a description now always means the **"Open in a new tab ↗"** button (`panels/details.tsx`, shown once the product is saved; a "save first" hint shows for a new, unsaved product since the pop-out route needs a real id). Shared setup lives in `product-editor/description-puck.ts` (`DESCRIPTION_LAYOUT_TYPE` + the sync channel) and, since v0.1.150, in `components/admin/description-builder/` - `StandaloneDescriptionBuilder.tsx` is the generic editor (props: `layoutType`, `eyebrow`/`title`/`backHref`/`backLabel`, `initialData`, `endpoint`+`field`, optional `onSaved`, `unsavedMessage`), with `shared.ts` holding the non-client bits its hosts need without pulling Puck in (`DESCRIPTION_BUILDER_CHROME_OFF_CSS`, `emptyDescriptionPuck`). `StandaloneDescriptionEditor.tsx` is now a thin product wrapper over it; the category description reuses it verbatim. Route `app/cactus-admin/shop/products/[id]/description/page.tsx` (→ dispatcher path `products/[id]/description`, `shop.products` gate + `catalogue_hidden`/not-found guards): inline `<style>` strips the admin shell (`.admin-sidebar`/`.admin-mobile-topbar` `display:none`, `.admin-content` full-viewport) and mounts `StandaloneDescriptionEditor.tsx` (client) - full-height `<Puck>` with its header suppressed (`overrides.header` returns an empty fragment) and its own Back/Save bar, saving just the field via `PUT /api/m/shop/admin/products/[id]` `{descriptionPuck}` (the products PUT is already all-optional, so a one-field body updates only that column), plus appearance-token injection and a `beforeunload` guard. The pop-out still calls `broadcastDescriptionSaved` on `BroadcastChannel('cactus:shop:product-description')` so an open `ProductEditor` adopts the saved doc into `state`+`baseline` (the `descriptionRev` remount it used to trigger is gone with the inline canvas). No core diff.
- **Categories carry card content (v0.1.150):** a category could only ever be a name, so a parent category page listed its sub-categories as bare text pills while the products beneath them were full cards. Categories now hold the same three things a product does - `short_description` (the blurb on the card), `image_url` (the picture) and `description_puck` (an opt-in designed long description, the product mechanism from `011` applied to `shp_categories`) - see the schema entry above and `012_category_content.sql`. Surfaces: **`components/public/ShopCategoryCards.tsx`** renders the tiles, deliberately reusing the *product* card's own stylesheet and class names (`shop-grid`/`shop-card`/`shop-card-img`/`shop-card-name`/`shop-card-blurb`/`shop-card-cta` from `parts/card-parts.tsx`) rather than inventing a second card look - a shopper meets both on one page, and restyling the card chrome restyles both at once. It does NOT stamp the Product Card layout: that template is built from parts that read a product's context (price, stock, badges, 3D), none of which a category has. **`components/public/ShopCategoryDescriptionBody.tsx`** picks which description wins - the designed document when it has content (an EMPTY document counts as no design, so opening the builder for a look cannot blank a perfectly good plain-text description), else the plain text, else nothing - and is shared by the block and the fallback page so the two cannot disagree. Wired into: the `ShopCategoryBrowser` block (now on `shopCategory` as well as `shopIndex`, with a new `ctaLabel` field), the new `ShopCategoryDescription` block, and the hardcoded fallback category page (`app/public/shop/categories/[slug]/page.tsx`), which leads with the sub-category cards, then the description, then the product grid. New starter `Sub-categories First` in `shopCategoryStarters`. `generateMetadata` prefers `short_description` over `description`, since the long one may now be a builder document with no plain text in it at all.
- **Sub-categories as pills (v0.1.190, working tree):** `ShopCategoryBrowser` gained a `display` select - `cards` (default, unchanged) or `pills`, a compact wrapping row of link chips for pages where the sub-categories are shortcuts above a filtered grid rather than the main event. Pills render via `components/public/ShopCategoryPills.tsx`; the stylesheet lives in `ShopCategoryPills.shared.ts` (no server imports) so the editor placeholder in `ShopCategoryBrowser.tsx` stamps the same `.shop-cat-pills`/`.shop-cat-pill` classes with sample names - canvas and live page share chrome. Tokens only (`--color-border`/`--color-surface`/`--color-text`/`--color-bg-subtle`). The fallback category page keeps cards.
- **Category admin + description builder (v0.1.150):** `CategoriesScreen`'s per-row edit panel gained Short description, Picture (via the shop's own `MediaPickerModal`, storing the picked item's `url` - the same convention product media uses) and Full description, plus a link out to the full-screen builder; each row shows a 24px thumbnail and a `Designed` badge. `listCategories()` now selects an explicit column list that **excludes `description_puck`** and returns `("description_puck" IS NOT NULL) AS has_designed_description` instead - every listing surface (admin tree, category cards, public categories API) would otherwise drag every category's whole builder document across the wire just to render a name; rows therefore come back with `descriptionPuck: null` on purpose, and the single-category fetches (`getCategoryById`/`getCategoryBySlug`, still `SELECT *`) are what carry the document. Route `app/cactus-admin/shop/categories/[id]/description/page.tsx` (-> dispatcher path `categories/[id]/description`, `shop.products` gate) mounts `StandaloneCategoryDescriptionEditor` over the shared builder, saving via `PUT /api/m/shop/admin/categories/[id]` `{descriptionPuck}` (layout type `shopCategoryDescription`, constant in `lib/category-description.ts` so the storefront RSC block can read it without pulling a 'use client' file in). No `BroadcastChannel` here, unlike products - the categories screen refetches the tree whenever it changes, so it picks a new description up on its own. No core diff.
- **Product image filing (v0.1.36, fixed v0.1.41; category nesting in working tree):** images belong in `Shop / <master category trail> / <product> / <slug><n>` (the master's full ancestor trail, so a sub-category nests inside its parent - see the Product image filing inventory entry below), and v0.1.36 filed them there on save via `reorganiseProductMedia`. In practice they sat in the library root, because two things fought it: the editor's `MediaPickerModal` POSTed to core `/api/admin/media` with **no `folderId`**, so every upload landed in the root by definition; and the same modal listed the library with no `folder` param, which `parseLibraryQuery` defaults to the **root scope**, so any image the save did file correctly then vanished from the picker - making the root look like the only place an image could live. v0.1.41: `getProductMediaFolderId(productId, {folderProductId?, masterCategoryId?})` is split out of `reorganiseProductMedia` (one definition of the target folder, shared by both paths) and exposed as `POST app/api/admin/products/[id]/media-folder` (gate `shop.products`, optional `masterCategoryId` query so a first upload follows the category picked on screen, not the last-saved one). POST, not GET, because it creates the folder: `MediaPanel` hands the picker a `resolveFolderId` callback that it calls **per upload** rather than on mount, so nothing is created for a product whose Images tab was merely opened and no upload can race ahead of a pre-fetched id. The picker appends the answer to the upload FormData and lists with `folder=all&type=image`. **Folder-aware browsing (working tree):** the same route gained a **GET** (same gate, same optional `masterCategoryId`) backed by new `findProductMediaFolderId(productId, {folderProductId?, masterCategoryId?, segments?})` in `modules/shop/lib/media/product-media.ts` - the identical path walk but look-only (mirrors `getOrCreateFolderByPath`'s cleanFolderName/skip-blank treatment), returning the deepest folder of the path that already exists, so browsing creates nothing. `MediaPickerModal` now browses per-folder like core's Puck picker (folder tree from `/api/admin/media/folders`, breadcrumb + subfolder tiles, `folder=<id|root>` scoping, search switches to `folder=all&q=`), opens at the caller's `resolveInitialFolderId` (MediaPanel and shop-variations' `VariationsPanel` pass the GET above), and keeps the selection in an id→item Map so picks survive navigating between folders. Upload still files via the POST resolver and the grid then jumps to that folder with the new image pre-ticked. Save-time filing stays as the backstop for renames, reorders and category changes, but its per-image `catch` now `console.warn`s instead of swallowing silently - that silence is why every image sat in the root with nothing reporting a problem. Relies only on core media APIs from v0.5.338 (`folderId` on the media POST, `folder=all` on the GET), the same release `reorganiseProductMedia` already needed, so no new core-version floor.
- **Picker paging + sort (v0.1.66):** `MediaPickerModal` listed a single hardcoded `perPage=50` page with no way past it and no sort control, so a folder with more than 50 images stranded the rest. Core's `GET /api/admin/media` already took `sort` and `page` and already returned `hasMore` (`parseLibraryQuery`/`queryMediaLibrary` in `lib/media/library-query.ts`) - the picker just never asked, so the fix is module-only, zero core diff. Now: a `Sort images` `<select>` in the modal header (`newest`/`oldest`/`name`/`name_desc` - core's size sorts are omitted, irrelevant when hunting a photo), a **Load more** button under the grid appending the next page (id-deduped, since an upload mid-browse shifts rows between pages), and `pageRef` reset to 1 whenever folder/search/sort changes. The upload path's hand-rolled duplicate re-fetch is replaced by a `reloadKey` counter that re-runs the listing effect, so there is one fetch shape. Inherited by every caller: shop's own media panel, `shop-variations`' variation images and `product-attributes-for-shop`'s `SwatchImagePicker`.
- **Variations hooks (v0.1.26):** shop gained three generic, reusable capabilities with `shop-variations` as the live consumer (nothing variations-specific in shop): (1) the `catalogue_hidden` product flag + `excludeHidden` filter on `listProducts` (public grid/search, admin product list, sitemap and product export all pass `true`; the public product page/route 404 a hidden row (the page has since gained the `shop.product-page-resolver` door, below, so a variant child's own URL can be aliased to its parent instead)); (2) a `shop.product-editor-sections` component slot rendered below `<ProductEditor/>` on `app/cactus-admin/shop/products/[id]/page.tsx` (mirrors `shop.order-messages`); (3) a `shop.cart-line-resolver` **server-function** extension point (precedent: `contact-form.thread-messages`) consumed in `lib/checkout.ts` - `lib/line-meta.ts` collects registered resolvers, and `resolveCartLines` calls each with `(product, line.meta)`, folding a server-authoritative `priceAdjust` into `unitPrice` and a normalised `persistMeta` onto the line (failing the line on invalid input). `CartLine` gained `lineId?`/`meta?` (personalised lines merge by `lineId`, plain lines by `productId` as before), `shp_order_items.line_meta` persists it, and shop renders the `{label,value,href?}` pairs generically wherever it lists line items (cart, order confirmation, confirmation email, admin order detail, member order detail).
- Full ecommerce foundation: catalogue (products - physical/digital/service, categories, tags, collections), checkout with a pluggable payment-provider interface (Stripe, PayPal, bank transfer, cash - all four fully built), orders with per-item refunds and a manual-order-entry route, customers (derived from orders by email, no dedicated table), discounts (coupon codes + priority-ordered automatic discounts), tax (per-zone rates, inclusive/exclusive mode) and shipping (postcode-prefix zones, flat/weight-banded/free rates), back-in-stock email subscriptions, pre-orders, CSV product import/export, and related-products/upsells (manual curation with an automatic same-category fallback). Optional integration with Members (guest checkout always works; saved addresses, order history, post-purchase account prompt when Members is enabled) and Reply Catcher (shop's side of a Customer Communications tab only - see Extension Points).
- Layout system integration (core mechanism, see Puck Integration above - Shop is the 4th module on it, joining Directory/Gazette/Boards): declares `layoutTypes` group "Shop" with seven types - `shopIndex` ("Shop Home"), `shopCategory` ("Category"), `shopCollection` ("Collection"), `shopProduct` ("Product"), `shopCheckout` ("Checkout"), `shopConfirmation` ("Confirmation"), `shopCart` ("Cart", added later when the cart page joined the layout system) - more types than any other module since Shop has more distinct page kinds than a category/entry pair. 2 new blocks in `components/puck/`: `ShopCategoryHeader`, `ShopCollectionHeader` (both `[ANCHOR]`, same shape as `DirectoryCategoryHeader` - re-fetch their own data from an injected slug, nothing else to inject). Existing blocks retagged by page: `ShopProductGrid`/`ShopProductCard` → `shopIndex`+`shopCategory`+`shopCollection` (one grid block reused across all three listing contexts, exactly like Gazette's `gazetteCategory` reuse); `ShopFeaturedCollection`/`ShopPromoBanner` → `shopIndex` only (`ShopCategoryBrowser` joined it on `shopCategory` too in v0.1.150, where its `parentCategorySlug` is injected with the category being viewed so one layout lists every category's own sub-categories); `ShopProductDetail`/`ShopBackInStockForm`/`ShopRelatedProducts` → `shopProduct`; `ShopCheckoutContact`/`Shipping`/`Payment`/`Review` → `shopCheckout`; `ShopUpsellProducts` → `shopProduct` + `shopCheckout` + `shopCart` (later); `ShopOrderConfirmation` → `shopConfirmation`; `ShopCartFull` (later) → `shopCart`. `ShopCartSummary` stays untagged (header-placement mini-cart widget, not part of any of these page types). `lib/inject-category-context.ts`/`lib/inject-collection-context.ts` inject `{categorySlug}`/`{collectionSlug}`; `lib/inject-product-context.ts` (pre-existing) injects `{productSlug, productId, inStock}` - unchanged, just now called from the generic path instead of the retired bespoke one. `lib/starterLayouts.ts` provides 3 starters per type (21 total) - `shopCategory`/`shopCollection` seed all-draft with the pre-existing hardcoded plain-grid pages as fallback (new templating, same principle as Directory/Gazette/Boards); `shopIndex`/`shopProduct`/`shopCheckout`/`shopConfirmation` have **no** hardcoded fallback (they were Puck-only from day one via the old table) so exactly one starter per type sets `publishByDefault: true`, carrying over the old table's default block arrangement so the storefront looks identical to before on first seed. `shopCart` is the hybrid: it KEEPS its hardcoded cart (`CartPageClient`) as a fallback like category/collection, yet still ships one `publishByDefault` starter (Cart block + upsells) so the basket is designable out of the box but can never go blank if the layout is unpublished. This replaced Shop's own pre-existing bespoke mechanism entirely (see "Retired" note under Database below) rather than running the two side by side.

**Database**
Table prefix: `shp_` (34 tables total, incl. addendum, the two shipment tables from `008` and the two order-request tables from `015`). Full DDL in `modules/shop/migrations/001_initial.sql`; later per-change files are numbered (`002_master_category.sql` adds the product master category to existing installs, idempotently; `003_category_nesting.sql` adds `shp_categories.product_display_mode` and flips the `parent_id` FK to ON DELETE CASCADE for the nested-category feature; `004_variations_hooks.sql` adds `shp_products.catalogue_hidden` BOOLEAN (purchasable but hidden from grid/search/sitemap/own URL - backs the shop-variations child rows) + index, and `shp_order_items.line_meta` JSONB (normalised per-line personalisation, `{fields:[{label,value,href?}]}`) - both mirrored in 001 for fresh installs; `008_shipments.sql` adds the `shp_shipments`/`shp_shipment_items` pair and the `PARTIAL_SHIPPED` email template for part-dispatch, likewise mirrored in 001; `012_category_content.sql` adds `shp_categories.short_description`/`description_puck`/`image_url` for the category card + designed category description, likewise mirrored in 001; `015_order_requests.sql` adds the `shp_order_requests`/`shp_order_request_items` pair for customer cancel/return requests, likewise mirrored in 001).

- `shp_products` - name/slug(unique)/type(PHYSICAL\|DIGITAL\|SERVICE)/status(DRAFT\|ACTIVE\|ARCHIVED)/description/short_description/sku(unique)/barcode, pricing (price mandatory + optional sale_price/retail_price/trade_price/cost_price, tax_class_id FK - `compare_at_price` was retired by `migrations/005_price_types.sql`, which carries its values into sale_price/price or retail_price before dropping it; which optional types are offered is the `enabledPriceTypes` config key, and `sale_price` is the only one that changes what gets charged), inventory (track_inventory/stock_count/low_stock_threshold/out_of_stock_behaviour BLOCK\|BACKORDER, `low_stock_alerted_at` dedupe marker for the daily cron - cleared on any stock_count write so a restock re-arms it), physical dimensions, digital_file_id FK + download_limit/download_expiry, SEO fields + `og_image_id` (no FK, core Media table), `master_category_id` (FK shp_categories ON DELETE SET NULL - the product's lead category; one per product, drives its media folder path; FK added via `ALTER` after shp_categories exists since it's a forward ref, plus idempotent `migrations/002_master_category.sql` for existing installs), pre-order fields (is_pre_order/pre_order_dispatch_date/pre_order_note/pre_order_max_quantity/pre_order_count), recommendation fields (related_mode/upsell_mode AUTOMATIC\|MANUAL, related_limit/upsell_limit default 4), best-seller ordering (`popularity_seed` given / `popularity` derived, both nullable INTEGER, `migrations/017_popularity.sql` + in 001 for fresh installs, index on `popularity DESC NULLS LAST`), timestamps.
- `shp_product_media` - product_id FK cascade, type(IMAGE\|VIDEO_FILE\|VIDEO_URL), url, alt_text, position, is_primary.
- `shp_categories` - self-referencing parent_id (**ON DELETE CASCADE** since `003` - deleting a category deletes its whole sub-tree, unlike Directory's RESTRICT; product links go via `shp_product_categories`' own CASCADE, the products themselves survive since `master_category_id` is SET NULL), name/slug(unique)/description/position/`product_display_mode` (`'rollup'|'exact'|NULL`=inherit the shop default)/SEO fields, plus the card content added by **`012_category_content.sql` (v0.1.150)**: `short_description TEXT` (the one-liner on a category's card, same role as `shp_products.short_description`), `description_puck JSONB` (opt-in designed description, exactly the product mechanism from `011`), `image_url TEXT` (the category's picture, holding the media item's **url verbatim** like `shp_product_media.url` - deliberately not a `Media` id as `shp_collections.image_id` is, so an RSC render needs no lookup and `lib/media-reference-rewriter.ts` can repoint it when core moves a blob). All three mirrored into `001` for fresh installs. Unlimited nesting depth. `shp_product_categories` join table (no position). A product stays a member of any number of categories here; the single lead one is `shp_products.master_category_id`. `getPrimaryCategoryId()` returns the master when set, else falls back to first membership (used by automatic recommendations). Tree helpers in `lib/db/catalogue.ts`: `getCategoryDescendantIds` (recursive CTE, cycle-safe via UNION - powers roll-up listing), `getCategoryAncestorPath` (breadcrumbs), `categoryReparentWouldCycle` (reparent guard), `reorderCategories(orderedIds, parentId?)` (writes `position` = array index for the group; when `parentId` is passed - `null`=top level - also writes `parent_id`, so one call both re-parents a dragged node and reindexes its destination siblings; omitted = position-only, used by the ↑/↓ arrows), `resolveCategoryProductFilter` (slug+default → exact vs roll-up product filter), `getCategoryProductCount` (one category) / `getCategoryProductCounts` (bulk `GROUP BY` map of direct product counts, powers the admin tree's per-row count badge).
- `shp_tags` - name/slug both unique. `shp_product_tags` join table.
- `shp_collections` - name/slug(unique)/description/image_id/position/SEO fields. `shp_product_collections` join table (has its own `position` - product order within that collection).
- `shp_tax_classes` (name/code unique), `shp_shipping_zones` (name, postcodes JSONB array of prefixes - not `TEXT[]`, matches Directory/Gazette's existing JSONB-array precedent), `shp_tax_zone_rates` (zone+class unique, rate NUMERIC(5,4)), `shp_shipping_rates` (zone_id FK, type FLAT\|WEIGHT_BASED\|FREE, flat_rate/weight_rates JSONB array of `{upToKg,rate}`/free_threshold/estimated_days/position/is_active).
- `shp_digital_files` (filename/url/size/mime_type) + `shp_digital_downloads` (order_id/order_item_id/file_id FKs, unique `token`, download_count, expires_at).
- `shp_coupons` (code unique, type PERCENTAGE\|FIXED_AMOUNT\|FREE_SHIPPING, value/minimum_order_value/usage_limit/usage_count/per_customer_limit/starts_at/expires_at/is_active) + `shp_automatic_discounts` (same shape minus code/usage tracking, plus free_shipping_threshold/priority).
- `shp_orders` - order_number (unique, generated from a dedicated `shp_order_number_seq` Postgres sequence, not a COUNT(*) scheme, so concurrent checkouts can never collide), status (8-value CHECK), member_id (nullable, no FK - Members is optional), customer snapshot (email/name/phone), shipping_address/billing_address JSONB (`ShpAddress` shape), financials (subtotal/discount_amount/shipping_amount/tax_amount/total/tax_mode snapshot/currency), coupon_id FK + coupon_code snapshot, payment_method/payment_status/payment_reference/paid_at, shipping_rate_id (no FK, snapshot only) + shipping_rate_name.
- `shp_order_items` - order_id FK cascade, product_id FK **SET NULL** (product may later be deleted, snapshot fields survive it), product_name/sku/type snapshot, quantity/unit_price/tax_rate/tax_amount/total, refunded_qty, is_pre_order + pre_order_dispatch_date snapshot.
- `shp_refunds` (order_id FK, amount/reason/provider_refund_id/status/created_by) + `shp_refund_items` (refund_id FK cascade, order_item_id FK restrict, quantity/amount).
- `shp_order_requests` (**migration `015_order_requests.sql`**, v0.1.181) - customer-initiated cancel and return requests. `order_id` FK cascade, `member_id` (plain TEXT, nullable - guest orders get claimed by an account later, same reasoning as `shp_orders.member_id`), `type` CHECK `CANCEL|RETURN`, `status` CHECK `PENDING|APPROVED|DECLINED|WITHDRAWN`, `reason` (a code from `lib/order-requests.ts`, not free text - it is what an owner filters on), `customer_note`, `admin_note` (shown to the customer with the decision; private notes still go on `shp_order_notes`), `decided_at`, `decided_by` (core User id, plain TEXT no FK, exactly as `shp_refunds.created_by`), timestamps. Indexed on `order_id`, `member_id` and `(status, created_at)`. **Partial unique index `shp_order_requests_one_open_idx` on `(order_id) WHERE status = 'PENDING'`** is what actually settles a race between two requests on one order - the eligibility check only sees what was committed when it ran, so `createOrderRequest` catches the violation by index name (message match, as `google-sheet-products-for-shop`'s pull-job guard does) and returns 409. Plus `shp_order_request_items` (`request_id` FK cascade, `order_item_id` FK **RESTRICT**, `quantity` with a `> 0` CHECK, unique on `(request_id, order_item_id)` so summing cannot double-count). Third table pair in the same header-plus-lines shape as refunds and shipments. **A CANCEL writes no item rows at all** - it covers the whole order, and "everything" is not a list.
- `shp_shipments` (**migration `008_shipments.sql`**) - `order_id` FK cascade, `shipped_at` (when the parcel actually left, which is not always when it was recorded), `tracking_number`, `carrier`, `notes`, `created_at`, `updated_at`; index on `order_id`. Plus `shp_shipment_items` (`shipment_id` FK cascade, `order_item_id` FK **RESTRICT** - exactly as `shp_refund_items` does, a dispatched line is not something to lose quietly - `quantity` with a `> 0` CHECK); indexed on both `shipment_id` and `order_item_id`, the latter because the dispatched-per-line total is the hot read and it groups by that column. Same shape as the refund pair on purpose: a header row per event and a line per order item with the quantity that moved. **Dispatched quantity is DERIVED by summing `shp_shipment_items`** - there is deliberately no `dispatched_qty` counter on `shp_order_items`, so one writer, one truth, and nothing to drift when a shipment is deleted. The `ShpOrderStatus` list is unchanged: "partly/fully dispatched" is a computed display state, not a status value. Everything in 008 is idempotent (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`) because 001 now creates the same tables for fresh installs.
- `shp_order_notes` (is_internal flag - false = customer-visible) + `shp_order_emails` (send log: subject/to/sent_at/trigger - `trigger` values incl. `MANUAL` for admin-composed sends and `REPLY_CATCHER` reserved for the extension point).
- `shp_saved_addresses` - member_id (no FK, bare string), label (NULL on any row filed automatically from an order - nobody was asked for one), is_default (single-default enforced app-side in a transaction), address JSONB. **Written by checkout as well as by the account page** - see `lib/order-address-book.ts` / `rememberAddressForMember` in `lib/db/addresses.ts`. No migration: the table has existed since `001_initial.sql` and gained nothing.
- `shp_member_carts` (**migration `016_member_carts.sql`**, v0.1.192) - the signed-in shopper's basket, so one started on a phone is waiting on the laptop. `member_id` TEXT **primary key** (no FK, same reasoning as `shp_saved_addresses`), `lines` JSONB defaulting `'[]'`, `created_at`/`updated_at`. One row per member, the whole basket in one array in exactly the shape the browser already keeps in localStorage (`productId`/`quantity`/optional `lineId`+`meta`), stored verbatim and never interpreted - a companion module's per-line `meta` survives the hop to the other device untouched. **Nothing here is trusted for money**: price, stock and per-line delivery are still resolved at cart validate and again at checkout, so the row is a shopping list, not a quote. `updated_at` is bumped on every write and handed back, because that stamp is how the other device works out whether what it is holding has been overtaken. Helpers in `lib/db/member-cart.ts` (`getMemberCart`/`saveMemberCart`/`deleteMemberCart`, `MEMBER_CART_MAX_LINES` = 200); mirrored in `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs; added to `teardown` and to the GDPR export.
- `shp_email_templates` - trigger(unique)/subject/body_html/is_active. Seeded (INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) with all 10 triggers: `ORDER_CONFIRMED` (has the one `{{#if hasPreOrderItems}}` conditional block the renderer supports), `STATUS_PROCESSING`/`STATUS_SHIPPED`/`STATUS_COMPLETED`/`STATUS_CANCELLED`, `PARTIAL_SHIPPED`, `ADMIN_NEW_ORDER`, `LOW_STOCK`, `BACK_IN_STOCK`, `IMPORT_COMPLETE`. `PARTIAL_SHIPPED` ("Part of an order dispatched" in the admin template list) is seeded in **both** `001_initial.sql` and `008_shipments.sql`, with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on each side, because the 001 seed only ever reaches fresh installs while existing shops get the row from 008 on their next deploy - whichever runs first wins and an owner's edits are never overwritten by the other. Its subject and body use two mutually exclusive `{{#if}}` flags, `hasOutstanding` and `isFinalPart`, so the same template also covers the parcel that finishes an order off.
- `shp_back_in_stock_subscriptions` - product_id FK cascade, email, member_id nullable, unique(product_id,email) (idempotent subscribe), notified_at (null = pending, retained after fulfilment for reporting).
- `shp_import_jobs` - status(PENDING\|PROCESSING\|COMPLETED\|FAILED), filename, total/processed/created/updated/skipped row counts, errors JSONB array of `{row,reason}`, column_map JSONB, created_by, started_at/completed_at.
- `shp_related_products`/`shp_upsell_products` (product_id+related_id or product_id+upsell_id composite PK, position, both self-FK cascade to shp_products) + `shp_auto_exclude_products` (per-product exclusions from the automatic-recommendation fallback).
- `shp_suppliers` (**migration `007_suppliers.sql`, v0.1.74**) - `name`, `account_number`, `discount_percent` NUMERIC(5,2) (CHECK 0-100; NULL = none recorded, which is not the same as a recorded 0%), `status` (CHECK ENABLED\|DISABLED), `contact_name`/`phone`/`email`/`address`/`notes`, timestamps. Unique index on `LOWER(name)`, since the name **is** the link to products - two suppliers differing only in case would split one supplier's product count in two. No FK from `shp_products`: the link is `shp_products.supplier` matched on name, so `renameSupplier` updates both tables in one transaction and `deleteSupplier` deliberately leaves the products' names alone (re-adding the name picks them all back up). Counts come from one grouped pass over `shp_products` split on `catalogue_hidden` - false = catalogue products, true = variation child rows - so the products/variations split works whether or not shop-variations is installed. Helpers in `lib/db/suppliers.ts`; shared create/edit validation in `lib/supplier-schema.ts`. Added to `teardown`.
- `shp_supplier_catalogues` (**migration `010_supplier_catalogues.sql`, v0.1.91**) - a supplier's own catalogues/price lists: `supplier_id` (FK -> `shp_suppliers` ON DELETE CASCADE - unlike products, which are name-linked, a catalogue only exists inside its supplier row), `name`, `sheet_url` (nullable; the Google Sheet the catalogue lives in), `position` INTEGER for the owner's ordering, timestamps. Unique index on `(supplier_id, LOWER(name))`. Written by `replaceSupplierCatalogues(supplierId, list)` - delete-then-insert in one transaction, because the editor always hands over the whole list and no id is ever shown to the owner; read by `listSuppliersWithCounts` (admin screen, one extra query for all suppliers' catalogues) and `listSupplierCatalogues` (export shape: name + status + catalogues, no count aggregate). Validation is `SupplierCatalogueInput` + the `catalogues` array on `SupplierBody` (absent = leave alone, `[]` = none; case-insensitive duplicate names rejected in Zod so the unique index never surfaces as a 500; URL must match `^https?://\S+$`). Added to `teardown` (before `shp_suppliers`, though the DROP is CASCADE anyway).
- `shp_settings` - singleton (`id='singleton'`), single `config` JSONB column holding the whole `ShpConfig` blob (Q2 decision - no `shopConfig` column added to core `SiteConfig`, everything lives in this one module-owned row instead).
- **Retired**: `shp_page_layouts` (key(unique: `index`\|`product`\|`checkout`\|`confirmation`)/builder_data JSONB) - the original single-layout-per-page mechanism, superseded by the generic `Layout` model (see Layout system integration bullet above and Puck Integration section). Dropped from `001_initial.sql` and from the shared test DB; its default block arrangements were carried forward as each type's `publishByDefault` starter so on-site appearance didn't change.

**Permissions**

`shop.access` (read-only GETs across orders/products/customers - every admin route below marked "or access" accepts this in place of its normal key), `shop.manage` (supersedes every other shop key - settings, email templates, tax/shipping config), `shop.products` (products/categories/tags/collections/CSV import-export CRUD), `shop.orders` (orders/refunds/manual payment confirmation), `shop.customers` (customer list/detail), `shop.discounts` (coupons/automatic discounts), `shop.reports` (tax/revenue reports, no read-only fallback). Enforced via `modules/shop/lib/access.ts`'s `requireShopUser(key, {allowAccess?})`/`hasShopPermission`. Page-layout editing is **not** one of these any more - since it moved onto the core Layout system, it's gated by core `layouts.manage` instead (same as Directory/Gazette/Boards' own layout types), not any `shop.*` key.

**API Routes** (all served through `/api/m/shop/…` via the generated router)

Public (`/api/m/shop/public/…`, unauthenticated unless noted; mutating ones rate-limited via a module-owned in-memory limiter in `lib/rate-limit.ts` - not table-backed like contact-form's, since a rate-limit-only IP column on shp_back_in_stock_subscriptions would be a schema change for a secondary guard; resets on cold start, doesn't share state across serverless instances):
- `GET /products` (filters: category/tag/collection/type/search/pagination, ACTIVE only), `GET /products/[slug]`, `GET /products/[slug]/related`, `GET /products/[slug]/upsells`, `GET /categories`, `GET /categories/[slug]`, `GET /collections`, `GET /collections/[slug]`, `GET /tags`.
- `GET /config` (client-safe config slice: currency, tax mode, enabled payment methods filtered by actual env presence, Stripe publishable key, checkout steps, shop status).
- `POST /cart/validate` (re-checks stock/price/status for client localStorage cart lines; media lookup runs in parallel with the line resolve, and the two module-registry reads collapsed to one behind a 30s TTL memo in `lib/line-meta.ts`).
- `POST /cart/upsells` (`{productIds[]}` (1-50) → merged, de-duplicated upsell suggestions for the whole cart in ONE request - `resolveUpsellsForProducts` batches the manual-link + product reads; replaces the strip's old catalogue-list + per-product-upsells waterfall).
- `POST /checkout/session` (server-only totals - subtotal/discount/shipping/tax/total, never trusts client maths), `POST /checkout/apply-coupon`, `POST /checkout/payment-intent` (**PROTECTED** - creates the PENDING `shp_orders` row + item snapshot per Q8, then the provider's payment intent), `POST /checkout/confirm` (**PROTECTED** - confirms via the provider, idempotent PAID transition, triggers `fulfillPaidOrder`).
- `GET /orders/status?orderNumber=&email=` (guest lookup, both must match - no enumeration), `GET /downloads/[token]` (**PROTECTED** - token/expiry/download-limit checks, then streams the file bytes through this endpoint rather than redirecting, so the permanent underlying storage URL is never exposed to the client). Three things about the response are deliberate: `Content-Disposition` is built by `lib/download-name.ts`, never interpolated from `shp_digital_files.filename` (the upload route writes that verbatim from the admin's `file.name`, and a quote or a CR/LF in it rewrites the header); `Content-Length` is relayed from the upstream response, never the `size` column, since a row disagreeing with its bytes truncates the transfer or hangs it; and `incrementDownloadCount` runs in the stream's `flush()`, so only a transfer that finished costs a customer one of their limited downloads. Always `attachment` + `nosniff`, as its sibling is: the attachment stops a browser rendering the bytes, and nosniff stops it overriding the stored `Content-Type` and rendering them anyway - worth more here than in the sibling, since this route's upload allowlist is by *declared* MIME type rather than by extension.
- `POST /back-in-stock` (idempotent subscribe), `DELETE /back-in-stock?token=` (**PROTECTED** - HMAC-signed unsubscribe token via `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, no DB lookup needed to validate it).

Member (`/api/m/shop/member/…`, `getMemberFromCookie()` gated): `GET /orders`, `GET /orders/[id]`, `GET/POST /addresses`, `PUT/DELETE /addresses/[id]`, `GET/PUT /cart` (the cross-device basket - GET returns `{memberId, lines, updatedAt|null}`, PUT replaces the whole `lines` array and returns the new `updatedAt`; 401 is the normal answer for a guest and is how the browser learns to stop syncing), `GET /gdpr-export` (internal-bearer only, `verifyInternalExportBearer` - called self-origin by core's member data-export assembler, feeds the `memberExtensions.dataExportPath` manifest entry).

Webhooks (`/api/m/shop/webhooks/…`, unauthenticated, signature-verified, **PROTECTED**): `POST /stripe` (verifies `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, handles `payment_intent.succeeded`/`payment_intent.payment_failed`/`charge.refunded`), `POST /paypal` (verifies via PayPal's own verify-webhook-signature endpoint using `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID`, handles `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED`/`PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED`). Both idempotent - `markOrderPaid`'s `WHERE payment_status != 'PAID'` clause makes a replayed event a no-op.

Cron (`/api/m/shop/cron/…`, `CRON_SECRET` bearer): `GET/POST /low-stock-alerts` - daily 07:00, also covers Q11 import-job retention (30 days) and Q8 abandoned-PENDING-order pruning (24h).

Admin (`/api/m/shop/admin/…`, session + permission gated per route above): full CRUD for `products` (+ `[id]/related`, `[id]/upsells`, `[id]/duplicate` (POST, clones the row + media/categories/tags/collections/manual-recommendation lists into a fresh DRAFT with a new slug and no SKU, returns `{id,slug}`), `bulk` (POST `{action:'delete'|'status', ids[], status?}` - capped at 200 ids, FK-violation → friendly 409), `export`/`import-template`/`import`(+`[id]` status poll)). The `GET` list now also takes `sort` (`newest`/`oldest`/`name-asc|desc`/`price-asc|desc`/`stock-asc|desc`, whitelisted to a fixed `ORDER BY` map, never interpolated) and `stock` (`in`/`low`/`out`), and its response carries `images` (one primary-image url per product for the list thumbnails, batched via `getPrimaryProductImages`); the single-row `DELETE` catches FK violations the same way as `bulk`. Order-line history survives any delete (`shp_order_items.product_id` is ON DELETE SET NULL). Sibling admin routes: `categories` (GET returns `{categories, productCounts}` - the latter a per-category direct-product-count map for the admin tree; POST/PUT accept `parentId` + `productDisplayMode`; PUT cycle-guards a reparent; DELETE cascades the sub-tree; `+ reorder` persists a sibling order), `tags`, `collections`, `tax-classes`, `tax-zone-rates`, `shipping-zones`(+ nested rates GET), `shipping-rates`, `coupons`, `automatic-discounts`; `orders` (list+manual-create; the `GET` list takes `search`/`status`/`paymentStatus`/`fulfilment`/`preOrder`/`open`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`/`sort`/`page`/`perPage`, all read through the single `lib/order-filters.ts` `parseOrderListFilter` the CSV export also uses, and returns `{orders, total, metrics, overview}` - `metrics` is one `getOrderRowMetrics` query for the whole page (line/unit/refunded/dispatched/outstanding counts + `hasPreOrder`, dispatched units summed through a subquery keyed by order item so a parcel can never fan a line out twice), `overview` only when `stats=1` (`getOrdersOverview`: awaiting-payment / to-send / pre-orders / 30-day paid revenue, each defined as exactly the filter its tile links to, so a counter and its list always agree)), `orders/bulk` (POST `{action:'status', ids[] (max 200), status, sendEmail}` - every id goes through the same `applyOrderStatusChange` as the single route, sequentially, and a per-order refusal is reported by order number rather than aborting the run), `orders/export` (CSV of the current filters, one row per order, paging ignored and capped at 5000, amounts unformatted for spreadsheets), `[id]` detail (now also returns `refundItems`, `customer` (`getCustomerSummary`: order count, paid count, total spent, first order) and `authors` (note/refund `created_by` resolved to display names via core `prisma.user`)), `[id]/status` (**PROTECTED** - thin wrapper over `lib/order-status.ts` `applyOrderStatusChange`, which holds the whole policy in one place because the bulk route makes the same change: decrements stock for pre-order items on SHIPPED per addendum B.4, only on a genuine transition, and refuses SHIPPED with a 409 + plain-English explanation while `preOrderMixedCartBehaviour` is HOLD_ALL and pre-order lines are outstanding; a genuine transition to CANCELLED releases the pre-order allocation), `[id]/notes`, `[id]/email`, `[id]/refund` (**PROTECTED** - per-item, delegates to `processRefund`, which validates under an order-wide advisory lock and calls the provider outside any transaction), `[id]/dispatch` (**PROTECTED**, part-dispatch: **POST** records one dispatch of a subset of the order's lines (`items[]`, optional `trackingNumber`/`carrier`/`notes`/`shippedAt` - a plain date string is coerced, since owners back-date a parcel that went out on Friday - and `emailCustomer`; every cap is enforced inside `createShipment` and its rejections are handed back verbatim because they already read as plain English; a failed dispatch email is logged and stepped over rather than rolling the shipment back). **GET** returns everything the order screen needs in one call: the per-line dispatch summary, the shipments already recorded, and `preOrderHold` (whether the shop's hold-everything policy currently applies, how many lines are outstanding and the latest expected date) - it rides on this route rather than the main order GET so the dispatch block can refresh itself without re-fetching the whole order. This route only EXPLAINS the hold; `[id]/status` ENFORCES it, and both read the same `outstandingPreOrderItems`. **DELETE** `?shipmentId=` undoes a dispatch recorded by mistake, scoped to this order so an id from elsewhere cannot be deleted through it - the totals fall back out on their own because they are summed from the shipment's lines), `[id]/confirm-payment`); `customers` (list, `[id]` keyed by URL-encoded email - no dedicated table); `reports/tax`(+`?format=csv`)/`reports/revenue`; `dashboard-widget`; `back-in-stock`; `suppliers` (GET list with per-supplier product/variation counts, or `?for=picker` for just the enabled names - the picker form skips the count aggregate, which is the right cost for the Suppliers screen and the wrong one for opening a product; POST create with a friendly 409 on a duplicate name; `[id]` PUT - a name change routes through `renameSupplier` - and DELETE. Both writes also accept an optional `catalogues[]` (`{name, sheetUrl}`) which is persisted with `replaceSupplierCatalogues`; omitted leaves the existing catalogues alone, `[]` clears them. `SuppliersScreen` edits them as a repeating name+URL block in the supplier form, blank rows dropped client-side, and lists them per supplier on the table as links); `settings` (shopConfig read/merge-update, and syncs the Suppliers sidebar link on both GET and PUT). Layout editing for all six page types goes through the core `/api/admin/layouts*` routes now (see Layout system integration bullet above) - there is no shop-specific layout-editing route any more (`admin/page-layouts/[key]` retired along with the table it served).

**Payment providers** (`modules/shop/lib/payments/`, **PROTECTED - entire directory**)
- `provider.ts` - the `ShpPaymentProvider` interface (`createIntent`/`confirmPayment`/`refundOrder`/optional `handleWebhook`/optional `getLabel`) every provider implements. `getLabel()` is for a method the site owner gets to name themselves: it is resolved per request, and the static `label` is the fallback when it is absent, blank or throws.
- `stripe.ts` - `stripe` npm SDK (new core dependency, see below), no `apiVersion` pinned (uses the account's dashboard default rather than guessing a literal date string the installed major might reject), server always re-fetches the PaymentIntent and validates its own status **and** amount/currency against the order before trusting a client "confirmed" claim.
- `paypal.ts` - raw REST, no SDK (spec's own instruction, keeps the bundle lean), OAuth token cached in-memory with expiry, sandbox/live base URL switches on `PAYPAL_MODE`, capture amount/currency checked against the order on confirm.
- `bank-transfer.ts`/`cash.ts` - instructions-from-config intents, `confirmPayment` always fails (admin confirms manually via the order detail page's "Confirm payment" action), refunds are manual-only.
- `registry.ts` - `paymentProviders: Record<ShpPaymentMethod, ShpPaymentProvider>` lookup used by every route above, plus `resolveProviderLabel(provider)` and the now-async `getPaymentMethodLabels()`. Both go through a provider's `getLabel()` where it has one, so an owner-set name reaches the checkout radio (`GET public/config`), the admin Payments tab (`GET admin/settings`) and the guest order lookup (`GET public/orders/status`) from one place.

**Sanctioned core diffs** (all outside `modules/shop/`, each minimal/isolated, flagged PROTECTED in-code):
- `package.json`/`package-lock.json` - added `stripe` (^22.x) as a core runtime dependency. Modules can't add their own npm dependencies (they compile inside core's Next build); precedent: `shiki` for Gazette, `leaflet`/`leaflet.markercluster` for Directory.
- `proxy.ts`'s `buildCsp()` - added `https://js.stripe.com` to `script-src`, `https://api.stripe.com` to `connect-src`, and a new `frame-src 'self' https://js.stripe.com https://hooks.stripe.com` directive (didn't exist before - Stripe Elements renders card fields and 3D Secure challenges in hidden iframes). **`blob:` joined `connect-src` in v0.5.484** for product-3d-views-for-shop's GLB textures (full reasoning in that module's section) - a `blob:` URL is same-origin, unguessable and readable only by the document that minted it, so it widens nothing. **A `worker-src 'self' blob:` directive joined it in v0.5.612** for the same module's Draco decoder, which three builds as a Worker from a Blob URL; it had to be spelled out because `worker-src` falls back to `child-src` then `script-src`, and `script-src` carries no `blob:`. Note `img-src` has carried `blob:` since long before and is **not** the directive a `fetch()` of a blob URL consults; that near-miss is exactly what made the bug read as a bad model file. **`'wasm-unsafe-eval'` joined `script-src` in the working tree (unreleased)** for product-3d-views-for-shop's WebAssembly mesh decoder (Draco/Meshopt) - without it the admin "Detect from model" button died with a CSP refusal on live sites. It permits only `WebAssembly.compile`/`instantiate`, not JS `eval()`; `'unsafe-eval'` stays banned.
- Product image filing (`lib/media/product-media.ts`, `reorganiseProductMedia(productId, {folderProductId?})`): runs on every product `PUT` after the media/category writes. Files each `IMAGE` in `shp_product_media` into the core media library under **Shop / <master category trail> / <product name>** (no master → "Uncategorised") via core's `getOrCreateFolderByPath(['Shop', ...<category ancestor names>, <product name>])` + `moveOrRenameMedia(id, {targetFolderId, exactName:true, collision:'suffix'})` - **no `newName` is passed, so the file keeps whatever name it was uploaded under; this only organises into the folder, it never renames** (until 2026-07-26 it also renumbered every image to `<product-slug><n>` on each save - removed, along with the now-dead `planImageRenames` renumber-ordering helper and its test, because renaming a file the owner uploaded was never something asked for). A same-folder name clash is given a numeric suffix (`collision:'suffix'`) rather than overwritten (`'replace'`, the old behaviour). **Category nesting (working tree):** the category segment is the master's whole `getCategoryAncestorPath` trail (root → … → leaf), so a sub-category product nests inside its parent's folder (`shop/office-tables/meeting-boardroom-tables/<product>`) rather than a flat leaf folder - `productFolderSegments` (shared by `getProductMediaFolderId`/`findProductMediaFolderId`, and therefore by the 3D/downloads/variations subfolder resolvers) builds it. **Existing products relocate on save:** before the per-image filing, `relocateProductFolderIfMoved` finds the product's current folder (off an existing managed image's `folderId`) and, if the category tree has moved its home, `moveFolder`s the whole folder under its new parent - one re-key carries the product's images, 3D models and downloads together, and each module's stored url follows (shop/variations media-reference rewriters repoint their tables; the downloads route heals `pdl_files` from `media_id` on next read). No-op when already in place, when the product has no folder yet, or on a destination name clash (two products sharing a name → per-image filing is the fallback and 3D/downloads re-file on next upload). Only urls resolving to a managed core `Media` row are moved (external urls / video embeds left as-is); the row's `url` is rewritten to the relocated one. Idempotent (an already-filed image is a no-op) and best-effort per image (one relocate failure doesn't fail the save). The editor refetches after save so thumbnails follow the moved blobs. `exactName` keeps the stored key nanoid-free so the url reads `…/shop/<category>/<product>/<slug><n>.<ext>` exactly - this filing is the **only** consumer of `exactName`, so it owns the uniqueness contract `lib/media/keys.ts` now keeps (a shared 40-char clip used to break it; see the Media section). `folderProductId` files a product's images under a **different** product's folder while still naming them from its own slug - the one consumer is shop-variations' variant `PATCH`, which passes the parent so variant images land beside the parent's (a variant child is a hidden, category-less product, so unaided it would file under "Uncategorised"). Two products sharing a name share a folder; filenames stay unique because the slug is.
- Category picture filing (`lib/media/category-media.ts`, v0.1.151): a category's own picture belongs in **Shop / <the category's ancestor trail>** - the folder holding its products' folders - not the library root it used to land in. `categoryFolderSegments(categoryId, {name?, parentId?})` builds `['Shop', ...<parent trail names>, <category name>]` through `sanitizeFolderSegment` (lower-cased, so the folder IS the storage path); the two overrides carry what the edit panel currently holds so a picture picked after a rename or a move is filed where the save is about to put the category. `getCategoryMediaFolderId` creates the path, `findCategoryMediaFolderId` walks it look-only (deepest existing folder, so browsing creates nothing) - the same create/find pair, and the same `GET`/`POST` route split (`app/api/admin/categories/[id]/media-folder`, gate `shop.products`), that products and `product-attributes-for-shop` swatches use. `fileCategoryImage(categoryId)` moves the picture with `moveOrRenameMedia(id, {targetFolderId, exactName:true, collision:'suffix'})` - no `newName`, so the uploaded name survives - and writes the relocated url back to `shp_categories.image_url` (the shop's media-reference rewriter would also catch it; the explicit write keeps the filing correct on its own terms). No-op unless the url resolves to a managed `Media` row, so nothing is created for a category with no picture or an externally hosted one, and best-effort: a failure `console.warn`s rather than failing the save. Callers: the category `PUT` (after the write, so it follows a rename or re-parent), the `POST` when it carries an `imageUrl`, and `categories/reorder` for each id when `parentId` is sent (a drag-drop re-parent; the arrows omit it). Descendant categories' pictures re-file on their own next save, mirroring how products under a moved category do. `CategoriesScreen` passes `resolveFolderId`/`resolveInitialFolderId` to `MediaPickerModal`, so uploads go straight into the folder and the picker opens there.
- `lib/media/upload.ts` - purely additive `NonImageUploadMode` type + `validateNonImageUpload(mimeType, sizeBytes, mode)` export for the digital-file upload path (declares its own mime/size allowlist, skips the sharp image-decode sniff entirely since there's no universal "valid PDF/zip" magic-byte check the way there is for images). The existing image-only `validateUpload`/`uploadMedia`/`deleteMedia`/`downloadMedia`/`saveMediaRecord` are untouched. Shop's digital files are **not** wired into the core `Media` table at all (no `saveMediaRecord` call) - they're stored in shop's own `shp_digital_files` table via `uploadMedia()`'s returned key/url only, since they're not part of core's page/logo Media referencing system.
- `.env.example` - added the seven Stripe/PayPal env var rows (all optional; a payment method with unset keys is filtered out of `enabledPaymentMethods` server-side, never offered at checkout - `modules/shop/lib/env.ts`'s `isStripeConfigured`/`isPayPalConfigured`).
- `app/api/admin/env/route.ts`'s `ALLOWED_KEYS` - added the same seven Stripe/PayPal vars so they're settable through the core env-var UI/API (Vercel project env vars, admin-only per `isAdmin()`). `lib/notifications/deployment.ts` gained a `PAYMENT_KEYS` set feeding `labelForEnvKeys()` → "Payment provider keys updated" on the existing deployment-needed notification.

**Admin pages** (`/cactus-admin/m/shop/…`)

`products` (**redesigned list, `ProductsScreen.tsx` + `products-screen-css.ts` prefix `sps-`, tokens only**: 40px thumbnails from the GET response's `images`, coloured type/status/stock badges (stock badge derives In/Low/Out/Not-tracked from `trackInventory`+`stockCount`+`lowStockThreshold`), a pre-order chip, compare-at strike-through price, and a per-row `⋯` menu (fixed-positioned so the table's overflow container never clips it - Edit / Duplicate / Delete). A filter toolbar drives the server: debounced name/SKU search, a status segmented control (All/Active/Draft/Archived), type + stock selects, and a sort select; results paginate 20/page (server `page`/`perPage`, `total` shown as "Showing X–Y of Z"). Row checkboxes + a select-all (indeterminate) header raise a sticky **bulk bar** - Set active / Set draft / Archive / Delete - posting to `admin/products/bulk`; selection is dropped on every reload so a bulk action can never touch an off-page row. Delete (single via the row menu, or bulk) confirms through the shop's own `useConfirm` dialog. Distinct empty states for no-products-at-all vs no-filter-match. Still carries the back-in-stock "N waiting" link, Export/Import-template buttons, and the "Import CSV" button opening `ImportModal.tsx` - upload → auto-detects header mismatches via `headerMatchesFormat()` and only then shows a column-mapping step → polls job progress, recent-imports log), `products/[id]` (**tabbed editor, rebuilt v0.1.38** - see "Product editor" below), `categories` (indented tree: search box, collapsible branches, **drag-and-drop** to reorder among siblings or re-nest under any category plus ↑/↓ arrows and an inline edit panel that renames/reparents/sets the per-category display mode), `collections` (flat list + inline rename/delete, no drag-reorder UI yet), `orders` (**redesigned list, `OrdersScreen.tsx` + shared `orders-screen-css.ts` prefix `sox-`, tokens only**: four overview tiles (Awaiting payment / To send / Pre-orders / last-30-days revenue) that double as one-click filters - the revenue tile deliberately does not link, since it counts by `paid_at` and the list filters on `created_at`; a debounced order-number/name/email search, a status segmented control, payment (incl. a synthetic `UNPAID` = PENDING+AWAITING_CONFIRMATION), dispatch-state and date-preset selects with custom from/to, "Pre-orders only" and "Hide cancelled" toggles, a sort select and 25/50/100 per page. Every control round-trips through the query string via `history.replaceState`, so a filtered list is linkable and the back button works. Rows carry payment / dispatch / status badges, item counts, a "Account" chip for a member order and a `⋯` menu (open, customer, mailto, copy email, quick status change); checkboxes + select-all raise a sticky bulk bar posting to `orders/bulk` with an "Email the customers" tick, and any per-order refusal is listed by order number. Export CSV carries the current filters. Distinct empty states for no-orders vs no-match), `orders/[id]` (**redesigned, `OrderDetailScreen.tsx`, two columns collapsing at 980px**: header with status/payment/dispatch badges and an action bar (Dispatch items / Email customer / Refund / Print); main column = items table (SKU, unit price, per-line sent/to-go/refunded/pre-order pills, `lineMeta` fields, link back to the product), Parcels with a per-parcel **Undo** wired to the long-unused `DELETE .../dispatch?shipmentId=`, digital downloads with a copy-link button (`/shop/downloads/<token>`, download count + expiry), "Agreed at checkout", and a single **History** timeline merging placed/paid/notes/emails/parcels/refunds newest-first with the note composer on top - the four separate lists it replaces made the chronology a mental exercise; sidebar = status select + email-on-change tick + "Payment received" for manual methods, customer panel (guest vs account, mailto/tel, prior-order count and spend, link to their orders), delivery and billing addresses with copy-to-clipboard, payment details, and totals incl. coupon code, shipping rate name, tax mode, refunded and kept. `EmailCustomerModal.tsx` finally gives `POST .../email` a UI (plain text escaped and wrapped to HTML here, logged to the order's history like any automatic email). A `@media print` block turns the page into a packing slip. Still renders the Customer Communications section only when another module - e.g. Reply Catcher - actually contributes to the `shop.order-messages` extension point, now in a matching card), `customers`, `customers/[id]`, `discounts` (Coupons/Automatic tabs via the shared core `TabStrip`, real forms - not `prompt()` - covering type incl. fixed-amount/free-shipping, expiry window, usage/per-customer limits, minimum order value, free-shipping threshold, priority; edit + delete on both coupons and automatic discounts), `reports` (Revenue/Tax tabs via the shared core `TabStrip`), `back-in-stock` (no nav entry - reached from the products list), `tax-shipping` (`TaxShippingScreen.tsx` - tax classes CRUD (new tax class's `code` auto-slugs from `name`, read-only until unlocked via a pencil button), zones (name + postcode-prefix list, empty list = catch-all matched when no other zone's prefix matches, so one zone can cover a whole country without listing postcodes) picker+detail, per-zone tax rate per class, per-zone shipping rates (flat/weight-banded/free) picker+detail). `ShopSettingsTab` renders on core `/cactus-admin/config`, internal `TabStrip` sub-tabs (General/Checkout/Payments/Notifications) covering the full `ShpConfig` shape: store identity+units/SEO/shop status, tax mode+checkout rules (guest checkout, min/max order value, phone requirement, per-step checkout-steps editor, back-in-stock account prompt, pre-order mixed-cart behaviour), the Payments sub-tab (delegated whole to `PaymentsSettings.tsx` - see the Payments settings entry below), and the order/low-stock alert addresses. The Email templates sub-tab is gone: the shop's ten order emails are registered with core through the manifest `emailTemplates` seam and edited on Settings > Email > Templates with every other email on the site (a line on the Notifications sub-tab says so). **Publishes two hosted-panel slots** (v0.1.53) for other modules' `settingsTabs` `host` entries: `shop.payments` (taken as the labelled shape since 0.1.174 - one chip per panel on the Payments sub-tab, matched to its payment method by `getModuleProviderEntryIds()` - GoCardless, Square, Crezco) and `shop.settings-sub-tabs` (each contributed panel gets its own labelled sub-tab after shop's own, in module-load order - product-3d-views-for-shop's "3D Viewer"). Contributed sub-tabs save through their own module's API, so shop's own "Save settings" button stands down while one is showing. Both slots are empty (render nothing) on a shop with no such add-ons. `requiresCoreVersion` **0.5.490** from v0.1.53 (imports `lib/modules/hosted-settings.ts`).

**Payments settings** (`components/admin/PaymentsSettings.tsx`, new in v0.1.174 - the whole Payments sub-tab, delegated out of `ShopSettingsTab.tsx`)

Chip strip, then one panel. First chip **Payment methods** (count badge "live/total"), then one chip per method that has settings of its own - shop's four built-ins, then each module-contributed method whose `panelId` matches a panel in the `shop.payments` slot, then any hosted panel no method claimed. Chips carry a status dot (green/amber/muted). Chip order follows the arranged method order, so the strip and the list agree.

- **The list** renders every entry of `paymentMethods[]` from `GET admin/settings`: drag handle (HTML5 DnD - `dragstart` is cancelled unless the event target is inside `[data-drag-handle]`, so the row's own buttons never start a drag) + ▲▼ buttons (which restore focus to the moved row's arrow afterwards, falling back to the opposite arrow when the one just pressed has become disabled at an end), label, a status badge derived from `methodState()` (**Showing at checkout** / **Not finished** / **Off**), a one-line reason, a Set up / Settings link into that method's chip, and a `role="switch"` on/off. Under it, "What a shopper will see" spells the live order out in a sentence, or warns in an `alert-warning` when nothing can be paid with at all.
- **Every mutation writes the order out in full** (`writeOrder(ordered.map(m => m.id))`), including a plain on/off - otherwise switching a method off and on again would send it to the back of the checkout queue, since the fallback order is `enabledPaymentMethods` and toggling appends.
- **The on/off writes both lists**: on = added to `enabledPaymentMethods`, removed from `disabledPaymentMethods`; off = the reverse. One rule for built-in and contributed methods alike, and it is the veto list that makes the switch mean something for a contributed method (whose own module still has its own enable toggle - shop cannot and does not write to it).
- **Built-in panels** (`BuiltInMethodPanel`) carry the switch, an honest alert when a method is switched on but not ready, the instructions textarea for BANK_TRANSFER/CASH (`bankTransferInstructions`/`cashInstructions`, saved by shop's own Save button) with a **Show this on the checkout page too** switch beneath it (`bankTransferInstructionsOnCheckout`/`cashInstructionsOnCheckout`, default true; off makes the method's `createIntent` return `{}` so the wording never reaches the checkout response at all - the thank-you page and the order page read it from config separately and are unaffected), and for STRIPE/PAYPAL the `/api/admin/env` credential boxes (own Save button, own "live from the next deployment" note, `envAdminAllowed === false` explains the gate) plus a read-only webhook address (`/api/m/shop/webhooks/stripe`, `/api/m/shop/webhooks/paypal`) built from `window.location.origin` in an effect.
- **A contributed panel gets no switch and no Save button** - it saves itself, exactly as a contributed sub-tab does. `ShopSettingsTab` hides its own Save whenever `isHostedPaymentPanelTab(paymentTab)`, which is why the active payments chip is lifted into the parent. A status band at the top of the panel says what state the method is in and links back to the list to change it.


**Product editor** (`components/admin/ProductEditor.tsx` + `components/admin/product-editor/`, rebuilt v0.1.38)

Tabbed shell with a sticky sidebar, replacing the single 700px column of stacked sections. Sidebar (collapses above the tabs under 1100px) carries status, a "View on the shop" link, cover thumbnail, at-a-glance price/stock/SKU, **the only Save button on the page**, and a **Manage card** (Duplicate product → POST `[id]/duplicate` then navigates to the new draft; Delete product → `useConfirm` then DELETE then back to the list). Both clear `dirtyRef` before their hard navigation so the unsaved-changes guard doesn't prompt - the product is being replaced or removed, so in-progress edits are moot. Own tabs: Details, Images, Pricing, Stock & delivery, Organisation, Recommendations, Search, plus Download (only when `type === 'DIGITAL'`). Files: `model.ts` (form shape, `toEditorState`/`toProductBody`, per-tab dirty compare, validation), `fields.tsx` (Field/Control/Select/Switch primitives; every field has a real `<label>`, hint and inline error wired through `aria-describedby`), `editor-css.ts` (prefix `spe-`, tokens only, injected once - real CSS so focus rings/hover/responsive work), `panels/*.tsx`, `context.tsx`.

- **Fields the old editor never exposed, all already accepted by the `PUT` and stored**: `barcode`, `weight`+`weightUnit`, `dimensionL/W/H`+`dimensionUnit` (these feed weight-priced shipping rates), and `regenerateSlug` (a "rebuild the web address from the name on save" switch; the API takes the flag, not a free-text slug). `catalogueHidden` is deliberately **not** exposed - it is the internal marker for variant child products, not a "hide from catalogue" toggle, and the page refuses to open a `catalogueHidden` product at all.
- **Numeric fields are held as strings** and converted once in `toProductBody`, so a half-typed `12.` or a cleared box stays what was typed. Validation is computed from the first keystroke but only shown after a save is attempted (`showErrors`); a failed save jumps to the offending tab via `tabForField`.
- **Position is the only cover.** `toProductBody` re-stamps `isPrimary: i === 0` from the array order. `setProductMedia` honours a supplied `isPrimary` over order and `card-template.tsx` reads `media.find(m => m.isPrimary) ?? media[0]`, so round-tripping the loaded flag unchanged would have meant drag-to-reorder moved the image but not the cover.
- **Save races.** The form stays interactive during a save. The post-save reload (needed because images may be re-filed server-side) only takes the server's copy wholesale when nothing was touched since the save started (`prev === current`); otherwise the admin's edits stand and the new baseline just marks them unsaved again. Silently binning what someone typed is the worst kind of bug.
- **`shop.product-editor-sections` is now a tab contract.** Manifest entries gained optional `label` (tab name; falls back to a prettified id) and `order` (sorted among the editor's own via `SHOP_TAB_ORDER`, default 999 = last). The page renders each contributed **server** component and passes it as a `ReactNode` into the client shell, which renders it inside `ProductEditorTabScope`. All panels stay mounted (`hidden` on the inactive ones) so a half-finished edit survives a trip to another tab and contributed tabs can report state while unopened.
- **`product-editor/context.tsx` is the public API for contributed tabs** (`shop-variations` and `product-attributes-for-shop` are the live consumers): `useProductEditorSave({dirty, save})` registers a tab's unsaved edits with the single Save button (throw an `Error` from `save` to fail it; the message is shown, prefixed with the tab name, and one failing tab does not roll the others back); `useProductEditorTabBadge(text)` puts a count on the tab label; `useProductEditorCurrency()` hands over the already-loaded currency symbol so a tab need not re-fetch shop config. All three are inert outside the editor. Registration keys off `useId()` + the scope's tab id, so a tab never names itself. Dirty tabs get an amber dot and a chip in the sidebar; errored tabs get a red one. Navigation away while dirty is guarded by core's `useUnsavedChanges` + `UnsavedChangesModal`.
