- Tab selection mirrors to `?tab=<id>` via `replaceState` (deep-linkable; `tab` is read once on the server and passed as `initialTab`, so no `useSearchParams` Suspense boundary). The active tab is **derived**, not stored, so a `?tab=` naming an uninstalled module, or a tab that vanishes when a product stops being digital, falls back to the first tab instead of stranding the view.
- **Panels must be allowed to shrink (v0.1.39).** `.spe-panel>*,.spe-grid>*{min-width:0}` in `editor-css.ts` is load-bearing for any tab holding something wide. Grid children default to `min-width:auto` (their content-based minimum), and a scroll container still propagates its contents' min-content size up through block flow, so without the floor a wide panel overflows the `minmax(0,1fr)` main column and the sticky sidebar paints over it - `shop-variations`' nowrap variants table hit exactly this. A contributed tab wanting a wide surface should wrap it in its own `overflow-x:auto`, which only works because of this rule. Note `minmax(0,1fr)` on `.spe-grid-2/3/4` floors the track, not the item, hence the separate `.spe-field{min-width:0}`.

**Public pages** (`/shop/…`, via `publicBasePath: "shop"`)

**CLOSED gate (v0.1.51).** `getShopGate()` (`modules/shop/lib/access.ts`) is the single check for `shopStatus === 'CLOSED'`, and **every** public page above calls it first, rendering `<ShopClosedNotice message={gate.message} />` (`components/public/ShopClosedNotice.tsx`) when `gate.blocked`. Staff who pass `canPreviewClosedShop()` (`shop.access`/`shop.manage`, and any protected role via `hasPermission`) instead get `gate.staffPreview` and see the real page with a `<ShopStaffPreviewBanner />` on top. Until v0.1.51 only `/shop` itself had this check inline, so a closed shop's product/category/collection/cart/checkout/order/account/download pages all rendered in full to anyone with the URL. The gate is per-page by necessity: module public pages are dispatched individually through `resolveModulePublicPage`, so there is no shared Next layout to hang it on - **a new page under `app/public/shop/` is unprotected until it calls `getShopGate()` itself.** `generateMetadata` on the product/category/collection pages checks it too, so a closed shop does not publish its product names. The same check backs the public data routes as `shopClosedResponse()` (503 + the owner's closed message), on `products`(+`[slug]`/`related`/`upsells`), `categories`(+`[slug]`), `collections`(+`[slug]`), `tags`, `cart/validate`, `cart/upsells`, `orders/status`, `downloads/[token]`, and back-in-stock `POST` - otherwise the catalogue stayed readable as JSON while the shop was shut. Deliberately **not** gated: `config` (carries `shopClosedMessage` itself and feeds the sitewide header cart), back-in-stock unsubscribe (`GET`/`DELETE` - links already in inboxes must keep working), and `checkout/confirm` (must not strand a payment already taken); `checkout/payment-intent` + `checkout/session` keep their own stricter `!== 'OPEN'` rejection, which also blocks staff.

`/shop` (index, resolves the `shopIndex` layout via `resolveThemeLayout`, honours `shopStatus` CLOSED), `/shop/products/[slug]` (resolves `shopProduct`, 404s if none published; `productSlug`/`productId`/`inStock` injected into `ShopProductDetail`/`ShopRelatedProducts`/`ShopUpsellProducts`/`ShopBackInStockForm` block props via `lib/inject-product-context.ts` - mirrors core's `resolveTemplateData` context-injection pattern for MenuBlock etc, since these blocks have no per-instance slug of their own in the stored template), `/shop/categories/[slug]` (resolves `shopCategory`, falls back to the original hardcoded plain grid when none published), `/shop/collections/[slug]` (resolves `shopCollection`, same fallback pattern), `/shop/cart` (resolves the `shopCart` layout via `resolveThemeLayout` and renders it with `getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig('shopCart')`; the `<h1>Your cart</h1>` stays in the page shell; falls back to the original hardcoded client-side cart UI + coupon field + `ShopUpsellProducts` when no `shopCart` layout is published, so never blank), `/shop/checkout` (resolves `shopCheckout`; wrapper is 1100px when a layout is published (v0.1.158 - two-column designs were unusable in the old 640px) and 640px for the fallback; no published layout -> renders the full hardcoded default flow (order summary + contact + shipping + payment + review), matching the cart page's fallback pattern, instead of a bare heading), `/shop/checkout/confirmation` (resolves `shopConfirmation`), `/shop/orders/[orderNumber]` (guest lookup form), `/shop/downloads/[token]` (friendly expired/limit-reached states, real download via the API route), `/shop/account/orders`(+`[id]`, +`[id]/receipt`)/`/shop/account/addresses` (member-session-gated, 404 when Members disabled, redirect to `{memberAreaPath}/login?redirect=` when signed out). From v0.1.181 all three wrap `MemberAccountShell` so they carry the account tab bar instead of rendering bare. **Orders list**: status/fulfilment/open-request pills, up to four product thumbnails, item count, total, and four filter chips (All / In progress / Completed / Cancelled) driven by `?show=` rather than client state, so it works with JS off. **Order detail**: the manual-payment instructions first of all on a bank transfer or cash order (warning-toned with the amount while the money is outstanding, plain once it is not, absent entirely on a cancelled or refunded one), then per-line thumbnails + `lineMeta` fields + dispatched/refunded/pre-order badges + a Buy again button, every parcel with carrier and tracking number and its contents, digital downloads, the full totals breakdown (items, coupon-named discount, named shipping rate, VAT with inclusive/exclusive wording, total, refunds, remainder), completed refunds itemised, delivery + billing addresses, the request panel, and a history of decided requests with the owner's reply. **Receipt**: one-page printable, deliberately called a receipt not a VAT invoice since the shop settings hold no registration number or trading address to back that claim.

**Extension Points**
- `core.admin-dashboard-widgets` (id `shop-summary`) - 30-day revenue/orders/AOV, low-stock chip, pending-manual-payment chip, active-pre-order chip.
- `members.account-section` (id `shop-orders`, **first module to use this point** - it existed in core unused until now) - was two text links; since v0.1.181 it is a "Your orders" card showing the latest order (number, status pill, date, item count, total, "Request open" pill) because the links became real tabs.
- `members.account-nav` (id `shop-account`, `lib/member-account-nav.ts` exporting `shopMemberAccountNav`, **v0.1.181, first module to use this core point**) - contributes the **Orders** and **Addresses** tabs to the member account nav, with a count pill on Orders for the member's PENDING cancel/return requests. Returns `[]` when Members is disabled or `getShopGate()` is blocked, so a tab never leads to a "we are closed" notice.
- `core.menu-entity-provider` (id `shop`, `lib/menu-entity-provider.ts` exporting `shopMenuEntityProvider`) - lets the admin menu builder's "Module content" picker link to shop pages. Four kinds: Shop home (`/shop`), Product (`/shop/products/{slug}`, `publiclyVisible` only when status `ACTIVE`), Category (`/shop/categories/{slug}`), Collection (`/shop/collections/{slug}`). Same shape as Gazette/Directory/Boards providers; URL scheme mirrors `lib/sitemap.ts`.
- `core.media-reference-rewriters` (id `shop`, `lib/media-reference-rewriter.ts`) - repoints the shop's url-holding columns when core moves a blob (optimise/resize/crop/replace/rename): `shp_product_media.url`, `shp_digital_files.url` and, from v0.1.150, `shp_categories.image_url`. Equality match, never substring - each column IS the whole url, so it cannot touch an unrelated row and the same image used twice is repointed on both.
- `core.media-usage-providers` (id `shop`, `lib/media-usage-provider.ts`) - contributes `shp_product_media.url`, `shp_digital_files.url`, `shp_products.og_image_id`, `shp_collections.image_id`/`og_image_id`, `shp_categories.og_image_id`/`image_url` - the catalogue's entire photography used to read as unused in the media library to core's media usage index, so the library's Unused tile and delete warning can see them.
- `shop.order-messages` (shop is the **consumer** here, not a publisher - no manifest entry needed) - the order detail page looks up any active module's `extensionPoints` for this point name and renders its contributed component with `orderId`/`orderNumber`/`customerEmail` props, mirroring the exact mechanism `members.admin-member-detail` already uses. Reply Catcher does not currently publish to this point (Q12 - shop builds only its own side; the reply-catcher-side contribution is out of scope), so the section never renders out of the box today.
- `shop.product-detail-parts` (**published by shop, v0.1.35**; contract + resolver in `lib/detail-slot.ts`, precedent `lib/line-meta.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a **claim-and-replace** point, unlike the additive ones above. `resolveShopDetailSlot(product)` is awaited once per product page inside `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (in the existing `Promise.all`, one extra query) and asks each active provider's `claimsProduct(product)`; the first to claim supplies optional `Gallery`/`Price`/`PurchaseArea` components, which ride to the parts as `DetailPartContext.slot` via the existing `_ctx` injector (`inject-part-context.ts`, attached by reference so components survive). `ShopDetailGalleryRsc`/`ShopDetailPriceRsc`/`ShopDetailAddToCartRsc` render the slot component instead of their own markup when `slot` is set, and shop's own markup unchanged when it is null (shop-only site, or any unclaimed product) - the starter layout's block list is **not** touched, which is how a variations-aware default PDP stays free of variations-specific blocks. Shop hands the provider its own `.spd-*` class names plus its server-loaded images/price so a replaced part looks native and paints on first byte. Replace (not render-alongside) because a claimed product has no single price/stock of its own - both rendering would show two prices and two buttons. **A claimed product's `PurchaseArea` owns availability outright: shop's `outOfStock` gate is deliberately skipped**, since stock lives on the chosen combination and gating on the parent row would strand a parent that tracks no stock of its own (`ShopDetailBadges` still reads the parent's `outOfStock`, so a mis-configured parent can show an out-of-stock badge above a working buy button). Nothing in shop names variations; the point is generic and the `git grep` leak check stays clean.

- `shop.product-detail-tabs` (**published by shop, v0.1.50**; contract + resolver in `lib/detail-tabs.ts`; live consumers `product-downloads-for-shop` and `reviews-for-shop`) - **additive**: a module contributes a tab to the product page's own tab strip, beside Description/Specification/Dimensions, rather than a block bolted underneath. Modelled on `shop.gallery-media` line for line, and additive for the same reason - a tab replaces nothing, so every provider resolves and one whose `load` throws is dropped and logged rather than taking the product page down. `resolveShopDetailTabs(productId)` is awaited once per page in `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (in the existing `Promise.all`) and rides to the parts as `DetailPartContext.detailTabs`, **not** awaited inside `ShopDetailTabsRsc` - the parts render synchronously, and `detail-parts.tsx` is dual-compiled into the client editor bundle, so it cannot import the extension-point registry (which reaches prisma) at all. Provider supplies `label`, optional `order`, `load(productId)` (server-only; payload crosses the RSC boundary so must be JSON-serialisable; **null means no tab**, which is what keeps the strip unchanged on products with nothing to add) and a `Panel` **client** component. `label`/`order` live on the provider object rather than in the manifest - unlike `shop.product-editor-sections`, whose manifest `label` is stripped by the install-time zod schema and only restored by `sync-module-manifests.mjs` on the next deploy, leaving a tab named after its own id in the meantime. Shop's own tabs are numbered in `detail-parts.tsx` (`TAB_ORDER`: desc 10, spec 20, dims 30, downloads 40); an unordered contribution lands at 50 and ties keep shop's own first (stable sort). Shop never learns what a tab holds.
- `shop.product-page-resolver` (**published by shop, v0.1.108-to-be, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/product-page-resolver.ts`, `resolveAliasedProduct`, precedent `lib/detail-slot.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a **slug-alias** point. Shop's product page and `generateMetadata` (`app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx`) resolve the URL slug; when what they find is not renderable - a `catalogue_hidden` row, an inactive or unknown slug - they await `resolveAliasedProduct(slug, found)`, which asks each active provider's `resolve(slug, found)` and takes the first product handed back as the one to render under that URL (first-claim-wins in active-modules order, exactly like `resolveShopDetailProvider`). Shop then renders that product off `product.slug` (layout scoring + `injectProductContext`), so a parent page can render while the address bar keeps the original link; nothing claims → `notFound()` as before. This is what turns a variation's own link - the `/shop/products/<variant-child-slug>` URL the cart builds and shoppers share - from a 404 into the parent page opened on that combination. Generic: shop names no variants and the `git grep` leak check stays clean. A resolver may record request-scoped state as a side effect (shop-variations stashes which combination to preselect), mirroring how the detail-parts provider's `claimsProduct` records the product slug.
- `shop.product-card-prices` (**published by shop, v0.1.116-to-be, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/card-price.ts`, precedent `lib/detail-slot.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a **batched "From £…"** point for product cards. A product priced by a companion module (variations) has no single price of its own, so shop's card must show a range. `resolveCardFromPrices(productIds)` is awaited once per card surface (`ShopProductGrid`/`ShopFeaturedCollection`/`ShopRelatedProducts`/`ShopProductCard` `.rsc` files, plus `product-attributes-for-shop`'s filter grid) - **batched deliberately**, one pair of queries for the whole grid rather than one per card - and asks each active provider's `fromPrices(ids)` for the cheapest figure per product it prices; results merge, first-to-price wins, a provider that throws is swallowed so its products just fall back to shop's own price (exactly as a shop-only site). The map rides into `buildCardContext(..., fromPrice)` → `CardPartContext.fromPrice` (decimal-pound string, null = price normally); `ShopCardPrice` and `MinimalCard` render `From £x` in place of the single price, dropping the struck-through "was"/RRP (no single figure to strike against a range). shop-variations' provider (`lib/card-price-provider.ts`) computes `min` over each parent's **enabled** variants' `effectivePrice` (shop's own, so a card's "from" and the till can never disagree). Generic: shop names no variants and the `git grep` leak check stays clean. **Admin counterpart (no new point):** the product editor registry (`product-editor/context.tsx`) gained a `priceManaged` flag - `useSetProductEditorPriceManaged(managed)` (set by `shop-variations`' `VariationsPanel` when the product has ≥1 variant) / `useProductEditorPriceManaged()` (read by the shop `PricingPanel`), which then locks its Price/sale/reference boxes behind a "priced per variation" note. The stored parent `price` is left untouched, so it stays valid; only the input stands down. On the product page, `shop-variations`' `VariantPricePart` shows `From £<cheapest enabled variant>` until every option is chosen, then the resolved combination price (`fromPrice` added to `use-variation-selection.ts`). **Missed surfaces, live bug, fixed shop v0.1.117 + product-attributes-for-shop v0.1.32:** three card renderers turned out not to be Puck part components at all and so never went through `buildCardContext`/`ctx.fromPrice` in the first place - `shp_products.price` (0.00 on a variation parent, since only its variants are ever priced) rendered straight through, and none of the three render a photo either. (1) `ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx`'s own local `renderTaggedCards` duplicates `MinimalCard` for its no-template-published fallback (comment: "shop's helper has nowhere to hang" the `data-pat-product` tag) - that duplicate read `product.price`/had no image branch at all; now mirrors `MinimalCard` exactly (`ctx.fromPrice` → image via `ctx.image`). (2) `app/public/shop/categories/[slug]/page.tsx` and (3) `app/public/shop/collections/[slug]/page.tsx` are the **bare fallback pages** rendered when no custom `shopCategory`/`shopCollection` Puck layout has been published for that site - a plain hand-rolled card, `effectivePrice(p, ...)` on the raw product row, image slot a permanently-empty `<div>` (no `<img>` ever, by design, unrelated to variations). Both now batch-fetch `getProductMediaForProducts` + `resolveCardFromPrices` alongside their product list and render a real photo + `From £` the same as everywhere else. Found by reproducing the live Deskwell "office-tables" category bug: DB-verified via direct psql over SSH to the OVH VPS (see [[reference_deskwell_vps_migration]]) that the parent had 42 enabled, correctly-priced variants and its own primary photo, then traced via the live RSC payload (`curl -H "RSC: 1"`) that the rendered markup (`<span style={{fontWeight:600}}>`, no className) matched neither `ShopCardPrice` nor `MinimalCard` - only the categories-page fallback's inline styles. **"From" is now conditional (shop + shop-variations + product-attributes-for-shop, working tree):** a product whose variations all cost the same was still labelled `From £x`, which is a range of one. The point's value type went from a bare string to `ShopCardFromPrice { price: string; varies: boolean }` (`lib/card-price.ts`); call sites are untouched (they still pass `fromPrices.get(id) ?? null` straight into `buildCardContext`), which flattens it into `CardPartContext.fromPrice` (unchanged, decimal string) plus new `fromPriceVaries: boolean`. All three renderers (`ShopCardPrice`, `MinimalCard`, `ShopAttributeFilterGrid`'s duplicate) prefix `From ` only when `fromPriceVaries`; the "was"/RRP stay suppressed either way, since the parent's own price boxes stand down on a variation product and its figures are not maintained. The provider tracks `max` alongside `min` and sets `varies` on a **>0.005 spread** (half a penny, so float crumbs cannot invent a range of nothing). Product page: `use-variation-selection.ts` gained `priceVaries` (same tolerance over enabled variant prices) and its `basePrice` fallback now prefers the single variant price over `payload.basePrice` when nothing is chosen and nothing varies - so the un-prefixed figure is the one the shopper will actually be charged, not the parent's unshown, unmaintained one; `VariantPricePart`'s `showFrom` gained `&& sel.priceVaries`. `VariantSlotPriceClient` needed no change - it reads `sel.price` and never printed "From" - but now shows the variation price rather than the parent's on an untouched all-same-price product. Needs patch bumps + releases + `modules.json` pins to reach a deployed site.
- `shop.gallery-media` (**published by shop, v0.1.43**; contract + resolver in `lib/gallery-media.ts`; live consumer `product-3d-views-for-shop`) - **additive**, the counterpart to the claim-and-replace point above: a module contributes extra items to a product's gallery (a 3D model) that appear as further thumbnails and take over the stage when picked. It exists *because* `shop.product-detail-parts` is winner-takes-all - shop-variations already claims Gallery on every product with options, so a second claimant could never reach exactly the products that need it most. Being additive, nothing replaces a part of shop's, so there is no two-prices failure to design around and **every** provider is resolved, not just the first; one whose `load` throws is dropped and logged rather than taking the product page down. `resolveShopGalleryExtras(productId)` is awaited once per page in `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (in the existing `Promise.all`) and rides to the parts as `DetailPartContext.galleryExtras` - resolved by the injector, **not** awaited inside the part, because `wrapResponsiveRender` (`lib/puck/config.tsx`) calls a block's `render` as a plain function. Provider supplies `load(productId)` (server-only; the returned payload crosses the RSC boundary so must be JSON-serialisable) plus `Thumbs`/`Stage` **client** components - a function cannot cross that boundary, which is why filtering by the chosen variation is the provider's own job rather than a callback shop calls into. Shop hands over its `.spd-thumb` class names and owns the strip, the stage box and which item is picked; it never learns what the item is. Rendered by **all three** galleries - shop's `ProductGallery`, shop-variations' `VariantSlotGalleryClient` (which passes the chosen child's id as `activeProductId`, the bit shop cannot know) and shop-variations' granular `ShopVariantGallery` block (which covers shop's Gallery slot, so it is the only strip on those layouts and must resolve extras itself).

- `shop.card-media` (**published by shop, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/card-media.ts`, precedent `lib/card-price.ts` + `lib/gallery-media.ts`; live consumers `shop-variations` and `product-3d-views-for-shop`) - **additive, batched** point that adds two things to a product CARD (the grid tile): extra **images** folded into the card's arrow carousel, and an **overlay** control pinned over the picture. `resolveShopCardExtras(productIds)` is awaited once per card surface (`ShopProductGrid`/`ShopFeaturedCollection`/`ShopRelatedProducts`/`ShopProductCard` `.rsc` files, alongside `resolveCardFromPrices`), asks each active provider's `load(ids)` (one query set for the whole grid) and merges into `{ images, overlays }` per product; a provider that throws is dropped + logged. Rides into `buildCardContext(..., extra)` → `CardPartContext.images` (product media first, then contributed, deduped by url) + `CardPartContext.overlays` (`{ id, Overlay, payload }`; `Overlay` a **client** component passed by reference like `gallery-media`'s Thumbs/Stage, `payload` JSON-serialisable). Rendered by the new client island `components/public/ShopCardMedia.tsx` (mounted by `ShopCardImage` only when `images.length > 1` or an overlay exists; single-image cards stay a plain `<img>`, and the editor canvas is untouched). **Card wrapper changed** (`card-template.tsx renderCards`): `<a class="shop-card">` → `<div class="shop-card"><a class="shop-card-link" …>` (a stretched link), so the carousel arrows and overlay controls are valid focusable buttons above the link rather than interactive content nested in an anchor; `shopCardCss` gained `.shop-card-link`/`.shop-card-nav*`/`.shop-card-overlay` and a fill-mode `pointer-events:none` on the floated text. Consumers: `shop-variations`' `lib/card-media-provider.ts` adds one photo per enabled variation (images only, no overlay); `product-3d-views-for-shop`' `lib/card-media-provider.ts` adds the "view in 3D" overlay (`components/public/CardModel3dOverlay.tsx`), which mounts `Viewer3d` in-place on tap, one live viewer at a time (a `window` `p3d-card-open` event closes any other). Generic: shop names no consumer in code and the `git grep` leak check stays clean. **Third contribution added in shop 0.1.128**: `ShopCardMediaPayload.facts` - an opaque, JSON-serialisable per-product blob shop renders **nothing** of. It merges into `ShopCardExtra.facts: CardFact[]` (`{ id, payload }`, tagged with the contributing entry's id) and rides through `buildCardContext` into `CardPartContext.facts`; the contributing module registers its OWN Puck block against the `shopProductCard` layout type and looks its payload up by id (`shop-variations`' `ShopCardVariationOptions`). Named `card-media` for history only - it is the one seam for everything a module pins to a card, which is why the resolved type is `ShopCardExtra`. Chosen over a new point deliberately: every card surface already awaits this resolver, so a facts contributor needs no per-grid wiring and can never be half-wired. **Companion change, same release**: `injectShopProductCardEmbed(data, ctx, extraPartTypes?)` - `CARD_PART_TYPES` was a hardcoded set of shop's own six blocks, so a module-contributed card block got `_ctx === undefined` and rendered its editor skeleton on the live storefront. `renderCards` now passes `config.categories.blocks.components` (every block registered for `shopProductCard`, which it already has from `getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig`); shop's six stay as a floor rather than being replaced. Passed in rather than read from the generated registry here because `module-rsc-components.ts` imports the very surfaces that call this (import cycle). **Fourth contribution (shop v0.1.189, 2026-08-04): a client-side carousel constraint** - not through the resolver at all, a DOM contract on the island itself (`ShopCardMedia.tsx` header documents it): a filtering module writes allowed `sourceId`s, space-separated, into `data-shop-media-sources` on the `.shop-card` element and dispatches `shop:card-media-sources` there; the island re-reads the attribute (also once at mount, in case the filter dressed the cards before hydration), shows only the listed contributed photos with the first leading, suspends the hover-swap while constrained, falls back to the full set when nothing matches, and restores everything when the attribute goes. Live consumer: `filters-for-shop`'s `FilterShell`.

**Contributed media leads the strip and opens the stage (shop v0.1.54, shop-variations v0.1.21, product-3d-views-for-shop v0.1.6).** In all three galleries the `extras.map` now renders **before** the photo thumbnails, so a 3D thumbnail sits at the front of the strip rather than trailing the photos. Order only - the host still owns the strip and the pick, and pick behaviour is unchanged. The opening view is the provider's call: `Gallery3dThumbs` (`product-3d-views-for-shop`) picks its first visible item once, on first paint, when nothing else is picked - so a product that carries a model opens the stage on the model instead of a photo. It fires only on mount (`ledWithModel` ref guard), so a later variation change that brings a model in does not yank the stage off a photo the shopper chose; a variation change that drops the picked model still hands the stage back to the photos via the existing `stale` guard.

**Puck Blocks** (all 20, registered in the generated `lib/puck/module-components.ts`)

`ShopProductGrid`, `ShopProductCard`, `ShopFeaturedCollection`, `ShopCategoryBrowser`, `ShopPromoBanner` (colour prop is a semantic token name, never hex), `ShopCartSummary` (client, reads localStorage cart, untagged - header-placement widget, not part of any `layoutTypes` page; "Who can see this" field `audience: everyone|admin` - 'admin' withholds the widget from the public and only renders it for a signed-in site admin, gated server-side in `components/puck/ShopCartSummary.rsc.tsx` via `getSessionFromCookie` + `connection()`, wired by `rscImport` in the manifest so the session read/next-headers stay out of the editor bundle; 'everyone' default skips the session read so the common case stays cacheable. **Field key MUST be `audience`, never `visibility`** - core's `withResponsiveVisibility`/`wrapResponsiveRender` (lib/puck/config.tsx) injects a per-block responsive-visibility field ALSO keyed `visibility` and destructures it out of render props, so a block field named `visibility` both clobbers the hide-on-device toggles in the editor and is stripped before the RSC render ever sees it - shipped that way in v0.1.99, silently rendered to everyone, fixed in v0.1.103; **click behaviour** field `clickAction: link|drawer` - 'link' is the original `<Link href="/shop/cart">`, 'drawer' turns the widget into a `<button aria-haspopup="dialog">` that opens the slide-out basket `components/public/CartDrawerClient.tsx` (portalled to `document.body` - the widget lives in the site header, routinely a clipped/positioned stacking context), plus 13 `drawer*` look/wording props whose shape and defaults live in `components/public/cart-drawer-options.ts` so the header bundle can read them without pulling the panel in; the panel itself is `next/dynamic` with `ssr:false`, fetched on the first click and kept mounted afterwards, open/shut being one `scd-in` class rather than a mount/unmount so both slide directions animate - the way IN is a `scd-slide-right`/`scd-slide-left` keyframe animation, NOT the transition, because that lazy mount paints its first frame already `.scd-in` and a transition has no previous frame to move from (the panel simply appeared until then); the transition still does the way out, and both are 240ms ease-out so an already-mounted panel behaves the same either way; the widget also **auto-opens the panel on add-to-cart** - `subscribeCartAdd` in `components/public/cart.ts` (a `cactus-shop-cart-added` window event fired by `addToCart` only, on top of the `cactus-shop-cart-changed` every write fires, so a quantity nudge or removal inside the panel cannot trigger it, and deliberately NOT wired to `storage` so another tab's add doesn't fling a panel open here); the add is counted into state and acted on in a follow-up effect rather than in the listener, because the same event has just changed the count and a `hideWhenEmpty` widget is only in the DOM one render later, and the effect skips when `triggerRef.current.offsetParent === null` so a theme rendering the widget twice (desktop + mobile header, one `display:none`) doesn't portal two panels onto `document.body`; the drawer re-runs the same `/cart/validate` + `subscribeCart` loop as `CartFullClient` including the bootstrap-from-`validated-cache` and monotonic-seq guards, shows the whole-basket `notes` above the total, and renders any per-line resolver control through the shared `components/public/CartLineControlView.tsx` (summary / radios / select, lifted verbatim out of `CartFullClient` - **CartFullClient still carries its own copy** and should adopt this component once its in-flight subgrid work lands, or the two cart surfaces will drift); styling is `components/public/cart-drawer-css.ts` (`scd-*`, reusing `cart-line-css.ts` chrome) - the panel's own line layout is a two-row grid `"thumb main side" / "deliv deliv deliv"`: price, quantity stepper and the `Remove` link are one stacked `.scd-side` track (single grid child, `justify-items:stretch` + a `min-width` floor, so all three are exactly as wide as each other and the price sets the width for any longer figure), and the resolver control spans the full width beneath the thumbnail and name because its option wording is the longest thing on a line; `.scd-side` compacts the shared `.scl-qtybox` (32px tall, 24px buttons) and overrides the shared `pointer:coarse` 44px button rule with its own taller/wider coarse rule, since a 5rem column cannot host it; `.scd-deliv` re-sizes the shared summary card for the panel - every padding and text size at 0.9x its cart-page value (written out, not scaled with `em`, because the shared card sizes itself in rem), the card's two lines re-grouped by `summaryLayout='stacked'` (date on top, service + price on `.scl-s-foot` at the bottom left), both rows shrink-to-fit through `components/public/fit-line.ts` and ellipsising via `sfit-clip` only once the 0.8 font floor is reached; **panel only** - `CartFullClient`/the cart page keep the `scl-*` layout unchanged; Esc/overlay/cross close it, body scroll is locked while open, Tab is trapped inside and focus returns to the trigger; **hidden on `/shop/cart`** - `CartSummaryClient` reads `usePathname()` and renders `null` there in BOTH click modes (the full basket is already on the page; the editor path is exempt via `preview` or the block would vanish from the header while that page is designed); **inert in the Puck editor** - the same `<button>` markup renders so editor/RSC parity holds, but clicking does nothing, because a `document.body` portal would cover the design canvas), `ShopCartFull` (client, full editable cart display - `CartFullClient` localStorage island wrapped by `components/puck/ShopCartFull.tsx`; ~33 look/behaviour options: rows/cards/table layout, spacing/dividers, optional heading, product-image toggle+size+radius, unit/line-price toggles, quantity control style (stepper/number/read-only), remove button text-or-bin, stock + pre-order badges, coupon field labels, item-count/subtotal toggles + labels, checkout button label/colour/text-colour via core `SiteColourField`/full-width/radius, empty-state copy + continue-shopping link, price-accent + panel colours; tagged `shopCart` (its layout type) but ALSO present on every core page via the all-module-blocks "Modules" category, so still droppable anywhere; ONE render path shared by editor and live for parity - editor render passes `preview` to seed sample lines with inert controls and no fetch, RSC render is a server wrapper passing only plain props into the client island, same trick as `ShopCartSummary`; no new API - reuses `/api/m/shop/public/cart/validate`, `/config`, `/checkout/apply-coupon`; each cart line restacks from a single flex row to a three-row grid below 640px (middle row = the delivery column, empty on a line with no picker) so a populated basket never forces a horizontal page scroll on mobile - shared `components/public/cart-line-css.ts` injects the media-query `<style>` and defines the `scl`/`scl-thumb`/`scl-main`/`scl-deliv`/`scl-qty`/`scl-price`/`scl-remove` class hooks, also applied to the `CartPageClient` fallback; the delivery picker sits in its own `.scl-deliv` column between the product and the price (a real `Delivery` column in the table layout), and a variant's name splits into a base-name line + a muted options line via the generic `displayTitle` resolver field; the delivery `<select>` stays width-capped so it can't push the row wide), `ShopCartItems`/`ShopCartTotals` (the same `CartFullClient` island as `ShopCartFull`, told which half to render via its non-Puck `section: 'items'|'totals'` prop, so a page can put another block - `ShopDeliveryArrivals`, typically - between the basket lines and the totals; items = list + empty-basket copy + undo toast, totals = coupon + item count + Subtotal/charges/VAT/Total + checkout button + sticky bar; an empty basket makes the totals block render `null` so the message and the checkout button are not duplicated/stranded; each is its own island and each re-validates, which costs nothing extra because `postCartValidate` single-flights identical concurrent payloads; fields come from the shared groups in `components/puck/cart-fields.tsx`, so the three cart blocks cannot drift apart), `ShopCheckoutItems` (`[ANCHOR]`, v0.1.157 - checkout order summary: every basket line with thumbnail, quantity, line price, variant secondary title and the per-line `lineMeta.fields` a resolver persisted - which is where advanced-shipping's chosen delivery service + promised date appear - plus whole-basket `notes` and an Edit basket link; reuses `POST /cart/validate` via the single-flighted `postCartValidate`, re-renders on cart events; editor path renders `preview` sample lines, RSC path live; seeded into all three shopCheckout starter templates - classic (wrapped in a narrow centred Section from v0.1.158) and compact put it first, Two Column (reworked v0.1.158 as a 40/60 split) puts summary + upsells LEFT and the four steps RIGHT; the block carries no max-width of its own, filling whatever column its layout provides; v0.1.159 adds `sticky: on|off` (default off - a sticky summary in a shared single-column flow would ride over the blocks below it; the Two Column starter turns it on and moves upsells below the split so the summary has its column to itself) + `stickyOffset` (CSS length, set to clear a sticky site header), a mobile-only Show/Hide fold (collapsed by default under 640px via matchMedia at mount, count+total stay in the heading), an 'N items · £X' heading line, and a distinct "items no longer available" message when a non-empty cart resolves to zero live products (previously a bare heading)), `ShopCheckoutContact`/`ShopCheckoutShipping`/`ShopCheckoutPayment`/`ShopCheckoutReview` (all `[ANCHOR]` - `permissions:{delete:false,duplicate:false}` - client components sharing state via a sessionStorage-backed `checkout-state.ts` store since Puck blocks don't share React state; the Payment block owns the mounted Stripe Elements instance and listens for a `cactus-shop-place-order` window CustomEvent the Review block dispatches, since only Payment has access to `stripe.confirmPayment()`; from shop v0.1.157 the steps follow checkout-form best practice - Contact carries `autoComplete`/`inputMode` attrs plus reasons for asking (email = where the confirmation goes, phone = only for delivery problems); Contact also fetches `public/config` for itself and, when `requirePhone` is on, drops the "(optional)" from the Phone label, sets `required`, and shows a blur-time "Enter a phone number." the same way Shipping does - up to and including shop 0.1.177 the setting was inert end to end (saved, published on `public/config`, read by nothing), so the box stayed labelled optional and the order route took orders without a number, Shipping is retitled 'Delivery address' with real <label>s (no placeholder-as-label), per-field `autoComplete` (given-name/family-name/address-line1/2/address-level2/postal-code) and blur-time specific error messages (`role="alert"`, `aria-invalid`, danger border), the shop-rate radios are headed 'Delivery method', Review's button states the amount ('Place order - £84.20') with encrypted-payment reassurance beneath, and Payment shows a padlock line beside the mounted card fields), `ShopOrderConfirmation`, `ShopProductDetail` (`[ANCHOR]`, add-to-cart non-removable; RSC render also emits the schema.org Product JSON-LD script tag), `ShopBackInStockForm` (auto-hidden via an `inStock` prop the product page injects), `ShopRelatedProducts`, `ShopUpsellProducts` (client, one `POST /cart/upsells` for the whole cart; refreshes only when cart MEMBERSHIP changes - qty tweaks and per-line option picks no longer reload the strip), `ShopCategoryHeader`/`ShopCollectionHeader` (both `[ANCHOR]`, added with the layout system integration above - breadcrumb + name + description, re-fetched server-side from an injected `categorySlug`/`collectionSlug`; from v0.1.150 the category header prints `short_description` and only falls back to `description`, the long one having moved to its own block), `ShopCategoryDescription` (`[ANCHOR]`, v0.1.150, `shopCategory` only - the category's long description in whichever form it exists: the designed `description_puck` document when it has any content, else the plain `description`, else nothing; deletable/duplicatable, unlike the header, since a layout may legitimately not want it).

**Configuration**

`ShpConfig` (`modules/shop/lib/config.ts`, Zod-validated, stored as the single `config` JSONB column on the `shp_settings` singleton, Q2): `currency`/`currencySymbol`/`storeEmail`/`orderNumberPrefix`/`weightUnit`/`dimensionUnit`, `enabledPriceTypes` (subset of sale\|retail\|trade\|cost, default `['sale','cost']`) + `showRetailPrice` (default false - prints the RRP beside the price on cards/detail when it beats the charged figure), `taxMode` (INCLUSIVE\|EXCLUSIVE), `priceDisplayTax` (AS_ENTERED\|INCLUSIVE\|EXCLUSIVE, default AS_ENTERED) + `priceDisplayTaxSuffix` (default '') - **what the storefront PRINTS, as against what `taxMode` says the stored figures MEAN**; see the price-display subsection below, `weightBasedShippingEnabled` (default true - the switch at the top of the Tax & shipping screen, saved through `PUT admin/settings` like any other config key and exposed on `public/config` so the product editor can read it alongside the price types; off drops the `WEIGHT_BASED` option from the shipping-rate Type dropdown, the Weight field from the product editor's Stock tab, and the Weight column from shop-variations' grid. Nothing is blanked: stored weights and existing weight-based rates are untouched, and an existing weight-based rate still lists its own type when opened for editing so it can't silently become a flat rate), `guestCheckoutEnabled`/`postPurchaseAccountPrompt`/`minimumOrderValue`/`maximumOrderValue`/`requirePhone` (enforced from the working tree after 0.1.177: contact-step label + `required`, the shared `isContactAndShippingComplete({ phoneRequired })` gate the Payment and Review blocks run, and a 400 from `POST public/checkout/payment-intent` - the same belt-and-braces shape as `businessNameRequired`)/`checkoutSteps` (ordered step array), `enabledPaymentMethods` (which of the four BUILT-IN methods are on; a module-contributed method never needed listing here and still doesn't) + `disabledPaymentMethods` (the shop-wide veto that beats everything, incl. a module provider reporting itself ready - the only off switch a contributed method has) + `paymentMethodOrder` (the order checkout offers them in, as arranged on the Payments tab; empty means fall back to `enabledPaymentMethods` order). All three are resolved at read time by `getAvailablePaymentMethods()`, which gates each provider through `paymentMethodAvailability()` then sorts by `sortPaymentMethods()`/`resolvePaymentMethodOrder()` from `lib/payments/admin-methods.ts`, `bankTransferInstructions`/`cashInstructions` + `bankTransferInstructionsOnCheckout`/`cashInstructionsOnCheckout` (default true - whether those words are also served to the checkout page as soon as the method is picked; gated inside `lib/payments/bank-transfer.ts`/`cash.ts` `createIntent`, the only caller of which is `POST public/checkout/payment-intent`, so off withholds them from the wire rather than hiding them in the browser. `public/orders/status` reads the config directly for the thank-you page, ungoverned by that switch, but only while the order's payment is outstanding - a settled order returns `instructions: null`, as does the account order page's own read), `adminOrderAlertEmail`/`lowStockAlertEnabled`/`lowStockAlertEmail`, `shopStatus` (OPEN\|BROWSE_ONLY\|CLOSED)/`shopClosedMessage`, `shopTitle`/`shopMetaDescription` (`shopBasePath` dropped per Q3 - fixed to `"shop"` via the manifest's `publicBasePath` instead of being runtime-configurable), `backInStockAccountPrompt`, `buyAgainEnabled` (default true - whether a past order line offers Buy again at all; read server-side in the member order detail page, no `public/config` exposure because nothing in the browser needs it), `cancelRequestsEnabled`/`returnRequestsEnabled` (both default true) + `returnWindowDays` (default 30, counted from the last parcel out; 0 takes returns off the website entirely), `preOrderMixedCartBehaviour` (HOLD_ALL\|PROMPT_SPLIT - a fulfilment policy, wired up 2026-07-23, see the Part-dispatch subsection below; also returned by `POST /public/checkout/session` so the checkout review step can word its pre-order notice), `supplierFieldEnabled` (default false) + `supplierLabelPreset` (Supplier\|Manufacturer\|Retailer\|Importer\|custom, default Supplier) + `supplierLabelCustom` (default '') + `supplierShowOnFrontend` (default false) + `supplierFieldScope` (PRODUCTS\|PRODUCTS_AND_VARIATIONS, default PRODUCTS) - the supplier field block on the General tab. `resolveSupplierLabel(config)` (same file) is the one place the preset/custom pair resolves to a display string, falling back to "Supplier" when custom is blank. Enabled adds the **Suppliers** sidebar entry and screen (see `shp_suppliers`) and a supplier dropdown to the product editor's Details tab; `supplierShowOnFrontend` additionally puts it on the Product Detail Specification tab (via `DetailPartContext.supplierLabel`, null when either switch is off); `supplierFieldScope` = PRODUCTS_AND_VARIATIONS adds the column to shop-variations' grid. Nothing is blanked by switching any of them off. Exposed on `public/config` as a `supplierField` object (enabled/label/showOnFrontend/scope) because the admin product editor reads its config from there.

**Price display tax - what the storefront prints, as against what is stored (shop 0.1.137, shop-variations 0.1.98, advanced-shipping-for-shop 0.1.21, working tree)**
`taxMode` says what the figures in the price box MEAN (INCLUSIVE = tax already in them, EXCLUSIVE = added at the till); the new `priceDisplayTax` says what the storefront PRINTS. `AS_ENTERED` (the default) converts nothing, so an upgrade moves no price. Arithmetic in the client-safe `modules/shop/lib/tax-display-shared.ts` (`displayPriceFactor`, `displayAmount`, `displayIncludesTax`, `displayTaxMode`, `displayOrderTotals`, `withPriceSuffix`; unit-tested in `tax-display-shared.test.ts`) - the `breakpoints-shared` split, because the basket does this in the browser. Server resolution in `modules/shop/lib/tax-display.ts`: `resolveTaxDisplay()` reads the config and, only when a side has actually been chosen, the rate table for `getDefaultTaxZoneId()` (a shelf price is printed long before an address exists); `makeDisplayAdjuster(taxDisplay, taxClassId)` returns **null** when the factor is 1, so the untouched-setting path is a no-op with no queries. **`effectivePrice` is deliberately NOT converted** - it is the checkout's, so what is SHOWN can never move what is CHARGED; `priceView(product, enabled, adjust?)` takes the converter and applies it to `now`/`was`/`rrp` only.
Applied at: `buildCardContext` (a `taxDisplay` on the existing `pricing` param, resolved once per surface in all six card call sites - grid, single card, related, featured, category page, collection page - and applied to the product's own figures AND a companion module's `fromPrice`, so the two can never end up on opposite sides of tax); `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (incl. the JSON-LD `offers.price`, so a search result cannot quote a figure the page does not); `POST public/cart/validate` (`unitPrice`, `lineSubtotal`, `charges[].amount` and a control option's numeric `priceAdjust` - a resolver's own already-formatted option LABELS are passed through untouched, as ever, so a module that prices options formats them itself); `POST public/checkout/session` (rows above the Total via `displayOrderTotals`, which scales `goodsSubtotal`/`charges` by one exact ratio so Subtotal − Discount + Shipping still lands on the server's Total to the penny; the Total itself and the persisted order are untouched); `POST public/cart/upsells`. `public/config` gains `priceDisplay { mode, storedIncludesTax, suffix, displayTaxMode }` - `CartFullClient` now takes its INCLUSIVE/EXCLUSIVE branch from `displayTaxMode`, because a basket handed converted lines adds up like an inclusive shop's whatever `taxMode` says. New `priceSuffix` on both `CardPartContext` and `DetailPartContext` (rendered as `.shop-card-taxnote` / `.spd-price-taxnote`) and an optional `priceSuffix` on `ShopDetailPriceSlotProps`. Admin UI is a **Prices on your shop** card at the top of `TaxShippingScreen` (three radios + a wording box; choosing a converted mode pre-fills "inc. VAT"/"ex. VAT" only where the owner has not written their own).
**shop-variations 0.1.98**: `getVariantSelectorPayload` converts the whole payload server-side at the PARENT's tax class - `basePrice`, each variant's `price`/`compareAtPrice`, and every add-on surcharge (`flatPrice`, `pricePerChar`, `choices[].price`, via `adjustAddonPrices`) - and adds `priceSuffix`. Deliberately one conversion on the way out rather than a multiplier in `use-variation-selection`: it keeps tax arithmetic off the client entirely and means a personalisation surcharge can never land on the other side of tax from the price it is added to. `sel.priceSuffix` renders in `VariantParts` and `VariantSlotPriceClient`. Nothing here is authoritative - the cart re-resolves each line from the products.
**advanced-shipping-for-shop 0.1.21**: a service charge is folded into `priceAdjust`, so it is taxed at the product's own rate and has to print on that same side. `line-resolver` converts the figure passed to `tierOptionLabel`/`tierOptionSummary` (its own wording, which shop never re-words) while leaving the numeric `priceAdjust` raw for shop's validate route to convert - converting both would double it. `estimate-service` converts `tiers[].priceEffective` (the printed figure; `tiers[].price` stays the raw configured setting) and now reads `tax_class_id` alongside the product name on the same query. Both dependants raise `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.137`.
**Known gap:** `minimumOrderValue`/`maximumOrderValue` are still measured against the stored subtotal, not the printed one.

`imageZoomOnHover` moved out of `ShpConfig` into the Puck "Product: Gallery" block itself (`shopDetailGalleryPuckComponent`, `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`) as a per-block `zoomOnHover` radio field (default off), so it's set per layout in the shop layout editor rather than shop-wide in admin settings. Flows straight from the block's own prop into the `zoom` prop on `ProductGallery`/`ShopDetailGallerySlotProps`, same as before - `DetailPartContext.zoomImages` is gone, `ShopSettingsTab`'s "Product images" section is gone.

**Product photos are square everywhere; the `shape` prop is gone (shop v0.1.44, shop-variations v0.1.11)**
One ratio, 1:1, for every product photo: the Product Detail stage (`.spd-stage`) and the card image (`.shop-card-img` in `card-parts.tsx`, `.spc-img` in `product-card-css.ts`, both previously `4/3`). The per-instance `shape` select (square/portrait/landscape) is **removed** from both the `ShopDetailGallery` and `ShopCardImage` Puck blocks, from `GalleryProps`/`ImageProps`/`ProductGallery`, from `ShopDetailGallerySlotProps` (so `shop-variations`' `VariantSlotGalleryClient` stopped reading it and no longer sets `aspectRatio` inline - it inherits the ratio from shop's `.spd-stage` via `classNames`, one definition rather than two modules agreeing to keep saying `1/1`), and from every `starterLayouts.ts` block (two set `landscape`). The `.shape-*` CSS classes are gone. Its only real effect was letting one shop's photos be three shapes depending on the layout a page used. Saved `Layout` rows may still carry `props.shape`; Puck passes unknown props through and nothing reads it, so they resolve square with no data migration - correct on this fresh-install platform. **Exempt: Overlay cards** (`.shop-card-img.fill-mode`, `aspect-ratio:auto` inside a `3/4` card) - the photo being the whole card is that design, not a shape. Non-square originals crop rather than distort (`object-fit:cover` in an `overflow:hidden` box). `shop-variations` declares `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.44`, since its gallery now leans on shop's square `.spd-stage`.

**Product: Tabs strip - one segmented track instead of loose pills (shop, working tree)**
The tabs now sit inside a single pill-shaped `.spd-tab-track` (`display:inline-flex`, 4px padding, 1px `--color-border`, `--color-surface` fill, `flex:none`), so the strip reads as a segmented control with a current position rather than a row of separately outlined buttons. `.spd-tab-btn` accordingly loses its own fill and outline (`border:1px solid transparent` kept so a tab does not resize when it lights up) and hovers to `--color-bg-subtle`; `.on` and `.spd-tab-action` are unchanged, still `--color-primary` over `--color-on-primary` with the `!important` that beats a site theme's own button fill. The track is the nav's **only child**, so the nav keeps doing the alignment (`justify-content`), the sticky pin, the divider and the sideways scroll exactly as before - which matters because `ProductSectionTabs`' overflow measurement, its `data-spd-anchor` nudge and the shell's fades/arrows all measure the NAV. Breakpoints: at `mobileBp` the track takes `width:100%` so the shrink-to-fit tabs have a row to share; at `SMALL_PHONE_BP` it goes back to `width:auto` so it is wider than the nav and the nav is what scrolls. Rendered in all four places for editor/RSC parity: `ProductSectionTabs` (island), `ShopDetailTabs` (editor preview), `ShopDetailSectionNav` (editor preview) and `ShopDetailSectionNavRsc`.

**Product: Tabs strip - own background colour, and the active tab scrolls itself into view**
Two per-block fields on `shopDetailTabsPuckComponent` (`modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`): `bgColour` (custom field, core `SiteColourField`, so it carries the light and dark arms in one stored `light-dark(l, d)` value - `lib/puck/lightDark.ts`) and `bgOpacity` (number, 0-100, default 100). `navBgVars()` folds the opacity into **each arm separately** via `color-mix(in srgb, <arm> N%, ...)` rather than wrapping the whole `light-dark()`, matching what `SectionBgColorField` already writes; `rgba()` can't wrap a `var(--color-N)` swatch, hence `color-mix`. It emits **two** custom properties on `.spd-tab-shell`: `--spd-tabnav-bg` (mixed over `transparent`, the strip's own fill) and `--spd-tabnav-fade` (the same colour mixed over `var(--color-page-bg, var(--color-bg))`, i.e. already composited onto the page). The edge fades and arrow buttons use the **fade** var, because they paint over the shell's own fill - a see-through colour applied twice would darken both edges relative to the middle. A blank colour sets neither var, so the CSS falls back to `transparent` / page-background exactly as before, and sticky still fills so the panel can't show through as it scrolls under. Editor preview (`ShopDetailTabs`) sets the same vars on the same wrapper for markup/class parity.

The mobile bug it shipped with: on a small phone the strip is an `overflow-x:auto` row, and the scroll-spy would light a tab (Downloads, typically last) that sat off the right-hand edge - the highlight was correct and invisible. `ProductSectionTabs` (`modules/shop/components/public/ProductDetailIslands.tsx`) now tags every pill `data-spd-anchor` (including the leading CTA, whose anchor is `spd-buy`) and, on `active` change only, nudges `nav.scrollTo` so the lit pill clears the 32px arrow/fade overlay at whichever edge it came in from. Guarded on `scrollWidth > clientWidth`, so it is a no-op on desktop and on the larger-phone shrink-to-fit tier, and it never fights a shopper dragging the strip by hand. Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` (jumps instead of smooth-scrolling). The standalone **Section links** block is static server markup and is untouched.

**Product Detail gallery, viewport fit (v0.1.42, reworked v0.1.44)**
The gallery column (`.spd-stage-col`, CSS in `galleryCss()`, `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`) is `position:sticky` so the photo stays with a shopper scrolling a taller buy column, and the stage fits the leftover viewport **by giving up width** - `aspect-ratio` takes the height with it, so it stays square and merely gets smaller. `--spd-fit` (`calc(100dvh - var(--spd-header-h) - 32px - var(--spd-thumbs-h))`) is that width budget; the stage is `flex:none;align-self:center;width:min(100%,var(--spd-fit));min-width:140px`. **v0.1.42 capped the column's height instead and let the stage flex-shrink into it, which squashed the square stage into a letterbox and cropped the photo** - the bug the square rule exists to prevent. `beside` mode overrides `--spd-fit` (the strip sits alongside, costing the stage no height) and uses `flex:1 1 auto;max-width:var(--spd-fit)`, since the strip is spending some of the row's width too.

**The Split's media track is `min(N%, var(--spd-gallery-fit))`, not `minmax(0,N%)`** - a track is a floor as well as a ceiling, and `minmax(0,N%)` always grew to the full N% however narrow the column inside it went. The two only agreed while `--spd-thumbs-h` was wrong: the moment the strip started being measured the column shed those 76px, the track did not, and the difference showed as dead white space between the photo and the buy column. `min()` sizes the cell to the same number the column is about to take, so the `1fr` beside it collects the slack (measured on `deskwell.co.uk` at 1800x760: cell 518 → 486, buy column 602 → 634, gap 32 → 0; at 1800x1010 the `45%` arm still binds and nothing moves). Not `fit-content(N%)` for the reason above - it floors the track at the item's definite width and sails past the cap - and `min()` takes no contribution from its contents at all. The calc is hoisted to `:root` as `--spd-gallery-fit` / `--spd-gallery-fit-beside` because the track needs it on the *Split*, which is not the element `--spd-fit` is declared on. `beside` keeps `minmax(0,N%)`: that column is `width:auto` and stretches to fill its track, so there was never a gap to close, and its budget is the stage's rather than the column's. **The mobile collapse rule now spells out all three variants** (`:has(.spd-stage-col)`, `:has(.spd-stage-col.beside)`, `:has(> :last-child .spd-stage-col.beside)`) - `:has()` counts what is inside it, so the `.beside` track rules outrank a bare `:has(.spd-stage-col)` and a phone would otherwise keep two columns.

Both numbers need measurements CSS cannot get. The site header's height: core does **not** publish it - the header is the Site Header Puck block (`lib/puck/config.tsx`), whose height is a per-site prop that may be `auto`, whose stickiness is a second prop, and which a site may omit. So `modules/shop/components/public/GalleryViewportFit.tsx` (client island, renders null) measures it and publishes `--spd-header-h` on `:root`, counting only `<header>` elements computing to `position:sticky|fixed` with `top <= 4px` (a static header scrolls away and costs the column nothing) and summing `height + top` (a header parked below an announcement bar). It also publishes `--spd-thumbs-h` - the stacked strip's height plus the column's `gap:12px`, `0` when there's no strip (no strip, no gap). Re-measures on `ResizeObserver` (headers + strip) and `resize`: late-decoding logo, wrapping nav, condense-on-scroll header, strip rewrapping rows. Fallbacks `96px`/`76px` cover pre-hydration and the editor canvas.

**The strip is not necessarily on the page when the island mounts, and a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` (childList + subtree) now watches for it arriving.** Observing "whatever exists right now" assumed it did. On a product with options - shop-variations' replacement gallery, i.e. the interesting half of a real catalogue - `VariantSlotGalleryClient` renders no strip until `thumbs.length + extras.length > 1`, which on Deskwell means until the shopper has picked a combination and the variant's own photographs arrive. The one measurement at mount therefore published `--spd-thumbs-h: 0px`, nothing was left observing anything, and the value never moved: the stage kept the strip's 76px share of the viewport **as well as its own**, so the sticky column ran 76px past the bottom of the screen and the thumbnails were cut off by the viewport edge (measured live on `deskwell.co.uk` at 1100x700: column bottom 722 against a 700px viewport, versus 684 - the intended `100dvh - 16px` - once the value is right). A window resize was the only thing that ever corrected it, which is why it read as intermittent. The callback is gated on the strip **element identity** changing, so an unrelated re-render costs one `querySelector`; `apply()` re-points the `ResizeObserver` at the new strip (and unobserves the old), and height changes stay the `ResizeObserver`'s job. Measurement is not deferred to `requestAnimationFrame` on purpose - a background tab pauses rAF, so a shopper configuring in one tab and returning to another would find the measurement still pending.

**A pinned section strip is the third measurement (`--spd-tabnav-h`, shop v0.1.148)**
The gallery is not the only thing pinned below the header: the **Product: Tabs** strip (sticky on `.spd-tab-shell`) and the standalone **Product: Section links** block (sticky on `.spd-tab-nav` itself) both pin at `top:var(--spd-header-h)`. A gallery clearing only the header therefore pinned *underneath* the strip, hiding the top of the photo and, on a configurable product, shop-variations’ "Your choice" pill in the same band. `.spd-stage-col` (and `.beside`) now read `var(--spd-tabnav-h,0px)` in **both** places: added to the sticky `top`, and subtracted from `--spd-fit`, because the width budget is what keeps the square stage inside the viewport and a strip left out of the sum pushed the stage off the bottom by its own height.

`modules/shop/components/public/StickyStripHeight.tsx` (client island, renders `null`) is the single publisher. It measures **by selector** (`.spd-tab-shell.sticky, .spd-tab-nav.sticky`) rather than by ref, because a page may carry both blocks and two mounts must agree on one number instead of each overwriting the other with its own strip’s height; it takes the **tallest, not the sum**, since both pin at the same `top` and so overlap rather than stack. The Tabs island moves `sticky` UP to its shell and leaves its own nav unpinned, so the two selectors never count one strip twice. A module-level refcount leaves clearing the property to the last unmount, and a `signal` prop re-runs the measurement when the markup changes rather than merely its size (the editor toggling `sticky`, or the tab count moving) - the dependency the old `[sticky, tabs]` effect provided. Mounted by `ProductSectionTabs`, by `ShopDetailSectionNavRsc` and by `ShopDetailSectionNav` (editor preview) for parity; renders nothing, so Puck editor/RSC markup parity is untouched. **The Section links block published this variable nowhere before**, being server-only, so with it pinned the sections’ own `scroll-margin-top` was short by the strip’s height and every jump link landed its heading behind the strip.

**The strip's width is deliberately NOT tied to `--spd-fit`.** Its height feeds that sum, so sizing it from the result would let a narrower strip wrap to more rows → taller strip → smaller budget → narrower strip: a loop the ResizeObserver would chase. It keeps its full column width (`flex:none`); only the stage moves. Rendered by `ShopDetailGalleryRsc`, **not** by `ProductGallery`, so a `shop.product-detail-parts` provider's replacement gallery gets it too - it wears `.spd-stage-col`. No `overflow` on the column: it would clip `.spd-thumb.on`'s `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px` ring on the edge thumbnails of every page, to catch only a ~35-image outlier. Below `tabletBp` the column goes `position:static` and the stage back to `width:100%` - stacked, it has the width to itself and shouldn't shrink for a viewport it no longer shares.

**Thumbnail strip overflow affordance (`GalleryThumbStrip`, v0.1.48)**

The strip below the stage is one nowrap `overflow-x:auto` row (above), which on a product with a dozen photos simply looked like it ended at the column's edge - nothing said the row ran on. `modules/shop/components/public/GalleryThumbStrip.tsx` (client) wraps it in `.spd-thumbs-wrap` and renders, at whichever end still has scroll left in it, a `.spd-thumbs-fade` gradient and a `.spd-thumbs-arrow` button - the same affordance, geometry (2rem fade inboard of a 1.5rem arrow) and 160px step as core's admin `components/admin/TabStrip.tsx`. State is `scrollLeft` vs `scrollWidth - clientWidth` on a `scroll` + `resize` + `ResizeObserver` check; both ends start "at" so the server's markup carries no arrows and the effect earns them. Keyed on `Children.count`, **not `children`**: the gallery re-renders on every pointer move while the magnifier is tracking, and keying on the nodes would tear the listeners down and rebuild them on each one.

`beside` strips pass straight through unwrapped - left/right means nothing to a column - so that layout's markup and CSS are exactly as before. `ShopDetailGallery` (editor preview) mirrors the same wrapper for markup/class parity; its four placeholders never overflow, so no arrows are earned there.

**The new rules are scoped to `.spd-thumbs-wrap`, not to `.spd-thumbs`, and that is load-bearing.** A `shop.product-detail-parts` provider's replacement gallery (shop-variations' `VariantSlotGalleryClient` / `ShopVariantGallery`) wears the `.spd-thumbs` class it is handed via `classNames` but renders it straight into `.spd-stage-col` with no wrapper. `flex:1 1 auto` reaching it there would read as grow-to-fill on the **vertical** axis (the column's main axis) and stretch its strip down the page; hiding the scrollbar would leave it with no overflow hint at all, having no arrows to replace it with. Hence `.spd-thumbs-wrap .spd-thumbs{flex:1 1 auto;scrollbar-width:none}` and an untouched `.spd-stage-col:not(.beside) .spd-thumbs`.

**`VariantSlotGalleryClient` now adopts `GalleryThumbStrip` (shop-variations v0.1.15), which is what actually put the arrows in front of shoppers.** The affordance shipped in shop v0.1.48 and, on a real catalogue, almost nobody saw it: any product with options is claimed by shop-variations' replacement gallery, and that is the half of the catalogue with the most photos. The strip on Deskwell's Chiro Plus overflowed (804px of thumbnails in a 796px column) with no arrow, no fade and a hidden scrollbar. The slot gallery now renders `<GalleryThumbStrip beside={thumbPosition === 'beside'} className={classNames.thumbs}>` - the `className`/`beside` props existed from v0.1.48 for exactly this caller and had no consumer until now - so `requiresModules: shop` moved 0.1.44 → **0.1.48**, the release that carries the component (the `product-downloads` lesson at the top of this file, applied on purpose rather than after the fact). Its thumb buttons gained `role="tab"`/`aria-selected` to earn the wrapper's `role="tablist"`, matching `ProductGallery`. `ShopVariantGallery` (the hand-placed Puck block, own `svr-gallery-thumb` styling, 56px) is a separate surface and is **not** wrapped - no live consumer asked for it. `GalleryViewportFit` is unaffected: it queries `.spd-stage-col:not(.beside) .spd-thumbs` as a **descendant**, so an interposed wrapper changes nothing it measures.

The hidden scrollbar slightly *raises* the photo's budget: its height was being charged to `--spd-thumbs-h`.

**Part-dispatch (shipments)**
An order used to be either shipped or not - the SHIPPED status was the whole record of dispatch, which cannot describe "three of the five went out on Tuesday". Data layer: `modules/shop/lib/db/shipments.ts` exports `createShipment`, `getShipmentsForOrder`, `getDispatchedQtyByOrderItem`, `getOrderDispatchSummary`, `isOrderFullyDispatched`, `deleteShipment`, plus the pure `isFullyDispatched`/`isPartiallyDispatched` so the UI can answer the same question from a summary it already holds. Types in `lib/types.ts`: `ShpShipment`, `ShpShipmentItem`, `ShpShipmentWithItems`, `ShpOrderItemDispatch` (`quantity`/`refundedQty`/`dispatchedQty`/`outstandingQty`, the last being `quantity - refundedQty - dispatchedQty` floored at zero), `ShpOrderDispatchSummary`. Load-bearing details:
- **Dispatched totals are aggregated in a subquery BEFORE the join to the order lines.** Joining `shp_shipment_items` straight onto `shp_order_items` fans a line out once per shipment and any later arithmetic counts it several times - the same trap that caused the real overselling bug in `decrementStockOnShip`.
- **The advisory-lock namespace is shared with refunds** (`0x53485250`, transaction-scoped `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` keyed on the order id). Refunds and dispatch police the same units of the same order, so they have to be mutually exclusive: a refund landing between a shipment's validation and its insert would otherwise refund units the dispatch had just decided were still dispatchable. One of the two simply waits, or is turned away with a 409 and a "something else is updating this order" message.
- **This layer records dispatch and nothing else - it does NOT touch `stock_count`.** Stock still moves in exactly two places: normal lines at payment (`lib/order-fulfillment.ts`) and pre-order lines when an admin sets the order to SHIPPED (`decrementStockOnShip`). Adding a decrement here would double-count against one of those and silently oversell. If dispatch is ever meant to own the pre-order decrement, the decrement has to MOVE, not be added alongside.
- Two lines for the same order item in one request are folded together before anything is validated, or each would validate against the same starting figure and together sail past the cap. "Fully dispatched" excludes an order with nothing dispatchable (empty, or refunded down to nothing) - there was never a parcel to send.
Admin UI: new `components/admin/DispatchModal.tsx` (built on `RefundModal`'s bones - a quantity per line capped at what is still owed, optional parcel details, server rejections shown verbatim; the real caps are server-side, so a refund landing while the modal is open is caught there). `components/admin/OrderDetailScreen.tsx` gains a Dispatched column on the items table, a "Dispatch items" action beside "Refund items", a Dispatches list, the HOLD_ALL banner, and a derived "Partly dispatched"/"All dispatched" pill next to the status select - **a marker, not a new `ShpOrderStatus` value**; it fetches `/admin/orders/[id]/dispatch` alongside the order.
Email: `lib/shipment-email.ts`'s `sendShipmentDispatchedEmail({orderId, shipmentId})` renders the `PARTIAL_SHIPPED` template. `STATUS_SHIPPED` says the whole order is on its way and only knows orderNumber/customerName/shopName, so sending it for three of five items would be a straight untruth; this one lists what went and what is still owed. It covers the final parcel too - the copy switches to "the last part of your order" via the `isFinalPart`/`hasOutstanding` flags - so the dispatch route calls it for EVERY shipment and never has to choose between templates. Item lists go in as ONE plain-text variable (`- name xN`, newline-joined) because `lib/email.ts` HTML-escapes every `{{variable}}`, so any `<br>`/`<li>` built here would reach the customer as visible angle brackets - the same trade-off `ORDER_CONFIRMED` already makes. Silent no-op when the order, shipment or its lines cannot be found: an email is not worth failing a dispatch that has already committed.
**`preOrderMixedCartBehaviour` is now actually implemented, as a FULFILMENT policy rather than a checkout restriction.** Neither value forbids a mixed basket, and nothing on the storefront blocks the Place order button - the payment-intent route carries an explicit comment saying so, since "add the gate here" is the obvious wrong fix. HOLD_ALL: `[id]/status` refuses SHIPPED with a 409 while any pre-order line is outstanding, naming how many items and the latest expected date and pointing at the two ways out (take the products off pre-order, or switch the setting to split shipping); the checkout review step tells the shopper the whole order is sent together once everything has arrived. PROMPT_SPLIT: part-dispatch is permitted and the shopper is told anything in stock can be sent straight away with the pre-order to follow. The shared rule is `outstandingPreOrderItems(items)` in `lib/db/orders.ts` - the line's snapshotted dispatch date is the primary signal, a line with no date falls back to the product's own `is_pre_order` flag (so unticking it once stock lands is the owner's escape hatch), and a line whose product row has gone is treated as ready rather than jamming the order shut for good. It lives in the data layer precisely because the status route enforces the policy and the dispatch route explains it, and two copies would drift into disagreeing about whether the shop is holding the order.

**Order, stock and money correctness (2026-07-23)**
- `decrementStockOnShip` aggregates `SUM(quantity) GROUP BY product_id` before joining to the product row. The plain join updated each product once however many order-item rows pointed at it, so a basket with two lines of the same product (which personalised lines deliberately allow) decremented by the larger line only - qty 1 + qty 3 took 3 off, not 4 - and silently oversold.
- Coupon usage is keyed on the resolved `coupon_id`, never the raw code: `fulfillPaidOrder` bumps `usage_count` only when `order.couponId` is set, `countPriorCouponOrdersByEmail` takes a coupon id (also immune to a later rename), and the payment-intent route stores `couponCode` only when a coupon genuinely resolved. A rejected or expired code previously burned the coupon's usage and the customer's per-customer allowance against an order it never discounted.
- Refunds go through `processRefund` (`lib/db/refunds.ts`), split into a short validation transaction and a settle transaction with the provider call between them. The validation half takes the order's transaction-scoped advisory lock, re-reads every cap under it and commits a PENDING refund row that reserves the order; a second overlapping request sees the live reservation and gets a 409 instead of validating against quantities that are about to move (the old code read the caps, called the provider and wrote afterwards, so two requests could both slip past). A PENDING row older than 5 minutes can only have been left by a request that died mid-flight - module routes are capped at 60 seconds - so it stops blocking, but its amount still counts against the caps because the provider may well have refunded it. The provider HTTP call runs with NO database transaction open, so a slow provider never pins a pooled connection, and the refund row id is passed as the idempotency key (Stripe's `idempotencyKey` request option, PayPal's `PayPal-Request-Id` header, GoCardless's equivalent) so a retried call cannot refund twice. A FAILED provider refund no longer increments `refunded_qty`.
- `markOrderPaymentFailed(id, reason)` takes `'FAILED' | 'CHARGEBACK'`. FAILED (the default, used by the Stripe/PayPal failure webhooks and the confirm route) still only touches a PENDING order, so a stray late failure cannot undo a paid one. CHARGEBACK (the GoCardless settle handler, when a settled payment is later charged back or fails at the bank) moves an already-PAID order to ON_HOLD with `payment_status='FAILED'` and writes an internal note telling the owner to check whether anything shipped against money that has since been clawed back - previously that case was a silent no-op, because the guard only matched PENDING.
- Stripe's `charge.refunded` handler resolves the order through `charge.payment_intent` and the new `getOrderByPaymentReference`. The `shpOrderId` metadata it used to read only ever exists on the PaymentIntent; Stripe does not copy it onto the Charge, so a dashboard refund matched nothing and the order was never marked refunded.
- `minimumOrderValue`/`maximumOrderValue` are enforced at `POST /public/checkout/payment-intent` as well as at `/checkout/session`. The session route only advises the browser, while the payment-intent route is what actually creates a payable order, so a direct POST skipping the session step produced a chargeable below-minimum order.
- `updateOrderStatus` is idempotent (`WHERE … AND status != status`) and returns whether the row changed; every once-per-transition side effect now hangs off that boolean. SHIPPED → COMPLETED → SHIPPED used to decrement the pre-order stock a second time, and `decrementStockOnShip` clamps at zero rather than erroring, so the shop quietly undercounted itself.
- `decrementPreOrderCount` (`lib/db/products.ts`) is the counterpart to `incrementPreOrderCount`, called by `releasePreOrderAllocationForOrder` on a genuine transition to CANCELLED; the refund settle path runs the identical statement inlined, because it has to execute on the transaction client rather than the shared one. `pre_order_count` previously only ever went up, so a cancelled pre-order kept its slot forever and, once the count had touched `pre_order_max_quantity`, the auto-flip left `is_pre_order = false` permanently - quietly taking a product out of pre-order mode with nobody actually waiting on those units. One statement, so the counter and the flag cannot disagree; re-enabling is deliberately narrow (only a product that was sitting at its cap, which is precisely the state the increment creates, and never one with no cap), so a product the owner switched off by hand is never switched back on. The release is guarded on `paid_at IS NOT NULL` (the allocation is only ever consumed by `fulfillPaidOrder`, so an order cancelled before it paid never took a slot) and on `quantity - refunded_qty`, so units a refund has already returned cannot be double-released.
- The CSV import engine rejects a negative price (`lib/import-engine.ts`), matching the same fix in google-sheet-products-for-shop's preview.

**Admin dialogs**
The shop admin no longer calls the browser's `confirm()`/`prompt()`/`alert()`. `modules/shop/components/admin/dialogs.tsx` exports three promise-based hooks - `useConfirm()`, `usePrompt()`, `useAlert()` - each returning `[invoke, node]`: call `await invoke(...)` and render `{node}` once in the screen. Styling matches the module's other overlays (colour tokens only, `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, Escape cancels, Enter confirms, delete confirms use the `btn-danger` class). Wired through CategoriesScreen, CollectionsScreen, ProductsScreen (new-item name prompts), DiscountsScreen (delete confirms + save-error alerts), TaxShippingScreen (delete confirms), ProductEditor (upload/save-error alerts).

**Money formatting**
All prices render through one helper - `modules/shop/lib/money.ts` `formatMoney(amount, symbol='£')` - which coerces the string/number a price arrives as and always emits `symbol` + 2dp (e.g. `£7.99`). Storefront pages/blocks and order emails pass `config.currencySymbol`; admin screens (client-rendered, no server config) read it via `components/admin/use-currency-symbol.ts` `useCurrencySymbol()` (fetches `/api/m/shop/public/config` once, module-cached, `£` fallback). Prices are decimal pounds end to end (`NUMERIC(10,2)`); nothing is stored or displayed in pence (the Stripe `×100` in `lib/payments/stripe.ts` is API-only). Discount "value" cells format per type: `%` for PERCENTAGE, `formatMoney` for FIXED_AMOUNT, `—` for FREE_SHIPPING.

**External Integrations**
Stripe (Payment Intents + Elements + webhooks, `stripe` npm SDK), PayPal (Orders v2 REST API directly, no SDK), core Members system (optional, guest checkout always works regardless), core Media/upload pipeline (`uploadMedia()` reused for digital files, but not `saveMediaRecord` - see core diffs above), core email (`renderEmailTemplate` + `sendEmail`; from v0.1.180 the shop's ten order emails are declared in `modules/shop/lib/email-templates.ts` and registered through the manifest `emailTemplates` seam, so core's `EmailTemplate` overrides, wrapper designs and editor cover them - `shp_email_templates` is retired and unread, left in place only so a rollback survives, and migration `014_email_templates_to_core.sql` copies across just the rows an owner had genuinely edited plus every `is_active` decision).

**Cron Jobs**
`0 7 * * *` → `/api/m/shop/cron/low-stock-alerts` - low-stock digest email (deduped via `low_stock_alerted_at`, re-arms on any stock_count write) + `shp_import_jobs` retention (30 days) + abandoned-PENDING-order pruning (24h, Q8). `CRON_SECRET` bearer-gated.

**Scripts**
None.

**Known Limitations** (v0.1.2 - flagged here rather than silently shipped as if finished)
