- Categories have an indented nested-tree admin UI with ↑/↓ sibling reorder, reparent, and per-category display-mode override; collections still have no reorder UI (the `position` column and API support it; only rename/delete are wired up in the collections screen). Neither uses drag-to-reorder (↑/↓ buttons only, like Directory).
- `shop.products-toolbar` (**published by shop, v0.1.61**; live consumer `google-sheet-products-for-shop`) - a module hangs a control beside the Products **list** header buttons (Export/Import-template/Import/New product). Resolved server-side in `app/cactus-admin/shop/products/page.tsx` (`resolveToolbarExtras`: reads each active module's manifest `extensionPoints`, permission-filters per entry, looks the component up in `moduleExtensionPointComponents['shop.products-toolbar']`) and passed as a single `toolbarExtras` `ReactNode` into the client `ProductsScreen`, which renders it after the New product button. Empty (renders nothing) on a plain shop. google-sheet uses it for its Google Sheet dropdown.
- `shop.products-tabs` (**published by shop, v0.1.92**; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a module hangs a whole-page **tab** beside "Products" on the Products **list** page. Same resolution shape (`resolveProductsTabs` in `products/page.tsx`: manifest read + permission filter + `moduleExtensionPointComponents['shop.products-tabs']`), building `ProductsTab[]` `{id,label,order,node}` passed to the client `ProductsScreen` with `initialTab` (from `?tab=`). `ProductsScreen` renders a `TabStrip` only when at least one tab is contributed (so a plain shop is unchanged), keeps the built-in "Products" list as the first tab, and mounts only the active contributed tab's `node` (its products fetch is skipped while a contributed tab is active). shop-variations uses it for the cross-product Variations browser.
- Reply Catcher's contribution to the `shop.order-messages` extension point is out of scope of this build (Q12) - the Communications tab section is real and will render the moment another module publishes to that point, but nothing does yet.
- The module-side rate limiter (`lib/rate-limit.ts`) is in-memory, not table-backed - resets on a cold start and doesn't share state across concurrent serverless instances. Acceptable for a secondary guard behind normal validation, but weaker than contact-form's DB-backed one.

v0.1.1 fixed five review findings from the original v0.1.0 build: Stripe/PayPal `confirmPayment` now validates charged amount/currency against the order (not just status/reference); `GET /downloads/[token]` streams the file through the endpoint instead of redirecting to the permanent storage URL; the `product`/`checkout` default page layouts now seed `ShopBackInStockForm`/`ShopUpsellProducts` (new installs only, per `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`); the product editor gained a real Recommendations panel, image picker, and digital-file upload; the Discounts screen, refund flow, CSV import, and page-layouts editor were all rebuilt from `prompt()`/raw-JSON placeholders into proper UI (see the Admin pages entry above for each).

### Shop Variations

- Slug: `shop-variations` (table prefix `svr_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/shop-variations`, manifest version 0.1.108 in the working tree (registry pin v0.1.107). `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.173` (0.1.173 adds the `shop.product-saved` seam the tax-class sync needs; 0.1.92 added the `shop.products-tabs` host slot the Variations tab needs; `GalleryThumbStrip` needed v0.1.15; previously 0.1.44, and before that 0.1.43 for `shop.gallery-media` - `product-editor/context` needed only 0.1.38 and `shop.product-detail-parts` only 0.1.35), `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.493`. Reuses shop's `shop.products`/`shop.reports` permissions (declares none of its own) and joins the existing **Shop** admin nav group with one entry ("Variation tools", was "Product options" until v0.1.72).
- **Publishes the chosen variation page-wide (v0.1.102):** `lib/selection-broadcast.ts` - `publishVariantSelection` fires window event `cactus-shop-variant-selection` with `{slug, parentProductId, productId, allOptionsChosen, chosenValueIds}` (`chosenValueIds` added in 0.1.104: every option value picked so far, in option order, so a consumer can say something sensible about a HALF-built combination - `productId` only lands once the last option is settled) and parks the same detail on `window.__cactusVariantSelection` for a late-mounting listener; called from `useVariationSelection` (so it reflects the resolved variant every part shows) and deduped by JSON equality, since every island on the page runs the hook. `productId` is null until a full combination is chosen. A browser event rather than an export ON PURPOSE: a consumer must not import `@/modules/shop-variations/...` (the path does not exist on an install without this module and would break that build), which is the same rule advanced-shipping's `variations-bridge.ts` follows server-side. First consumer: that module's `ShopShippingOptions` picker.
- **A variation's tax class follows the listing (v0.1.108):** `lib/tax-class-sync.ts` - `syncVariantChildTaxClass(parentId)` is one `UPDATE` putting every child of that parent onto the parent's `tax_class_id` (skipping the ones that already agree, so it is safe to repeat and a no-op on a product with no variations), and `syncVariationsOnProductSaved(productId, changed)` is the `shop.product-saved` listener that calls it, gated on `changed.includes('taxClassId')` so a price, a description or a stock count costs nothing. The children still copy the class at creation (`generateMatrix`, `createSingleVariant`, `upsertVariantForCombination`); this is what keeps them right when it is set or changed AFTERWARDS, which nothing did before - the basket rates a line from the child while the product page prices from the parent, so the two disagreed silently. Deliberately one-directional: a per-variation class was never selectable, so a child that differs is drift, not a decision. Unit-tested in `lib/tax-class-sync.test.ts` (the gate, and that the parent id rides as a bound parameter).
- `core.media-usage-providers` (`lib/media-usage-provider.ts`) - contributes `svr_option_values.swatch` + `svr_uploads.media_ref`/`media_key` to core's media usage index.
- Adds product options to the shop: fixed **variant matrices** (e.g. Size × Colour, each combination its own price/SKU/barcode/stock/weight/image) and free-form **personalisation add-ons** (text, long text, number, priced dropdown, checkbox, date, file upload). A variant is a real but `catalogue_hidden` child `shp_products` row created through shop's own `createProduct`, so basket, checkout, inventory, orders and refunds work unchanged; the storefront selector resolves the chosen combination to that child id and calls shop's `addToCart(childId, qty, {meta})`. Personalisation rides in the generic `line_meta` carrier, priced server-side by the registered resolver.

**Database**
Table prefix: `svr_` (7 tables). Full DDL in `modules/shop-variations/migrations/001_initial.sql` (idempotent); later per-change files are numbered (`002_image_option_type.sql` widens the `svr_options.control_type` CHECK to admit `IMAGE`, also mirrored in 001; `003_requires_previous_option.sql` adds `svr_options.requires_previous_option`, also mirrored in 001; `004_option_source.sql` adds `svr_options.source_provider`/`source_ref` + `svr_option_values.source_ref` and the `(option_id, source_ref)` index, also mirrored in 001; `005_option_name_overridden.sql` adds `svr_options.name_overridden`, also mirrored in 001; `007_delete_children_with_parent.sql` adds function `svr_delete_variant_child()` + AFTER DELETE row trigger `svr_variants_delete_child` on `svr_variants` - deleting a variant row deletes its child `shp_products` row, which is what finally cleans up when a PARENT product is deleted from shop's own UI: the parent's cascade removes `svr_variants` but no module code runs, so children used to survive as orphans still holding SKU + slug. Module code paths delete the child first (cascade removes the variant row), so for them the trigger's re-delete matches nothing; TRUNCATE (backup restore) fires no row triggers); `009_variant_tax_class.sql` adds **no DDL at all** - it is the one-off data catch-up that puts every existing variation child onto its parent listing's `tax_class_id`, touching only the children that disagree, so it is idempotent by construction and matches nothing on a fresh install). Cross-module FKs to `shp_products` are safe because shop installs first.

- `svr_options` - `id`, `product_id` FK→shp_products (cascade, the parent), `name`, `control_type` (DROPDOWN\|SWATCH\|PILL\|IMAGE - IMAGE added by `002_image_option_type.sql`, which drops and re-adds the CHECK constraint, and mirrored in 001 for fresh installs), `position`, `requires_previous_option` (BOOLEAN, default false - added by `003_requires_previous_option.sql`, mirrored in 001; when true the storefront holds this option back until **every** option before it by position has a value chosen, not just the one immediately before - see `isOptionVisible`), `source_provider?`/`source_ref?` (TEXT, both added by `004_option_source.sql`, mirrored in 001 - the extension-point provider id that built this option and that provider's own opaque ref for the source; both null on a hand-typed option, set together or not at all), `name_overridden` (BOOLEAN, default false - added by `005_option_name_overridden.sql`, mirrored in 001; true once the owner named the option something other than the source's own name, set on create when the two differ and on every PATCH rename. Suppresses the refresh's `nameDiffers` report, so a deliberately renamed copy is never nagged - which is what makes adding one source to a product twice, under two names, liveable), `card_display` (BOOLEAN, default false), `card_label?` (TEXT), `card_limit?` (INTEGER) - all three added by `006_card_display.sql`, mirrored in 001; the per-option "Display in categories" switch, the heading the product CARD prints instead of `name` (null/blank = use `name`), and how many values a card shows before the "+N" marker (null or <= 0 = all of them). See the card-summary note below.
- `svr_option_values` - `id`, `option_id` FK (cascade), `label`, `slug` (TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE `(option_id, slug)` - added by `008_value_slug.sql` with a slugified+per-option-deduped backfill from `label`, mirrored in 001. **The value's identity within its option**: labels may duplicate ("Black" in two materials, told apart by swatch), slugs may not; the CSV/sheet round-trip writes every Value cell as `(slug)Label` via `lib/value-cell.ts` and resolves slug-first on import. Copies from an option source take the source's slug where free, deduped by `ensureUniqueOptionValueSlug`), `swatch?` (hex colour for SWATCH, image url for IMAGE, null otherwise and for a value nobody has styled yet), `position`, `source_ref?` (TEXT, added by `004_option_source.sql`, mirrored in 001 - the source value this one was copied from, opaque here; null on a hand-added value, which a refresh then never touches. Indexed `(option_id, source_ref)` because a refresh matches on that pair).
- `svr_variants` - `id`, `product_id` FK (parent, cascade), `child_product_id` FK→shp_products (cascade, unique - the hidden child), `enabled`, `position`.
- `svr_variant_values` - composite PK (`variant_id` FK cascade, `option_value_id` FK cascade) - which values define a variant.
- `svr_addons` - `id`, `product_id` FK (cascade), `type` (TEXT\|TEXTAREA\|NUMBER\|SELECT\|CHECKBOX\|DATE\|FILE), `label`, `required`, `position`, `config` JSONB (max length, min/max, flat/per-char price, priced choices, file limits).
- `svr_uploads` - `id`, `token` (unique), `media_ref` (public url, used as the line_meta href), `media_provider?`/`media_key?` (for orphan blob cleanup), `filename?`, `size`, `mime_type`, `order_item_id?` (unused link, retained), `ip_hash?`, `created_at`. Not FK'd to order items - orphan cleanup cross-checks `media_ref` against `shp_order_items.line_meta`.
- `svr_settings` - singleton (`id='singleton'`): `max_upload_mb` (10), `allowed_upload_types`, `upload_retention_days` (30), `max_variants` (200).

**Permissions**: none of its own - admin writes gate on `shop.products` (via shop's `requireShopUser`), the report on `shop.reports`.

**API Routes** (through `/api/m/shop-variations/…`)

- Admin (`shop.products`): `GET admin/variations` (v0.1.72 - cross-product variations list for the Variations tab on Shop › Products; every variation with its primary image, option-value label, price/SKU/stock and any contributed columns; filters by product, by missing image, by missing SKU (`missing=sku` - `c."sku" IS NULL OR btrim(c."sku") = ''`, alongside the image one in SQL rather than in JS, since both live on the variation's own child product row), by a missing contributed column, or - `missing=lost:image` / `missing=lost:<column id>` - by a **lost file**, one still recorded against the variation whose url no longer resolves; all resolved in `lib/variations-list.ts`, which merges contributed columns by heading through `lib/variation-columns.ts` and checks urls through `lib/lost-files.ts`), `GET admin/products/[id]` (deep-editor payload), `POST admin/products/[id]/options`, `POST admin/products/[id]/generate-matrix`, `POST admin/products/[id]/clear-variants`, `POST admin/products/[id]/delete-variants` (bulk delete a chosen set - `{variantIds: string[]}` → `deleteVariants(parentId, ids)`, each id verified to belong to the parent before its hidden child is deleted; backs the grid's select-all + **Delete selected**), `POST admin/products/[id]/variants` (create one hand-picked combination - `{optionValueIds: string[]}` → `createSingleVariant`; rejects a partial combination or a duplicate value-set, builds a hidden child like the matrix does, then `resequenceVariantPositions` renumbers every row so the new variant lands in the slot a full generate would have given it), `POST admin/products/[id]/addons`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/options/[id]`, `POST admin/options/[id]/values`, `POST admin/options/[id]/refresh` (re-read a sourced option from its provider - additive only, see the option-source point below), `GET admin/option-sources` (every contributed source with its values + a suggested control type, for the picker; empty list when no module contributes one), `PATCH/DELETE admin/option-values/[id]`, `POST admin/products/[id]/resequence-variants` (0.1.61 - renumber a parent's existing variants into matrix order after an option/value drag, and re-compose the child names option order feeds; a renumber, never a regenerate, so ids and their stock/prices/photos/orders are preserved), `PATCH/DELETE admin/variants/[id]` (PATCH edits the child product via shop's `updateProduct`/`setProductMedia` + `enabled`, and as of 0.1.52 carries the **optional price types** as well as `price` - `salePrice`/`retailPrice`/`tradePrice`/`costPrice`, each `.nullable()` so clearing a variant's sale price stays distinct from setting it to zero; the image field is **`imageUrls: string[]`**, not a single url - the whole ordered set is written to `shp_product_media` (index 0 `is_primary`, `position` = index, duplicates dropped) and an empty array clears them; on a non-empty set, calls shop's `reorganiseProductMedia(childProductId, {folderProductId: parentId})` so the variant images file into the parent product's media folder. DELETE removes one variant by deleting its hidden child product, which cascades the `svr_variants` + `svr_variant_values` rows away - the same path `clear-variants` takes per row), `PATCH/DELETE admin/addons/[id]`, `GET admin/export` (CSV), `POST admin/import` (CSV). `GET admin/reports` gates on `shop.reports`.
- Public: `GET public/by-slug/[slug]/variations` (storefront selector payload - options, per-variant price/stock/image, base images, add-ons; looked up by slug so no product-context injection is needed in shop), `POST public/upload` (anonymous, rate-limited, size/type-validated personalisation file upload → core media provider + `svr_uploads` row, returns a token).
- Member: `GET member/gdpr-export` (internal bearer; the member's personalisation from their orders' `line_meta`).
- Cron: `GET/POST cron/cleanup-uploads` (`Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, daily 03:00) - prunes orphaned uploads past the retention window, deleting the blob then the row.

Admin pages (`/cactus-admin/m/shop-variations/…`): `reports` (parent-grouped variant sales), `import` (CSV import/export). A shared `VariationsTabs` sub-nav keeps these two under one Shop-group nav entry, **"Variation tools"** (landing on `import`), renamed from "Product options" in v0.1.72. **The cross-product variations list moved out (v0.1.72) to the Variations tab on Shop › Products** via `shop.products-tabs` (below); the old `products` admin page, its `admin/products` overview route and `VariationsListScreen` are gone. **Extension point consumed: `shop.products-tabs` (v0.1.72)** - `VariationsBrowser` (client, id `variations`, permission `shop.products`) fetches `GET admin/variations` and renders a searchable product filter plus a two-group filter dropdown: **Nothing set** ("Without Image", "Without SKU" (0.1.111), "Without <attribute>"/"Without 3D Files" - each contributed column, for free through the `variant-field-provider` values; the first two are built in, listed in `BUILT_IN_MISSING` in `lib/variations-list.ts` so a non-built-in target is the thing that means "contributed column") and **Broken links** ("Lost Image", "Lost 3D Files" - only the image and the columns whose provider declares `kind: 'file'`, since asking whether an attribute is a broken link is nonsense). No 3D or attribute code lives here. Contributed columns are **merged by heading** server-side (`lib/variation-columns.ts`), so an attribute used across the catalogue is one column and one filter entry rather than one per product. Read-only overview; each row links to its product's Variations tab. **There is no standalone per-product editor** (`products/[productId]` was deleted in v0.1.6): the whole thing is now the **Variations tab** on shop's product editor, contributed via `shop.product-editor-sections` → `ProductVariationsSection` (server wrapper; returns `null` for a `catalogue_hidden` variant child, since a variant of a variant is not a thing) → `VariationsPanel` (client: options builder with inline rename and drag-to-reorder (v0.1.18 - options are draggable cards, values draggable pills within their own option; only a grab handle is `draggable`, so the inline rename/swatch/delete controls keep their click and text-select behaviour, and a value drag is pinned to its option id and never crosses; a drop reassigns `position` on the moved rows through the existing `PATCH admin/options/[id]` / `PATCH admin/option-values/[id]` routes, then refreshes. **"No variant re-sync is needed" was wrong and is fixed in 0.1.61**: the grid *label* is indeed composed live from option order in `getEditorPayload`, but `svr_variants.position` is stored, so a drag left every variant sitting in the running order the old value order implied - visible as a grid whose rows no longer match the options above them, until the next generate. `persistPositions` now fires one `POST admin/products/[id]/resequence-variants` after all the moved rows have landed, which calls `resequenceVariantPositions` + `syncVariantChildNames`. **Once per drag, not once per PATCH**: the row PATCHes go out concurrently, and hanging the resequence off each one would both repeat the work N times and race - every call re-reads the option order to recompute slots, so a slow early one could write its now-stale answer last. Names are re-composed on both drags even though only an *option* reorder can move one (a child is named from its value labels joined in option order), because the sync only writes rows whose name actually differs), matrix generate/rebuild/clear, bulk variant grid, personalisation fields). **The grid carries every price type the shop has switched on** (0.1.52): the panel takes an `enabledPriceTypes` prop, read server-side by `ProductVariationsSection` from shop's `getShopConfigCached()` (rather than a second config fetch of the panel's own), and renders a column per switched-on type - Sale, RRP, Trade, Cost - beside the mandatory Price. The same wrapper reads `weightBasedShippingEnabled` off that config and passes it down (0.1.58): false drops the Weight column and its inputs, matching what shop's own Stock tab does, while per-variant weights already stored are left alone. Emptying one of those boxes writes `null`, not `0`: a blank sale price means "not on offer" and a zero one means free. Two save models on purpose: structural work (add option, generate matrix, add addon) applies immediately because it is an action, while per-variant grid edits are held locally and written by the product editor's single Save via `useProductEditorSave` (dirty rows tint, and only the rows actually written are cleared, so a row edited mid-save survives). Tab badge = variant count. A stale-matrix warning appears when the option combinations no longer match the variant count; because `generateMatrix` only fills the gap (existing rows kept), a big matrix that timed out part-built is resumable, so the action button reads **Continue building options** while the count is short of expected (and the warning says as much, "build a batch at a time, keep pressing Continue"), falling back to **Rebuild from options** when there are more variants than the options now call for. The grid also offers a per-row **Delete** (the DELETE route above) for the odd variant a big matrix throws up that is never actually sold, and its first column (the variant label) is `position: sticky; left: 0` so it stays put while the rest of the grid scrolls sideways. An **Add a single variant** control below the grid (`AddSingleVariant` in `VariationsPanel.tsx`) builds one hand-picked combination - a dropdown per option, each defaulting to its first value - via `POST admin/products/[id]/variants`, for the site owner who wants to grow the list one row at a time rather than generate the whole matrix. Ordering is the point: the server's `resequenceVariantPositions` (`variants-service.ts`) recomputes every variant's `position` as its canonical cartesian index (mixed-radix over the options in display order, the last option moving fastest - the same order `generateMatrix` walks), written back in one bulk `setVariantPositions` statement, so an individually-added variant appears exactly where the full auto-generate would have placed it, not tacked on the end.

**Filtering the variants grid by option (working tree, unreleased).** `VariationsPanel` gained an `optionFilter` state (`Record<optionId, valueId>`, `''`/absent = Any) and a `VariantFilterBar` sub-component rendered above the bulk-controls row - one plain `<select>` per option in option order, values off the same `data.options[].values` rows the storefront renders, so the admin asks the question the shopper's way. Deliberately plain selects regardless of `controlType`: a swatch grid sells a colour, this files one. Three derived memos, no new fetch and no server change (`data.variants[].optionValueIds` was already on the editor payload): `activeFilter` (filter READ through a live-value-id set rather than pruned into state on reload - a retired value stops counting and the select falls back to Any, which avoids a `setState` in an effect), `visibleVariants` (a variant is shown when it carries EVERY chosen value; options on Any ask nothing, so a partial choice narrows rather than matching nothing - the opposite of the storefront's "half a choice is not a product"), and `reachableValues` (per option, the value ids present among variants matching every OTHER option's choice, so the dropdowns narrow each other; the option's own choice is excluded from its own test, and the currently-chosen value is always kept in its list or the select renders blank with no way back to Any). **Scope changes that matter:** the header tick box and `toggleAll` now act on `visibleVariants` (add/remove them from `selected`, leaving off-screen selections alone) and `bulkSet` takes the row list as an argument and is handed `visibleVariants` - a filtered "fill every row" that rewrote all 625 prices would be the expensive kind of surprise. `BulkControls` gained a `scoped` boolean that only changes its wording ("Fill the rows shown:" + matching aria-labels). `Delete all`, `Rebuild from options` and the `matrixStale` warning still count the whole matrix, which is what they are about. `tbody` maps `visibleVariants` with a `colSpan={99}` "nothing matches those choices" row when empty.

**Option control types: DROPDOWN, PILL, SWATCH, IMAGE (v0.1.16).** All four are one column, `svr_options.control_type`, and the two swatch types share one nullable `svr_option_values.swatch` column - a hex colour for SWATCH, an image url for IMAGE. No second column: the column already meant "whatever the control shows beside the label", so IMAGE only needed the CHECK constraint widening (`002_image_option_type.sql`). The API-edge cap on it is `SWATCH_MAX_LENGTH` (`lib/types.ts`, 1000), shared by the three routes that accept a swatch - it was 200, which is roomy for `#ff0000` and too tight for a hosted media url carrying a folder path.
- Admin: `InlineImageSwatch` (`VariationsPanel.tsx`) sits where `InlineSwatch` sits for colours - a 22px thumbnail on the value pill, click to open shop's `MediaPickerModal` (the shared core media library, `GET/POST /api/admin/media`, with its own upload button, so picking a filed image and uploading a new one are the same two clicks). It saves on the pick rather than behind a tick, because unlike the colour control there is no hand-typed hex box to half-finish and therefore no draft to hold.
- A value's picture is set **after** the value exists, not while adding it: `AddValueInline`'s extra field stays colour-only, so the comma-separated "S, M, L" flow still works for an IMAGE option and each value is then given its picture from the dotted placeholder. A value with no picture renders as the bare label on the storefront - the same fallback an uncoloured SWATCH value gets.
- Storefront (`OptionControl` in `VariantParts.tsx`, shared by the granular blocks and the slot path): SWATCH, IMAGE and PILL are all one row of buttons; IMAGE adds a 28px thumbnail and **keeps the label** beside it, because a shopper who can't see the picture would otherwise have nothing to go on.

**Guided configuration (shop-variations, working tree).** The option controls and the buy row read as a numbered sequence with a locked destination, rather than a stack of loose pickers over a live button. Everything below is shared by both storefront hosts (the granular `VariantOptionsPart`/`VariantAddToCartPart` and the slot path's `VariantSlotPurchaseClient`), because the controls are the same components.
- **Numbered option titles.** `OptionControl` takes an optional `index` (1-based) and renders `OptionNumber` before the option's name: an outlined circle while the option is unanswered, filled with `--color-primary` once it has a value. Both hosts number the options **as shown**, not by payload index, so one held back by `requires_previous_option` leaves no gap in the count (`VariantOptionsPart` numbers its already-filtered `visibleOptions`; the slot path maps → filters on `isOptionVisible` → numbers). The accordion layout draws the marker on its own section heading instead, since that heading IS the label there (the control inside runs with `hideLabel`). The label span became `inline-flex` to sit the marker on the name's baseline, with a `display:block` wrapper (`labelRow`) on the stacked path so it still occupies its own line - the `beside` float path is unchanged and still floats the whole span.
- **Price hints under a choice.** `valuePriceRange(payload, selection, optionId, valueId)` and `optionAffectsPrice(payload, selection, optionId)` in `lib/selection-logic.ts` (pure, unit-tested in `lib/selection-logic.pricing.test.ts`, 18 cases) are surfaced on the hook as `sel.valuePrice()` / `sel.optionAffectsPrice()`. Both filter variants **directionally** - buyable, carrying the value, and consistent with the picks ABOVE the option only - exactly as `isValueAvailable` does, so a later pick can never move what an earlier option says it costs. The control prints `from £246` (or the bare figure where the value pins the price exactly) as a second line under the value's label, and only where `optionAffectsPrice` is true: an option whose choices all start from the same figure would otherwise print the same number four times. A dropdown has nowhere for a second line, so the hint rides the `<option>` text as ` - from £246`. `moneyShort` trims a bare `.00` for these hints only.
- **Chosen state.** A picked value keeps its 2px `--color-primary` border and gains a `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 16%, var(--color-surface))` wash (tinted, not filled - the label and its second line still have to read, in both schemes), a `ChosenTick` badge overlapping its top-right corner, and `Selected` in place of the price hint. The badge is absolutely positioned, so the button is now `position: relative` and nothing in the row may take `overflow: hidden`. The swatch-only look has deliberately given up its text and gets the tick but no second line.
- **Locked buy button + selection summary.** `sel.canAdd` now spells out `allOptionsChosen` rather than relying on `inStock` implying it (the two agreed, but only by accident of the stock check needing a resolved variant). `sel.missingOptionNames` (display order) feeds `missingOptionsSentence()` → "Choose Width and Storage first", which is BOTH the button's tooltip and the written note under the row - a tooltip is no use on a phone or to a screen reader. The tooltip's `title` sits on a wrapper `<span>` because a disabled control takes no pointer events and so never shows its own; that wrapper carries `flex:1` with **no** `min-width`, so shop's `.spd-add` 200px floor still makes the row wrap rather than squeezing the CTA. `SelectionSummary` (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`, `role="status"`) prints "Ready to add: 140cm · 2 Drawer Fixed Pedestal · Black" above the row from `sel.chosenSummary`, only once every visible option is answered, on the `--color-success-bg`/`-border`/`--color-success` token trio.
- **"Your choice" pill + reset clears the chosen view.** `YourChoicePill` (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`) sits top-left inside the gallery stage - shop's `.spd-stage` is already `position: relative`, so it is clipped to the same rounded box - whenever every option is answered AND the stage is showing the shopper's own configuration: a contributed stage (their variation's 3D model) or one of the variant's own photographs. A base photo they clicked back to earns no pill. Pressing **Reset options** bumps a new `resetEpoch` counter on the store entry (`resetOptionValues`), surfaced as `sel.resetEpoch`; both galleries watch it and clear the thumbnail override, the tap-zoom and the contributed stage, and put the reset counter in the `<extra.Thumbs>` key so a contributor holding its own memory of the settled variation (`Gallery3dThumbs`' `lastResolved`) is remounted back to the product's own media. A counter, not "nothing is chosen": a page OPENS with nothing chosen and must keep the view it opened on.

**Option summaries on product cards (shop-variations 0.1.88 / shop 0.1.128).** An option ticked **Display in categories** (`svr_options.card_display`) summarises its values on the product CARD wherever cards render - category grids, shop home, related/featured rows. Three moving parts:
- `lib/card-options.ts` - prisma-free: the `CardOptionSummary`/`CardOptionsFacts` types, the `CARD_OPTIONS_FACT_ID = 'variations-card-options'` tag, and the pure `summariseOptionForCard()` (label fallback `card_label?.trim() || name`; `kind` = swatch/image/text from `control_type`, PILL folds into text; `card_limit` null **or <= 0** means no cap; `more` = the remainder, 0 when everything fitted; returns null when not ticked or the option has no values). Unit-tested in `lib/card-options.test.ts` (9 cases). **Kept separate from the provider on purpose**: the card block below is registered as an editor component too, so anything it imports at runtime lands in the client bundle, and the provider reaches for prisma.
- `lib/card-options-provider.ts` - registered at shop's **`shop.card-media`** point under id `variations-card-options` (a second entry at the same point alongside `variations-card-media`; the resolver keys providers by entry id, so two are fine). Batched: one `getOptionsWithValuesForProducts` for the whole grid.
- `components/puck/card-variation-options.tsx` - the `ShopCardVariationOptions` Puck block (`layoutTypes: ["shopProductCard"]`, label **Card: Variation options**, `inline: true`, `dragRef` on its own root, no fields). Reads its payload out of `_ctx.facts` by id; inline styles only (no CSS file in this module, and a `<style>` per part would repeat once per card). No `_ctx` = editor canvas = a two-row sample skeleton. Same render fn for the editor and RSC halves, so markup is identical by construction.
- **Placement is the owner's**: nothing shows until they drag the block into the published `shopProductCard` layout. `VariationsPanel` prints a one-off reminder in the Options section the moment any option on the product has `cardDisplay` set.
- Admin: `CardDisplayControls` in `VariationsPanel.tsx` - the tickbox plus a **Label** text box (placeholder = the option name) and a **Swatches shown**/**Options shown** number box (placeholder "All"; the wording follows the control type). Both commit on blur/Enter, not per keystroke (each commit is a PATCH + full refetch). Drafts are seeded from the saved values and **never** synced by an effect - the parent keys the component on `` `${cardLabel}|${cardLimit}` `` so a commit remounts it (react-hooks/set-state-in-effect otherwise fires). Empty box sends `null`, which the PATCH route treats as "clear the override" - a blank `card_label` is stored as null, never as `''`.
- Wire format: `PATCH admin/options/[id]` gained `cardDisplay?: boolean`, `cardLabel?: string|null` (max 80), `cardLimit?: number|null` (int 1-50). All three nullable-optional on purpose: undefined = leave alone, null = clear. `updateOption()`'s whitelist and `mapOption()` extended to match.
- **Not wired**: `product-attributes-for-shop`'s `ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx` has its own `renderTaggedCards` and never called `resolveShopCardExtras`, so that surface shows no option summary (and, pre-existing, no variation photos or 3D badge either). Deskwell does not use it - both `/shop` and the category pages go through shop's `renderCards`.

**Dependent options - "reveal in order" (`requires_previous_option`).** Any option from the second onward can be flagged to stay hidden on the storefront until the option immediately before it (by display order) has a value chosen, so a shopper works through them one step at a time. Pure progressive disclosure: it changes nothing about the variant matrix or `resolveVariant`, only which controls are on screen. The gate is one pure helper, `isOptionVisible(payload, selection, index)` (`lib/selection-logic.ts`), surfaced on the hook as `sel.isOptionVisible(index)` and applied in both storefront render paths (`VariantOptionsPart` in `VariantParts.tsx` and `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` in `DetailSlotPartsClient.tsx`). It chains: if the option before is itself hidden and unchosen this one stays hidden too, and it is dormant on the first option (nothing before it to wait on), so a flag left on an option later dragged to the front simply does nothing. Admin: a checkbox on each option card from the second onward (`VariationsPanel.tsx`, gated on `oi > 0`), labelled with the previous option's name, saving through `PATCH admin/options/[id]` (`requiresPreviousOption` boolean).

**Pinned mobile gallery (`lib/use-sticky-mobile-gallery.ts`, working tree).** On a stacked (mobile) product page, and only for a product that actually has options, `VariantSlotGalleryClient` pins the gallery under the site header while the shopper scrolls the option pickers: the hook flips the column to `position:fixed` via the `svr-mstick` class (CSS emitted by the client, restyling shop's `spd-*` classes at equal specificity but later in the document - stage at half width, thumbnails beside it as a 2×2 grid whose overflow scrolls vertically; the `spd-thumbs-wrap` collapses to `display:contents` so the same rules land whether the strip arrives wrapped (below) or bare (beside)), while a hidden sibling spacer holds the column's slot in the flow so pinning never jumps the scroll. The options' extent is found through the `svr-options` marker class worn by both option hosts (`VariantSlotPurchaseClient`'s inline area and the granular `VariantOptionsPart`). It releases both ways: scrolled back toward the top the gallery drops back into the flow unchanged; scrolled on past the options' bottom edge it lets go and leaves with them. "Mobile" is detected from geometry (options stacked below the gallery in the same column) rather than a breakpoint, so per-site breakpoint settings are honoured without widening shop's slot contract; the pin's top edge rides shop's live-measured `--spd-header-h`, so shrink-on-scroll headers stay snug. Desktop layouts (options beside the gallery) never match and keep shop's own sticky column.

**Extension point published: `shop-variations.option-source` (v0.1.49, working tree).** Another module offers ready-made options - "here is a Colour list with twelve values" - which the Variations tab turns into a real `svr_options` row. Live consumer: `product-attributes-for-shop` v0.1.9 (`lib/option-source-provider.ts`, `productAttributesOptionSourceProvider`), offering each attribute as a source and each attribute value as a source value.

- **Data-only by design.** A provider contributes no UI at all: `listSources()` / `getSource(ref)` return plain `{ref, name, groupLabel?, values: [{ref, label, swatch}]}`, and shop-variations owns the whole picker (`components/admin/OptionSourcePicker.tsx`). That keeps the word "attribute" out of this module entirely and keeps the provider free of admin-UI code. Contrast `variant-columns`/`variant-field-provider`, which do cross a component over.
- Resolver `lib/option-sources.ts` (`resolveOptionSourceProviders` / `resolveOptionSourceProvider`, same manifest-read + permission-filter + registry-lookup shape as the variant-field resolver), plus `suggestControlType(values)` - all-hex swatches suggest SWATCH, all-non-hex suggest IMAGE, mixed or none falls back to DROPDOWN rather than rendering half a swatch grid as blanks.
- **The browser never supplies the labels.** `POST admin/products/[id]/options` takes `source: {provider, ref, valueRefs[]}` and re-reads the source server-side, so what lands in the DB is what the provider says now; only the option name, control type and the picked refs come from the client. The name is the deliberate override - it starts as the source's name and is the shop owner's from then on.
- **Refresh is additive, never destructive** (`lib/option-refresh.ts`, `POST admin/options/[id]/refresh`). Matching is by `source_ref`, not label, so a renamed source value updates its copy rather than orphaning it. New source values are appended; copies whose source value is gone are **kept and reported as stale**, never deleted, because each option value has real variants (hidden child products with their own price/stock/SKU) hanging off it; hand-added values (`source_ref` null) are always left alone; the option's own name is never overwritten, only reported as differing. Renames that would collide with an existing label on the same option are skipped, matching the rename endpoint's own duplicate refusal. The route re-runs `fileSwatchImage` for any swatch that came across and `syncVariantChildNames` when anything changed, since variant child names are composed from value labels.
- **One source may be added to a product more than once** (v0.1.50, working tree) - a frame colour and a seat colour off one Colour attribute. Nothing keys on `source_ref` per product, so the only constraint is the option-name one, now enforced on **create** as well as rename: `POST admin/products/[id]/options` trims the name and 409s on a case-insensitive duplicate (previously unchecked, so the typed-in path could make the duplicates the importer and the rename endpoint both refuse). The picker takes `existingOptions` (name + source refs) instead of `existingNames`, badges a source that is already on the product with the names it uses, starts the name box **empty** when the source's own name is taken, warns live and disables Add while the typed name clashes. `name_overridden` is set on create when the chosen name differs from the source's and on every PATCH rename, and `refreshOptionFromSource` reports `nameDiffers` only when it is false - otherwise every refresh of a deliberately renamed copy would nag about a name the owner chose.
- **A source is now the only way in** (shop-variations v0.1.55). The typed-in "Add an option" form (name + control type + comma-separated values) is gone from `VariationsPanel`; the tab offers `Add from attributes` alone, so every option on every product traces back to one source row and one colour cannot exist under three spellings across three products. `POST admin/products/[id]/options` still accepts its `{name, controlType, values}` shape - the CSV importer and `lib/csv.ts` build options through the db layer, and the route's manual branch is left as the documented contract - so the gate is the UI, not the route.
- **New values travel back to the source** (shop-variations v0.1.55 + product-attributes-for-shop v0.1.15). `OptionSourceProvider` gains an **optional** `createValue(ref, {label, swatch})` returning the stored `OptionSourceValue`. `POST admin/options/[id]/values` calls it on the hand-typed branch whenever the option is sourced and the provider implements it, then copies the returned `ref`/`label`/`swatch` down - so a value typed on the Variations tab lands on the attribute too and is **sourced from birth**, matching on a later Refresh instead of being an orphan. The source is the authority on what it stored: a reused label comes back with the source's own spelling and swatch. A provider that refuses (source deleted, blank label) is a **hard 400, not a quiet local write** - a local-only row would look saved while the attributes screen silently disagreed. Providers without `createValue` keep the old local-only behaviour. `attributes` implements it with the same reuse-by-label rule its own `reuseExisting` POST body uses, plus `ensureUniqueValueSlug` / `nextValuePosition` / `fileSwatchImage` so a value made this way is indistinguishable from one made on the Attributes screen. `VariationsPanel.addValue` now surfaces the refusal in `optionError` instead of ignoring the response.
- Degrades to a dead end rather than to nothing: no contributing module means an empty `GET admin/option-sources`, and since the typed-in form has gone, the tab now says so in words and points at setting attributes up first, rather than showing a button with nothing behind it. shop-variations still does **not** declare `requiresModules: product-attributes-for-shop` (that would invert the dependency - attributes is the optional companion), so a variations-only install can price and edit existing options but cannot add a new one. Uninstalling the provider later leaves the copied options fully working - they are the product's own rows - and only removes the Refresh and Add affordances.

**Extension point published: `shop-variations.variant-columns` (v0.1.12)** - another module hangs an extra column on the variants grid, one cell per variant, resolved in `ProductVariationsSection` (manifest read + permission filter + registry lookup, none of which can happen in the browser) and passed to `VariationsPanel` as `columns: VariantColumn[]`. **No live consumer as of the current working tree**: `product-3d-views-for-shop`'s **3D** column used to ride this point, but moved to the dynamic `variant-field-provider` sibling (below) so its 3D files round-trip through the CSV/Google Sheet. The static point stays published for any column that genuinely needs no CSV presence.

- It exists because the alternative broke module isolation: setting a variation's picture and its 3D model are the same errand, but the grid belongs to this module and the model to one this module has never heard of and does not depend on. So the grid learned about *columns*, not about 3D - there is **no 3D code in shop-variations**, and without that module installed there is no such column.
- Contract: a cell gets `productId`, `variantId`, `childProductId` (the knowledge only this module has - a variation IS a hidden child product) and `label`, and owns its own storage, fetching and saving.
- **A contributed cell must be a client component.** `VariationsPanel` is a client island that fetches its own variants, so cells render per row in the browser and only client references survive the crossing - same rule as `shop.gallery-media`'s `Thumbs`/`Stage`.
- Contributed cells **save themselves** and are deliberately not wired into the editor's Save button: this point exists for uploads, and holding a 40 MB file as a pending in-memory edit would be a lie that costs the admin their upload.
- `label`/`order` ride along on the manifest entry (the `shop.product-editor-sections` trick), each with a fallback for manifests written before they existed.

**Extension point published: `shop-variations.variant-field-provider` (v0.1.29)** - the *dynamic* sibling of `variant-columns`. A static variant-column is one manifest entry = one column resolved without knowing the product; a **field provider** returns a set of columns that **depends on the product** (`listColumns(productId)`), so one module can contribute a different number of columns per product - e.g. one per attribute a product uses for its variations. `lib/variant-field-providers.ts` holds the contract + `resolveVariantFieldProviders(user?)` (manifest read + optional permission gate). The provider object is one export carrying: `listColumns`, `getValues(productId, childIds)` (per-child column values, for CSV export), an **optional** `beginImport(productId, childIds)` (v0.1.37 - preload once per parent, returns an opaque ctx), `applyImportedRow(productId, childId, row, ctx?)` (CSV import writes its own columns back, using the preloaded ctx), an **optional** `rowChanged(productId, childId, row, ctx?)` (v0.1.64-to-be, working tree - **read-only** twin of `applyImportedRow`: would applying this row write anything? Must create/update/delete nothing, including the lazily-created rows `applyImportedRow` may make - an attribute value for an unseen label counts as a change without being created. Lets the google-sheet Pull preview count changed provider columns instead of always previewing "0 to update" for them then applying anyway. A provider without it is invisible to the preview, as all were before), and a client `Cell` (the admin grid control, `columnKey` telling it which column it is). `VariantFieldColumn` is `{key, label, order?, kind?}`; **`kind: 'text' | 'file'`** (working tree, default `'text'`) says the value holds file urls rather than a label, which is the only thing that lets the cross-product browser offer its **Lost <column>** filter without knowing what any provider contributes. Note the key is **per product** (attributes key by assignment), so `variations-list.ts` merges contributions by heading before they reach the browser - see `lib/variation-columns.ts`. **Import batching (v0.1.37):** `applyImportedRow` used to be one round-trip *per row* per provider - the last per-row DB ceiling after the v0.5.519 shop/shop-variations batch. `csv.ts` now calls each provider's `beginImport` once per parent (child ids from `upsertCtx.existing`) and threads the returned ctx into every `applyImportedRow`, so provider reads drop from O(rows) to O(parents). Fully back-compatible: a provider with no `beginImport` gets `ctx === undefined` and behaves as before. A variant **created mid-import** is absent from the preload snapshot, so a ctx miss MUST default to empty current state - a brand-new variant still gets its values written (contract spelled out in `variant-field-providers.ts`, covered by each provider's `variant-field-provider.test.ts`). The **same object drives three surfaces**: `ProductVariationsSection` builds dynamic `VariantColumn`s from it for the grid, and `csv.ts` appends the columns to `exportVariationsCsv` (union of labels, after Weight) and feeds every row of `importVariationsCsv` back through `applyImportedRow`. Because the columns live in the CSV, **the Google Sheet sync carries them with no google-sheet code change** (`gridToImportCsv` is generic; the importer round-trips whatever the header names). `upsertVariantForCombination` now returns `childProductId` for the import path. **This module knows nothing of what the columns mean** - no `pat_` reference - exactly the isolation `variant-columns` was built for. Live consumers: `product-attributes-for-shop`'s per-variant attribute columns (its **Use for variations** attributes), and `product-3d-views-for-shop`'s **3D Files** column (a `|`-separated list of the variant's model urls, always offered - any variant can carry a model; attach-by-url on import, `deleteModelCascade` for a url the sheet dropped).

**The variant's own price types ride the CSV (shop-variations' own columns, not a provider).** `exportVariationsCsv` emits **Sale Price, RRP, Trade Price, Cost Price** (constant `PRICE_TYPE_COLUMNS`) straight after **Price**, blank where a variant hasn't set one - the same optional figures the product editor's Pricing tab holds, read off `VariantEditorRow.{salePrice,retailPrice,tradePrice,costPrice}` which already come from the hidden child product. `importVariationsCsv` reads them by header (`optPrice`: present-but-empty clears to null, a number sets it, unparseable → null - Products-import parity) and threads them into `upsertVariantForCombination`'s `fields`; that function's change-detection and update object grew the four, and `getChildProductFields` (the pre-loaded diff source) selects `sale_price`/`retail_price`/`trade_price`/`cost_price` so a re-import diffs them in memory. On the google-sheet side only two touch-points were needed: `FIXED_VARIATION_COLUMNS` lists the four (so a narrowing Push treats them as owned), and `pull-diff.ts`'s `variationRowChanged` compares them (blank = cleared) so the Pull preview counts a changed RRP/trade/cost as an update. No `shp_*`/`svr_*` column was added - the child rows have carried these since shop's `005_price_types.sql`.

**The variant's own image also rides the CSV (shop-variations' own column, not a provider).** `exportVariationsCsv` emits an **Image** column carrying `VariantEditorRow.imageUrls[0]` (the hidden child product's primary media url; the CSV/Sheet carries **one** image per variant, so a variant with several exports only its first, and a changed cell replaces the lot) after Weight and before the provider columns; `importVariationsCsv` reads it (`imageCol`) and writes it via shop's `setProductMedia` + `reorganiseProductMedia(child, {folderProductId: parent})` - the same write `PATCH admin/variants/[id]` makes. Empty cell clears the image; a value failing the `http(s)` `isHttpUrl` guard is pushed to `errors`, not stored; and the whole block is skipped when the sheet carries no Image column, so a sheet made before this column existed never wipes an image. This is what makes the Google Sheet's Variations tab carry variant pictures.

**Puck Blocks** (editor + RSC parity, colour tokens only): composite `ShopVariantPurchase` (layout `shopProduct` - gallery + options + personalisation + live price + variant-aware add-to-cart) and five granular parts on `shopProductDetail` mirroring shop's `ShopDetail*`: `ShopVariantOptions`, `ShopVariantPersonalisation`, `ShopVariantPrice`, `ShopVariantAddToCart`, `ShopVariantGallery`. Each is a server wrapper → a client island; editor render is a labelled skeleton (preview), RSC render is live. Parts share one selection per product keyed by slug (`lib/use-variation-selection.ts`), so they sync when placed independently. `ShopVariantOptions` carries a field **Option name position** (`labelPlacement`, radio, `above` | `beside`, default `above`): `above` is the long-standing stacked look, `beside` puts each option's name on the same row as its choices for a narrow column. It threads block → `VariantOptionsPart` → `OptionControl`; the slot host (`DetailSlotPartsClient`) passes nothing and so keeps `above`, since a slot render has no block props to read. **Choices this combination cannot have** (`unavailable`, radio, `show` | `hide`, default `show`, v0.1.100) governs what becomes of a value the picks above it have ruled out: `show` keeps it in the row struck through and disabled with a line underneath saying where it IS to be had ("available in 160 to 180cm"), `hide` is the older behaviour of dropping it from the row entirely (the current pick and a stranded "ghost" pick always stay either way, so a control never blanks out). The sentence comes from `availableWith` + `availableWithSentence` in `lib/selection-logic.ts`, surfaced on the hook as `sel.availableIn(optionId, valueId)`: `availableWith` names each chosen upstream value that single-handedly rules the target out and, for each, which values of that same option would allow it (held against the upstream picks that are NOT culprits, buyable variants only), flagging whether they are one unbroken run of the option's display order; `availableWithSentence` collapses an unbroken run of 3+ measurements to "160 to 180cm" (shared trailing unit said once, and only where both ends end in a digit - "Oak, Ash or Walnut" is listed out) and otherwise lists them with a final "or". Empty when no single pick is the culprit (a clash needing a combination, or a value nothing buyable carries at all), where the choice just reads "unavailable" - it never invents a reason. Unavailable pills are dashed-bordered and `--color-text-muted` rather than the old `opacity: 0.4`, and the strike-through moved from the button onto the label span alone, or it would have struck out the one line the shopper is meant to read. In the accordion layout a section is collapsible on `option.values.length > 1` when `show` (vs reachable-count > 1 when `hide`), or an option narrowed to one pickable value would hide its "available in …" lines behind a disclosure that refuses to open. Covered by `lib/selection-logic.available.test.ts`. **`beside` is a float, not flex, and cannot become one** (v0.1.44): the name is `float: left` inside a `flow-root` container and the choices stay inline-level, so the first row clears the name and every wrapped row after it runs the full width. Flex was tried twice and is wrong in both directions - as a flex item the choices div is measured at its full unwrapped width when the row breaks its lines and gets pushed below the name entirely (v0.1.43 patched that with `flex: 1 1 0` + `min-width: 0`), and even once it sits beside the name a flex container is a block formatting context, so it is shoved aside by the float whole instead of flowing around it, leaving every wrapped row in a column beside the name with the space beneath the name wasted. Consequences: the choices' `gap` moves onto the buttons as margins (`gap` does nothing to inline layout) with a `-0.5rem` bottom margin on the wrapper swallowing the last row's, buttons get `vertical-align: top` so an image swatch's baseline cannot drag its row about, and containment is `flow-root` rather than `overflow: hidden` because hidden would clip the image swatch's absolutely positioned hover peek. Indicative storefront pricing and the authoritative server pricing use the same pure `computeAddonPricing` (`lib/addon-pricing.ts`), so they can't disagree.

**The page opens with nothing chosen (v0.1.13).** `firstPreselect` is gone from `lib/selection-logic.ts` and neither entry path (`seededEntry`, `ensureLoaded`) seeds a selection: the opening `optionValues` is `{}`, so the price shows the parent's `basePrice`, `resolveVariant` returns null and `canAdd` is false until the shopper picks. Preselecting the first buyable variant meant a combination nobody had chosen sat in the controls looking chosen, and the buy button was live over it. Two consequences worth knowing:
- **"Out of stock" must gate on `allOptionsChosen`, not just `!inStock`** (`VariantPricePart`). `inStock` is `hasOptions ? !!(variant && enabled && inStock) : true`, and with nothing chosen there is no variant - so the unguarded check labelled *every* options product sold out on load. The purchase parts were already safe: their `reason` chain tests `!allOptionsChosen` first and says "Choose your options".
- **`ResetOptionsLink`** (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`) renders after the last option in **both** hosts - the granular `VariantOptionsPart` and the slot path's `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` - and calls `resetOptions()` → `resetOptionValues(slug)`, clearing `optionValues` only. Personalisation (`addonValues`) survives on purpose: it's typing, not a click. It renders only when `anyOptionChosen`, which is also why RSC and hydration agree - a server render never has a selection, so neither emits the link.

- **The RSC halves live in their own files (v0.1.7): `components/puck/variant-parts.rsc.tsx` and `ShopVariantPurchase.rsc.tsx`, pointed at by the manifest's `rscImport`** (same split, same reason, as shop's `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx`). They resolve the selector payload server-side via `lib/variation-bootstrap.ts` and pass it to the island as `initial`, so the option controls are in the page's first HTML. Before this the RSC halves were pass-throughs that rendered nothing but the editor's skeleton, and every island waited for hydration → read the slug off `window.location` → `GET public/by-slug/[slug]/variations` + `GET /api/m/shop/public/config`, which is why the options arrived a beat after the rest of the page.
- **`lib/variation-bootstrap.ts` (server-only, pulls prisma - never import from a `'use client'` file).** `getVariationBootstrap(slug)` is React-`cache`d, so all six blocks share one query per request; it returns the payload plus shop's currency symbol (killing the second fetch). Puck's `<Render>` gives a block only its own saved props and shop injects context into its own part types alone (`inject-part-context.ts`), so there is no prop carrying the slug - instead `rememberProductSlug` records it into a `cache()`-scoped, therefore per-request, slot from the detail-parts provider's `claimsProduct`, which shop calls once per product page before any block renders. `currentProductSlug()`/`bootstrapForCurrentProduct()` read it back. A null is survivable, not fatal: the island falls back to the old fetch-after-mount path (the composite block on a bare `shopProduct` layout, say).
- **The selection store must not be written during a server render.** Module state is per-tab in the browser but per-process on the server, outliving the request: an entry seeded into `store` server-side would sit there marked loaded and hand the *next* shopper of that product whatever price and stock that render happened to see, until the instance recycled. So `useVariationSelection` builds a throwaway entry from `initial` when `typeof window === 'undefined'` and touches no module state; the browser seeds the shared store as normal (first seed per slug wins, so a re-render can't discard a live selection). The currency symbol rides on the entry rather than the module-level `let` for the same reason - otherwise a server render prints the `£` default and hydrates into the real symbol.

**Extension points provided**: `shop.product-editor-sections` → `ProductVariationsSection` (component); `shop.cart-line-resolver` → `resolveVariationLineMeta` (server function; maps a variant child back to its parent, loads the parent's add-ons, re-resolves file tokens from `svr_uploads` server-authoritatively, prices via `computeAddonPricing`, and returns a `displayTitle` - base name + chosen options, split by stripping the authoritative parent-name prefix in `lib/variant-title-cache.ts` (request-scoped batch, warmed by `prefetchVariationLineMeta`) - so the cart renders a variant's name and its options on separate lines); and `shop.product-detail-parts` → `shopVariationsDetailParts` (`lib/detail-parts-provider.ts`, an object, id `variations-detail-parts`) - **this is what makes shop's default Product Detail layout handle options with no layout editing**. `claimsProduct` runs server-side once per product page and returns true when the product has options or add-ons and is not itself a `catalogue_hidden` variant child; shop then renders this module's `Gallery`/`Price`/`PurchaseArea` in place of its own `ShopDetailGallery`/`ShopDetailPrice`/`ShopDetailAddToCart`. Those slot components are distinct from the granular Puck blocks below: they render into shop's own `.spd-*` class names (handed down as props) and from shop's server-loaded images/price, so the swap is invisible and paints on first byte. As of v0.1.7 they are split like the Puck blocks: `components/public/DetailSlotParts.tsx` holds **async server** halves that await `getVariationBootstrap(props.slug)` (shop hands the slug down on every slot prop, so no request-scoped lookup is needed here) and pass it to the islands in `DetailSlotPartsClient.tsx` as `initial`. Awaiting is within shop's contract - it types the slots as plain components but only ever renders them from its own RSC halves (`ShopDetail*Rsc`). `OptionControl`/`AddonControl` are shared with `VariantParts.tsx` so the hand-placed blocks and the automatic slot render the identical control. Unclaimed products, and shop-only sites, are untouched. **Also consumes `shop.product-page-resolver`** (id `variations-deep-link`, `lib/product-page-resolver.ts` `shopVariationsProductPageResolver`) - resolves a hidden variant child's own URL (the cart's product link) to its parent so the deep link opens the parent page with that combination pre-selected. `resolveVariantDeepLink` (`variants-service.ts`) does the child→parent + option-value-ids lookup (`getVariantByChildProductId` + `getVariantValueMap`); the resolver records the ids via `rememberPreselectOptionValues` (`variation-bootstrap.ts`, a second request-scoped `cache()` slot beside the product slug), which `getVariationBootstrap` surfaces as `VariationBootstrap.preselectOptionValueIds` (filtered to values the payload holds) and `use-variation-selection`'s `seededEntry` seeds as the opening `optionValues`. Because the page renders under the parent's slug (shop injects it) and every part reads that slug from its explicit prop, all three storefront paths key the selection store by the parent slug on server AND client, so the preselect hydrates with no slug mismatch - `window.location` (the child slug) is never consulted. **Also provides `shop.card-media`** (id `variations-card-media`, `lib/card-media-provider.ts` `shopVariationsCardMedia`, working tree) - one representative photo per enabled variation (its primary, else first still image), batched across the grid and folded into the product card's arrow carousel; images only, no overlay.
  - **`coveredSlots(blockTypes)` - not claiming a job the layout already does by hand.** The point assumed shop's part was the only thing doing each job. Layouts written before it existed do the same job with this module's granular blocks (Deskwell's product page carries `ShopVariantPrice` and `ShopVariantOptions` beside shop's `ShopDetailPrice`/`ShopDetailAddToCart`), so taking the slot as well rendered the price and the option picker twice. Shop now passes every block type in the layout (`collectLayoutBlockTypes`, walks `content` **and** `zones` - the default Product Detail keeps its parts in a Split's zones) and this module returns the covered slots: `ShopVariantGallery`→Gallery, `ShopVariantPrice`→Price, `ShopVariantAddToCart`→PurchaseArea. Shop then renders **nothing** for those (`ctx.slot.covered`), rather than falling back to its own part - a static parent price beside a live variant price is two different figures for one product. Only applies to claimed products; an unclaimed one never consults `covered`, so shop's parts render normally.
  - **A replaced part inherits none of shop's behaviour, only its classes (v0.1.9).** Shop's `imageZoomOnHover` setting (shop settings > General) reached `VariantSlotGalleryClient` as the optional `zoom` prop from shop 0.1.40 and was simply ignored, so the shop-wide zoom silently did nothing on exactly the products this module claims - anything with options. The island now implements it: pointer-tracked `transformOrigin` + `transform: scale(2.5)` on the stage image, mouse magnifying on hover, touch on tap-drag-tap, reset when the variant image or thumbnail pick changes. Shop's behaviour is **reimplemented, not imported** - its copy lives inside `ProductGallery`, which knows nothing of variant images, and the `zoomable`/`zoomed` modifier classes behind it are shop CSS the `classNames` contract does not hand over; the two declarations they carry (cursor, and `touch-action` while magnified) go on inline instead, keeping the fix inside this module. The scale constant is duplicated deliberately and must stay level with shop's, or one setting means two things depending on the product. Generalises: any future prop shop adds to a slot is inert until a provider reads it, and nothing fails loudly when it doesn't.
  - Options and personalisation have no shop part to replace, so they can't be handled that way: they ride inside `VariantSlotPurchase`, which drops them itself when `layoutBlockTypes` (on every slot prop) shows `ShopVariantOptions`/`ShopVariantPersonalisation` already placed. Shop only ever passes block-type strings it attaches no meaning to; this module is the only side that knows what they mean. Resolution is split - `resolveShopDetailProvider(product)` (the claim, still parallel with the template fetch) then the pure `narrowShopDetailSlot(provider, blockTypes)` once the template's blocks are known.

**Cron Jobs**: `0 3 * * *` → `cron/cleanup-uploads`.

**Known Limitations**: a layout that *hand-places* a granular `ShopVariant*` block next to shop's equivalent (`ShopVariantPrice` beside `ShopDetailPrice`, etc.) now double-renders on a claimed product, because shop's own part is variant-aware via the slot as of shop 0.1.35 - the two can't see each other (the slot is per-product, the blocks are per-layout, and shop knowing about `ShopVariant*` types is exactly the coupling the point exists to avoid). Stock layouts are unaffected (they contain shop's parts only); the fix for a hand-built one is to drop the now-redundant `ShopVariant*` block. Also: a variant's image set can only be cleared wholesale (the × drops all of them) - there is no per-image remove in the grid cell; `svr_settings` has no admin UI (defaults only) in v1; CSV import requires the parent product to exist by slug (creates options + child variants, not parents); deleting a parent product leaves its hidden children orphaned (retention cleanup covers uploads; child-product cleanup on parent delete / uninstall is a documented follow-up); a hidden child 404s on its own URL rather than redirecting to its parent.

### Product Attributes for Shop

- Slug: `product-attributes-for-shop` (table prefix `pat_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/product-attributes-for-shop`, manifest version 0.1.39 in the working tree (registry pin v0.1.17). `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.65` (raised in 0.1.6 for `MediaPickerModal`'s `resolveInitialFolderId`), `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.493` (raised in 0.1.6 for `core.media-reference-rewriters` + `moveOrRenameMedia`). Reuses shop's `shop.products` permission (declares none of its own) and joins the existing **Shop** admin nav group with one entry ("Product attributes").
- Adds shop-wide **filterable attributes** (Material, Colour, Room) with values. Each product carries a **set** of them (`pat_product_attributes`, v0.1.3): tick values for ordinary attributes, or flag one **Use for variations** to set its value per variant (a column on the Variations tab) and **Show in shop filters** off to keep it internal to that product. A storefront Puck block filters the catalogue by them. shop-variations is an **optional** companion, not a `requiresModules` entry: every `svr_` read goes through `lib/variations-bridge.ts` as raw SQL guarded by a `to_regclass` probe (30s cache, `resetVariationsProbeCache()` test seam), because `@/modules/shop-variations/...` does not resolve on an install without it and a static import would break that build. It also registers a **field provider** on shop-variations' `variant-field-provider` point (see below), likewise inert without shop-variations.

**Database**
Table prefix: `pat_` (6 tables). Full DDL in `modules/product-attributes-for-shop/migrations/001_initial.sql` (idempotent); later per-change files numbered (`002_product_attribute_sets.sql` adds `pat_product_attributes`; `003_image_control_type.sql` widens the control-type CHECK - no new column; `004_attribute_groups.sql` adds `pat_attribute_groups` + `pat_attributes.group_id`; `005_repeatable_product_attributes.sql` swaps both composite PKs for surrogate ids, adds `pat_product_attributes.name_override`/`position` and `pat_product_values.assignment_id`, and backfills each existing product-level tick onto the one helping it can have come from; `006_variation_columns_per_helping.sql` adds **no DDL at all** - it stamps `assignment_id` onto the per-variant rows 005 deliberately left NULL, so a variations column can belong to a helping rather than to an attribute; `007_swatch_size.sql` adds `pat_attribute_values.swatch_size`; `009_repoint_renamed_option_values.sql` adds **no DDL** - it is a data repair that re-points `svr_option_values.source_ref` onto the attribute value its label actually names, for copies a sheet rename left linked to their old value. 001/002 are **not** mirrored for these - both are idempotent and run on a fresh install too, so the end state is the same either way. 006 skips itself via `to_regclass('public.svr_variants')` when shop-variations is absent). Cross-module FKs to `shp_products` are safe because shop installs first.

- `pat_attribute_groups` (v0.1.7) - `id`, `name`, `slug` (unique), `position`, `created_at`. Admin-side folders only; nothing public reads them.
- `pat_attributes` - `id`, `name`, `slug` (unique; the storefront filter's query key), `control_type` (CHECKBOX\|SWATCH\|DROPDOWN\|IMAGE - IMAGE added 0.1.6), `position`, `show_in_filters` (shop-wide gate), `group_id?` FK → `pat_attribute_groups` **ON DELETE SET NULL** (v0.1.7 - deleting a folder must tip its attributes back onto the ungrouped pile, never cascade them and every product assignment away), `source_option_name?` (the shop-variations option name it was imported from, so a re-import updates rather than duplicates), `created_at`.
- `pat_attribute_values` - `id`, `attribute_id` FK (cascade), `label`, `slug` (unique per attribute), `swatch?` (**one column, two mediums as of 0.1.6**: a hex colour for a SWATCH attribute, a media url for an IMAGE one - same arrangement as `svr_option_values.swatch`), `swatch_size?` (**`007_swatch_size.sql`, v0.1.14** - the real-world size of the picture swatch, free text as typed: "20cm", "200mm", "0.2m" or a bare number; NULL/empty means "not given", which every value written before 007 is, so nothing may read a missing size as an error), `position`.
- `pat_product_values` - `id` PK (surrogate, added by `005_repeatable_product_attributes.sql`; was a composite PK on `(product_id, value_id)`), `product_id` FK→shp_products cascade, `value_id` FK cascade, `assignment_id?` FK→`pat_product_attributes` cascade, UNIQUE **NULLS NOT DISTINCT** `(product_id, value_id, assignment_id)`. `product_id` covers **both** parent products and shop-variations' hidden variant children - that is what makes per-variant attributes work with no second table. `assignment_id` says which *helping* of an attribute a tick belongs to. Since `006_variation_columns_per_helping.sql` that includes rows on a **variant child** (they carried NULL under 005, when one attribute meant one column and the row needed no further identity) - it is the only thing telling "Oak on the main finish" from "Oak on the edge", which are otherwise the same product, value and attribute. Still **nullable**: a row whose parent no longer uses that attribute for variations, or one written before 005, has no helping to name. The `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` clause keeps those de-duplicating properly.
- `pat_product_attributes` (v0.1.3) - `id` PK (surrogate, added by `005_repeatable_product_attributes.sql`; was a composite PK on `(product_id, attribute_id)`), `product_id` FK→shp_products cascade, `attribute_id` FK cascade, `name_override?` (TEXT, 005 - the name this helping goes by; NULL means "call it whatever the attribute is called"), `position` (INTEGER, 005), `use_for_variations` (bool, default false), `show_in_filters` (bool, default true - **per-product** filter gate, narrower than `pat_attributes.show_in_filters`; both apply), UNIQUE **NULLS NOT DISTINCT** `(product_id, attribute_id, name_override)`. The product's attribute "set" plus its per-helping flags. **A product may hold the same attribute several times** (005) - "Top material" and "Frame material" both off Material - with all but one carrying a `name_override`; the unique constraint is what enforces that, and the editor + PUT both state it in words first so the constraint is never what the owner meets. Membership is *not* a filter gate on its own - an assigned value still filters unless hidden here, and `getEffectiveValueIdsByProduct` only counts an attribute hidden when **every** helping of it on that product is (`HAVING bool_or(show_in_filters) = false`).
- `pat_settings` - singleton (`id='singleton'`): `hide_empty_values` (true), `include_variant_values` (true).

**A picture swatch carries its own real-world size (working tree, v0.1.14, unreleased)**: `007_swatch_size.sql` adds `pat_attribute_values.swatch_size` (nullable TEXT), surfaced as `PatAttributeValue.swatchSize` and validated at `SWATCH_SIZE_MAX_LENGTH` (40) in `lib/types.ts` - a length cap only, since the units are the reader's problem, not the store's. Set on the **Attributes** screen and, crucially, **editable afterwards**: an IMAGE attribute's add-value row gains a "Size, e.g. 20cm" box, and every existing value chip gains a small size button (shows the size, or "size?" when unset) that prompts for a new one and clears on blank - the figure usually arrives from the supplier after the photograph does, and deleting the value to re-add it with a size would drop every product ticked against it. Routes: `POST /attributes/[id]/values` and `PATCH /values/[id]` both take an optional `swatchSize`, normalising `''` to NULL so a cleared box and a never-filled one are one thing downstream; `createAttributeValue`/`updateAttributeValue` carry it (`!== undefined` guard on the update, so an explicit null clears). Column is deliberately **not** constrained to IMAGE attributes - an attribute can be switched between control types and losing the size on the way through would be a data-loss trap, the same reasoning `swatch` already follows. Not imported from shop-variations (no such field there) and not propagated to `svr_option_values` by `syncSourcedOptionValues` - the size is this module's fact about its own picture. Consumed by product-3d-views-for-shop's material configurator (see below).

**Permissions**: none of its own - all reads/writes gate on `shop.products` via shop's `requireShopUser` (GETs pass `allowAccess: true`).

**API Routes** (through `/api/m/product-attributes-for-shop/…`, all admin, all `shop.products`)

- `GET/POST admin/attributes`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/attributes/[id]` (rename re-slugs; case-insensitive duplicate name **within the same group** → 409 - see Attribute groups), `POST admin/attributes/[id]/values`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/values/[id]`. The values POST takes an optional `reuseExisting: true` (v0.1.5) that turns the duplicate-label 409 into "return the value that already has that label" - set by the two in-context add boxes on the product editor, left off by the attributes screen so a duplicate typed *there* is still reported as the mistake it is. Either way the response now carries the whole value row (`{ id, slug, value, reused }`), so a client can splice it into its list without a refetch. Both the values POST and the value PATCH validate `swatch` through `isValidSwatch` (hex **or** picture url, `SWATCH_MAX_LENGTH` 1000) rather than the old hex-only regex, and file a picked picture via `fileSwatchImage` before responding - filing can rewrite the url, so both re-read the row and hand back the **stored** url (`value.swatch` / `{ ok, swatch }`) instead of echoing what was sent.
- `POST admin/attributes/[id]/values/reorder` (v0.1.17) - whole-list drag reorder for one attribute's values; also pushes the order into any variation option copied from the attribute and renumbers the variants already generated from it. See "Value ordering" below.
- `POST admin/attributes/reorder`, `POST admin/groups/reorder` (v0.1.7) - take `{ ids: string[] }`, the **whole** running order, and write `position = index` in one transaction (`setAttributePositions` / `setAttributeGroupPositions`). Whole-list rather than "move this one up" because `position` is not unique-enforced, so two rows on the same number would make a swap a silent no-op; restating every row repairs the order as a side effect. A list with duplicates is 400; one that does not exactly match the ids on record is **409** ("reload the page") - a partial list would renumber the named rows to 0..n and leave everything else on its old number, shuffling rows nobody touched. Static-vs-dynamic precedence is safe: `scripts/generate-module-router.mjs` sorts static segments above `[param]` ones, so `attributes/reorder` cannot be swallowed by `attributes/[id]`.
- `GET/POST admin/groups`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/groups/[id]` (v0.1.7) - the attribute folders. POST/PATCH slugify and refuse a case-insensitive duplicate name with 409, same shape as attributes. PATCH on a rename and DELETE both **re-file the picture swatches** of every attribute involved (the group name is a folder segment); DELETE reads the membership *before* dropping the row, because the FK nulls `group_id` on the way out and there would be nothing left to walk. `PATCH admin/attributes/[id]` gains `groupId` (`string | null`, `null` meaning ungrouped - the zod field is `.nullable().optional()` so "take it out" and "leave it alone" stay distinct), 404s an unknown group, and re-files that attribute's pictures afterwards; `POST admin/attributes` takes the same optional `groupId` to create straight into a folder.
- `GET/POST admin/attributes/[id]/media-folder` (v0.1.6) - where the picture picker opens (GET, look-only, creates nothing) and where an upload should be filed (POST, creates). Same two-verb split, same reasoning, as shop's `products/[id]/media-folder`.
- `POST admin/refile-swatches` (working tree, unreleased) - walks every attribute and runs `refileAttributeSwatches`, moving each picture swatch into its `Shop/Attributes/[group]/<attribute>` folder. Idempotent (already-filed pictures are no-ops). Surfaced as a **Tidy picture folders** button on the attributes screen.
