Found on live Deskwell's Chiro Plus - `colourOptionId` on both slots is a bare `svr_options` id (Upholstery Colour / Back Colour), and its `sizeAttributeId` pointed at a `pat_attributes` row that **no longer exists**, so the legacy fallback resolved to nothing and every colour tiled at repeat 1 (a tile every ~0.93cm - the flat-grey mipmap symptom). `resolveFabricForChild` now also builds `swatchSizeByUrl` (every `pat_attribute_values` row with an http swatch and a non-empty `swatch_size`, keyed by the picture url, first row wins on a contradiction) and passes it to `composeFabricBundle` as an optional 6th argument. Lookup order per slot: the painted attribute value's own `swatchSize` → `swatchSizeByUrl[textureUrl]` → the legacy `sizeAttributeId`/`sizeManual`. **Matching on the picture is exactly as strong as the claim being made** - the size describes the photograph, so the same photograph in an option value and an attribute value is the same real material. Verified against live Deskwell: all 44 of that product's option values join 1:1 to an attribute value on `swatch`, with **zero** urls carrying two different sizes; resulting repeat 0.047 for a 20cm swatch (1 model unit ≈ 90.5cm), against 1.0 before. Three more cases in `resolve.test.ts` (40 tests), including two swatch sizes on one product - which a per-product size could not express at all. **A DB fix was considered and rejected**: re-pointing the config at the attribute would have painted nothing, since the variant children carry no `pat_product_values` for the colour attributes (only Overall Height).
- **Out of scope (v1)**: fabric↔leather (a material-*type* change, not baseColor), non-square swatches (parser takes the first number), independent U/V tiling. **Data-entry prerequisite**: swatch **size** and **overall height** attributes filled on all variant children; where missing, that slot stays at repeat 1 (colour applied, scale neutral) until filled.

**Known Limitations**: OBJ carries no materials (the `.mtl` sibling is never uploaded) so it renders plain white; a `.gltf` referencing external `.bin`/textures loads geometry only - GLB is the format to recommend and the editor says so. No settings tab. No reorder UI (models append). A model is not shown on product cards or in the cart, only on the product page. `loadModel`'s cache hands every caller `.clone(true)`, which **shares materials and textures** with the cached parse, so `disposeModel` on any one instance disposes them for all - benign today (three re-uploads from the surviving `ImageBitmap` on the next frame, confirmed by probe) but a real trap for anything that later assumes it owns its materials.

### Google Sheet Products for Shop

- Slug: `google-sheet-products-for-shop` (table prefix `gsp_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/google-sheet-products-for-shop`, manifest version **0.1.55**, pinned in `modules.json` at **v0.1.55** (0.1.8 was the resumable-Pull + Products-page-toolbar bump; 0.1.19 added the Supplier Catalogues tab; 0.1.21 the diff-at-start Pull rework; 0.1.42 the per-product variation tabs + resumable stepped Push; 0.1.44 the designed-description column; 0.1.45 the sheet's-own-column-order fix; 0.1.46 the Sheets-quota pacing + backoff below; 0.1.47 named every product/variation as a Pull writes it; 0.1.48 the batched tab reads below; 0.1.49 the read-only `variations` count column below). `requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.486 (re-confirm at tag time). `requiresModules`: **`shop >= 0.1.91`** (raised from 0.1.68 for `listSupplierCatalogues`; 0.1.61 was the release that published the `shop.products-toolbar` extension point this module's dropdown needs) and `shop-variations >= 0.1.105` (a hard dependency - a shop-without-variations site cannot install this; raised from 0.1.65 for the value-slug column and `lib/value-cell.ts`).
- **Status: registered and released**, pinned in `modules.json` at the version above.
- A hand-synced Google Sheet mirror of the shop catalogue. Two human-pressed buttons: **Push** (DB → sheet) and **Pull** (sheet → DB, after a diff preview and confirm). No crons, no background polling. It is a transport adapter: it moves grids between Google and shop's existing CSV export/import functions and shop-variations' `exportVariationsCsv`/`importVariationsCsv`, and writes no product-field mapping of its own. Adds no columns to `shp_*`/`svr_*`. Because it round-trips whatever those CSVs name, the Variations tab **automatically** gained the variant **Image**, **3D Files** and (working tree) the four **price-type** columns when shop-variations added them - the only in-module follow-ups were `FIXED_VARIATION_COLUMNS` (owned-column set) and the `pull-diff` change check.
- **The sheet's column order is the owner's (working tree, unreleased)**: a Push used to write the canonical export order over the tab, so dragging any of the module's own columns about was undone on the next Push - and, because header compatibility is all-or-nothing, that also flattened every formula on the tab, skipped the deleted-row plan (orphan rows, owner notes left beside the wrong product) and abandoned the sheet's row order. `orderColumnsLikeSheet` (`lib/formula-preserve.ts`) now permutes **every** pushed column to the sheet's existing header order, not just the open-ended attribute tail; a label the sheet has never seen (a column an update adds) appends at the far right of the block. Its `ownsColumn` param is gone - ownership no longer decides whether a column may move. `pushGrid` returns the `header` it actually wrote, and `pushProductsGrid` feeds that to `applyProductsValidation` rather than the canonical `productColumns()`, since a dropdown is cell state and a moved column would otherwise strand its rule on whatever now sits at the old index; `productsValidationRequests` (new pure export in `lib/workbook.ts`, unit-tested) clears validation across the pushed block before re-applying, owner columns to the right untouched. Variation tabs are no longer identified by "Parent Slug" in **A1**: `isVariationTab` (previously exported but unused) now looks across the whole header and is the single rule used by both `readMergedVariations` (Pull - a rearranged tab was invisible, reading as "the tab has gone") and `deleteOrphanVariationTabs` (Push - kept in step so one leg cannot read a tab the other ignores); `readFirstCells` became `readHeaderRows` (`values.batchGet` of `1:1` per tab, still one batched call). **Pull needed no change** - every reader already resolves columns by header name (`row-products.ts`, `pull-diff.ts`, shop's `resolveColumnMap`, shop-variations' csv, `variation-tabs.ts` `readLayout`), which is why rearranging survives a Pull and only the Push leg had to learn it. Renaming a heading is still fatal (that is the only thing identifying a column); an owner column left in the middle of ours is still nudged right rather than written over. Read me tab + wiki document both. No schema change, no version bump yet.
- **Designed description column (v0.1.44, working tree)**: the Products tab now carries `shp_products.description_puck` - the Puck document the storefront's `ShopProductDetail.rsc` renders in place of the plain-text description - in a column named `description_puck`, sitting **after** all of `CSV_COLUMNS` and **before** the open-ended product-field-provider tail. Deliberately NOT added to shop's `CSV_COLUMNS`: a JSON document has no business in a CSV a human opens, so shop's own export/import is untouched and this stays a column the sheet module owns (same reasoning as the provider columns). `lib/description-puck.ts` is the single contract, unit-tested (`description-puck.test.ts`, 21 cases): `descriptionPuckCell` (compact JSON, `''` for no design, and the `TOO_LARGE_CELL` sentinel above `CELL_CHAR_LIMIT` 45,000 - Google caps a cell at 50,000 and a **truncated** document written back on the next Pull would destroy a working product page), `readDescriptionPuckCell` (blank → clear, sentinel → skip, validated Puck shape → doc, anything else → `invalid` with an owner-readable reason; never a best-effort write), `canonicalJson` (key-sorted, array order preserved) and `descriptionPuckChanged`. Push: `buildProductsGrid` fills it from the `getProductsBySlugs` map it already loads, and `PRODUCT_COLUMN_NAMES` (the `ownsColumn` set) now includes it, or a Push would treat it as the owner's own column, shove it rightwards and never clear it. Pull: `diffProductRows` compares **document to document** through `canonicalJson` (so re-indented or re-keyed JSON is not an edit re-flagged on every Pull) and reports the change in words - `design (3 blocks)` → `no design` - because the confirm dialog prints changes inline and a whole document would bury the list; an unreadable cell counts as a change so the row is reported rather than silently skipped. The write-back is `lib/description-puck-pass.ts` (`applyDescriptionPuckPass`), run per products chunk in `pull-run.ts` right after `applyProductFieldsPass` for the same reason (the engine cannot see the column, and an unbounded pass will not fit under the dispatcher's 60s ceiling); it reads current state for the chunk in one query, writes through shop's `updateProduct` (which owns the `::jsonb` cast), and turns an invalid cell into a row error with the stored design left standing. Row→product matching was extracted out of `product-fields-pass.ts` into `lib/row-products.ts` (`matchRowsToProducts`, SKU-then-slug exactly as the import engine) and is now shared by both passes. Products tab only: variant children have no description designer. Read me tab and wiki updated.
- **Variation count column (0.1.49)**: the Products tab carries a `variations` column - how many variations each product has, which is exactly the row count of that product's own variation tab. `lib/variation-count.ts` (`VARIATIONS_COLUMN`, `getVariationCounts`) is one grouped `COUNT(*) … FROM "svr_variants" … GROUP BY "product_id"` for the whole catalogue, no per-row query; it counts every `svr_variants` row, enabled or not, because `getVariants` (which `exportVariationsCsv` runs off) applies no enabled filter, so the figure and the tab can never disagree. Written as a real number so the column sorts/sums, `0` rather than blank where a product has none. Sits after `description_puck` and before the product-field provider tail, and is added to `PRODUCT_COLUMN_NAMES` so a Push owns and clears it rather than mistaking it for the owner's own column. **Read-only**: it is not one of `CSV_COLUMNS`, so `resolveColumnMap` drops it and the import engine never sees it, and `diffProductRows` only compares columns it owns - an overtyped cell changes nothing and is corrected on the next Push. A product-field provider whose label normalises to `variations` is skipped with a `console.warn` (same rule as the existing duplicate-label guard) rather than emitting two columns under one header. Read me tab and wiki updated.
- **Google's rate limit is paced and retried, not hit (working tree, unreleased)**: `sheets.googleapis.com` allows **60 read and 60 write requests a minute per user** (per signed-in account, not per project), and per-product tabs made both easy to exceed - a Pull start is `readGrid(Products)` + `getSheetIds` + one `readGrid` **per variation tab** fired at concurrency 10 (`readMergedVariations`), and Preview does the identical sweep, so Preview-then-Pull was 2N+4 reads inside a minute; a Push spends 1-4 reads and 2-5 writes **per tab** in `pushGrid` (`readGridWithFormulas` before, `getSheetIds` when columns/rows shift, a second `readGridWithFormulas` when formulas were kept) with only a 35s clock stopping the loop. Google's answer is `429 Quota exceeded for quota metric 'Read requests'…`, and nothing except `writeFormulaRuns` retried it: `ok()` threw and the whole step FAILED. New pure `lib/rate-limit.ts` (unit-tested, `rate-limit.test.ts`, 12 cases) holds a `TokenBucket` (`perMinute`, `capacity` defaulting to it - starts full so a small catalogue is never slowed, then settles to 1/sec) with **separate read and write buckets** since Google counts the two quotas apart, a promise-chain queue so concurrent callers cannot all read the same stale token count and stampede, plus `shouldBackOff` / `backoffMs` / `MAX_BACKOFF_RETRIES`. `googleFetch` (`lib/sheets.ts`) now `awaitSlot(isRead)`s before every call (`isRead` = method GET, which classifies `values:batchGet` correctly) and retries with backoff: **429 on any method** (refused outright, never executed, so re-sending is safe) but **5xx on reads only** (a write that 500s may have been applied, and a repeated `insertDimension`/`deleteDimension` would shift the owner's columns twice). `Retry-After` is honoured in seconds or as an HTTP date, capped at `MAX_BACKOFF_MS` 10s, else exponential 1/2/4s with jitter; the body is drained before a retry so the connection is released. `writeFormulaRuns` keeps its own 3-try loop for **5xx only** now (429 having moved up into `googleFetch`) - it is the one write that must not be lost, since the write before it has already flattened those cells to plain values, and re-sending fixed formula text to fixed cells is idempotent. `push-run.ts` gained `STEP_MAX_TABS = 15` alongside the 35s budget, because small tabs are fast enough that one step could burn a whole minute's allowance and leave the next step throttled. `sheetFailureReason` gained a 429 branch in plain English ("Google is limiting how fast it will let us read and write this sheet… wait a minute, then carry on from where it stopped") - the raw message names `project_number:…` and means nothing to an owner. **Bucket scope is the process**, so it paces the burst that actually causes the 429 (one Pull's tab reads, one Push step's writes); two requests on two serverless instances can still overlap, which is what the backoff covers. **Known gap, closed in 0.1.48** (hit for real on Deskwell 2026-07-30): a Pull start big enough to be paced (over 60 tab reads) spent its extra second-per-read inside the dispatcher's 60s ceiling, so a workbook past roughly 110 variation tabs timed the route out before the quota stopped it - fixed by batching the reads (next bullet), not by moving them into the stepped job. tsc + eslint + 135 module tests clean. Wiki updated ("Google's speed limit"). No schema change, no version bump yet.
- **Batched tab reads (0.1.48, working tree, unreleased)**: a Pull start (and Preview, which runs the identical sweep) read every per-product variation tab with its own `values.get` - one token each from Google's 60-reads-a-minute allowance, so a workbook past ~110 tabs queued for minutes inside the dispatcher's un-overridable 60s ceiling and the owner saw only the 504 ("It ran out of time (sixty seconds) before your site answered") - the rate-limit entry's known gap, which Deskwell's ~200+ tab workbook then hit. Now the sweep is `values:batchGet`, which costs ONE quota token per request however many ranges it carries. New pure `lib/batch-ranges.ts` (unit-tested, `batch-ranges.test.ts`, 6 cases): `tabRange` (moved out of `sheets.ts`) and `batchGetGroups`, which groups tab titles so each batchGet URL stays ≤ 40 ranges and ≤ 6,000 encoded chars (Google rejects ~8KB request lines; a single monster title still gets a group of its own rather than being dropped). `lib/sheets.ts` gains `readGridsBatch` (whole tabs by the group, stringified exactly as `readGrid`) and `readHeaderRows` now chunks through the same groups - it previously put every title in one URL, fine for Push's handful of leftover-tab suspects, fatal for hundreds. `readMergedVariations` (`lib/pull-variations.ts`) becomes: `getSheetIds` → `readHeaderRows` over every non-reserved candidate (one row each, so an owner's own big tab costs a header, not its body) → `isVariationTab` filter → `readGridsBatch` of just the variation tabs; the concurrency-10 `mapLimit` fan-out is gone. A ~300-tab Pull start falls from ~300 paced reads (4+ minutes, dead at 60s) to ~16 requests (seconds), and Preview-then-Pull no longer drains the read quota Push wants moments later. Push's write side is untouched (writes are per-tab by nature and already stepped). tsc + eslint + 141 module tests clean. Wiki "Google's speed limit" updated.
- **Stock count and trade price are optional columns (0.1.55, working tree)**: `include_stock` / `include_trade_price` on `gsp_connection` (**migration `011_column_toggles.sql`**, both default true) decide whether `stock_count`/`trade_price` appear on the Products tab and `Stock`/`Trade Price` on each product's variation tab. New pure `lib/columns.ts` (`ColumnPrefs`, `DEFAULT_COLUMN_PREFS`, `columnPrefsFrom`, `excludedProductColumns`, `excludedVariationColumns`; `columns.test.ts`) is the only place the two names are mapped between tabs. **Push is the whole mechanism** - `productColumns(prefs)` / `buildProductsGrid(prefs)` / `splitWideGridByProduct(wide, excluded)` just leave the column out, and `planTabPush`'s existing narrower-grid clear (both names still in `ownsColumn`) sweeps the old one out of the sheet. The Pull needed no special case: `diffProductRows` compares only headers it finds, shop's engine `put()`s only when `hasColumn()`, shop-variations guards each optional column with `col >= 0`. Two fixes made it safe: `mergeVariationTabs` no longer pads an absent fixed column in blank (a blank `Stock` column reads as "clear every variant's stock" - it now emits a fixed column only when at least one tab carries it, which also covers a column an owner deleted by hand), and `missingProductsColumns(grid, excluded)` filters the switched-off columns out of the Pull's header refusal, with `lib/preview.ts` calling it instead of `missingFormatColumns` so preview and Pull agree. The stock **count** only: `track_inventory`, `low_stock_threshold` and `out_of_stock_behaviour` are settings, not figures, and stay. Switching a column either way shuffles the header, so that Push flattens formulas in our own columns (the owner's columns to the right are untouched) - documented in the wiki. Read me tab gained "COLUMNS YOU CAN LEAVE OUT".
- **Pull reuses the preview's sheet snapshot (0.1.54, working tree)**: Preview and `POST /pull` ran the identical Google sweep (Products `readGrid` + `readMergedVariations`) seconds apart - the re-read existed only so a stale preview could never start a Pull against a sheet that had moved on. New singleton table `gsp_sheet_snapshot` (**migration `010_sheet_snapshot.sql`**; `products_grid`/`variations_grid` jsonb + `drive_modified_time`; in `teardown`): the preview fetches Drive `modifiedTime` BEFORE its grid reads (so an edit racing the read files the snapshot under the OLD time and it simply never matches) and stores what it read, best-effort (`saveSheetSnapshot` - a failed save costs a re-read, never the preview). `POST /pull` loads the snapshot + one Drive `modifiedTime` call in parallel; `snapshotIsCurrent` (pure, `sheet-snapshot.test.ts`) demands EXACT ms equality with null-never-matches, so any hand edit, Push, missing snapshot or unanswered Drive falls back to the fresh sweep unchanged. The catalogue diff is recomputed either way - only Google reads are saved, so DB-side edits between preview and pull are always picked up, and the manifest guard still runs against whichever grids were used. Also `PROD_ROW_CHUNK` 25 → 40 (`pull-run.ts`) - each chunk re-parses CSV + re-resolves the column map, and chunk size never risks the 60s ceiling because the 35s step clock bounds chunk STARTS. Backup gate re-run for the new table: schema-coverage green, round-trip **real PASS (6/6)**. tsc + eslint + 182 module tests clean.
- **Push is batched and skips unchanged tabs (0.1.53, working tree)**: the Push leg finally got the treatment Pull's reads got in 0.1.48 - it used to spend 1-4 reads and 2-5 writes **per variation tab** (`pushGrid`), so ~200 tabs meant several quota-paced minutes. `lib/push-grid.ts` is refactored around a pure per-tab planner `planTabPush` (column alignment → widening insert → doomed rows → row ordering → formula preservation → clear ranges → skip decision; unit-tested in `push-batch.test.ts`) and a batched executor `pushGrids(spreadsheetId, inputs[])`: ONE `readGridsWithFormulasBatch` (new in `lib/sheets.ts`: `spreadsheets.get` with many `ranges=` + `includeGridData` + the same fields mask, grouped by `batchGetGroups`, matched back by sheet TITLE) for every tab in the batch, ONE atomic `spreadsheets.batchUpdate` for all structural inserts/deletes, ONE `values:batchUpdate` RAW for all grids (`writeGridsBatch`), ONE `values:batchClear` for stale rows/columns (`batchClearRanges`), ONE formula-restore and ONE verify-read + flatten - about 2 reads + 5 writes per 15-tab group instead of ~45+. `writeFormulaRuns`/`writeRawCells` now take tab-qualified runs/cells (multi-tab in one call); `pushGrid` survives as a one-entry wrapper (Products + Suppliers unchanged). **Skip-unchanged, two layers**: (a) `planTabPush` skips a tab whose pushed rectangle already matches cell-for-cell (`valuesMatch`, so formula cells pass on their evaluated value and survive untouched instead of being flattened-and-restored; error cells never pass), and clear ranges that are already blank are no longer written at all; (b) the manifest (`variation_tab_manifest`) entries now carry a sha256 `hash` of each pushed grid (`lib/grid-hash.ts`), and the next Push skips a tab **without even a read** when slug+title+hash match AND Drive `modifiedTime` ≤ `max(last_push_at, last_pull_at, last_push_attempt_at)`+120s (same trio and skew as the route's edit guard; `last_push_attempt_at` is in the baseline because our own earlier steps bump modifiedTime). Uncertainty (no Drive answer, no hash) just means the ordinary read-and-compare path. `push-run.ts`: VARIATION_TABS now works in `PUSH_GROUP_TABS = 15` groups via `pushVariationTabsBatch`, `STEP_MAX_TABS` 15 → 60, cursor/`written_titles` bank per group (skipped tabs still recorded - the orphan sweep would delete them otherwise), `stampLastPushAttempt` only when a group actually wrote; missing tabs are created formatting-and-all in ONE `batchUpdate` (`createVariationTabsBatch` in `lib/workbook.ts` - `addSheet` with EXPLICIT collision-free `sheetId`s so `headerFormattingRequests` can ride the same atomic call; `ensureVariationTab` kept for single use). **Quota is env-tunable (module env vars, both optional)**: `GSP_SHEETS_READS_PER_MINUTE` / `GSP_SHEETS_WRITES_PER_MINUTE` size the two token buckets (`perMinuteFromEnv` in `lib/rate-limit.ts`, ≥1, floored, default 60) for owners who get Google's per-user quota raised in the Cloud Console; declared `required:false` in the manifest. tsc + eslint + 179 module tests clean. Wiki "Google's speed limit" rewritten + new "Asking Google for a higher speed limit" section.
- **Pull runs with row errors stop reading as clean successes (0.1.51)**: `finalizePullJob` (`lib/pull-run.ts`) used to stamp both `gsp_sync_log` audit rows COMPLETED even when `prod_errors`/`var_errors` were non-empty, so shop-variations 0.1.104's per-row SKU-blocker errors were recorded but never surfaced - the run read as clean. Each tab's audit row now gets `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` when its error list is non-empty (new status value; migration `009_sync_log_partial_status.sql` widens the `gsp_sync_log_status_check` CHECK, `001` updated in step for fresh installs; `SyncStatus` union widened in `lib/types.ts`). The Recent-syncs modal (`components/ProductsToolbar.tsx` `LogsModal`) shows "N rows failed" in `--color-warning` beside the counts, expandable (`<details>`) to the per-row list (sheet row + reason); the error display keys off the stored `errors` rows rather than the status, so pre-009 rows logged COMPLETED with errors show theirs too. Version 0.1.51 in both `package.json` and `cactus.module.json`. tsc + eslint + 164 module tests clean. Wiki "Sheet logs" section updated. Not applied by hand to any DB - the migration runner picks 009 up on next deploy.
- **Per-product variation tabs (v0.1.42, working tree)**: variations no longer mirror into one wide "Variations" tab. Every variable product gets its OWN tab (named after it), carrying only the option/field columns it uses - no blank padding for some other product's fifth option. `lib/variation-tabs.ts` is the pure core (unit-tested, `variation-tabs.test.ts`): `productTabTitle` (sanitise Google's forbidden `[]:*?/\`, ≤100 chars, dedupe against reserved + taken), `splitWideGridByProduct` (Push: the wide DB grid → one narrow grid per product), `mergeVariationTabs` (Pull: read every product tab → back to the wide superset grid the whole Pull pipeline still works off, unchanged). Split and merge are exact inverses by column name (round-trip test). Reserved tab titles: `Products`, `Suppliers`, `Read me` (+ legacy `Variations`, `Supplier Catalogues`); a variation tab is any non-reserved tab with `Parent Slug` in A1.

**Database** (table prefix `gsp_`)

- `gsp_connection` - singleton (`id` keyed `'singleton'` by every writer). Encrypted (`lib/crypto/secrets`) `oauth_client_id_encrypted`, `oauth_client_secret_encrypted`, `oauth_access_token_encrypted`, `oauth_refresh_token_encrypted`; `oauth_token_expires_at`, `google_account_email` (display only), `spreadsheet_id`, `spreadsheet_url`, `include_cost_price` (bool, default true - **now vestigial**: the toggle was removed and cost price is always pushed, so nothing reads or writes this column any more; kept to avoid a needless migration), `include_stock` / `include_trade_price` (bool, default true, `011_column_toggles.sql`, 0.1.55 - the live column switches; off means the column is left out of the next Push and therefore never synced back, see `lib/columns.ts`), `last_push_at`, `last_pull_at`, `last_push_attempt_at`, `push_lock_until`, `variation_tab_manifest` (jsonb `[{slug,title,hash?}]`, added by `007_push_job.sql`, working tree - the product tabs the last Push wrote; the Pull refuses if a recorded slug is nowhere in the sheet, so a renamed/deleted product tab can't be read as "these variants were removed"; `hash` (0.1.53) is the pushed grid's sha256 so the next Push can skip an unchanged tab - absent on older manifests, no migration needed), `created_at`, `updated_at`.
- `gsp_sync_log` - one row per push/pull per tab. `direction` (PUSH|PULL), `tab` (PRODUCTS|VARIATIONS), `status` (COMPLETED|COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS|FAILED - the middle value added by `009_sync_log_partial_status.sql`, working tree: a finished Pull whose tab accumulated row errors is no longer logged as a plain COMPLETED; `finalizePullJob` picks the status per tab from `prodErrors`/`varErrors`), `created_count`/`updated_count`/`skipped_count`/`archived_count`, `errors` (jsonb), `run_by` (admin user id, no FK), `created_at`. Index on `created_at DESC`. All three CHECK constraints idempotent (`DO $$ … duplicate_object`; 009 is drop-then-add, idempotent as a pair). No row-id mapping table by design: products match by `sku`, variants by `Variant ID` (child product id, a sheet column since the working tree) falling back to parent slug + value-set. Backup round-trip re-run (real PASS, not skipped); schema-coverage backstop parses the migration - all column types (TEXT/BOOLEAN/TIMESTAMP(3)/INTEGER/JSONB) already supported, no sequences.
- `gsp_sheet_snapshot` (migration `010_sheet_snapshot.sql`, 0.1.54, working tree) - singleton (`id` `'singleton'`), the preview's sheet read kept for the Pull that follows: `products_grid`/`variations_grid` (jsonb, the full unfiltered grids exactly as read), `drive_modified_time` (the sheet's Drive modifiedTime fetched BEFORE the grids were read), `created_at`/`updated_at`. Overwritten on every preview, never cleared (a stale row's modifiedTime matches nothing). In `teardown`.
- `gsp_pull_job` (migration `002_pull_job.sql`, `deletion_plan` added by `003_deletion_plan.sql`, `products_done` added by `004_products_cursor.sql`, `current_item`/`current_offset`/`recent_items` added by `008_row_progress.sql`) - one row per Pull, the resumable job the browser drives step by step. `status` (RUNNING|COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELLED), `phase` (PRODUCTS|DELETIONS|VARIATIONS|DONE), `products_grid`/`variations_grid` (jsonb, **now diffed-and-filtered at start** - only rows that create/update/error, not the whole sheet - nulled once finished), `deletion_plan` (jsonb, `StoredDeletionPlan`, computed at start from the FULL sheet snapshot before it's filtered and applied verbatim by the DELETIONS phase; NULL on a job predating this column, in which case the runner falls back to re-planning from the stored grids), `last_push_at` (deletion baseline captured at start), `shop_import_job_id` (the `shp_import_jobs` row that carries live products progress), `detected` (jsonb, the confirm dialog's headline counts including `productsUnchanged`/`variationsUnchanged`, display-only, computed server-side from the diff - never client-supplied), `products_total`/`products_done`/`variations_total`/`variations_done` (the `*_done` pair double as each phase's resume cursor, counting only the filtered rows), accumulated `prod_*`/`var_*` counts, `prod_errors`/`var_errors` (jsonb), `error`, `run_by`, `created_at`/`updated_at`, plus the display-only live commentary `current_item` (text, the row an importer is writing right now), `current_offset` (int, rows of the chunk in flight already behind it - added to the phase's cursor for display, reset to 0 whenever the real cursor is banked, deliberately NOT a cursor itself because shop-variations flushes a parent's writes at the end of its group) and `recent_items` (jsonb string array, last 8 finished, newest first). Two CHECK constraints (status, phase) idempotent; index on `(status, created_at DESC)` for the "latest unfinished job" lookup. In `teardown`. Backup gate re-run for the new column: schema-coverage green, round-trip **real PASS (3/3)**.
- `gsp_push_job` (migration `007_push_job.sql`, working tree) - one row per Push, the resumable job the browser drives step by step (the Push mirror of `gsp_pull_job`, because per-product tabs turned a Push from a handful of writes into dozens - past the 60s ceiling and Google's write quota). `status` (RUNNING|COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELLED), `phase` (PRODUCTS|VARIATION_TABS|CLEANUP|DONE), `force` (bool, owner confirmed overwriting an edited sheet), `products_grid` (jsonb, built once at start), `variation_tabs` (jsonb `[{slug,name,title,grid}]`, the split per-product grids), `written_titles` (jsonb, tabs written so far - drives the CLEANUP orphan-tab sweep), `tabs_total`/`tabs_done` (`tabs_done` doubles as the resume cursor), `products_rows`/`variations_rows`/`suppliers_rows`/`formulas_kept`, `step_lease_until` (atomic-UPDATE step lease, pooler-safe, mirrors pull's `withPullStepLock`), `error`, `run_by`, `created_at`/`updated_at`. Two CHECK constraints idempotent; index on `(status, created_at DESC)`; **partial unique index `gsp_push_job_one_running` on `((1)) WHERE status='RUNNING'`** (at most one live Push). In `teardown`. Backup gate: schema-coverage green (all column types already supported), round-trip **real PASS (6/6)** (the earlier fail was `npm run` picking up a stale `.claude/worktrees/*` copy - `--root` main tree passes).

**Permissions**: `googlesheets.manage` (single; gates the settings tab and every route).

**API Routes** (served through `/api/m/google-sheet-products-for-shop/admin/…`)

- `GET /oauth/google/start` - mints state (cookie `cactus_gsp_oauth_state`), returns the Google authorize URL (scope `openid email drive.file`, `access_type=offline` + `prompt=consent`).
- `GET /oauth/google/callback` - verifies state, exchanges the code, stores tokens + account email, redirects to `…/config?tab=google-sheet-products-for-shop`.
- `GET/PATCH /settings` - status booleans + display fields (never secrets) / save client id+secret (paired), plus the `includeStock` / `includeTradePrice` column switches (0.1.55, `saveColumnPreferences`, each written only when sent). The `ENCRYPTION_KEY` 503 guard sits inside the credentials branch, so a checkbox-only PATCH (which stores nothing encrypted) is not refused for want of a key. No cost-price toggle any more (cost price is always pushed).
- `POST /disconnect` - null the tokens + email (keeps client creds + spreadsheet).
- `POST /sheet` - create the workbook (idempotent: returns the existing one). `POST /reset` - create a fresh workbook and repoint (old one left in Drive, not deleted).
- `POST /push` - **start a resumable Push (v0.1.42).** Snapshots the catalogue - `buildProductsGrid` + `buildVariationTabs` (the wide DB grid `splitWideGridByProduct` into one narrow grid per product), assigns each a tab title (reusing the manifest's title per slug so an existing tab is written into, not orphaned) - into a new `gsp_push_job` row and returns `{pushJobId, tabsTotal, phase:'PRODUCTS'}`; the writes happen in `/push/step`. The **overwrite guard runs once here** (before the job): reads Drive `modifiedTime` (`getSheetModifiedTime`) and, unless `{force:true}`, 409s `{error, needsConfirm:true, modifiedAt}` when newer than `max(last_push_at, last_pull_at, last_push_attempt_at)` by >120s skew. 409s `{pushJobId, resume:true, status}` when a Push is already unfinished. Was a synchronous one-shot before per-product tabs turned it into dozens of writes. **Formula preservation** (now applied **per product tab**) (`lib/push-grid.ts` + pure planner `lib/formula-preserve.ts`, tested in `lib/formula-preserve.test.ts`): each tab is read first with `readGridWithFormulas` (`spreadsheets.get?includeGridData=true&fields=sheets.data.rowData.values(userEnteredValue,effectiveValue)` - one call for both the formula text and its result), then written RAW as before, then the surviving formulas are put back with `writeFormulaRuns` (`values:batchUpdate`, `valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED`, contiguous cells grouped into runs). A formula survives only when **row index, column index and computed result are all unchanged**: written formula text does not shift its references the way a copy-paste would, so a preserved `=B5*1.2` in a moved row would point at the wrong product. Header comparison is prefix-based, so an owner's extra columns to the right do not block preservation; any header difference within the pushed width disables it wholesale. Numeric results compare with a 1e-9 *relative* tolerance (`=12.5*1.2` really is 15.000000000000002); text compares exactly with no numeric fallback (`"0100"` is not `100` in a barcode); an erroring formula is never preserved. `clearTab` is no longer used by Push - `clearRange` clears only rows the catalogue has given up (across the pushed columns only) and only columns it has given up that the tab **owns** (`ownsColumn`: `CSV_COLUMNS` for Products, the fixed names + `/^(Option|Value) \d+$/` for Variations). Known gap: a Variations column contributed by a variant-field provider module that has since been uninstalled has an unrecognisable label and is left behind as a stale column (Pull ignores unknown columns). Row identity for matching is SKU-then-slug (Products) and Variant ID-then-Variant SKU-then-(Parent Slug + option values) (Variations), the same fallbacks Pull matches on. **Overwrite guard**: before writing, reads the sheet's Drive `modifiedTime` (`getSheetModifiedTime` in `lib/sheets.ts`, `drive.file` scope covers metadata on the app's own file) and, unless the body carries `{force:true}`, 409s (`{error, needsConfirm:true, modifiedAt}`) when it is newer than `max(last_push_at, last_pull_at)` by more than a 120s clock-skew margin - i.e. the owner edited the sheet since Cactus last synced it. The toolbar turns that 409 into a `confirm()` and re-POSTs with `{force:true}`. The app's own syncs stamp their timestamps *after* their sheet writes, so they never trip it.
- `POST /push/step` `{pushJobId}` - run one bounded batch (`lib/push-run.ts` `stepPushJob`, under an atomic step lease) and return the live `PushStatus`. Browser loops/auto-retries exactly like `/pull/step`. Phases: PRODUCTS (`pushProductsGrid` from the snapshot + `applyProductsValidation`, one tab) → VARIATION_TABS (cursor `tabs_done`, 35s budget, **groups of 15 tabs** as of 0.1.53: hash+modifiedTime skip check, `createVariationTabsBatch` for the group's missing tabs in one call, then `pushVariationTabsBatch` = batched `pushGrids`, cursor banked per group, per-group CANCELLED check) → CLEANUP (`pushSuppliersTab`; `deleteOrphanVariationTabs` - any non-reserved tab NOT just written and carrying `Parent Slug` in A1 is a renamed/removed product's tab, deleted via one `readFirstCells` + `deleteSheets`, owner's own tabs spared; `setVariationTabManifest`; stamp `last_push`; `finalizePushJob` writes two `gsp_sync_log` rows once, atomic COMPLETED flip). Idempotent per phase.
- `GET /push/status?pushJobId=` - live `PushStatus` snapshot; with no id, the latest unfinished Push for the toolbar's Continue prompt, or null.
- `POST /push/cancel` `{pushJobId}` - abandon (tabs already written stay); returns `{ok, status}`. Same `AND status<>'CANCELLED'` write-guard + per-tab CANCELLED check as pull, so Stop lands within one tab.
- `POST /pull` - **start a resumable Pull.** Reads Products + **merges every per-product variation tab** (`readMergedVariations` - `getSheetIds`, batched `readHeaderRows` over every non-reserved candidate, then `readGridsBatch` of the `Parent Slug`-marked tabs in `values:batchGet` groups of ≤40, `mergeVariationTabs` back to the wide grid), **guards against a missing tab** (`variation_tab_manifest` slug not present in the merged grid → refuse, naming the tab, rather than delete its variants; a pre-manifest workbook falls back to the old "no Parent Slug header while shop has variants" refusal), then **diffs both against the shop right here** (`lib/pull-diff.ts`'s `diffProductRows`/`diffVariationRows`, the same functions the preview uses) and plans deletions from the full snapshot, then snapshots only the filtered grids (create/update/error rows) into a new `gsp_pull_job` row along with the full deletion plan, creates the linked `shp_import_jobs` row, returns `{pullJobId, productsTotal, variationsTotal, detected}` (202) - `detected` is computed here, not accepted from the request body, so the toolbar cannot start a Pull against stale or spoofed counts. No heavy work beyond the diff itself, no `after()`. 409s (`{error, pullJobId}`) if an unfinished job already exists.
- `POST /pull/step` `{pullJobId}` - run one bounded batch (`lib/pull-run.ts` `stepPullJob`) and return the live `PullStatus`. The browser loops this until `done`; a failed/errored step is **auto-retried by the browser loop** (up to 5 consecutive failures, backoff 2s..8s, counter reset whenever the phase/cursor advances) and reopening the modal onto an unfinished job auto-resumes - the Continue button is only the last resort once retries are exhausted. Phases: PRODUCTS (the **filtered** products CSV - unchanged rows already dropped by `/pull` - through `processImportJob` **25 rows per chunk under the same 35s step budget as variations, cursor `products_done` banked after every chunk (004)**; it used to be ONE unbounded call, so a big changed-row count died at the module dispatcher's 60s ceiling before the phase could advance and every retry restarted from row one - the "stuck on Updating products…" bug; after each chunk the running totals are written back onto the `shp_import_jobs` row so shop's own import listing reads true, and chunk-relative error row numbers are shifted by the cursor) → DELETIONS (status pass over the filtered products grid + the **stored** `deletion_plan` from job start, falling back to `planPullDeletions` only when a job predates that column, + `applyProductDeletions`/`applyVariationDeletions`, one step) → VARIATIONS (**50** rows/step-chunk via `importVariationsCsv` - up from 25, halving the per-parent preload repeats at chunk boundaries - filtered grid) → finalize (two `gsp_sync_log` rows, `skipped_count` now including the diff's unchanged-row count on top of the importer's own skips + stamp last-pull + clear grids). Every phase idempotent, so a replay after a failure/closed tab is safe. A failed step marks the job FAILED with the cursor intact. **Steps are serialised (2026-07-23):** `withPullStepLock` wraps the step in a `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` on `(0x67737001, hashtext(jobId))`, returning without running when another worker already holds it, so the browser's retry loop plus a reopened modal (or two tabs) cannot run two batches of the same job at once and double-apply a cursor. A transaction-scoped lock, deliberately, not a session-level one: a step killed at the module dispatcher's 60s ceiling takes its lock down with the request rather than stranding a lease, and it behaves correctly through connection pooling. The transaction's own `timeout` is therefore 60s (a step runs right up to the ceiling) with a 10s `maxWait` to get a pooled connection.
- `GET /pull/status?pullJobId=` - the live snapshot the progress UI polls (products-done is now the job's own `products_done` cursor - no `shp_import_jobs` read per poll). With no id, returns the latest unfinished job (RUNNING|FAILED) for the toolbar's Continue prompt, or null.
- `POST /pull/cancel` `{pullJobId}` - mark an unfinished job CANCELLED (whatever batches landed stay; they were idempotent writes). Returns `{ok, status}` - the snapshot as at cancellation, so the modal can show the tally of what did land. **Cancels a running Pull too (v0.1.22)**, not just a paused/failed one: `updatePullJob` now carries `AND "status" <> 'CANCELLED'` on its UPDATE, so every write left in an in-flight step (including the `catch` that would mark it FAILED) is a no-op and cannot resurrect the job to RUNNING; the VARIATIONS chunk loop calls the new `getPullJobStatus(id)` before each 25-row chunk and returns on CANCELLED, so a Stop lands within one chunk rather than at the end of the 35s step budget; and `finalizePullJob` bails on a cancelled job before writing the two `gsp_sync_log` rows or stamping last-pull (those go through their own writers, so the UPDATE guard alone would not have stopped a "COMPLETED" audit pair for an abandoned Pull). The PRODUCTS phase is now chunked too (25 rows via `processImportJob`, cursor `products_done`), with the same per-chunk CANCELLED check as variations - a Stop during it lands within one chunk instead of waiting out the whole products grid.
- `POST /pull/preview` - dry-run diff (creates/updates/unchanged/rowErrors, `products.toDelete` list, `variations.toUpdate`/`variations.toDelete` **lists** (`{parentName, label}` each, delete also carries `childProductId`; UI shows both, updates capped at 25 with an "and N more"), staleness), writes nothing. Now built on the shared `lib/pull-diff.ts` (`diffProductRows`/`diffVariationRows`) - the same functions `/pull` runs to decide what actually gets stored on the job, so the confirm dialog's counts are provably the Pull's counts, not a parallel calculation that can drift from it. Product-field comparison covers every `CSV_COLUMNS` column present in the sheet's header (enum/boolean columns case-insensitively), replacing the old preview's hand-picked subset. Row validation rejects a **negative** price as well as a missing or non-numeric one (matching shop's own `lib/import-engine.ts`) - `Number('-5')` is neither falsy nor NaN, so a minus sign in a sheet cell previously sailed through and created a product with a negative price. Variations "to update" is a **real field diff** (`variationRowChanged` mirrors `upsertVariantForCombination`'s changed check + the importer's image compare, column-present-only); a matched row whose values are identical counts as unchanged, so Push→Pull with no edits previews (and now actually runs) 0 updates instead of the whole catalogue. It **also asks each variant-field provider** (`resolveVariantFieldProviders(...).rowChanged`, preloaded per parent via `beginImport`) so a changed **3D Files** or **attribute** cell counts as an update too. A provider that owns columns but has no `rowChanged` makes "unchanged" unprovable for every one of its rows, so every matched row is conservatively counted as an update rather than silently skipped - slower than a real diff, never wrong.
- `GET /log` - recent `gsp_sync_log` rows.

**Supplier Catalogues tab (v0.1.19, working tree)** - a fourth workbook tab, `TAB.SUPPLIER_CATALOGUES = 'Supplier Catalogues'`, written by `lib/push-supplier-catalogues.ts` (`pushSupplierCataloguesTab`) at the end of a Push. **One-way**: Push writes it, Pull never reads it, and no `gsp_sync_log` row is written for it (the table's `tab` CHECK is `PRODUCTS|VARIATIONS` and this tab does not warrant a migration to widen it). Columns `Supplier | Status | Catalogue | Google Sheet URL`, one row per catalogue plus a catalogue-blank row for a supplier with none, sourced from shop's `listSupplierCatalogues()`. Goes through the same `pushGrid` as the other tabs purely for the **stale-row clear** - a deleted supplier or catalogue shortens the grid and the abandoned rows have to be cleared; row identity is `['Supplier','Catalogue']`, so a supplier with no catalogues forms no key and keeps no formulas. Workbooks created before the tab existed grow one on their next Push: `ensureSupplierCataloguesTab` (`lib/workbook.ts`) calls the new `addTab` (`lib/sheets.ts`, `batchUpdate.addSheet`, returns null when the title already exists) at index 2 and then applies the shared `headerFormattingRequests` (freeze/bold/protect/width, extracted from `createWorkbook` so creation and back-fill format identically). `TAB_ORDER` and the Read me both updated.

**Settings tab**: `google-sheet-products-for-shop` ("Google Sheet"), component `GoogleSheetSettingsTab`, permission `googlesheets.manage`. **Setup-only now** (Google connection, create/reset sheet); Push/Pull/Open/Logs moved to the Products page. The old cost-price toggle is gone - cost price is always included. A "What goes in the sheet" card (0.1.55) carries two save-on-click checkboxes - Stock count and Trade price - which PATCH `/settings` on change and revert the box if the save fails.
**Products-page toolbar**: `extensionPoints` entry `{ point: "shop.products-toolbar", id: "google-sheet-products-toolbar", permission: "googlesheets.manage", component: GoogleSheetProductsToolbar }` (`components/ProductsToolbar.tsx`) - a **Google Sheet ▾** dropdown (Open sheet / Push / Pull… / Sheet logs) rendered beside the Products header buttons, shown only once a sheet is connected. Pull opens the preview→confirm→live-progress→Continue modal; Sheet logs opens the Recent-syncs table as a modal. The point is published by shop (see Shop → `ProductsScreen.toolbarExtras`, resolved in `products/page.tsx`). **Pull modal, reworked:** the confirm view now shows how many rows already matched the shop and were skipped, a collapsible "what's changing on N products" detail listing each changed field (`from` → `to`, capped at 25 with a "…and N more" tail), and a plain "Your sheet already matches your shop" state with just a Close button when there is genuinely nothing to do. The button that starts the Pull no longer POSTs the browser's own `detected` guess - the server computes and returns it, so a preview left open for a while can't start a Pull against stale numbers. The live-progress view adds a `PhaseTracker` step strip (Products → Removals → Variations, with a ✓ on completed phases) above the two progress bars, and a line noting how many rows were skipped as unchanged. Small copy pass throughout: `n()` pluralises singular/plural properly ("1 product" not "1 product(s)"). **Stop pull (v0.1.22):** the live-progress view has a **Stop pull** button (confirm first) whenever the loop is running, including while it is auto-retrying a failed batch - previously the only Cancel was on a paused/failed job, so a running (or retry-looping) Pull could not be got out of. Pressing it sets a `stopRequested` ref that breaks the step loop before it asks for another batch, POSTs `/pull/cancel`, and renders the returned snapshot; the loop also breaks on any step whose status comes back `CANCELLED`. While the in-flight request finishes the dialog reads "Stopping - finishing the batch already under way…", then settles on a "Pull stopped" title, the tally of what landed, and a Close button (the phase tracker is hidden once cancelled). **Push is now a modal too (v0.1.42):** "Push to sheet…" opens `PushModal`, which starts the job on open (or resumes an unfinished one), then loops `/push/step` with the same auto-retry/Stop/Continue machinery as Pull; a `PushPhaseTracker` shows Products → Product tabs → Tidy up, one progress bar tracks tabs written, and a "Resume push…" menu item appears when the toolbar's `/push/status` load finds an unfinished job.
No nav entries, no Puck blocks, no public pages, no cron.

**Env vars**: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (required, token encryption), `SITE_URL` (required, OAuth redirect URI), `GSP_SHEETS_READS_PER_MINUTE` / `GSP_SHEETS_WRITES_PER_MINUTE` (optional, 0.1.53 - per-minute Sheets quota the token buckets pace to, default 60; set only after Google grants a raise).

**Key design points**: `drive.file` scope only (non-sensitive - no Google verification), which is why the module *creates* its own sheet rather than accepting a link. Owner registers their own Google Cloud OAuth client. The Testing-mode 7-day-refresh-token trap is surfaced inline in the settings tab and as a plain-English error on refresh failure (`GoogleAuthError`). Push builds the products grid directly (no CSV escaping, RAW write); pull converts the grid to import CSV with structural escaping only (no formula guard, so cells starting with `= + - @` aren't corrupted with a stray `'`). **Pull deletes on the sheet's say-so** (changed from the original archive-on-tick design): a product absent from the sheet is hard-deleted (cascading its variants); a variant absent from the sheet is pruned - partial (some rows removed) and full (a parent's whole block cleared) both handled. All deletion logic lives in one shared planner `lib/deletions.ts` (`planPullDeletions`), used by both the preview and the pull so their counts cannot diverge; execution helpers in `lib/delete-pass.ts` (`applyProductDeletions`/`applyVariationDeletions`, both `bulkDeleteProducts`). **Safety anchor**: only ever removes something whose `created_at <= last_push_at` - Push mirrors the whole catalogue, so anything created in the admin after the last push was never in the sheet and is spared; with no push on record, Pull deletes nothing. Uses shop `bulkDeleteProducts` and shop-variations `getEditorPayload` + `getProductIdsWithVariations` (the latter finds parents whose whole block was cleared). Order history survives deletion via `shp_order_items.product_id` ON DELETE SET NULL. Replaced files: `archive-pass.ts` and `reconcile-variations.ts` deleted; `pull-variations.ts` (create/update import) kept.

**Shop-side (Phase 0, in shop's own working tree, `shop` v0.1.55-to-be)**: three silent-data-loss bugs on a plain CSV export→import round trip, fixed in shop because they are shop's independently of this module. (1) `tax_class` was exported empty → import nulled every product's tax class; now exports the real code via new `getTaxClassCodesByIds` (`lib/db/tax-shipping.ts`). (2) media flattened to `IMAGE` and alt text dropped; now type-prefixed cells `TYPE:url` in `image_urls` with a new positionally-aligned `image_alt` column, backwards-compatible (un-prefixed → IMAGE), via `serializeMedia`/`parseMediaCells` (`lib/csv.ts`). (3) export clamped to 100 products (listProducts' public-list guard); now paginated via new `collectPaged` (clamp untouched). `CSV_COLUMNS` gains `image_alt`; `headerMatchesFormat`/new `missingFormatColumns` treat `image_alt` + `cost_price` as optional. Pure round-trip test `lib/csv-roundtrip.test.ts` (17 cases).

**The format now carries every owner-editable product field (working tree, shop + google-sheet-products-for-shop, unreleased).** `CSV_COLUMNS` was 24 columns and had drifted well behind `shp_products`, so the sheet (and the CSV) silently omitted `slug`, the dimensions, the digital-download rules, the pre-order fields and the related/upsell settings. Now 39 columns; everything added after the original 24 is in `OPTIONAL_CSV_COLUMNS`, so a pre-existing export still passes `headerMatchesFormat`. Deliberately still absent, and pinned by a test: id-shaped FKs (`digital_file_id`, `og_image_id`, `master_category_id`), derived counters (`pre_order_count`), and `catalogue_hidden` (shop-variations' own system state). Row-building moved to one place, new `modules/shop/lib/csv-rows.ts` (`buildProductCsvRows`), consumed by both the export route and the module's `push-products.ts` - the two hand-maintained copies are what let the drift happen. `import-engine.ts`: `ImportFields` is now `Partial`, and a field is only written when the CSV **carries its column** (absent = leave alone, present-but-blank = clear); row identity prefers the `slug` cell over `slugify(name)`; a slug edit renames the product (uniqueness excludes itself); `status` is now honoured on update as well as create (blank/invalid leaves it alone). `createProduct` gained the columns it accepted but never inserted (`weight_unit`, `meta_title`, `meta_description`, dimensions, download rules, pre-order, related/upsell) - imported products were losing them until re-saved in the admin. Module side: `NUMERIC_CSV_COLUMNS`/`BOOLEAN_CSV_COLUMNS` drive `typedCell` in `push-products.ts` so prices/stock/weights land as real numbers rather than text cells Sheets shows as `'100` (sku/barcode stay text - leading zeros); `writeGrid` takes `CellValue = string | number | boolean`; `sheetProductIdentity` (`deletions.ts`) counts **both** the row's slug cell and `slugify(name)`, without which a name edit would have made the Pull delete the product; `preview.ts` matches on the same identity and diffs the new fields; `related_mode`/`upsell_mode` gained sheet dropdowns and the Read me tab a slug section.

### Stock Imports for Shop

Module `stock-import-for-shop`, tablePrefix `stk_`, v0.1.1 (repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/stock-import-for-shop`, registry pin still v0.1.0 - 0.1.1 is working-tree only, unreleased; `requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.965, `requiresModules` shop >= 0.1.61 - the version that published `shop.products-toolbar`). Refreshes `shp_products.stock_count` from a supplier CSV url, matched on SKU, on an owner-chosen schedule or on demand.

**Database** (`stk_`): `stk_settings` singleton (`csv_url`, `sku_column` default `ProductCode`, `stock_column` default `FreeStock`, `frequency_hours` 0-168 CHECK, `missing_behaviour` CHECK IGNORE|ZERO, `enable_tracking`, `auth_user`, `auth_password_encrypted`, `last_run_at`); `stk_import_job` singleton (`status` CHECK FETCHING|APPLYING|COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELLED, `trigger` CHECK MANUAL|CRON, `pending` jsonb `[[sku, qty], ...]`, counters, `bad_values` jsonb, `lease_until`); `stk_import_log` (last 50, pruned on write). All three in the manifest `teardown`.

**The 60-second problem is the whole design.** Module routes carry an un-overridable `maxDuration=60`, and Deskwell's catalogue is 21,960 products / 21,577 SKUs against a 53,497-row, 6.4MB supplier file that takes ~5.5s just to download. So a run is a resumable job: FETCH (download, diff, park the writes in `pending`) then APPLY, 1,000 rows per `UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...)`, progress saved after every batch, stopping at a 45s budget with 15s of headroom. Whoever arrives next carries on - `POST admin/run/step` for the button (which loops until done), or the next hourly cron tick for an unattended run. `lease_until` (90s, `make_interval`) is what stops the button and the cron treading on each other; `claimJob` is a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE` so two callers racing produce exactly one winner, and the lease expiring by itself means a request that dies mid-run cannot wedge it shut.

**Why only changed rows are written.** `getSkuStock()` reads `sku`/`stock_count`/`track_inventory`/`type` for every product with a SKU and the diff (pure, `lib/diff.ts`) emits a write only where the count actually moved - a file that has not changed produces no writes at all. The pending pairs carry the shop's **own** SKU spelling, read back out of the table, so `applyStockBatch` compares `p."sku" = v."sku"` and uses the unique index rather than an `upper(btrim(...))` expression that would seq-scan once per batch; the case-insensitive matching happened once, in JavaScript. `low_stock_alerted_at` is cleared when the new count clears `low_stock_threshold`, or shop's daily low-stock cron would never re-alert after a restock.

**The frequency is a setting, which a Vercel Cron schedule cannot be.** The manifest registers one hourly tick (`5 * * * *`); `isRunDue` (`lib/schedule.ts`) decides whether enough of the owner's chosen interval has passed. The 10-minute tolerance is load-bearing: strict `elapsed >= frequency` would slip a daily run forwards a minute or two every tick until it had wandered an hour and started skipping days. A `last_run_at` in the future (clock skew, restored backup) is treated as due rather than wedging the schedule shut. `markRunStarted` stamps at **claim** time, not completion, so a broken feed pushes the next attempt out by a full interval instead of retrying hourly against someone else's server. **This needs a host that allows sub-daily crons - Vercel Hobby caps them at once a day** (Deskwell's team is Pro).

**Reading the file** (`lib/csv.ts`, `iterateCsvRows` is a generator - the import never holds 6.4MB of parsed rows): BOM, CRLF/CR/LF, quoted delimiters, doubled quotes, and a delimiter auto-detected from the heading line across `, ; \t |`. Columns are found **by name** (`findColumn`, case/space/underscore/hyphen-insensitive) so a supplier inserting a column upstream cannot silently shift which figure gets imported. `parseStockValue` reads `360`, `360.00` (floors - never rounds up), `1,250`, and floors `-4`/`(5)` at 0; **a blank or unreadable cell returns null and the product is left alone**, counted into `bad_values` rather than zeroed - guessing there is how a shop refuses orders it could have taken. `missing_behaviour` ZERO is opt-in for the same reason: right when the file is the whole catalogue, catastrophic when it is one supplier's slice.

**Feed safety** (`lib/feed-url.ts`, kept free of the prisma import so it is testable): http(s) only, and `isPrivateHost` refuses loopback/RFC1918/link-local/ULA/`.internal`/`.local` - the fetch is made by the site's own server, which can reach things the owner's browser cannot. `fetchFeed` reads through a reader with a 64MB ceiling rather than `response.text()`, times out at 30s, sends optional HTTP basic auth (password encrypted via `encryptSecret`), and rejects a body that starts `<!doctype html`/`<html`/`<?xml` - a login page served in place of the download is the commonest false success.

**Routes** (`/api/m/stock-import-for-shop/…`): `admin/settings` GET+PUT (`shop.manage`), `admin/test` POST (probe: columns, sample rows, and **how many of the file's codes match a product in the shop** - a valid CSV sharing no codes with the catalogue looks exactly like success), `admin/missing` GET (`shop.manage`; the products the **saved** feed never mentions, `?format=csv` for the download), `admin/run` POST, `admin/run/step` POST, `admin/run/status` GET (also returns `configured`, because the toolbar needs that and only managers may read settings), `admin/run/cancel` POST, `admin/log` GET, `cron/import` GET (`CRON_SECRET` bearer; resumes an unfinished job before considering a new one).

**Naming the products the file does not cover** (0.1.1; `lib/missing.ts`, `lib/missing-csv.ts`, `listMissingProducts` in `lib/db.ts`, `MissingProducts` in `components/SettingsTab.tsx`). The run log has always carried the `missing` **count**; the count is the wrong end of the question, because "412 products are not in the file" could be a dropped supplier range, a batch imported under the wrong codes, or four hundred variations of one chair. Points that matter: (1) **the comparison stays in JavaScript** - `findMissingProducts` builds the file's key set with the same `normaliseSku`, then hands `listMissingProducts` the shop's own SKU spellings for an exact `p."sku" IN (...)` match. Repeating the case-insensitive normalisation as `upper(btrim(...))` in SQL would be a second definition of "the same code" free to drift, and a list that disagrees with the count beside it is worse than no list. (2) **The SKUs travel as one jsonb parameter** (`SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb)`) - there can be 21,577 of them and a statement with 21,577 bind parameters is a different kind of problem. (3) **`svr_variants` is read when it exists, guarded by `to_regclass`** - shop-variations is deliberately NOT a declared dependency, and on Deskwell 21,505 of 21,577 SKUs are hidden variation children, so without the parent listing name the list is unusable; without the module the column simply says every product is a listing of its own. (4) **Reads the SAVED settings, not the form** - a report on a url nobody has committed to is a report on nothing. (5) Screen is capped at `MISSING_DISPLAY_LIMIT` 2,000 with `truncated` flagged; the CSV is uncapped. (6) `csvCell` prefixes `=`/`+`/`-`/`@` with an apostrophe - these are opened in Excel. Covered by `lib/missing-csv.test.ts` (12) and five new cases in `sql-shapes.live.test.ts` including both the with- and without-`svr_variants` branches and a 20,001-element parameter.

**UI**: settings sub-tab "Stock" hosted at `shop.settings-sub-tabs` (`shop.manage`); **Fetch Latest Stock** button contributed to `shop.products-toolbar` (`shop.products`), rendered only once a `csv_url` exists. The "Products not in your supplier's file" panel sits under Save: code, product (linked), parent listing (linked), status, current count and whether it is enforced, with a client-side search, 100-at-a-time paging and a blob download. It derives the admin path from `window.location.pathname` - hosted settings panels are handed no props but the tab is only ever on screen at `/<adminPath>/config` - and swallows Enter in its search box, which would otherwise submit the settings form it is nested inside. Deskwell reference point: 20,857 of its 21,577 SKUs match `https://edi.dynamicos.co.uk/Uploads/178/STK.csv` directly, no transformation.

### Advanced Shipping for Shop

Module `advanced-shipping-for-shop`, tablePrefix `ash_`, v0.1.32 (requiresCoreVersion 0.5.698; `requiresModules` shop >= 0.1.169 - the `shop.order-payment-state` point and `LineMeta.data`; before that the `shop.cart-summary` point, the summary picker types, the `CartLineCharge` attribution, the shared `CartLineControlView` and `subscribeCartAdd` all live there - product-attributes-for-shop >= 0.1.27). Concrete working-day delivery dates plus per-item delivery services (with shopper-facing descriptions) priced into the cart and snapshotted onto the order.

- **Tables** (`migrations/001_initial.sql` + `002` → `007_merge_rules_into_services`): `ash_settings`, `ash_service_tiers`, `ash_tier_scope_config`, `ash_holidays`. `ash_delivery_rules` and `ash_product_overrides` are GONE as of v0.1.18 (manifest `teardown` still lists them for stale installs).
- **v0.1.18 merged the rules layer into the services.** Live data had degenerated every rule into "base transit per range" (cut-off/dispatch/ship-days identical across all six rules; overrides table empty; MTO/backorder/supplier-binding all unused), yet each estimate resolved TWO most-specific-wins stacks and summed deltas across them. Now: shop-wide dispatch timing (`cutoff_time`/`dispatch_lead_days`/`ship_days`) lives on `ash_settings`; each service carries ABSOLUTE `transit_days` + `min_lead_days` (+ new shopper-facing `description`); a scope row can override both absolutely (NULL inherits). Offering = existence of a matching scope row (range > category > supplier > default; `settings.default_tier_key` is offered everywhere at £0). `007` folds old numbers exactly (per-scope absolute = old deltas + same-scope rule base, materialising rows for DEFAULT-priced services under scoped rules; supplier-bound tiers' DEFAULT rows become SUPPLIER rows) then drops the old columns/tables - dry-run verified against live Deskwell: standard 5 (Impulse 25 / Fast Track 15 / Cut Outs 15), installation 10 (Impulse 30), express 1, identical to the old effective numbers. Dropped concepts: `fulfilment_mode`/MTO lead (unused; pre-order still stock-driven), `backorder_lead_days` (a BACKORDER line now promises normal timing, flagged `isBackorder`), per-product overrides, tier `supplier` binding (a single SUPPLIER scope row does the same job), dispatch/transit deltas.
- **Extension points consumed**: `shop.cart-line-resolver` + `shop.cart-line-resolver-prefetch` (id `shipping-tier`, `lib/line-resolver.ts` - prices the chosen service, offers the cart's per-line picker with per-option `description`, blocks a per-person service with no readable count), `shop.cart-summary` (id `delivery`), `shop.order-payment-state` (id `deferred-delivery`, `lib/order-payment-state.ts`), and three `shop.tax-shipping-tabs` (Delivery services / Holidays / Delivery settings). The `shop.product-editor-sections` Delivery tab is gone with the overrides.
- **Puck blocks**: `ShopDeliveryEstimate` ("Product: Delivery estimate", layouts `shopProductDetail`/`shopProduct`) and `ShopDeliveryCartSummary` ("Delivery: basket cut-off countdown", layout `shopCart`). Both are two-file client islands that fetch `POST /api/m/advanced-shipping-for-shop/estimate` - no server product context needed. The cart block **renders the countdown and nothing else** as of v0.1.16: it used to lead with a grouped "Arrives in 2 deliveries: Fri 31 Jul (1 item)…" list, which restated dates every cart line already shows beside its own tier picker. The block type is unchanged, so a placed instance survives the change; only the editor label moved.
- **Routes**: `POST /api/m/advanced-shipping-for-shop/estimate` (public; per-item estimate + grouped "arrives in N deliveries"; items carry `tiers[].description`, `isMadeToOrder` is gone from the payload), a `/admin/*` set for tiers, tier-config, holidays (+ import), options, preview (dispatch timing + optional service timing) and settings (now incl. `cutoffTime`/`dispatchLeadDays`/`shipDays`), and `cron/refresh-holidays` (`0 3 * * 1`). `/admin/rules` and `/admin/overrides` are gone.
- **Basket-wide delivery note (v0.1.19):** `lib/cart-summary.ts` `summariseCartDelivery` provides `shop.cart-summary` (manifest id `delivery`) - walks the cart lines, takes each one's chosen service via the newly exported `chosenTierKey(delivery, meta, defaultTierKey)` (shared with the line resolver so the two can never disagree), and returns `everything by <formatDeliveryByLabel(latest)>`. Reads the prefetched request cache, so it is date arithmetic, not queries; lines with no date (blocked/out of stock) are skipped, and an all-dateless basket returns null (no note).
- **`cartControlStyle` gained `'summary'`, now the default (working tree):** `CartControlStyle = 'summary' | 'dropdown' | 'radios'` (`lib/types.ts` + `isCartControlStyle`), defaulted in `lib/db/settings.ts` (FALLBACK, `mapRow`, `updateSettings`), widened in the settings `PATCH` zod enum, and offered in `SettingsScreen` as "Chosen service, with the rest as chips". `lib/line-resolver.ts` maps it to shop's `renderAs` and every option now carries `summary` from the new exported `tierOptionSummary(label, price, symbol, byLabel, dateLabel)` - "Arrives by Thu 6 Aug" / "Flat-pack" / "Flat-pack by Friday" / "Free"|"+£25.95"|"Per person" (unit-tested). **A stored `'dropdown'` still wins**, so an existing install keeps its dropdown until Delivery settings is changed.
- **"Arrives by" dates spelled out in full (v0.1.20, working tree):** `formatDeliveryDate` went from `Wed 29 Jul` to **`Wednesday 29th of July`** (`WEEKDAY_FULL` + a new `MONTH_FULL` table + the existing `ordinal`; `WEEKDAY_LABELS` is now unused and gone, `MONTH_LABELS` survives for the short label). That is every "Arrives by …" headline, the arrivals cards, the order-line snapshot and the `(was …)` half of an upgrade chip. `formatDeliveryByLabel` is deliberately UNCHANGED - it is the tight-space label (switch chips, sticky bar), still "Friday" inside a week, "Friday 7th" to 28 days, "Friday 7th Aug" beyond. 7 new ordinal cases in `working-days.test.ts` (1st/2nd/3rd/11th/12th/13th/21st).
- **Two more `shopCart` Puck blocks + a richer estimate payload (v0.1.20, working tree):** `ShopDeliveryBasketOffers` ("Delivery: whole-order upgrades") and `ShopDeliveryArrivals` ("Delivery: basket arrivals summary"), both two-file client islands over the same estimate route. To feed them, `POST /api/m/advanced-shipping-for-shop/estimate` gained an optional per-item `ref` (echoed back untouched - the caller sends its `cartLineKey` so two lines of one product can be told apart), and `estimateItems` now returns `name` per item (one extra batched `shp_products` query, `getProductNames`), `priceEffective`/`targetDate`/`targetLabel` on EVERY tier rather than only the chosen one (IO-free `computeEstimate` per tier over already-resolved data), and `deliveries[]` groups carrying `names[]` + `tierLabels[]` as well as the count. Offers row gates on >= 2 cart lines; arrivals panel gates on >= 2 distinct dates (one date is what each line already says beside itself).
- **`lib/basket-offers.ts` (pure, unit-tested in `basket-offers.test.ts`, 10 cases):** `buildBasketOffers(items, todayStr)` turns an estimate result into `BasketOffer[]` - a `sooner` offer (every line onto its earliest-arriving service, price-broken ties) plus one per named service offered on 2+ lines, each carrying `extraCost` (summed delta), `itemCount`, finished `detail` copy and the `changes[]` (`{ref, tierKey}`) the island writes back via shop's `setLineMeta`. Refuses any move it cannot price (a per-person service with no readable count) rather than quoting a total the checkout would then disagree with; drops an offer whose `changes` duplicate one already listed; `describeDates` leads with the LAST date (when the order is complete), falls back to the first, and says plainly when a service lands later. `formatOfferPrice` words `+£13.90` / `£4.00 off` / `Included`.
- **`lib/line-resolver.ts` now attributes its charge:** the resolution carries `charges: [{ label: 'Delivery', amount: priceAdjust }]` (per unit, positive only), so shop's cart can show the service money on a Delivery row instead of burying it in the goods subtotal. It is an attribution of money already inside `priceAdjust`, never an addition.
- **The picker follows the chosen variation (v0.1.23, working tree):** on a variations catalogue the listing product often carries NO delivery scope at all (Deskwell keys delivery off the Range attribute, and Range is a per-variation option there: 4582 of 4622 products have one, and every variations LISTING is in the 40 that do not), so `hasEstimate:false` and the block hid itself on every product page. Two halves. (1) `shop-variations` v0.1.102 publishes the resolved variation page-wide - `lib/selection-broadcast.ts`, event `cactus-shop-variant-selection`, latest detail parked on `window.__cactusVariantSelection`, published from `useVariationSelection` and deduped by JSON equality since every island on the page runs the hook. A browser event, NOT an import, in both directions: `@/modules/shop-variations/...` does not exist on an install without the module, so a static import would break that build (same rule as `variations-bridge.ts` on the server). (2) `advanced-shipping-for-shop` listens for it: null selection asks about the listing with a new per-item `variantFallback: true`, a settled selection asks about that exact child product id. `variantFallback` makes `estimateItems` resolve the listing's enabled variation children (new `getVariantChildIds` in the variations bridge) and merge them in `mergeVariantDeliveries`: the INTERSECTION of service keys, the dearest price across the children, and the timing/stock of the slowest child - so the preview can never be undercut or withdrawn once a combination is chosen. The cart never sets the flag (its lines are the variations already).
- **Product-page service picker (`ShopShippingOptions`, v0.1.22, working tree):** "Product: Shipping options" (layouts `shopProductDetail`/`shopProduct`, one `heading` text field, empty by default as of v0.1.24 - the options state their own outcome, so a label over them only repeats it), a two-file client island over the same estimate route. It renders **shop's own** `CartLineControlView` with shop's `CART_LINE_CSS`, never a copy of that markup, so the product page shows the identical picker to the basket. `lib/product-control.ts` (pure) rebuilds shop's `CartLineControl` from an `ItemEstimate` - `optionsSelfLabelled`, `renderAs` from the owner's `cartControlStyle`, per-option `label`/`summary`/`description`/`priceAdjust` - and the wording comes from the new pure `lib/tier-labels.ts` (`effectiveTierPrice`, `tierOptionLabel`, `tierOptionSummary` lifted out of the server-only `lib/line-resolver.ts`, which now re-exports them so existing callers and tests are unchanged). Feeding it: `estimateItems` adds `tiers[].targetByLabel` (the tight-space "by Friday" wording the switch chips need) and a top-level `controlStyle`, and `lib/product-slug.ts` holds the URL→slug helper both product-page islands share. Behaviour of a pick: remembered per product in `sessionStorage` (`cactus_ash_product_tier:<slug>`, session-scoped, not a standing preference), written immediately onto any basket line of the same product id via shop's `setLineMeta`, and otherwise applied to the line the next add-to-cart creates (keys diffed against a snapshot taken at mount/last add, since shop fires its change event BEFORE its add event) - which covers a variation adding its own product id. Only a pick the shopper actually made is written; an unoffered service is ignored by the cart-line resolver, which falls back to the shop default, so a variant that lacks the chosen service is still priced correctly.
- **Every service shown, the ones this variation cannot have crossed out (working tree):** the listing preview only ever showed what ALL variations agree on (`mergeVariantDeliveries` intersects), and once a variation was settled the picker asked about that child alone - either way a service another variation carries simply vanished, and nothing told the shopper a different width would bring it back. Now the estimate answers for the whole listing: new per-item request flag `variantAlternatives` (zod-validated in the route, threaded through `EstimateItemInput`) makes `estimateItems` find the listing (up via `getVariantParents` when the item IS a variation, else the item itself), resolve every enabled child once - the same resolve the `variantFallback` merge already needed, now shared between the two - and return `ItemEstimate.otherTiers: UnavailableTierOption[]` = every service some sibling offers that this product does not, each with `label`, `description`, `priceEffective` (dearest across the variations that DO carry it, tax-display adjusted) and a finished `note`. Deliberately NOT merged into `tiers`: every existing reader treats `tiers` as "what this line may switch to" (basket offers, "everything sooner"), and these carry no date because there is no honest date for a service that needs a different product. New pure `lib/tier-availability.ts` (unit-tested, `tier-availability.test.ts`, 12 cases) builds the note - `availableWithGroups` names only the options that actually narrow it down (an option every variation satisfies, or one the shopper's own pick already satisfies, is not the culprit) and `availableWithPhrase` words it "Available in 120 to 160cm and Oak" / "Available With Arms", falling back to "Not available on this choice". The grammar is a deliberate re-statement of shop-variations' own `availableWithPhrase`, not an import (that path does not exist on an install without the module). New bridge reads in `lib/variations-bridge.ts`: `getListingSiblings` and `getVariantOptionValues` (option name/position + value label/position per child, straight off `svr_*`). `DeliveryServicePicker` sends the flag on both request shapes and renders the extras as a second row under the live chips - struck-through label, price, note line, dashed border and muted ink to match an out-of-reach variation choice, inert (no radio, no hover lift) - and now renders that row even when the product has no picker of its own (`control` null + `otherTiers` non-empty), which is exactly the listing whose variations agree on nothing.
- **The crossed-out services are worded against the picks so far, not the listing (working tree):** the first cut answered "where is this service to be had?" from the whole listing, which on Deskwell's Eclipse Plus Deluxe Mesh listed 14 of its 24 colours as carrying express - true range-wide (14 colours have at least one `Range=Seating` child) but wrong for the shopper, who had already picked Adjustments and Arm Option and for whom only 4 of those colours actually carry it. So `shop-variations` 0.1.104 adds `chosenValueIds` to its `cactus-shop-variant-selection` broadcast (every option value picked so far, in option order; `productId` only appears once the LAST option is settled, so there was nothing else to read a half-built combination from), the picker forwards it as a per-item `chosenValueIds` on the estimate request (zod-validated, cap 50), and `availableWithGroups` now answers in three stages: (1) still reachable on the current picks -> name only the UNPICKED options, measured among the variations that match those picks; (2) a pick is in the way -> relax each picked option in turn to find which one, and what it would have to become; (3) nothing single explains it -> the old listing-wide answer. Return type went from `AvailableWithGroup[]` to `AvailableWith { groups, join }` because stages 1 and 3 are conjunctions ("in 160cm and Oak" - both) while stage 2's groups are independent ways out ("in Seat Height & Backrest Tilt or Height Adjustable & Folding Arms" - either), and joining those with "and" told the shopper to do twice the work. Verified against the live Deskwell matrix (192 enabled children): the same listing that read 14 colours now reads 4 on Loop Arms, 8 on Height Adjustable & Folding Arms, and names the two adjustments/arms escapes where a combination carries no express at all. Reading `chosenValueIds` is defensive - an older shop-variations publishes the event without it, which reads as "nothing picked" and gives exactly the old behaviour.
- **Product-page picker chips 10% smaller than the basket's (working tree):** `.ash-svc`-scoped overrides of `.scl-hints`/`.scl-hints-t`/`.scl-hint`/`.scl-hint-fee` (every value shop's own x 0.9, coarse-pointer padding included so a fingertip target survives). The cart and the slide-out basket keep their own sizes.
- **Arrivals cards can show photos instead of names (working tree, unversioned):** `ShopDeliveryArrivals` gained an `itemDisplay` radio field (`'names'` | `'photos'`, defaulting to `names`; an older saved block has it undefined, which reads as `names`). In photo mode `DeliveryArrivals` fires shop's `postCartValidate` alongside the estimate call - the same single-flighted helper the basket's own islands use, so on a cart page carrying both it is one shared round-trip, not two - and matches the two responses by cart line key (`ItemEstimate.ref` ↔ `lineId ?? productId`) into `Record<date, ArrivalItem[]>`.
